==Description==
Bookkeeper Andros is an [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. He offers information related to The Old World. He is crucial towards the obtainment for [[Oath: Soulbreaker|Soulbreaker]] telling you about the King's Ardour and his abilities providing a lot of information about him, and provides information about [[The Lord Regent]] in the quest to defeat [[Duke Erisia]].

==Location==
Bookkeeper Andros is located in [[Etris]] in his small library that is nearby the inn, he stands near the chimney.
<gallery widths="300px">
Bookkeeper Andros's Library.png{{!}}His Library
Bookkeeper Andros's Location.png{{!}}Bookkeeper Andros's Location
</gallery>

==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{{#tag:tabber|Base Dialogue=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Oh! Uh, hello. Pardon me, I was rather deep in thought.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}About what?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Well, I was reading through a book my grandfather left me... one of the {{g|The Old World|old world}}, yes?... It spoke of the trade routes frequented in those days, but peculiarly these journeys were taken by horse and carriage, rather than by sea.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}[Continue]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Isn't that remarkable? That they travelled such distances by animal? Just what world did our ancestors live in?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Enemy Reputation=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Huh? I'm sorry... I don't have anything for you. Please, I could get into a lot of trouble for speaking to you.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}
}}

|-|Subsequent Encounters=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}These old books are more of a passing fancy of mine, but I've heard there's an order of scholars that devote their life to researching the {{g|The Old World|old world}}. Don't you wonder what things were like back then?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is there anything you can tell me about Etris?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is there anything you can tell me about the Old World?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}If you head past the inn, you'll find the Lord Regent's estate. I would not advise entering without an invitation, however. Even a bookish fool such as I knows when I am not welcome.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}There is much for us all to learn about it and its people. I'm by no means an expert, but my grandfather was one of the {{g|The Old Stewards|Old Stewards}}, the keepers of the knowledge of the {{g|The Old World|Old World}}. Perhaps if you were able to find one of these {{g|The Old Stewards|Old Stewards}} they might be able to answer any burning questions of yours.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Who is this Lord Regent exactly?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}The Lord Regent is the 'acting regent' of Etrea. That is to say, he is not the prophesied King, but he still holds absolute power over Etrea. In recent years, he has sequestered himself away in his palace, rarely making an appearance. Some worry that he has grown ill, but considering that his duties have not been passed on to any of his officials, I doubt this is the case.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

|-|Unlockable Dialogues=
{{#tag:tabber|Old King of Etrea=
This dialogue is unlocked if the player has spoken to [[Theadre]] and asked "What do you think of The Lord Regent?"
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}These old books are more of a passing fancy of mine, but I've heard there's an order of scholars that devote their life to researching the {{g|The Old World|old world}}. Don't you wonder what things were like back then?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I've heard about a King of Etrea, what can you tell me about him?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Ah, hard to avoid hearing about him here. He's somewhat of a mythical figure, though there was a real man behind all the myth. King Rolen Vashtir I reigned through the early 6th century CE and made quite a name for himself and Etrea on the world stage. As fate would sadly have it, he set off on a voyage with a small fleet of ships and never returned
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}The 6th century CE?! They don't seriously think he's coming back, do they?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Even if it's farfetched, I suppose waiting for his return gives people something to hope for.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Well, you know how myths and legends are. You could call it wishful thinking, but with the strange state of our world, crazier things have happened, no?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Quite so. The Kingdom has never quite bounced back from the loss of their king. Though he was by no means a perfect man in life, he has grown into something larger than just a man in myth?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}So there haven't been any kings since?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Indeed. Since the King's departure, the Kingdom has been governed by a line of Lord Guardians - stewards of the throne who are er... ''warming the seat'', so to speak. Of course, the Lord Regent does not style himself as such... Ahem. Was there anything else you wanted to know?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Who is this Lord Regent exactly?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is what they say of the King's Ardour true? Or is that just a myth, too?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See previous instance]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*The Bookkeeper flashes a brief smile at you before tidying away some notes.*'' Oh, it's quite true. And not just Ardour, either. Many sources suggest he was capable of wielding all three.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}All three? How's that?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}The myths differ in their accounts, but they speak of him travelling to the {{g|The Southern Luminant|Southern Luminant}} to strike a deal with an entity of some kind. Some attribute it to {{g|Mur of Light|Mur}}, others to something more ancient. Perhaps even something from ''below''...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}A deal?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Mm. Much like the Splinterblade that the King is famed for, the legends say that the deal he struck split his soul into three parts in order to accomplish the feat.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Mur of Light=
This dialogue is unlocked if the player has spoken to [[Theadre]] and asked "This King - is he some kind of god?"
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="6" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}These old books are more of a passing fancy of mine, but I've heard there's an order of scholars that devote their life to researching the {{g|The Old World|old world}}. Don't you wonder what things were like back then?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What's the deal with this 'Mur' figure?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}Well, you'll get a lot of conflicting answers depending on who you ask. Here in Etrea, she's fabled as the Goddess who blessed the Etreans of the {{g|The Resurgence|Resurgence}} with the understanding of {{g|Soul Murmur|Murmurs}}, The more ''contemporary'' views here is that she was a {{g|The Celestials|Celestial}} who aided Etrea. Though, uh. Be careful who you bring that up around. There are many in these parts who adhere to the old faith rather zealously...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}And what do you think?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}''*He nervously scratches behind his ear.*'' What I can say is... Ah... Well. I can't say that I have ''personally'' seen a great deal of information about {{g|Mur of Light|Mur}} ''outside'' of Etrea.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}So...
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Speaking rather tactically here, aren't we?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}Well, it's possible that she only made herself known to those of the {{g|The Etrean Luminant|Etrean Luminant}}. And it's also possible that if she appeared in other lands, they may well have given her another name... ''*He sighs.*'' When it comes to {{g|The Celestials|Celestials}}, there's really no way of knowing unless you find the damned things and talk to them.
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}''*He gives you a wry smile.*'' The tolerance of historians and recordkeepers only extend so far as you don't start contradicting what people already hold to be true. Books are... flammable things. Accidents happen. Often to historians with mysteriously large paper cuts in their abdomen.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Have you spoken to a Celestial?
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}So...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}''*His attention affixes itself to the grain of the wood behind you.*'' No. Don't be foolish, I'm not so fortunate as that. Anyway. Was there anything else you'd like to know about?
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is there anything you can tell me about Etris?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is there anything you can tell me about the Old World?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What's the deal with this 'Mur' figure?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Lord Regent=
This dialogue is unlocked if the player has started the "Lord Regent Who?" [[Quest]].
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}These old books are more of a passing fancy of mine, but I've heard there's an order of scholars that devote their life to researching the {{g|The Old World|old world}}. Don't you wonder what things were like back then?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is there anything you can tell me about Etris?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}If you head past the inn, you'll find the Lord Regent's estate. I would not advise entering without an invitation, however. Even a bookish fool such as I knows when I am not welcome.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Who is this Lord Regent exactly?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}The Lord Regent is the 'acting regent' of Etrea. That is to say, he is not the prophesied King, but he still holds absolute power over Etrea. In recent years, he has sequestered himself away in his palace, rarely making an appearance. Some worry that he has grown ill, but considering that his duties have not been passed on to any of his officials, I doubt this is the case.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Do you know anything about his rise to power? A guard I met is curious about what has become of Etrean politics.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}What's perhaps more interesting is that we ''don't'' know all too much about his rise to power. Before his rise to power, there was an officially recognised historian in the Etrean court. I had once hoped that I myself could fill such a position, but it no longer exists. It's said that when the Lord Regent came to power, half of the books in the libraries disappeared overnight.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Do you know what happened to those records?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}It didn't seem wise to make a fuss over them. They were simply articles of public knowledge at the time, so I doubt they were stolen or anything like that. Whatever became of them is clearly nothing of anyone's business, so I'd recommend you don't dig further...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}
}}
</tabber>

*Bookkeeper Andros was one of the first NPCs added to Deepwoken closed community testing.

title: Books
content:
File:Book GFX lmfao.png
==Description== Books are items that are found in the world of Deepwoken and are a separate category from loot, tools, weapons, etc. Books can be obtained by looting the various bookshelves around the world or as a guaranteed item sold at a Traveling Merchant Ship. Upon opening a book, player's are given a small sum of Intelligence XP. Besides that, most books have no purpose besides providing additional lore and information regarding Deepwoken's world and history; excluding [[Training Gear#Attribute_Training_Gears|Intelligence or Charisma Training Gears]] and [[Training Gear#Attribute_Training_Gears|Weapon Training Gears]]. Books can also be donated in a [[Guild Bases]]' library for future reading. A select amount of books allow the player to perform an instrumental version of the associated song with a [[Instruments|Worn Songbook]]. Some books are obtained in specific areas only, and cannot be found outside of it. Such books include: *Debriefing Log on Operator Polaris Enigvidion: [[Greathive Aratel]]. *The Gideshu March: [[Castle Light]], [[Fort Merit]], or rarely on [[Random Encounters#Traveling Merchant|Merchant Ships]]. *The Interrogation Of Ranger Santiago Talo: [[Castle Light]], [[Fort Merit]], [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|The Ethironal Shrine]]. *Neatly Embelished Notebook: [[Greathive Aratel]], [[Lightkeeper Temple]]. *Operation 'Distant Light' Report: [[Fort Merit]]. *Operation 'Puppet Master' Report: [[Fort Merit]]. *Ossuary Maintenance: [[Greathive Aratel]]. *Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel): [[Summer Isle]]. *The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation: [[Castle Light]], [[Fort Merit]], [[Lightkeeper Temple]]. *Strange Missives: [[Greathive Aratel]], [[Lightkeeper Temple]]. Some books are part of specific quests or are physically in the world, and thus cannot be obtained multiple times on a character. Such books include: *A Light In The Sky: [[Galpin Spellhardt, Musicologist Extraordinaire]] ({{cl|hallowtide|Hallowtide}} exclusive). *Coldheart's Journal: [[The Cold Forge]]. *Diver's Journals: [[Second Layer]]. *Legion Intelligence: Talking to [[Caitus]]. *Ministry Field Report: [[Outpost Antumbra]]. *Jericho's Journal: [[Fort Merit]], behind [[Warden Jericho]]. *Words of Light: Defeating the [[Kyrsgarde Champion, Kyrsa's Star]]. Some books are playable as songs on [[Instruments]]. Such books include: *[[The Gideshu March]] *[[A Light In The Sky]] ({{cl|hallowtide|Hallowtide}} exclusive) *[[The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation]] Uniquely, the [[Fading Book]] is obtained when a different book is removed from the game, being the placeholder item counterpart for books. ==Books== Currently there are 32 books and book collections: *[[Archivist Journal: 'Megalodaunt']]: The biology, characteristics, and origins of [[Megalodaunt]]s. 661 words, 3m reading time. *[[Capran Aphorisms]]: A trio of sayings regarding Jurik, Nemit, and Ku. 104 words, <1m reading time. *[[Children of the Aftertide]] **Children of the Aftertide I 781 words, 3m reading time. *[[Coldheart's Journal]] *[[A Deathscribe's Journal]] *[[Debriefing Log on Operator Polaris Enigvidion]] *[[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Azel]] *[[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Hero]] *[[Diver's Journal: Journeyman Skeli]] *[[Eggs In A Basket]]: A sailor's shanty. 107 words, <1m reading time. *[[Fading Book]]: A placeholder for removed books. Its pages fading, crumbling. ~50 words. *[[The Ferryman's Lullaby]]: The lyrics of a folk song regarding [[The Ferryman]]. 222 words, 1m reading time. *[[The Gideshu March]]: [[The Central Authority]]'s anthem and its brief history. Playable on [[Instruments]]. ~500 words. *[[The Hammer's Call]]: [[The Ignition Union]]'s anthem and its brief history. ~400 words. *[[The Interrogation Of Ranger Santiago Talo]] 1,559 words, 7m reading time. *[[A Light In The Sky]]: A single page paper with a music sheet, a poem, and a post-script note written by [[Galpin Spellhardt, Musicologist Extraordinaire|Prof. Galphin Spellhardt]] regarding [[Constellia|a place he treasured]]. Playable on [[Instruments]]. ~200 words. *[[Lumen's Folklore]] **Lumen's Folklore: Volume 'Attunement' **Lumen's Folklore: Volume 'North' *[[Ministry Field Report]] 435 words, 2m reading time. *[[Munet Journal]] **Munet Journal, XIV 107 words, <1m reading time. *[[Neatly Embelished Notebook]] *[[O Pardoner of Mine]] 419 words, 2m reading time. *[[Operation 'Distant Light' Report]] 1,861 words, 9m reading time. *[[Operation 'Puppet Master' Report]] 865 words, 4m reading time. *[[Ossuary Maintenance]] *[[Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel)]] *[[The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation]]: Playable on [[Instruments]]. ~2,600 words. *[[Strange Missives]] *[[Studies on Canticlysm]] **Studies on Canticlysm, Vol. IV 1,376 words, 6m reading time. *[[Tale of the Storm]] *[[Vows by the Sea: Inheritance]] 896 words, 4m reading time. *[[Words of Light]]: A Kyrsan Manifesto. 559 words, 2m reading time. ===Removed books=== Currently 7 books were fully removed from the game: *[[Diver Journal, I]] *[[Diver Journal, II]] *[[Diver Journal, III]] *[[God in the Machine]] *[[Lament of Cirryn]] *[[My Warm Blood]] *[[Stars Above, and the Blade between]] ==Gallery== Bookshelf Normal.png|Books on a bookshelf ==Trivia== *Children of the Aftertide I, A Deathscribe's Journal, Eggs In A Basket, The Ferryman's Lullaby, The Gideshu March, The Hammer's Call, The Interrogation Of Ranger Santiago Talo, Operation 'Distant Light' Report, Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel), The Song of Fathoms/Oscillation and Tale of the Storm were written by game composer Naktigonis. *Debriefing Log on Operator Polaris Enigvidion was written by developer yayafino. *The Diver Journals, God in the Machine, Lament of Cirryn, My Warm Blood, and Stars Above, and the Blade between were written by former developer iltria. *Ossuary Maintenance and Strange Missives was written by contributor Hautdesert. *Operation 'Puppet Master' Report was written by developer ragoozer. *It is implied that Ryrda from God in the Machine is the same Ryrda in Lament of Cirryn. **In both stories, they are [[Vesperian]]s. **In Lament of Cirryn, the main character Ekhusa keeps a shard of Ryrda's mask for good luck, and hopes that she will meet him again. ==References== [[Category:Items]] [[Category:Books]]

title: Boons and Flaws
content:
{{PathfinderEx}} '''Boons and Flaws''' are unique attributes that players must choose when creating their character. All characters must have at least one Boon and at least one Flaw. They are modifiers that effect gameplay in various ways, including vital core mechanics such as ether, hunger, and reputation, for the better, or worse. ==Boons== Boons are positive and helpful effects that are chosen in Character Creation. The number of Boons able to be picked is dependent on the number of Flaws that have been picked, with more selected Flaws equaling more Boon Points, and therefore more Boons. You can only have a maximum of 2 Boons at once. |-|Base Boons= These Boons can be chosen at character creation with no requirements for obtainment. {{{!}} class="article-table sortable" style="border: 2px solid #003d3d; margin:0; text-align: center;" {{!}}'''Name''' {{!}}'''Description''' {{!}}'''Effect''' {{!}}'''Additional Info''' {{!}}'''Point Cost''' {{!}}- {{!}}id="Autodidact"{{!}}'''Autodidact'''
[[File:Autodidact Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You get a free attribute to invest at every level. {{!}}Gain 3 free investment points every Power up, consuming an investment each use. {{!}}Uses general experience upon use, possibly taking you into exp debt. Cannot be used to bypass the 330 investment point limit. Stacks with the [[Adret]] aspect Talent, Maudet, giving you 6 free points on every Power up. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Gourmet"{{!}}'''Gourmet'''
[[File:Gourmet Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Foods are much more nutritional. {{!}}Grants a 50% increase to Stomach and Thirst gain from consuming food. {{!}}This also increases the duration (amount of the food bar the buff affects) of your [[Food]] buffs by 50%. Having this alongside the {{t|Gourmand}} Talent will increase the Stomach and Thirst gain when eating food by 80%. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Maverick"{{!}}'''Maverick'''
[[File:Maverick Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Doing things alone yields greater experience. {{!}}Increases EXP gain by an unknown percentage if no other players aid you when defeating mobs or completing events. {{!}}N/A {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Packmule"{{!}}'''Packmule'''
[[File:Packmule Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You have a much higher max carry load, and can carry much larger quantities of food. {{!}}Carry load is increased by 50, item stack limits are increased by 25% (rounded), and the maximum quantity of food you can carry is increased by 5. {{!}}This affects certain [[Relics]] such as [[Dye Packet]]s. Stacks with the {{t|Cook's Kit}} Talent, granting you a combined total of +10 to the amount of food you can have on your person, double that of what the base is. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Scrapper"{{!}}'''Scrapper'''
[[File:Scrapper Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You gain an extra [[Aces|Ace]] every other [[Whisper Draw|Whisper roll]]. {{!}}Every other Mantra hand from leveling grants an additional Ace, granting +6 Aces by the time you reach Power 20. {{!}}Grants an Ace at Powers 4, 8, 10, 14, 18, and 20. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Steadfast"{{!}}'''Steadfast'''
[[File:Steadfast Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Your armor retains more durability when attacked. {{!}}Reduces the amount of armor durability lost from being hit by 25%. {{!}}Stacks multiplicatively with other armor durability damage reduction sources like {{t|Armor Conserver}}, {{t|Bulletproof}}, and the [[Armorer's Ring]]. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Survivalist"{{!}}'''Survivalist'''
[[File:Survivalist Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You are resistant to environmental effects. {{!}}Grants immunity to acid rain. Parasites also accumulate on you ~33% slower. {{!}}N/A {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- |-|Unlockable Boons= These Boons can be chosen at character creation, but require an additional requirement to unlock them permanently. {{{!}} class="article-table sortable" style="border: 2px solid #003d3d; margin:0; text-align: center;" {{!}}'''Name''' {{!}}'''Description''' {{!}}'''Effect''' {{!}}'''Additional Info''' {{!}}'''Obtainment Method''' {{!}}'''Point Cost''' {{!}}- {{!}}id="Sly"{{!}}'''Sly'''
[[File:Sly Boon.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You sweet talk your way out of trouble and are naturally more stealthy, gaining less bad reputation from committing crimes. {{!}}Reduces the amount of negative reputation gained from all sources. {{!}}Also grants +15% [[Stealth]]. {{!}}Unlocked from [[Reputation#Bribe|paying off]] negative reputation with any [[Reputation|faction]]. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- ==Flaws== Flaws are negative and harmful effects, most often chosen in Character Creation. Most Flaws can be rerolled by talking to the [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts]] or [[Shrine of Blasphemy]] if you are over Power 17 or if you have ready used the Power Up deal with the Shrine. Flaws grant Boon Points, allowing the player to choose more Boons. You can only select 2 Boon Points worth of Flaws in Character Creation. |-|Base Flaws= These Flaws can be chosen at character creation with no requirements for obtainment. Most base Flaws '''can''' be obtained by Flaw granting deals, such as those with [[Deep Shrines]] or [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]]. {{{!}} class="article-table sortable" style="border: 2px solid #003d3d; margin:0; text-align: center;" {{!}}'''Name''' {{!}}'''Description''' {{!}}'''Effect''' {{!}}'''Additional Info''' {{!}}'''Points Given''' {{!}}- {{!}}id="Deficient"{{!}}'''Deficient'''
[[File:Deficient Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You regenerate Ether more slowly. {{!}}Your Ether regeneration is reduced by an unknown percentage. This affects the boosted Ether regeneration from Tempo as well. {{!}}This does not affect things that grant a flat amount of Ether, such as instant Ether [[potions]] or the {{t|Ether Absorption}} Talent. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Glutton"{{!}}'''Glutton'''
[[File:Glutton Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Your hunger and thirst is depleted faster. {{!}}Stomach and thirst meters passively decrease ~50%-100% faster. {{!}}Does not affect the stomach loss any non-passive source, such as the [[Gluttony]] Enchant or [[Chef's Toque]]. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Haemophilia"{{!}}'''Haemophilia'''
[[File:Haemophilia Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You bleed more {{!}}Blood loss from taking damage is increased by an unknown amount. {{!}}Does not affect '''blood drain''' effects (see [[#Trivia|Trivia]] for more info). {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Manic"{{!}}'''Manic'''
[[File:Manic Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}All insanity gained from attacks is heavily amplified. {{!}}All incoming insanity and insanity damage is increased greatly. {{!}}Does not affect percentage based sanity damage, such as {{t|Heretic's Sutra}} or {{t|Shared Misery}}. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Obvious"{{!}}'''Obvious'''
[[File:Obvious Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Enemies detect you more easily. {{!}}Grants -20% [[stealth]], meaning Monsters and other NPCs can detect you at a further distance. {{!}}N/A {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Simple"{{!}}'''Simple'''
[[File:Simple Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You learn things at a slower rate than others. {{!}}Sharply increases the EXP curve, making leveling slower, especially on later levels. Reduces [[Knowledge]] gain by 25%, rounding to the nearest whole number. {{!}}Despite being a base Flaw, this Flaw cannot be obtained from the [[Shrine of Blasphemy]]. {{!}}2 Boon Points {{!}}- {{!}}id="Squeamish"{{!}}'''Squeamish'''
[[File:Squeamish Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Having to physically take the life of another makes you lose stomach. {{!}}Lose around 2-3% of your stomach meter when manually gripping NPCs or players. {{!}}Effectively disabled with the {{t|Carnivore}} Talent. Can also be circumvented by gripping your opponent via other means like drowning or burning. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Vegetarian"{{!}}'''Vegetarian'''
[[File:Vegetarian Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Eating the flesh of animals has a chance to make you vomit. {{!}}Eating meat-based foods has an ~50% chance to make you vomit. {{!}}You cannot obtain {{t|Carnivore}} if you have this Flaw. Despite being a base Flaw, this Flaw cannot be obtained from the [[Shrine of Blasphemy]]. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- |-|Unlockable Flaws= These Flaws can be chosen at character creation, but require an additional requirement to unlock them permanently. Unlockable Flaws '''cannot''' be obtained from Flaw granting deals, such as those with [[Deep Shrines]] or [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]]. {{{!}} class="article-table sortable" style="border: 2px solid #003d3d; margin:0; text-align: center;" {{!}}'''Name''' {{!}}'''Description''' {{!}}'''Effect''' {{!}}'''Additional Info''' {{!}}'''Obtainment Method''' {{!}}'''Points Given''' {{!}}- {{!}}id="Blind"{{!}}'''Blind'''
[[File:Blind Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}You cannot see. {{!}}You gain a less extreme version of the [[Talents#Miscellaneous|Blinded Talent]], cascading everything in darkness; making things even if close up hard to discern from your other surroundings. {{!}}This Flaw provides protection from [[Flame Blind]] and [[Gaze]]. As [[Gremor]]s are blessed by Navae, you gain an area around your character in which there is light, greatly assisting your ability to see. Your character's eyes become a pale grey/white. Additionally, instead of pure darkness, the Blind effect for Gremors has a more green hue instead. {{!}}Unlocked after obtaining [[Blindseer]] for the first time. {{!}}1 Boon Point {{!}}- {{!}}id="Fugitive"{{!}}'''Fugitive'''
[[File:Fugitive Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Your past isn't so spotless. All [[Reputation|Factions]] hate you. {{!}}You start with much lower reputation towards all factions, putting all faction reputation in the negative. {{!}}Reputation can still be gained normally. Your starting reputation is low enough for guards to aggro on sight and for you to be [[Bounty Hunting|bounty hunted]] at Power 5, but depending on your origin, not low enough for [[blacksmith]]s and [[antiquarian]]s to be disabled. {{!}}Gain negative reputation from any faction you originally have positive reputation for (e.g. going from '''{{cl|liorange|Neutral}}''' to '''{{cl|lipurple|Enemy}}''' Etrea reputation). {{!}}2 Boon Points {{!}}- |-|Special Flaws= These Flaws are granted via specific means instead of being chosen during character creation or granted via a deal with a [[Deep Shrines|Shrine]]. Special Flaws often have harsher downsides and do not grant Flaw Points. Some Special Flaws can be removed from your character if you complete a specific task, but are unable to be removed in any other fashion. {{{!}} class="article-table sortable" style="border: 2px solid #003d3d; margin:0; text-align: center;" {{!}}'''Name''' {{!}}'''Description''' {{!}}'''Effect''' {{!}}'''Additional Info''' {{!}}'''Obtainment Method''' {{!}}'''Removal Method''' {{!}}- {{!}}id="Disgraced"{{!}}'''Disgraced'''
[[File:Disgraced Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}A stain upon your honour. Defeat Maestro to remove it. {{!}}Lowers your HP and Ether regeneration by an unknown value. {{!}}N/A {{!}}Obtained by losing to [[Maestro Evengarde Rest]]. Defeating Maestro at any point removes the ability to obtain this Flaw. {{!}}Removed upon defeating [[Maestro Evengarde Rest]]. {{!}}- {{!}}id="Restless"{{!}}'''Restless'''
[[File:Restless Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Something haunts your past. A fragmented memory of a promise you made to yourself? You find it harder to Rest properly. {{!}}You regenerate less HP at campfires. {{!}}N/A {{!}}This Flaw is currently unobtainable. {{!}}? {{!}}- {{!}}id="Tarnished"{{!}}'''Tarnished'''
[[File:Tarnished Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Your [[Resonance]] is harder to call forth. {{!}}Increases Resonance startup by 1 second, along with a varying unique debuff depending on the Resonance. This Flaw prevents you from rerolling your Resonance with [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]] until it's removed. {{!}}Unobtainable if you have the '''[[Soul Plasticity]]''' [[Echo Unlock]]. {{!}}Obtained from rerolling your Resonance with [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]] or when using an [[Idol of Yun'Shul]] to do the same thing. {{!}}Removed by giving [[Yamaketzal]] {{c|notes|1,000}}, [[Carrion, Father of Evolution]] {{c|knowledge|1}}, or by obtaining Clarity from [[Misérables]] for {{c|knowledge|15}}. Also cleared from all slots permanently if you purchase the [[Soul Plasticity]] [[Echo Unlock]] for 500 Echoes. {{!}}- {{!}}id="Vacant"{{!}}'''Vacant'''
[[File:Vacant Flaw.png|20px|20px]] {{!}}Something is missing. {{!}}You lose your soul, preventing you from interacting with some of the game's mechanics. {{!}}You cannot enter [[Castle Light]] nor can you partake in a [[Vow of Mastery]]. All currently active Vows of Masteries that you are a part of are permanently severed. {{!}}Gained from making a deal with [[Developer Specs#Arch Mage (Haske Vantage)|Arch_Mage]], a developer for Deepwoken, who has an ability that allows players to make a deal with him for their soul. Additionally has a chance of being gained from making a deal with [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]]. {{!}}? {{!}}- {{!}}id="Wishbound"{{!}}'''Wishbound''' {{!}}Isn't this what you wanted? {{!}}Gain insanity during the night. {{!}}N/A {{!}}Gained from making a wish with [[Developer Specs#Iltria (Leafre Spellhardt) (Retired)|Iltria]] (Retired), a developer for Deepwoken, who has an ability that allows players to make a wish from her, from one of three options. {{!}}? {{!}}- ==Breakdown of Boons== *Your Boon choice is fairly consequential, as they cannot be changed after leaving Character Creation. Though, with that being said, Boon choice is ultimately up to personal preference, with most of them granting minor benefits. *Some boons are more worth taking than others: **'''Autodidact''' is useful to help level up certain stat quicker or level up stats that are annoying to do manually. If you die, you can also Power up to restore your lives. However, a side effect of free investment points is that you will often be in EXP Debt, as you will "progress" more without meeting proper EXP quotas, hitting training caps faster. Unfortunately, this Boon becomes useless once you reach Power 20. This Boon stacks with the [[Adret]] Aspect Talent, Maudet, granting 6 free training points on every level up. **'''Gourmet''' is a well-rounded boon that even stacks with its Talent variant. You spend less time making food overall which is great for extended adventures with limited supplies. Additionally, Gourmet's ability to increase the duration of [[Food]] buffs by 50% makes it second to none if you wish to engage with this mechanic. It is recommended that you additionally take the {{t|Tavernkeep}} Talents with this Boon to maximize the satiation and effects from eating certain foods. **'''Maverick''''s exp boost is a nice bonus but is fairly unnoticeable, and is negated by playing with some friends. Unfortunately, it becomes useless once you are fully invested. **'''Packmule''' is very useful for builds that need to carry around a lot of loot, such as bank slots or PvE builds. While nice to have, it's not as impactful as many other Boons unless you're going for one of the aforementioned builds. **'''Scrapper''' gives you more control over your build by granting additional [[Aces]]. This Boon is less necessary for players that have a good way to generate [[Knowledge]], such as a stash of [[Moonseye Tome]]s. If you happen to obtain the [[Ace of Spades]] Regalia, this Boon will become obsolete. **'''Sly''' is largely seen as a waste of a Boon, as all it does is reduce the amount of reputation lost when doing things that might upset factions. It however may be useful for people who gank, especially in [[the Depths]] and around [[Castle Light]], and for builds that want a very high [[Stealth]] stat (e.g. for [[Tacet]]). The [[Stealth]] from this Boon is affected by Stealth multipliers, such as [[Felinor]] and crouching/{{t|Lowstride}}. **'''Steadfast''' grants a pretty big boost to your overall armor durability by reducing armor damage taken. This Boon is generally seen as a must-take on almost all builds due to its universal bonus that affects all types of combat. All other forms of armor durability reduction stack multiplicatively with this Boon, meaning there are diminishing returns if you plan to use more sources of this effect. **'''Survivalist''''s immunity to [[Acid Rain]] might seem limited in usage since Acid Rain only happens naturally at [[Upper Erisia]], but it can prove invaluable for spending time there. Acid Rain can also be triggered through the [[Rain (enchantment)|Rain]] enchantment if you also have a [[Stench]] enchantment equipped, making Survivalist a must have if you plan on using this enchantment combo. Survivalist also avoids the dangerous event of your [[Gliders|glider]] breaking when gliding into Acid Rain. In addition, it decreases the rate at which parasites in the [[Second Layer]] kill you. ==Breakdown of Flaws== *Your Flaw choice during Character Creation is largely inconsequential (barring Blind), as you can exchange any non-Special Flaw for a random Base Flaw at the [[Shrine of Blasphemy]]. Simple and Vegetarian cannot be obtained through this. Note: You need to be Power 17+ or have used the Shrine of Blasphemy Power Up deal prior to unlock Flaw conversion. *Some Flaws are more worth taking than others: **'''Blind''' gives you the {{status|b=y|Blinded}} effect constantly, heavily limiting your field-of-vision. If you can live through it long enough to obtain [[Blindseer]], you can negate the Flaw's downside entirely. This Flaw also provides protection from [[Flame Blind]] and [[Gaze]]. Blind also grants your character milky-white eyes. [[Gremor]]s notably have a small vision radius while blinded, and lighting sources can also be used (such as the [[Pathfinder Lantern]]) to slightly mitigate the downsides of this Flaw. **'''Deficient''' is a downside for all builds that intend to use Mantras, and is generally not worth taking. However, if you decide to go for [[Silentheart]], the effect is minor, though still a downside, as Ether can still be useful on this Oath. **'''Fugitive''' can be worked around by taking quests on [[Job Boards]] designated by Factions to farm Reputation. Despite still being able to have above neutral reputation for every faction (excluding the Etrean Royalists), Fugitive sets your base reputation lower than it usually would be. This means if you want to obtain Blightsurger which requires high ally reputation with The Hundred Legions and your origin is Deepbound for example (initially starts with low reputation with the Hundred Legions) then you will not be able to meet the requirement for obtaining Blightsurger. If you care about having good reputations with most or all Factions, this Flaw can be a serious time sink, and may not be worth taking for players dislike this aspect of the Flaw. This Flaw is effectively negated by the [[Noble]] Regalia, as it gives you a large amount of starting reputation for all factions. As this Flaw grants two Boon Points, it cannot be chosen alongside another Flaw, while still allowing you to choose two Boons, making Simple very appealing to a lot of players. Simple also grants two Boon Points, making it a great alternative for those who do not wish to use Fugitive. Rolling Fugitive off your character using the Shrine of Blasphemy will bump up your reputation with all the factions. **'''Glutton''' forces you to handle provisions more smartly, since you will likely need more food for extended sessions, but this can be somewhat worked around by using the {{t|Carnivore}} and {{t|Grand Feast}} Talents or the [[Guild Bases|guild base]] Mess Hall. This Flaw is '''entirely''' negated by the [[Hungerless]] Regalia, as it entirely disables passive stomach/thirst drain. **'''Haemophilia''' is basically a free Flaw in most 1v1 situations, as the increased blood loss won't have an impact when you'll be knocked before your blood runs out, but in ganks you can die to blood before health runs out after some time. This Flaw (luckily) doesn't affect '''blood drain''' effects, such as utilizing or being hit by [[Bloodrend]] Mantras, the blood cost from the Blood Loss [[Resonance#Corrupt Resonances|Corrupt Resonance]] downside, [[Alchemy|blood loss potions]], or whiffing with or being hit by the [[Curse of the Bloodthirsty]] enchantment, as blood drain effects are unaffected by blood loss modifiers. **'''Manic''' is usually a free Boon Point; the increased Sanity loss is minimal, Sanity damage comes from few sources, and scratching can be completely avoided with some Talents. Additionally, having low Sanity can even benefit some builds. **'''Obvious''' grants -20% [[stealth]] on spawn, increasing the radius at which enemies will detect you. Because of this, this Flaw will largely only affect PvE with one exception being [[Tacet]]'s range, as that is affected by your Stealth stat. This Flaw can be dangerous in areas like [[the Depths]]. The Stealth from this Flaw is affected by Stealth multipliers, such as [[Felinor]] and crouching/{{t|Lowstride}}. The [[Felinor]] aspect's innate 20% Stealth and 1.2x Stealth multipliers makes it so an Obvious Felinor starts with -4% Stealth; counteracted by a mere 2 [[Agility]] investment. This Flaw should not be taken on any [[Inquisition Division]] [[Authority Ensign]] builds that wish to utilize the {{t|Fatal Stealth}} Talent, as the negative Stealth from this Flaw contributes to that Talent, applying a damage deficit to your backstabs. This Flaw's downside can be mitigated through [[Agility]] investment, [[Equipment]] and [[Outfits]], etc. see [[Stealth]] for a list of all Stealth gain sources. **'''Simple''''s EXP gain rate decrease is not problematic for the patient, but it can be annoying to power up at higher levels. It'll also mean it takes more time to get back your first life via powering up. The exp gain downside of this Flaw is negated when fully progressed. The reduced [[Knowledge]] gain from this Flaw can hurt, but there are some workarounds; if you gain Knowledge in increments of 1 or 2 (most Knowledge gain sources fall under this range), the Flaw will not hurt you as it rounds. Alternatively, gaining Knowledge in increments of any even number that is not divisible by 4 will cause your Knowledge gain to round up. The [[Insightful]] Regalia somewhat overpowers the decreased Knowledge gain downside of this Flaw, allowing you to gain slightly more Knowledge than you would previously. As this Flaw grants two Boon Points, it cannot be chosen alongside another Flaw, while still allowing you to choose two Boons, making Simple very appealing to a lot of players. Fugitive also grants two Boon Points, making it a great alternative for those who do not wish to use Simple. **'''Squeamish''' will cause you to lose stomach upon manually executing enemies. As [[food]] buffs are tied to your stomach bar, you'll also lose those more quickly than other character might. Other than that, you typically won't eat more than other characters. Regardless, be sure to carry an ample supply of food. This Flaw can be effectively negated if you obtain the {{t|Carnivore}} Talent, as this will cause you to instead gain stomach and hydration after killing foes. Any form of automatic execution (e.g. [[Blood Scourge]], blood loss, drowning, or {{status|Burn|burning}}) will not trigger this Flaw. **'''Vegetarian''''s inability to consume meat can be easily avoided; there are many other food sources other than meat/meat related items and the [[Guild Bases|Guild Base Mess Hall]] sells a Vegetarian option. Vegetarian only grants a ~50% chance to vomit when eating meat-based foods, so they are still viable options in a pinch. Picking this Flaw will make it impossible to obtain the {{t|Carnivore}} Talent, which some players may find useful. [[Bloodrend]]'s ''Carnivorous'' [[Elemental Cantrips|Cantrip]] does not negate this Flaw's effects; you still have a chance to vomit when consuming raw meat. *Ideally, all Special Flaws should be removed from your character as soon as possible, as they only apply negative effects with no silver lining. ==Trivia== *Prior to the official release of the game, Blind was a selectable Flaw for 1 point. This was removed during testing for unknown reasons, although was it was brought back during the {{VersionHistory|2022|August 16th}} update, being unlocked after gaining [[Blindseer]]. *Deepbound used to be a Flaw, but it was changed to be an unlockable [[Origins|origin]]. *The Restless Flaw was originally obtainable when [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Oathbreaking]] [[Oathless]] and using [[Shrine of Order]], however this Flaw is currently unobtainable. *The [[Shrine of Order]] used to grant a random base Flaw on use, this was removed during the {{VersionHistory|2025|September 6th}} update. *There used to be more Boons and Flaws. The currently known ones are Adept (likely the original version of the Talent) and Seasick. *The icon for the Restless Flaw [[File:Restless Flaw.png|16x16px]] is a {{w|Troll Face}} of [[Developer Specs#Arch Mage (Haske Vantage)|Haske Vantage]], developer Arch_Mage's [[Primal Vesperian]]. *While not confirmed, Wishbound's passive insanity gain shares some similarities with the Latin concept/word, lunaticus. Within it's Latin origins, the word refers to diseases caused by the moon, such as madness or epilepsy. [[File:Blind at night.png|alt=Being Blind during night (it sucks)|thumb|500x500px|Having the ''Blind'' Flaw at night. (No, this isn't just a black image. Look carefully.)]] {{History}} [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Character]] [[Category:Creation]] [[Category:Features absent in Vow of Iron]]

title: Bosses
content:
''This page is for bosses. For Monster enemies, see [[Monsters]]. For non-monster enemies, see [[Enemies]].''
File:Ethiron Slam GFX (not 003).png
==Overview== '''Bosses''' in ''Deepwoken'' are powerful [[Enemies]] and [[Monsters]] that possess heavy backstories and unique abilities. They award Resonance [[Resonance|Progress]], [[Knowledge]], and unique [[weapons]] such as the [[Purple Cloud]], [[Dissonant Chimecaller]], and the [[Frostthorn]]. ==Bosses== The concrete, in-game method of determining if an Enemy/Monster is a '''Boss''' is whether or not they can be used to obtain [[Echoes|Chain of Perfection]]. However, every Boss has most, if not all of the secondary criteria below. *Unique Summoning System or Guaranteed Spawn Locations *Unique & End-Game Drops *Grants [[Echoes]] upon defeat. *Grants [[Resonance Progress]] upon defeat. *Grants [[Knowledge]] upon defeat. *Grants [[Pluripotent Alloy]] upon defeat. *Grants [[Ardour Manifestation]] upon defeat. *Being in a Boss' combat tag allows you to zoom your camera out farther than normal. *Unique healthbar. ===Pathfinder=== {{EnemyGallery |Chaserfinal.png|Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract |Kaijufinal.png|Dread Serpent |Dukefinal.png|Duke Ishamon Erisia |Ferrymanfinal.png|The Ferryman |Knellbossicon.png|Knell, The Lunatic Resonator |Kyrsgarde Champion Icon.png|Kyrsgarde Champion |Maestrofinal.png|Maestro Evengarde Rest |ParliamentIcon.png|Parliament |PrimadonIcon.png|Primadon, Titan of the East |TitusIcon.png|Titus Fulminus Destellus }} ===Vow of Iron=== {{EnemyGallery |DravikIcon.png|Dravik, The Rat King |General Titus Juventius.png|General Titus Juventius |ShogunBaseIcon.png|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard (Temple of Mur) |TrueEnmityIcon.png|True Heart of Enmity |ZieerIcon.png|Zi'eer, the Fourth Prophet }} == World Bosses == Exceptionally strong enemies that may require multiple people to take down. World Bosses usually have a set spawn, and reward players with 1 or 2 [[Knowledge]], Double [[Resonance]] progression, 1-2 [[Crowns]], and an insane amount of Experience on defeat. {{EnemyGallery |DoomOfCaeranthil.png|The Doom of Caeranthil |ElderPrimadonIcon.png|Elder Primadon, The Titan Warlord |Enmityfinal.png|Heart of Enmity |ParasolIcon.png|Interluminary Parasol |Scionfinal.png|Scion of Ethiron }} ==Mini-Bosses== Mini-Bosses are particularly strong Enemies/Monsters, but are not true Bosses due to lacking the Chain of Perfection criteria. However, they fulfill many of the secondary criteria, and are still unique challenges with unique purposes and rewards in their own right. ===Pathfinder=== {{EnemyGallery |Aska.png|Aska |BlizzardknightIcon.png|Blizzard Knight |BonekeeperIcon.png|Bone Keeper |Coldheart Fortinbras Icon.png|Coldheart Fortinbras |Deep Widow Icon.png|Deep Widow |EnforcerIcon.png|Enforcer |Exotic Megalodaunt.png|Exotic Megalodaunt |Drowned Delver.png|Finnegan The Lost |The fisherman, but....png|The Fisherman |FuryNautilodauntIcon.png|Fury Nautilodaunt |GrudgeNPC.png|Grudge |Lodestar.png|Lodestar |The Ministry IRS Agent..png|Ministry Agent |MudskipperBroodlordIcon.png|Mudskipper Broodlord |NautilodauntIcon.png|Nautilodaunt |Prime Megalodaunt.png|Prime Megalodaunt }} ===Vow of Iron=== {{EnemyGallery |Bloodstarved Hunter.png|Bloodstarved Hunter |Etrean Apostle.png|Etrean Apostle |Nautilodaunt Officiate.png|Nautilodaunt Officiate |Phantom Hunter.png|Phantom Hunter |ShogunBaseIcon.png|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard |Shogun Specialist.png|Shogun Specialist }} {{History}} {{Nav|Bosses}} [[Category:Bosses]] [[Category:Mechanics]]

title: Bounder
content:
{{Topbuttons|p, [[Bounder/Gallery|Gallery]]}} {{Quotes|quote=Deep gashes creating elegant lines decorate the body. They're beast-like in nature, with an extreme depth to each one. A sense of dread washes over you, almost as if you were in the gaze of a predator.|author=Mauled Diver Corpse Interaction}} {{Monster Infobox |health=4700 11750{{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |behavior=Hostile |drops=*[[Bounder Claw]] *[[Mantra Modifiers]] |attacks=*Leap *Slash *Charge |image1=Bounder.png |challenges= {{Bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}}}} ==Description== Bounders are monsters that dwell within the [[Second Layer]] of [[The Depths]] and can spawn {{cl|corrupted|Corrupted}} within [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. They are infamous for their lethality, with an equally horrific appearance. Bounders have significantly hunched posture, elongated limbs, six ringed eyes, disturbingly humanoid hands and notably, an upsettingly wide mouth with two sets of gigantic teeth. Bounders aren't naturally bipedal, instead moving around in a quadrupedal manner. Whenever an entity enters the territory or hunting grounds of a Bounder, an echoing growl can be heard, signifying their presence (though not necessarily their aggression). By default, they will crawl around at a relatively slow pace, only ever displaying their speed and agility while hunting. Bounders are comparatively harder to kill than most other monsters in the world of Deepwoken due to their high damage and their above average health pool. While they have a relatively simple moveset, their erratic movements and devestating strikes make them difficult to pin down. They are unforgiving terrors that can finish off anyone who isn't accustomed to their behavior within seconds. ==Moveset== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Leap'''
(★★☆) |The Bounder leaps either a long or a short distance towards their prey, slamming down to damage and disorientate them. Move out of the way to avoid this. {{AttackTags |indicator = avoid |parry.n, block.n, dodge.n, ragdoll }} |- |
'''Slash'''
(★☆☆) |The Bounder slashes its arms at its prey either once or twice, utilizing their claws to tear through them. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Bound'''
(★★★) |The Bounder lowers its head and continuously stomps its foot before charging in the direction of their prey, knocking them down and damaging them in the process. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, movement, ragdoll }} |} ==='''Passives'''=== *'''Strong Monster Resistance''' - Physical attacks deal 50% less damage to Bounders. == Finisher == {| class="fandom-table" ! Name !Description |- |'''Feast''' |Picks the victim up with both hands and opens it's mouth wide open, then places them in it's mouth, eating them. |} ==Trivia== *They're considered the spiritual successor to [[Jack]], the second Monster ever created for Deepwoken. *Despite its resemblance to the Megalodaunt, its anatomy more-so resembles a frog, evident by their posture and ability to leap long distance, and the way they attack prey. *Like every other monster in the Second Layer, [[Regalias#Mute|Mute]] has no effect on Bounders. *Curiously, Bounders are social creatures, as shown by their ability to create nests and live as a pack. Beyond this, there isn't much evidence that can support both the extent of their social behavior, or even how they are capable of reproducing. *Bounders are often considered by the community as one of the most dangerous monsters in the Second Layer, if not the entire game due to their insane damage *It was said by Arch_Mage that there was supposed to be a type of Bounder that was infected with Parasites. However, this concept never made it into the game. *Their cry is a heavily distorted wolf howl. *Their item drop, the Bounder Claw, can be taken out of the Second Layer without having to defeat [[Chaser, Scholar of the Burning Blood|Chaser]] (either by using the Light Hook or Ignition Deepdriller). *On 12/27/24, it was discovered that the icon for the Bounder when it killed someone was the texture of its inner cheek/gums, which resembled an inappropriate image. It was deemed ''The Boundingaling Incident''. Bounder flash.png|The 12/27/24 incident {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Layer 2]] [[Category:The Depths]]

title: Bounty Hunting
content:
{{Quotes|quote=This is the way.|author=Bounty Hunter guild}}
[[File:Board.png|thumb|A Bounty Board located in Etris.]]
==Description==
Bounty Hunting in Deepwoken is the process of hunting someone with a low reputation in any given [[factions|faction]]; once they are dead, the hunter gets a chest full of loot and EXP. You can choose which player to hunt on a Bounty Board via a poster. The poster will show their name, [[Aspects|Aspect]], [[Oaths|Oath]], and amount of bounty stars. If the player has no Oath, it will read "Pathfinder."

Bounty Stars are determined by the target's bounty points ranging from 1 to 8 stars
* Unhuntable = under 20 points
* ★ = 20-39 points
* ★★ = 40-59 points
* ★★★ = 60-79 points
* ★★★★ = 80-99 points
* ★★★★★ = 100-119 points
* ★★★★★★ = 120-139 points
* ★★★★★★★ = 140-159 points
* ★★★★★★★★ = 160 or more points

A target's bounty points are determined using several factors:
* 5 points per power
* 15 points from having a resonance
* 10 points from having an Oath
* 10 points from having an enchant/legendary weapon
* 5/10/15 points depending on armor tier (5 from adept, 10 from expert, 15 from master/unique)

When a bounty is taken, at the top left corner of your screen it will say the name of the person you're hunting and where they are located. The location will be refreshed every two minutes.
[[File:Huntt.png|thumb|The details of the Bounty.]]

When you manage to successfully hunt someone and kill them, you'll get a chest filled with loot depending on how many stars the person you hunted has, as well as some EXP. The person who got killed will have their reputation pushed towards their default value, usually neutrality.

If you are being hunted instead and manage to kill off your hunter, YOU will get a chest filled with loot.

== Tips and Advice ==

* By having neutral or above [[reputation]] with Etrea {{FactionIcon|Etrea}}, The Central Authority {{FactionIcon|Central Authority}}, The Hive {{FactionIcon|Hive}}, the Summer Company {{FactionIcon|The Summer Company}}, the Ignition Union {{FactionIcon|Ignition Union}}, The Divers {{FactionIcon|Divers}}, and The Knives of Eylis {{FactionIcon|Knives of Eylis}}, you will entirely remove yourself from bounty boards. '''''If you're looking to get rid of [[Voidwalker]]s, this is the way.'''''
* If you are getting voidwalked and wish to avoid the fight, if you haven't been combat tagged you could try to glide away if you are high up, or just log, but if they combat tag you, FIGHT BACK, NEVER RUN as running only exposes yourself and they can catch up relatively easy
* Taking as many bounties as possible is recommended as it gives you easy access to where people in your server are; especially useful if others plan on hunting you.
* If hunting as a team, make sure the bounty holder contributes enough damage and performs a '''MANUAL''' execution or uses [[Blood Scourge]] on the target for the bounty to be counted as complete.
* If you are struggling to find targets, you may have better luck by using the server browser to locate populated servers with more targets.
* Carrying rocks will prove useful to prevent your adversaries from logging, as not many people will appreciate your hunting.
* Bounty hunting is [[Tacet]]'s best application as it allows you to get within range of your opponent to enter combat without giving them the chance to log; be aware however that tacet is known to commonly bug in PvP not actually making the user invisible once activated.
*Players who take the Fugitive flaw will appear on every single faction's bounty board as soon as they reach power 5 if they haven't fixed their reputation with each of them.
*Equipping different outfits/weapons that don't give bounty points allows one to lower their current bounty stars and take lower star bounties/avoid being hunted by those outside of their new bounty star range, this can be useful both for taking bounties you otherwise could not as well as avoiding being hunted.

title: Brainsucker
content:
{{Topbuttons|p, {{iv|Lavasucker}}}} {{Quotes|quote=Cephalorins were some of the first monsters to be noted in historic records, though they were initially described as small bat-like creatures that predated on rodents and poultry. It seems that they've since grown up somewhat, and moved on to larger prey.|author=Bestiary Entry}} {{Monster Infobox |image1=Gargoyle.png |attacks=Skull Dive
Talon Rake |health=250 ([[Minityrsa]])
450 ([[Duke Erisia's Manor]])
600 (Scales on islands)
1500 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |drops=Rare chance to drop [[Mantra Modifiers]] |locations=*[[The Etrean Sea]] *[[The Aratel Sea]] *[[Voidsea]] *[[The Starswept Valley]] *[[Minityrsa]] *[[Duke Erisia's Manor]] |challenges= {{Bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}} }}''Also referred to as Bat.'' ==Description== '''Brainsuckers''', or known by their academic name Cephalorins, are beaked flying creatures which earned their moniker thanks to their tendency to latch onto the heads of fallen prey in order to feed on their brains, they resemble many things, having bat-like wings, a beak, three eyes, and all of it forming a body that looks like a gargoyle. They can only be found flying, which allows them to easily follow you on your voyage and pester you when you slow down. Brainsuckers are a [[Monsters|monster]] that spawns alone above the waves of the [[The Etrean Sea|Etrean Sea]], [[The Aratel Sea]], and [[Voidsea]]. It also spawns in packs of two or three in [[Minityrsa]], [[Starswept Valley|The Starswept Valley]], and [[Miner's Landing]]. Multiple Brainsuckers are also encountered in [[Duke Erisia's Manor]]. Being some of the oldest creatures discovered, their common name comes from the fact that they attach to the head of their victim's corpses to feed upon their brain. ==Moves== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description !Media |- |
'''Skull Dive'''
(★★☆) |The Brainsucker flies back and proceeds to swoop down for the player. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Brainsucker Skull Dive.gif|center|200x200px]] |- |
'''Talon Rake'''
(★☆☆) |The Brainsucker raises its legs to strike the players head. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Brainsucker Talon Rake.gif|center|200x200px]] |} ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Carrion Feast |The Brainsucker rapidly shreds open the player's torso with its talons, killing them. |} ==Tips== *Due to its moving hitbox, Skull Dive can be difficult to parry consistently. However, its relatively low damage makes it possible to simply tank the attack and defeat the Brainsucker before it can kill you. == Gallery == File:Brainsucker concept art.png|Concept Art File:Brainsucker Concept Art 2.png|Concept Art File:Brainsucker Model Render.png|Model Render File:BrainsuckerBestiary.png|Bestiary Art File:BrainsuckerIcon.png ==Trivia== *The Brainsuckers' name may be a reference to the [https://bloodborne.wiki.fextralife.com/Brainsucker Brainsucker] from ''Bloodborne''. *They only suck the brains of the foes they have already killed due to it bringing them 0 risk to do so opposed to trying to eat the brains of an already alive victim as they would attack and harm them. *The Brainsuckers were initially described as small bat-like creatures that predated on rodents and poultry, It seems that they've since grown up somewhat and moved on to larger prey *Cancelling a Brainsuckers gripping animation may cause whoever is being gripped to desync. *Uppercutting a Brainsucker or ragdolling them while above the ocean will cause them to fall underwater. *It is implied that there is a "Greater Brainsucker," because its name is "Lesser Brainsucker." *They might be communal or live in small groups or duos due to being found in pairs of two or three frequently. *After a certain period of time they will end up despawning via flying upwards towards the sky including in combat. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]]

Brasidas Spellhardt is [[Lightborn]] found within [[The Floating Keep]]. He is the Treasurer and [[Antiquarian]] for the Keep and [[Spellhardt family]].

He appears fond of metaphors to do with storms.

He wears a [[Megalodaunt Coat|Red Megalodaunt Coat]] with the [[Pathfinder Thaumaturge]] [[Outfit]] underneath.

title: Brinepool Passage
content:
{{Location|name=Brinepool Passage|caption=Warmer waters brush past you with the current, a contrast to the bitter chill beneath your feet.}}[[File:subzeropassagecover.png|thumb|900px|center]]

'''Brinepool Passage''', formerly "Sub-Zero Passage" is a [[Locations|location]] that is accessible by breaking a wall of ice inside of a fallen tower that leads to [[Castle Light]]. It is a sub-location in the [[Celtor Wastes]].

==Overview==
Brinepool Passage leads to the [[The Cold Forge]] which has some relation to the [[Dormant Splinter]]. The walls are covered in ice and there is a blue mist circulating throughout the cave. 

Ice spikes will fall from the ceiling at many parts of this location. There are many falling/disappearing platforms as you travel through this area that drop into the void. There is many not collideable ice chunks, it is advised to not trust any ground in this area.

==Notes==
*You '''need''' a lot of agility or mobility mantras to get through this area.
*Monsters can spawn here at extremely uncommon rate.

== Trivia ==

* Initially, the location was called Sub-Zero Passage before being changed for unknown reason.

title: Bullets
content:
{{Stub}}
Bullets are ammunition for [[Guns]] that can apply special effects when fired. Effects can be added by adding [[Bullet Casings]]. == Obtainment == There are 2 ways to obtain bullets: * Purchase them for {{c|notes|5}} from the [[Etris]] weapon store or [[Summer Isle]] * Craft them using 1 [[Ores#Iron|Iron]] per 50 bullets == Bullet Casings == Bullet Casings can be used in combination with some [[Ores]], like [[Ore|Erisore]] or [[Ore|Umbrite]], to make special bullets with [[Status Effects|effects]] that can aid you in battle, though they do have downsides. These can be found in [[Summer Isle]], in [[The Furnace]] by talking to an NPC named [[Mag]]. You can also get a gunsmith in your Guild Base's blacksmith room for {{c|notes|1000}}, which does the same things as him. You require 1 Note for 5 Bullets Encased, rounding up to the nearest note. (ex. You need 27 notes for 133 bullets encased, rounded up to 135) It should be important to state that the maximum number of Bullets you can encase with just a single ore is 200. The maximum amount of cased bullets you can have in your inventory is capped at 999. ==Bullet Effects== |-|Iron= Iron bullets give a 10% PEN bonus. Because they are considered normal bullets, they do not have any disadvantages. |-|Gold= Gold bullets will slow down the target on hit at a downside of dealing 10% less damage and the speed of the bullet being reduced (speed is possibly bugged). [[File:Gold_Bullet_Casing.gif|frameless|360x360px]] |-|Umbrite= Umbrite bullets will have 10% increased damage on hit and apply wither, but has the downside of the firing speed of the gun being reduced by 25%. [[File:Umbrite GIF.gif|frameless|360x360px]] |-|Erisore= Erisore bullets will apply a 50% anti-heal on hit for 12 seconds at a downside of the damage being reduced by 20%. [[File:Erisore Bullet GIF.gif|frameless|360x360px]] |-|Irithine= Irithine bullets will apply increased shaky block on hit similar to [[Authority Ensign]] inquisitor's Hidden Blade, at a downside of the damage being reduced by 20%. [[File:Irithine Bullet GIF.gif|frameless|360x360px]] |-|Gale= Gale bullets deal 5% less damage while on the ground, but deal 25% more damage and apply [[Suffocation]] if landed while midair. Currently bugged, the bullets don't apply suffocate. |-|Frost= After landing 7 hits, apply [[Status Effects#Frozen|Frozen]] to the target or alternatively detonate their [[Talents#Glassdancer|Crystals]]. 5 second cooldown. Your bullets will deal 5% less damage. == Trivia == * Coal, rock, iron (not the default bullets), and astruline, are minerals not compatible with bullets and therefore cannot be used to encase them. * [[Stormseye|Stormeye's]] and [[Rosen's Hellflame|Rosen's Hellflames's]] shots can use encased bullets. * Erisore's bullets seem to simply apply the same effect as the [[Ring of Pestilence]], so it's more advisable to use the ring and avoid the damage reduction. * The effects of minerals on bullets actually only apply to the "explosion" of the shot and not the projectile, this ironically makes using encased bullets more convenient in rifles and 2H pistols than 1H pistols. [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Items]]

title: C'lantaa
content:
{{CutContent}}
{{NPCInfobox
|name=C'lantaa
|aspect=Tiran
|pronouns=He/him
|location=[[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City]]
|image1=C'lantaa New.png}}

==Description==
C'lantaa was a [[Tiran]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]].

He was found in [[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City]] in a building with the teleporter to the tunnel near the vent into [[The Sunken Railways]]. Similar with other residents of the city, he is unable to recall his past aside from not having a well-off one.

He attempted to communicate with the local [[Kyrsgarde]], but was wounded in the process. He suspects the mist is the vector by which [[Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron]] is enslaving the Kyrsgarde.

He wore the [[Cala-Mariner]] outfit.

==Dialogue==
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="18" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="18" |You see it too, don't you? The mist surrounding us, enshrouding the city.
|-
| colspan="18" {{cl|reply}} |The mist below?
|-
| colspan="18" |Aye. It makes me wonder the true fate of the people here... This place is so, so extravagant, and yet not a sane soul to be seen. 
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Do you think something happened here?
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Sane?
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |What are you doing here?
|-
| colspan="6" |So it seems. I personally think that these people have been enslaved by {{g|Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron's}} presence, bending their wills to his own. Lacking in true free will, as {{g|Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron's}} pawns... It disgusts me. 
| colspan="6" |{{g|Kyrsan / Kyrsgarde|Kyrsgarde}} drones wander the streets aimlessly, and I cannot understand why... I believe they seek to protect {{g|Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron}}, although I cannot be certain. Trying to talk to them has, well, not provided me with anything good. ''*He glances down upon his chest, a small gash pulsing right near his heart.''* So... I've avoided 'peace and love' since then. 
| colspan="6" |*''He raises his brow.''* The same as you, I suppose. Riches, the desire to seek the unknown, perhaps a wanting for something more in life. The Kyrsan treasures here are worth quite a lot on the {{g|The Surface|Surface}}... Although, to say if I make it back alive is a gamble.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |There were kind folk above this city.
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Do you not fear death?
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Something more in life?
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Is there anyone else down here?
|-
| colspan="12" |...Hm, then my theory may have more weight after all. Something isn't right in this place. The influence of {{g|Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron}} may simply be too much for the {{g|Kyrsan / Kyrsgarde|Kyrsgarde}} to handle. Gods below only know how long ''we'' can stay ourselves down here...
| colspan="2" |''*He gives a weak smile, looking toward you with amusement.*'' Aye, I suppose that's one way to put it. I think... life is something not everyone can get away with. Your luck runs out some day, one close call and then... You know the rest. I don't think life is something I can get away with. ''*He looks up at you once more.*'' You think you've already gotten away though, haven't you?
| colspan="2" |Mm. Well.. the same sky gets boring eventually. There's no thrill in living the same life as yesterday for eternity. I s'pose you could say I'm a thrillseeker of sorts... Maybe to a fault. ''*He flashes a bright smile at you.*'' Some call it stupidity, I can see why. But for me, there's nothing else. This is what I have to live for... And if I die by it, so be it.
| colspan="2" |''*He lets out a sigh, looking up at you with mournful contempt.*'' There was. Now, only drones, and the occasional straggler like yourself.
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Perhaps it's just devotion.
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |What else does Ethiron influence?
| colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="6" |''*He lets out a hearty laugh, evidently amused by that prospect.*'' Aye! Devotion to a world-eating husk! What a life, what a life I inhabit... I wish to see through the meaning of all of this. This may be an end for me, but I will not allow an end for my legacy.
| colspan="6" |Huh? You think I'd know that? I'm no scholar, no, I'm no ''aristocrat''. I wouldn't be down here if I had a cushy, easy life like that!
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

Caitus is a [[Khan]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. They are a member of [[The Hundred Legions]] and currently belonging to the 11th Scouting Legion. They stay with their group composed of [[Atra]], [[Lars]], [[Gaius]] and [[Amara]].

Caitus tasks the player with delivering [[Legion Intelligence|a message]] about a [[Titus Fulminus Destellus|certain someone]] in an [[Merit Detainment Core|Authority Prison]]. They will teach the [[Imperium Kata]] style to the player upon reporting back after delivering said message.

Taking upon Caitus' quest requires above Ally reputation with The Hundred Legions.<gallery widths="200">

| colspan="4" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="2" |Brilliant, brilliant! Just need some correspondence delivered - a menial task, really. Just letting a certain someone in those damned {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}} prisons know that we haven't forgotten him.
| colspan="2" |Damn! I really need the help... Come back when you've got a free moment, yeah?
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Uh, okay?
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="2" |''*They briskly snatch a letter out of their pocket - a small note bound with a detailed seal - and shove it into your hands.*'' You think you could sneak in there and drop it off to him? I know it's easier said than done, but I'll be in your debt, spondeō.
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |Sounds easy enough.
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |I'm sorry - *sneak into an Authority prison?*
|-
| colspan="1" |Yes, that's the spirit! Let me know once you've delivered it, alright? It'll be worth your while, promise.
| colspan="1" |Oh yes, if you could, please... What? Don't give me that look, you seem perfectly capable. And, knowing the {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}}, I'm sure it shouldn't be too hard. He's being held in the prison beneath Fort Merit. Let me know once you've delivered the letter, yeah? It'll be worth your while, promise.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], Legion Intelligence obtained
|}

|-|Subsequent Encounters=
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="6" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="6" |''*The Khan is deep in thought, their brow furrowing periodically.*''
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Hello...?
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Defeated [[Titus]]]
| colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Player has [[Imperium Kata]]]
| colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Legion Intelligence Quest not complete]
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|action}} |[Defeated Titus]
| colspan="1" {{cl|action}} |[Defeated Titus in a group, without the Legion Intelligence]
| colspan="2" |''*They turn to briefly, yet amicably, acknowledge you.*'' Ah, salvete once again! Hope you're enjoying your reward, friend? Thanks again for the help, on behalf of the Hundred Legions.
| colspan="2" |Hm? Haven't you delivered the letter yet? Gods know how much he's suffering in that cell, get to it
|-
| colspan="1" |''*They smile, clasping their hands together with the tact of a bureaucrat.*'' Ah, salvete again, friend! I hope that everything went swimmingly, though you are looking a little worse-for-wear. I hope the {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}} didn't cause you too much trouble?
| colspan="1" |Salvete, friend, good to see you!... Uh... What's with that look? Something bothering you?
| colspan="4" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |Your friend... *attacked* me?
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |You sent my friend to deliver a letter, and the guy nearly killed us.
|-
| colspan="2" |''*Their brow furrows, before they pinch the bridge of their nose tightly.*'' Are you telling me... He kicked off? Over a polite message to wait? And here I thought Titus was a man of great strategic patience. Well! Well... This is ''quite'' unexpected, I suppose.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |You don't seem too bothered by his fate?
|-
| colspan="2" |Hey, hey! Don't presume me to be heartless, yeah? I've heard enough to know that a warrior of his calibre doesn't die that easily. And judging by the fact that you're not dead, I'm guessing he let you go. A happy ending for you, right? I don't think the higher-ups will appreciate his actions, though... I can certainly mourn his loyalty.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Just who was that man?
|-
| colspan="2" |'''Titus Fulminus Destellus''', a prolific general amongst our ranks. Just this absolutely mythical figure to most, you know... Incredibly strong, with an unrivalled strategic mind. He was supposed to peacefully retire after his final missions, including this one... Guess he's thrown that straight into the sea.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |He said he'd play along for now, or something.
|-
| colspan="2" |''*They raise an eyebrow with interest.*'' ...Really? Suppose I underestimated the both of you, then. I've heard nothing can change Titus' mind when he's set on something. But I guess you're stronger than you look, if the beatdown you gave him made him reconsider things.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |How did someone like him end up in the Fort Merit dungeons?
|-
| colspan="2" |Not for lack of strength, that's for sure! I heard high command had him surrender on purpose. I haven't the foggiest on specifics, mind you. Rumour has it he was meant to gather intel from the inside, then break out - or be broken out. Some say it was meant to be some sort of pincer attack on Merit. Guess the plan's had some delays, though... And, suppose Titus wasn't too keen on waiting any longer. I dunno how the higher-ups will take his disobedience... But they've won either way - Fort Merit's in shambles, at least for now.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Well... What now?
|-
| colspan="2" |As much as I didn't expect any of this to happen, I did promise to repay the favour. Take this, it also plays its part in something greater.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], player obtains Imperium Kata Fist style
|}
</tabber>

==Trivia==
*Some words said by Caitus are derived from Latin terms:
**[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/nemo#Latin Nemo] is a Latin word for "nobody", which they refer to the player as under Ally reputation.
***Nemo was a name used in place of the Outis alias in Latinized versions of ''The Odyssey'' for the hero Odysseus, who is referred to as Ulysses in the Latin version.
**[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/salve#Latin Salve, in a Latin context], is used for greetings and farewells.
***Salvete is the plural form of this word, which is mostly (and incorrectly) used by Caitus.
**[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/teneo#Latin Teneō] has various meanings, but in this context, may be used for "understand".
**[https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/spondeo Spondeō] literally means "I promise".
*You don't need to speak to Caitus before defeating Titus in order to get Imperium Kata.

This Outfit additionally requires the player to be at least [[Power]] 15 and have at least 5 [[Willpower]] to be crafted. ===''Armor Stats''=== The Outfit has 2200 durability, grants {{stats|phys|+25% Physical resistance}}, {{stats|elm|+35% Elemental resistance}}, {{stats|wnd|+30% Wind resistance}}, {{stats|bld|+25% Blood resistance}}, {{stats|sanity|+20 Sanity}}, and {{stats|ether|+45% Ether Regeneration}}. *Due to resistances being combined multiplicatively instead of additively, the total resistances are: {{stats|phys|25% Physical}}, {{stats|wnd|54.5% Galebreathe}}, {{stats|bld|51.25% Bloodrend}}, and {{stats|elm|35% Elemental|wnd=n|bld=n}}. Additionally, it provides the {{t|Tidal Shock}} Talent. This makes your Critical attacks apply short Daze and trigger Tidal Shock's effect. On {{t|Tidal Shock}} proc, for the next 4s, any Mantra that hits you will have its damage voided. Tidal Shock has a 13 second cooldown. Visually, when Tidal Shock is enabled on the wearer, the user emits bubble effects. When Tidal Shock procs on the user, they will let out a [[Nautilodaunt]]'s vent. File:TidalShock.gif|Tidal Shock being applied on the wearer == Gallery == File:CalaMarinerConceptArt.png|Concept art ==Trivia/Notes== *This outfit has one of the most expensive Outfit crafting recipes, being beat out by only the [[Titanslayer's Adornment]] and [[Titus's Raiment]]. Cala-Mariner requires 5 [[Odd Tentacle]]s and a [[Nautilodaunt Beak]], so expect to farm a lot of [[Nautilodaunt]]s if you wish to obtain this outfit for yourself. *The outfits name is a pun on calamari and mariner. *The oufit resembles the outfit of Jack Sparrow from ''Pirates of the Caribbean''. *When you have the {{t|Tidal ShocK}} CD, you cannot use {{t|Whistleguard}}, and when you use Whistleguard and critical hit with Cala-Mariner, Whistleguard will break. {{History}} {{Nav|Outfits}} [[Category:Outfits]] [[Category:Outfits with Talents]] [[Category:Outfits with Exclusive Talents]]
