title: Combat Mechanics
content:
This page contains basic information about '''combat''' and its associated mechanics. This includes details on status bars, attacks, status effects, and more ''Knowing this information is absolutely crucial to prolonging your life, and will give any voyager a fighting chance when they inevitably enter a skirmish with their future adversaries, or worse-- allies.'' == GUI == [[File:Verse2GUI.png|alt=|center|thumb|477x477px]] ''There are many elements to the GUI, each one playing its own part. In order to have a chance at surviving, learning these is essential.'' {|class="article-table" !{{anch|Health Bar}} |A visual representation of the player's health. Players start with 220 Health (224 at Power 1); things like [[Fortitude]] (0.5 Health per invest from 0-50 invest, and 0.25 per for 50+ invest), Health bonus from [[Talents]] and [[Equipment]], [[Vitality]] (10 Health per Vitality), and [[Power]] (4 Health per Power) increase the max health. Upon reaching 0% Health, the player gets knocked {{status|b=y|Unconscious}} and is at the mercy of anyone around them. *Regeneration is sped up while sitting at a [[Campfire]], and slowed down while the player is in combat. *Natural health regeneration is disabled if their hunger bar is below 12.5%. *The lower your Health is, the slower you get. In short, Health directly affects your agility. The player's Health bar has four states: [[File:HDHP.png|center|435px|thumb|This is the normal state of the health bar.
The player will lose one life on death (excluding the [[Hollow]] modifier).]] [[File:Stained Health Bar.png|center|thumb|435x435px|This is the state of the health bar after dying once. It is rusted and more jaundiced compared to its normal state.The player will be sent to [[The Depths]] on death.]] [[File:Healthbar_rusted.png|center|435px|thumb|This is the state of the health bar in a [[Voidzones|Voidzone]] if you have not died once. It is rusted unlike its normal state.
The player will be sent to [[The Depths]] on death.]] [[File:Void Threshold.png|center|thumb|435x435px|This is the state of the health bar in The Depths.
The player will be sent to [[Fragments of Self]] on death.]] The stained part represents your void health, which means if your health bar doesn't reach the stained part you can jump into the void you will be sent to the [[Second Layer]] rather than wiping. If your health bar reaches the stained part and you jump into the void your character '''WILL''' be sent to [[Fragments of Self]] rather than the [[Second Layer]]. |- !{{anch|Posture|Posture Bar}} |A visual representation of the player's ability to guard against attacks. Building this bar indicates negative standing, you should do your best to keep this bar as low as possible during combat. When the next attack causes the posture to exceed the bar, the next blocked hit will instead guard break, stunning you for 1.05s. * Posture can be restored through many methods: the passive Posture regeneration when not sprinting or blocking, Parrying attacks, landing a Taunt ({{input|keybind|T}}), or through the use of certain [[Talents]]. *Posture can have multipliers effecting the maximum & minimum given from various [[Talents]], [[Enchantments]], or other effects. posture damage dealt has a soft cap of 1.5x where all posture multipliers after get halved with a maximum hard cap of 1.75x where you cannot do more than 175% of the posture damage an attack was meant to deal. Posture damage received has a hard cap of 0.5x where you cannot take less than 50% of the posture damage the attack was meant to deal. *When blocking while in shaky block frames, your posture bar glows red to indicate that your block isn't full yet. [[File:Posturebarweak.gif|center]] [[File:Block Exhaust bar.png|center|464x464px]] |- !Cooldown Icons |Icons that indicate whether or not the player can do certain actions. When these icons become reddened/grayed out indicates that the specified action is currently on cooldown. *The first icon represents roll cooldown. *The second icon represents parrying cooldown. *The third icon represents if block is available. *The fourth icon represents cancels and feints cooldowns. *The fifth icon represents [[Resonance]] cooldown. Only visible if you have one. *There is an additional sixth icon at the bottom of your equipped weapon's item slot. This icon displays your weapon's critical cooldown. File:Dodge CD indicator.png|
Dodge File:Parry CD indicator.png|
Parry File:Block CD indicator.png|
Block File:Feint CD indicator.png|
Feint File:Resonance CD indicator.png|
Resonance File:Critical CD indicator.png|
Critical |- !Cooldown Indicators |Cooldown Indicators represent the cooldown for mostly everything in-game excluding Mantras, from Talents like Kick Off, Propagandist, and Audacity, to Criticals, Feints, Resonances, and even special attacks/effects such as [[Gran Sudaruska|Sudaruska's Fury]] and [[Immortal Helm|Immortality]], with the name of the cooldown on the left side, and the amount of time until you can use it again on the right.[[File:Cooldown Indicators .gif|center|thumb]] |- !Ether Bar |A visual representation of the player's Ether amount. Ether is Deepwoken's form of mana, and [[Mantras]] cannot be used without sufficient Ether. * you can increase Ether regeneration via wearing certain [[outfits]] usually master [[outfits]], or via various [[Talents]]. *Different Mantras use varying amounts of Ether. Adding [[Mantra Modifiers]] will increase the amount of Ether required to cast. *Ether passively regenerates in combat as long as you have tempo. If you run out of tempo you regenerate 0.5% of your ether bar per second. *Ether also regenerates passively and faster when out of combat. [[File:HDEther.png|center|477x477px]] |- !{{anch|Vent|Tempo}} |A visual representation of the player's Tempo. Tempo increases Ether regen during battle, as well as permitting the player to vent if they have a certain amount of Tempo stored. The base Tempo starts at 120. *Tempo is gained by hitting or being hit *Tempo decreases over time (1% per 0.6s) and is "stored" when out of combat *With at least 40 Tempo, press {{Input|keybind|G}} to Vent. This pushes away anyone near you but can be parried and blocked, if you get your vent parried or blocked it leaves you stunned, if you miss your vent entirely you also get left stunned. With more [[Erudition]], venting becomes easier to do as you will have more Tempo, as well as Tempo regen. [[File:Tempo.png|center|370px]] |- !Armor Durability |A visual representation of the player's current [[Outfits|armor]] durability. When this bar is depleted, the player's armor is considered "broken", and you will start taking damage as if you have no armor on at all from your [[Outfits|outfit]], [[Equipment]] or any other sources. *Armor can be repaired through various methods, such as a Blacksmith, using [[Talents]], the Metal [[Enchantments|Enchantment]], or a [[Bloodiron Ring]]. Assuming you managed to pick up the {{t|Exoskeleton}} Talent or if you are a [[Vesperian]], there will be two armor bars instead- the white representing [[Outfits|Armor]], and the green representing Natural Armor. [[File:HDArmor.png|center|501x501px]] |} ''Let it be known that applying these things will take some time to master.'' ''As you play the game and face hardships, knowing how to properly watch over these values will begin to come to you naturally. Ward your frustration should you become disappointed in your progress- there is still the road ahead, Pathfinder.'' == Maps == Upon talking to a shipwright or spawning a boat, you'll unlock the ability to write down your navigations. With places that have not been explored yet obscured, and places you have already visited fully written. It also identifies you of your current location with a yellow (blue if in the depths) marker, and the waterlocks leading to the next Luminant. It will also provide you of the whereabouts of your guildmates with their first and last inital, and points of interest in your current location. You will also be shown if you cross out of the maps boundaries as an arrow to the side of the map. If you have [[Dimensional Travel|Dimensional Travel/Kamui]] in your possession, using a map inside of it will also inform you of your physical location. File:Marks of interest map.png|Points of Interest Map File:Out of bounds map.png|Out of Bounds Map File:Guild mates map.png|Guild Mates Map File:Greyed map.png|Obscured Map File:Etrean lum map.png|Etrean Luminant Map File:Eastern lum map.png|Eastern Luminant Map File:Layer 1 map.png|Layer 1 Map File:Maps combined.png|Maps Combined == Keybinds == Upon pressing the settings button, you can find a keybinds section next to the settings page. Keybinds will allow you to have two different keys for an action, with the first one already being there when you start. To revert something, all you would need to do is press the reset button next to the action you're changing. Certain actions such as [[Ironsing]]'s pull and [[Murmur]]s require you to have access to them on the character you're currently using in order to change their Keybinds. Currently, you are unable to change Keybinds for ritual casting. [[File:Keybinds.gif|none|thumb]] == Survival Basics == [[File:Survivalbars.png|thumb|right]] These are stats that are you required to maintain in order to survive in the world of ''Deepwoken''. These stats will gradually deplete over time during your travels, but the depletion can be sped up by varying environments, creatures, or other players. *In order to survive, the player will need to eat food to replenish their ''Stomach'' and hydrate to replenish their ''Water''. Many food items also contain water within them, such as the [[Mushroom Bisque]], allowing you to regenerate both. *''Once both are depleted, you will begin to lose Blood and your health will be reduced to half of your max health.'' *''Once every bar reaches zero, you will enter a combat state and be rendered helpless unless you consume food within the next few seconds. Should you not consume food, you will be knocked until you inevitably die from blood loss and/or starvation.'' *These stats can be found at the bottom-left of your screen, in the main game. {{Clear}} {| class="article-table" !{{anch|Blood}} |A visual representation of how much ''Blood'' is currently in the player's body. Being attacked or taking damage in some form will cause the player to lose ''Blood''. Upon reaching zero Blood, the following happens: *The player will always be combat tagged. *The player's Water and Stomach bar will rapidly decrease. *Getting hit while bleeding out drains a large amount of Water and Stomach *Blood loss is based off of damage. ''Maximum blood is equal to half of your max HP.'' ''Different damage sources deals an amount of blood damage, scaled with the attack damage.'' ''When healing at a campfire, your Water and Stomach will work together to replenish your Blood.'' |[[File:HDBlood.png|thumb|center|200x200px]] |- !Water |A visual representation of how much ''Water'' is currently in the player's body. Water isn't too vital for survival and will deplete over time. You will lose 50% of the bar upon vomiting. Upon reaching zero ''Water'', the following happens: *The player's screen will become blurry. *The player will start to move slower. ''Your Water will drain slightly faster when replenishing blood at a campfire or swimming.'' |[[File:HDWater.png|thumb|center|200x200px]] |- !Stomach |A visual representation of how much [[food]] is currently in the player's body; essentially your hunger bar. You will lose 50% of the bar upon vomiting. Upon reaching zero Stomach, the following happens: *The player will gradually lose health and blood. *The player's max health will be reduced. *Attempting to swim while starving and with less than 50% HP will immediately knock the player, resulting in drowning if not assisted. ''Your Stomach will drain slightly faster when replenishing blood at a campfire or swimming.'' |[[File:HDFood.png|thumb|center|200x200px]] |} == Inventory== ''Your inventory will be color-coded to assist you in finding types of items. Should you be unable to find an item in your mountain of objects, simply use the search bar in the bottom and type the item name in to quickly find it.'' {| class="article-table" ! rowspan="11" |Item Type | colspan="10" | All items in you see in your UI whether in the inventory or in your hotbar have a color based off of what type of item they are. These categories take different priority in the sorting of your inventory so misc items like books will be seen at the bottom of your inventory while training items and utility like flint are seen at the top. Items also have a frame on them with the color defining its rarity or otherwise worth. Grey for common, yellow for uncommon, red for rare and cyan for legendary. Purple frames are seen on potions and enchants. Grey is always seen on elemental weapons like Crypt Blades. (These item frames aren't always correlated to the items drop-rate hence why some "Legendary" items may appear to drop commonly when you do the math) *During the 2/9/24 update, the Inventory UI received a category revamp. It brought along 9 different categories, combining old item categories making a clean separate line for each category, and listing the number amount of items in each category on the right side. *During the 2/16/24 update, the Inventory UI received a further addition of 3D model icons. This can be changed in the settings and can be disabled or extended to only show if the item is hovered over. It also added collapsable categories with a down arrow next to the category amount, which collapses the category upon being clicked. And the addition of the 10th category; Relics. File:3d item icon.png|"3D Icon Behavior" setting on "Always" File:3d icon hover.png|"3D Icon Behavior" setting on "Hover" |- Abilities - Weight: None
1st place in the inventory. Consist of activatable Talents like Chime of Dwelling, Guild Officer, Voideye and Call of the Deep. Also consists of equipped Mantras should you lack space in your hotbar for them. Tools - Weight: None
2nd place in the inventory. Consists of usable items like Campfires, Fishing Rods, Gliders, harvesting tools, guild tools or the [[Hunter's Brace]]. Training Gear - Weight: None
3rd place in the inventory. Consists of items that train your character's [[attributes]] such as Ankle Weights, Dumbell, Vest/Boulder, and Encyclopedia Equipment - Weight: 0.1 - 2
4th place in the inventory. Consists of equippable armor and clothing pieces if you meet the requirements. Weapons - Weight: 2
5th place in the inventory. Consists of equippable weapons and off-hand items if you meet the reqirements. Schematics - Weight: 1
6th place in the inventory. Consists of blueprints you can turn in at blacksmiths to craft them. Quest Items - Weight: None
7th place in the inventory. Consists of items that interact with certain [[quests]]. Consumables - Weight: Varies
8th place in the inventory. Consists of foods and potions. Relics - Weight: None
9th place in the Inventory. Consists of Mythical Items that can rewrite fate, such as alloys that can enhance or even Enchant items, to books, parchment or idols that can change or enhance your resonance or knowledge. Materials - Weight: Varies
10th place in the inventory. Consists of materials from foraging or chests used for crafting and/or alchemy. It also consists of Mantra modifiers, ingredients that are used to further enhance Mantras, such as increasing their size or range. |- !Carrying Capacity | colspan="8" |''Carrying Capacity,'' also known as [[Carry Load]], dictates how much weight in items your character can hold before their speed is reduced and they can no longer safely have items. ''You may check an item's weight by hovering over the item in your inventory and seeing the number held in the small blue box in the corner. Hovering over the item may also give you a description along with how many notes it'll sell for at an [[Antiquarian]].'' There exists a soft cap, which is the listed capacity in digits on the right in your inventory. You may carry more items beyond that amount, reaching the hard cap. There then exists a hard cap, upon reaching the cap; your carrying capacity will be colored red. Detailed when you try to carry more items than you're currently capable of. Eventually, your character will be unable to hold onto any more items, and enough items must be dropped to make room to pick up another. The closer you get to the hard cap, the slower your movement will be. *For example, if the soft cap would be 240; the hard cap would be anything past that. |[[File:CarryCapacity.png|thumb|center]] |- !Locking Items | colspan="8" | By right-clicking on a sellable/droppable item, you can lock it. By locking it you prevent the item from being sold or dropped while giving it an appearance of chained borders. |[[File:Locking icon.png|center|thumb]][[File:Locked item.png|center|thumb]] |} ==Combat Basics == ''When fighting, while dealing damage is important, reducing their posture can also help in reducing the volatility of your fellow adversary. Should they block one of your attacks, rest assured that you still dealt some form of damage to them by placing them in negative standing.'' {| class="article-table" !Basic Attacks |[[File:attack.gif|right|thumb]] Left clicking ({{Input|keybind|M1}}) allows you to swing your weapon, dealing damage to whoever is hit unless they block, parry, or dodge your attack. In the case of getting your attack blocked, your attack will instead deal a different type of damage in the form of "Posture Damage", taking into account the weight of your weapon rather than your damage output. When a certain number of hits are swung consecutively without pauses(typically 3 hits then flourish, whilst for rifles it's 4 & 2h guns or never for 2h twinblade), your character will kick your adversary away in an action called a Flourish. This is an "end" to your string of swings before it resets, and has a small amount of endlag before you can swing again- which can be circumvented by casting a Mantra directly after the Flourish. Landing a Flourish causes the target hit to be launched away from you, essentially preventing an infinite combo. Flourishes can only be feinted by casting a Mantra. *''Many Talents modify your Flourish in different ways, from blurring someone's screen when they get pushed into a wall with the Concussion Talent, burning someone with the Flaming Flourish Talent or placing down Ice with the Chilling Flourish Talent.'' Hitting or parrying opponents applies stun, which, for a slight moment, lowers their movement speed, disables their rolling, cancels their ability to attack, and nullifies the hitbox of any current Mantras they are casting despite the continuing animation and visual effects. *In continuation of the ending point, if someone uses Ice Lance but you manage to score a hit as they drive it towards you, you will take no damage from the Ice Lance- it won't even stick into you, even if you were meant to be hit by it. Performing an M1 while running performs a ''Running Attack'', forcing your character to strafe forward and strike with increased range- stopping your character in place directly after, and has increased end-lag and slightly increased windup. While some of these properties may sound negative, it can be handy when in need of having to catch your adversary off guard. If a Running Attack is used against an adversary with their back turned to you, you shall charge into them with a gust of wind and strike. The only way to feint a ''Running Attack'' is to cast a Mantra. Getting hit will negate your ability to throw in an M1 for a little longer than it takes for you to be able to roll so it's not at all recommended to try to M1 in the middle of your opponents combo. |- !Critical Attacks |[[File:CriticalAttack.gif|right|thumb]] ''Critical Attacks'', or "Crit(s)" for short, can be initiated by pressing {{Input|keybind|R}} or clicking {{Input|keybind|M3}} (Pressing down the scroll wheel). Personally advised to use {{Input|keybind|R}}. ''Critical Attacks'' have various uses. They are mainly used to deal high posture damage, especially Heavy weapons. Some work as a way to throw off/confuse your adversary's rhythm, such as with [[Crescendo]] or [[Rifle Spear]]'s criticals. Others work as a way to help high damage, such as [[Rosen's Hellflame]] or [[Wretched Mawblades]]' criticals. Others can serve as utility for the player, such as [[Petra's Anchor]] (Dash) or [[Darksteel Greatsword]] (Hyperarmor), while some others may be used to simply pressure to the opponent, such as [[First Light]] (Zoning) and [[Flareblood Kamas]]' (Ranged) criticals. '''''A mass majority of Critical Attacks cannot be feinted. When you perform one, make sure you are committed to doing so.''''' |- !{{anch|Parry|Parrying}} |[[File:Parrying.gif|right|thumb]] Pressing the {{Input|keybind|F}} key causes your character to enter a stance of deflection for a moment. Enemies hitting you during this timeframe have their attacks parried, causing them to be momentarily stunned and dealing posture damage to them, as well as reducing your own posture. It should be noted that whether your tap or hold {{Input|keybind|F}} doesn't matter, as it will result in a parry at the beginning of the button press regardless. Successful parries gives your character 0.3 seconds of auto-parry in which all incoming attacks are parried automatically. Parrying also resets its cooldown so that you may parry immediately again. '''''It's also possible to attack during it's auto-parry frames, but this is difficult to do safely.''''' Parrying will cancel all attacks (except for some monster attacks), as well as the damage for that attack, even if they come from behind your character. '''''However, this is not the case for Blocking (see below).''''' ''Parrying has a 1.2 second cooldown. If you miss your parry, you may hold'' {{Input|keybind|F}} ''to Block and nullify/reduce any imminent damage you would otherwise take for missing the parry.'' Parrying physical attacks like Mantras or M1s will completely interrupt your opponents action, even if the animation continues. So, without their action getting in the way of their parry, they are able to parry whatever move you throw out next. This does not apply to all Mantras however, especially projectile based ones. You may alternatively attempt to roll their Mantra which MAY have an 100% chance of an M1 if you throw it out quick enough. ''Whilst Blocking and Parrying share the same hotkey'' ({{Input|keybind|F}})'', you'll perform a parry instead of a block if a parryable attack hits you during parry frames. You can know when you're currently in a state of parry frames by taking note of your character's distinct stance and hearing a subtle "whoosh" sound immediately after pressing'' {{Input|keybind|F}}. |- !{{anch|Block|Shaky Block|Blocking}} |[[File:Blocking.gif|right|thumb]] By holding the {{Input|keybind|F}} key after this stance of deflection has worn off, your character will hold their defensive stance and brace for incoming attacks, increasing your posture rather than lowering your health if you were hit during the block. The blocker can act slightly before the attacker, but not as much as if they parried. '''''Remember, letting your posture exceed its maximum hold will result in you being block-broken.''''' If you are hit, your block will be disabled and you will instead be forced to parry. You may also Vent by pressing {{Input|keybind|G}} if you have enough Tempo. If you attempt to parry immediately after getting hit, you will be put in '''shaky block'''. Shaky block is a form of hitstun that prevents blocking. The duration of your shaky block is based on your weapon's swing speed. If your weapon has above 1x swingspeed, your shaky block duration will be reduced proportionately to your swingspeed amount over 1x, capping at -20% with 1.2x swingspeed. Shaky block is indicated by your arms shaking and you covering your head and your posture bar having a red highlight. ''Against most attacks, blocking only prevents attacks in front of your character. Some attacks have the 360° block property however, allowing them to be blocked from all angles.'' |- !{{anch|Vent|Venting}} |[[File:Venting.gif|right|thumb]] When the player has at least 40 Tempo (indicated by a small notch on the tempo bar), pressing the {{Input|keybind|G}} key will make the player Vent. Venting pushes others nearby away and grants a brief period of relief, allowing the player to get out of tricky situations such as being comboed or overcrowded, along with dealing a miniscule 5 damage, enough to cancel attacks and knock your adversary if they have sufficiently low health. Venting also clears certain [[Status Effects]], such as Knockdown. Should the Vent fail to land or be parried/blocked, you will be stunned in place, unable to do anything. This will provide a window for your adversary to close in on you. Should you be lucky, this window won't be exploited. *While block-broken or assassinated, you cannot Vent. Vents are parryable, blockable and rollable which all negate the knock back you'd normally receive. Parrying it however does stun the person venting in place as if they missed the vent. |- !{{anch|Feint|Feinting}} | Right-clicking- or otherwise using {{Input|keybind|M2}}- during the moment your character pulls their weapon/arm back for a swing will allow you to fake-out the opponent with a ''Feint''. You can also hold the button down which will feint your M1 as soon as possible and allows you to attack again even sooner more easily. *You may feint ''Running Attacks'' and ''Uppercuts'' (see below) by using a Mantra just before you strike. *You may feint Mantras by using {{Input|keybind|M2}} during a cast. *You may feint a swing into a Mantra by casting a Mantra during the moment your character pulls their weapon/arm back. This allows you to play mind games with your adversary, and is very essential for mid-high level combat. For example, feinting can bait them to block- disabling their ability to parry and instead forcing them to roll. When they roll, you can follow through their roll and attack them through it. The strongest way to use feints is to use them without a pattern or rhythm. People can learn the way your feints work, and turn your feints from a tool into a downfall by swinging at you when they know you will feint. *Alternatively, you can make a makeshift feint by intentionally missing an attack, which spares you of the cooldown. This technique is a gamble, but with risk comes rewards. ''Feinting has very slight end-lag, and will briefly disable your ability to make any attack for a very small moment.'' |- !{{anch|Roll|Rolling}} |[[File:Dashing.gif|right|thumb]] Pressing {{Input|keybind|Q}} allows you to Roll towards your desired direction, granting you immunity frames against most attacks, with the exception of a few. You can roll-cancel by right-clicking- or otherwise using {{Input|keybind|feint}}- during the movement of your roll. This will guarantee you an extra roll that can also be canceled. For many experienced players, roll-canceling replaces Rolling as it is simply better in most cases, given that it cancels the endlag of your Roll as well as asserting yourself in combat and sizing up your adversary.
Many Talents exist to add properties to your Rolls. For example, if a [[Galebreathe]]r obtains the rare card Gale Dash, they will gain a wind-empowered dash upon initially dodging an incoming attack. ''Pressing {{Input|keybind|Q}} in the air initiates an Air Dash, sending you towards a direction depending on where your camera is facing. Air Dashes are counted as rolls, meaning that they will be able to dodge attacks.'' |- !{{anch|Weapon Stance|Stance Change}} |[[File:StanceChange.gif|right|thumb]] Pressing the {{Input|keybind|Y}} button will change your ''Stance'' from one-handed to two-handed. Many Light Weapons cannot switch their stance except for Fists, which can switch between their unlockable fist styles at will. '''''One Handed Stance:''''' This stance is the default for Light and Medium weapons, and Heavy weapons can use this stance after obtaining 40 HVY. Offhand equipment, such as shields, parrying daggers, and guns will be accessible. An alternate idle animation is used if you do not have anything on your offhand. '''''Two-Handed Stance:''''' This stance is the default for Heavy weapons, with Medium Weapons also having access to it. Any offhand equipment will be put away, such as shields. '''This stance increases posture damage dealt by 10% hitting their block.''' '''''Dual Wielded Stance:''''' This stance is exclusive to a [[:Category:Dual-wielded Weapons|few select weapons]]. Dual Wielding is mechanically the same as One Handing, with the only major difference being that you cannot use offhand weapons. Most weapons with this Stance cannot swap to other Stances. |- !{{anch|Assassination}} |When crouched, one can sneak up behind '''most''' humanoid enemies- excluding Songseekers for example- and {{Input|keybind|M1}} from behind to perform an ''Assassination''. This will deal a large amount of damage to NPCs, and 15% to a players max health when assassinated scaling up with agility to a max of 25%. If you backstab a NPC it will cause the victim to ragdoll for 5 seconds (NPCs) and place their Vent on cooldown while they are knocked out. Auto-executes NPCs if the damage dealt is high enough. ''If the target is not killed by the initial attack, it is recommended to swing at them as much as possible before they get up.'' The range at which enemies won't detect you while crouching can be improved by increasing your [[Stealth]] stat through various equipment. |- !{{anch|Uppercut}} |You may hit your adversaries up into the air with an ''Uppercut'' by pressing {{Input|keybind|M1}} or M2 while holding {{Input|keybind|Ctrl}}. If your opponent is a monster, they will fail to rise with you and instead remain grounded. Victims hit by Uppercuts are lifted into the air temporarily being unable to move, and parry timing is seemingly tighter, which makes Uppercuts play a big role in combos. Comboing will keep you in the air, while parrying or getting parried will drop both of you. Certain Talents- such as ''Flaming Flourish'' can also affect the potency of Uppercuts by adding properties to them the same way some Talents add properties to Flourishes or crits. Uppercuts have their own unique windup speed of 0.9, regardless of whatever weapon type you may be using, making Uppercuts especially useful for Heavy weapons with slow swing speeds. Uppercuts also scale the damage relative to the swingspeed so fast swinging weapons will do higher damage on uppercut than M1 If you land an Uppercut against a dodge or block, then the reduced end-lag should allow you to strike your opponent with an M1 before they can retaliate. Landing a flourish on an opponent suffering from the stun of your aerial combo will automatically kick them to the floor, which will result in any wall-bang Talents occurring- such as ''Bulldozer'' and ''Breathing Impact.'' ''Missing an Uppercut will completely immobilize you and leave you vulnerable- akin to failing to Vent, but you can typically parry an incoming attack if your opponent is on edge.'' |- !{{anch|Spit|Taunt}} |By pressing {{Input|keybind|T}}, you can perform a taunt, colloquially refered to as a "spit" or "spitting". When taunting, the player character spits directly in-front of them. Whilst initially unassuming, the taunt has a special application in combat. By spitting while your face is right up against another Humanoid's face (or perhaps spitting towards a Humanoid whilst they're facing the opposite direction you are when they're a few studs away from you), their vision will be briefly blurred (exact amount of time unconfirmed) and you will heal ~2% of your health and restore a moderate sum of your posture. This is a risky maneuver, though, as taunting has a considerable amount of startup and endlag, and you're usually better off just attacking your opponent. Due to this glaring flaw, the Taunt should only be used as a method of, well, taunting foes you deem inferior, or perhaps even as a risky mixup. ''Based on the name, it's possible that more taunts were meant to be added, but this is not confirmed by any developers.'' |- !{{anch|Chase Attack}} |By initiating a running attack while chasing an opponent, speed up to catch your opponent and attack them. |- !{{anch|Air Counter}} |Pressing {{input|keybind|feint}} midair while your opponent preforms a wall jump or certain air based moved such as {{t|Strong Leap}} quickly closes the distance and hits them. Air Counters innately do not deal damage, instead being used as tools to chase your opponent. Air Counter can be initiated by pressing {{input|keybind|feint}} while midair when your opponent: climbs something, uses the Galebreathe Talent {{t|Wind Step}}, uses a vertical mobility Mobility Mantra such as [[Flame Leap]] or [[Strong Leap]], gets hit by [[Eyes of Ethiron]]'a two-handed critical, or uses a [[Lifevents|Lifevent]]. Having the {{t|Cut to the Chase}} Talent will add 10 True damage to your air counters. |} ''On paper, this looks like a lot to memorize, but do not worry. These things will come more naturally as you play the game, just do not forget that these exist. Improving your combat potential and your ability to conquer those that stand in your way lies in your ability to '''master what must be mastered.''''' ==Telegraphed Attacks== ''Some attacks will be accompanied with an audiovisual cue, that being a colored glyph which is sometimes paired up with an identically colored outline and a sharp distinct sound effect. These attacks mostly require specific action to avoid and are usually associated with a certain level of threat.'' ''However, do note that:'' *''The telegraph shown on an attack is usually the most optimal way to avoid it, and if not, the only way that it can be avoided.'' *''The glyph of a telegraph may vary depending on its source, though its color will not.'' *''If the "Simple Telegraphs" setting is on, glyphs will not show up and only colored outlines will.''

Spell feinting is performed by pressing {{Input|keybind|M2}} during the Mantra's wind-up. Spell feinting will '''not''' refund the Ether cost. It's possible to feint and feint your spell at the same time. Double feinting like this will often draw out your opponent's parry and roll. It's still fairly possible to retaliate against but dealing with this technique is tricky, especially when used with very quick Mantras, which easily overwhelms most unexperienced players. |} ==Advanced Movement == {| class="article-table" !{{anch|Roll Cancel}} |When you roll, you can {{Input|keybind|feint}} similar to how feinting works and cancel your roll. Useful against enemies after perfect dodging to immediately attack or to fake out your opponent. Gives you the same i-frames as a normal perfect roll until the feint. |- !{{anch|Ragdoll Cancel}} |After being ragdolled, you can {{Input|keybind|feint}} to do a backflip that ends the ragdoll early for some attacks- such as a [[Thresher]] tail whip. |} ==Alliances== The Alliance mechanic assists players in minimizing damage from friendly fire, rather than a complete damage immunity mechanic typically found in other games. In ''Deepwoken'', the game runs an "ally check" when calculating damage or deciding to proc abilities. Players and NPCs considered allies will receive less damage dealt by you. Some [[Talents]] increase this effect further and can also proc additional effects. Allies can view messages from you anywhere in a server through Shouts. In Dungeons and other instanced servers, all messages are automatically shouted to other allies in the server. In public servers, you can send a shout by prefixing your message with an exclamation mark (!). For example: "!give me 30,000 notes". It can also work through allies with '''Vow of Allegiance'''. If you are in a [[Guilds|guild]], all other members of that guild are treated as allies. You can form alliances with players outside of your guild through a '''Vow of Allegiance'''. To form a Vow of Allegiance, you must say "Wanna make a vow of allegiance [name]?" near your target. The target can accept the vow by saying "yes", which will then show the confirmation window. There are no stat or Talent requirements to make this vow. Vows of Allegiance persist on the slot (not to be confused with the Character or Account), and each slot can only form 50 allegiances. You can break your Vows of Allegiance through a [[Yun'Shul]] wish (you must make this wish at the [[Temple of Hearts]] as the [[Relics|Idol of Yun'Shul]] does not have this option). However, this breaks '''''ALL''''' vows made on the slot. The ally check can be disabled by turning on the "No Holds Barred" in-game setting, useful if you would like to spar with teammates as your attacks will deal normal damage and proc Talents/abilities that normally would not. ==Trivia== *The overall parry-based combat is heavily inspired by ''Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice'', even possessing [https://sekiroshadowsdietwice.wiki.fextralife.com/Perilous+Attacks Perilous Attacks] in the form of unparriable attacks. The inclusion and appearance of a [https://sekiroshadowsdietwice.wiki.fextralife.com/Posture Posture Bar] is also very similar to ''Sekiro''. *The Health and Survival GUI have 5 separate bars in them that represent 20% each. This will help you to interpret damage dealt, health percentage, and help you to interpret the percentage of water and food each consumable fills. *Taunting/Spitting on passive NPCs angers them. If you have at least 55 Charisma, though, they will instead thank you for spitting on them. *The most flat amount of posture with bonuses from shields, equipment, and talents as of 2/21/2025 is '''70''' *Some people refer to Ragdoll Cancelling as a Tech/Teching, a reference to a common mechanic in Fighting Games where if you input block/parry right before hitting a surface whilst being launched, your movement will be cancelled, you'll leave hitstun, and you'll be able to act again almost immediately. title: Combat Tag
content:
==Description==
Combat Tag (also known as In Combat or In Danger, commonly abbreviated to Ctag), is the state a player enters upon getting hit by or interacting with an attack from any [[Enemies|enemy]], [[Monsters|monster]], [[Bosses|boss]], player, or other hazard. This includes dodging, parrying and blocking.

''(Note: Allies through [[Vow of Mastery]], [[Vow of Allegiance]], [[Guilds|guildmates]], or being friends on Roblox do not proc combat tag if they hit you.)''

Its main purpose is to punish rage-quitting and leaving during combat.

===Indicated by===
*The light blueish purple/orange/red skull is visible at the top of the screen.
*Combat music of the [[Locations|Location]] you're in will start playing.

===Consequences of entering combat===
*The damage modifier soft cap is reduced from +50% damage to +25%.
*Your natural health Regeneration is reduced, as well as healing from [[Campfire]]s.
*Some [[Talents]] activate upon inflicting a Combat Tag or by being inflicted with one.
**Example: {{t|Ready Or Not}} will cut the damage from the first hit you take outside of combat in half.
*You cannot [[Stealth|assassinate]] enemies without the {{t|Dustlunge}} Talent.
*You cannot switch weapons or equipment (unless you're a [[Silentheart]]).
*Certain NPCs will have unique dialogue, often disallowing their services.
*You cannot use certain items like [[Idol of Yun'Shul]]s.
*You cannot use the [[Chime of Dwelling]] or enter [[Guild Bases]].
*You cannot use the [[Beast Whistle]].

Hovering over the skull will show you the name of the entity that put you into combat tag or prolonged it, and the amount of time you will remain tagged for. When in PvP, it will also show the number of players that you're currently in combat with next to it.

==Combat Tags==
Being tagged by enemies, monsters, bosses, and anything else (PvE) differs from being tagged by players (PvP).
An icon displaying two swords will appear to the left of your combat tag if you've combat tagged an enemy. Right clicking this will allow you to remove the combat tag from players.
<gallery widths="125" position="center" bordersize="none">
File:Combat Tagged.png|<center>Combat tagged an enemy
File:Combat Tag PvE.png|<center>PvE combat tag
File:Combat Tag Boss.png|<center>Boss combat tag
File:Combat Tag PvP.png|<center>PvP combat tag
</gallery>

===PvE: Blue Skull===
The blue skull means you're in PvE combat tag. This combat tag will last 30 seconds, or until all the mobs that caused you harm are killed. If you get hit by a player or a boss while you are in PvE combat or vice versa, your PvE tag will be overwritten by the player or boss tag. Self-applied and environmental combat tags are considered PvE combat tags.

This comes with limitations:
*If you leave the game or disconnect during this while below 60% health, the game will treat it as death, even sending you to the depths or wiping you if you are already in them.
**The 60% health threshold does not apply to [[Vow of Iron]] and certain enemies like [[Aska]]. Instead, you die immediately when you disconnect.

====PvE: Orange Skull====
The orange skull means you've been combat tagged by a boss. This combat tag will last 3 minutes, or until the boss that caused you harm has been killed. This combat tag is prioritized over all other combat tags. This has all of the same limitations as the regular PvE combat tag.

===PvP: Red Skull===
The red skull means that you are currently being assaulted by a player and lasts 1 minute and 20 seconds. Turning on "No Holds Barred" in settings will make it so that attacking your allies will put them in danger. If you get hit by non-boss NPC while you are in PvP combat or vice versa, your PvP tag will overwrite the PvE one. Next to the PvP combat tag, there will be a number listing the amount of players who have combat tagged you. Hovering over this number will display the in-game names of said players.

This comes with limitations:
*If you leave the game or disconnect at all, you will die regardless of your HP.
*You will no longer be healed by knocking NPCs or killing monsters, only by knocking players.
*The damage modifier hard cap is reduced from +75% damage to +50%.
*If you are above Power 16, the void threshold (% of HP you must be over for falling into the void in the [[First Layer]] resulting in you being sent to the [[Second Layer]] instead of wiping) will be increased. This scales on your level, being 75% of your maximum HP at Power 20.
**Each additional combat tag you gain will reduce the threshold by 5%, down to a minimum of 40% health at 8 combat tags.

You can remove Combat Tag from players you've combat tagged by saying "mb [First Name]" or "sorry [First Name]". Alternatively, you can say "all" instead of the player's name to remove your combat tag from all players. This can also be done by right clicking the swords icon to the left of the combat tag and clicking on the player's name or "all combat tags".

==Combat Quotes==
When the skull at the top appears, there is a quote under it that varies depending on your state and [[Locations|Location]].

List of Quotes:

#"The Depths coil around your soul like a knot." - Obtained while in [[the Depths]].
#"The Void's influence draws you ever closer to the Depths." - Obtained while in a [[Voidzones|Voidzone]].
#"Your heart beats faster as the end draws near." - Obtained while your health bar is stained.
#"Adrenaline surges into your veins as tensions thicken." - Obtained while your health bar is not stained.
#"You feel a heavy weight on your body; one hit is all it takes to collapse." - Obtained if you have the [[Glass Bones]] Echo Modifier.

==Trivia==
*There are 3 exceptions to being punished for leaving while combat tagged:
*#Server shutdown for hotfix or weekly updates.
*#Being teleported by a Dungeon teleporter ''(Example: [[The Ferryman]]'s summoning ring, [[Light Hook]] teleport)''
*#Jumping into the void in the [[First Layer]] while above the void threshold.
*You can still swap weapons in combat via abilities that replace your current weapon such as [[Crazy Slots]].
*[[The Lord Regent|Lord Regent]] applies Combat Tag when he uses Judgement against you.
*If you dodge an [[Environmental Hazards|environmental hazard]] or a [[Bloatskipper]] explosion, the name of the attacker will be "'''''God'''''".
*Allies used to be able to tag you normally with a shorter PvP timer, this is no longer the case.

title: Conquest
content:
{{CutContent}}
==Description==
Conquest was an upcoming game mode in which multiple teams take battle against each other in return for end-game exclusive content, as well as a casual mode that you enter with a fresh character like Battle Royale, which boasts no rewards.

The Confirmed Conquest Rewards are:

*[[Bloodsworn Effigy]]

The official Conquest release date is unknown, with Conquest Testing being a couple weeks before the official Conquest release. Conquest Testing would be a public test that would be open for some time that would allow the general community to play a more rough, unfinished version of Conquest to prepare it for the official release, though it is unknown if this is still going to happen.

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="300">
File:Conquestleak.png|UI found in Conquest from an Agamatsu stream.
conquestciity.png|A city found in Conquest.
conquestorb.jpg|A point of interest in Conquest.
Conquestthumbnail-min.png|Conquest-themed thumbnail as seen on the Deepwoken game page, made by #guh0115
ConquestConceptArt.png|Concept Art
Conquest Mobs.png|Mobs that are part of the game mode
</gallery>

== Trivia ==
* Casual Conquest Testing will have no exclusive rewards, and will be "rougher around the edges."
* [[Saintsworn]] was previously thought to be a Conquest reward, but it was confirmed by Dexerius that though it will be coming with Conquest, it wont be one of its rewards.
** However, [[Saintsworn]] was added before Conquest due to its delay.
* The Deepwoken Twitter account has leaked one of the core points of the game mode, which is a statue in similar fashion to a previously leaked statue a few months earlier, boasting a health bar and shooting fireballs.<ref>https://vxtwitter.com/Deepwoken/status/1745887869334430022</ref>
* Conquest was planned to be released in December 2023, but had to be delayed to January 2024 due to some map changes, and has now been further delayed to release at an unknown date.
* [[Jack]]'s appearance will be a live event during Conquest, as stated by Arch_Mage.
* According to the twitter post showing map sneaks, there is no smooth terrain on the Conquest map, but as seen in other images, there might still be.
* [[Inquisitor's Duster]], similarly to [[Saintsworn]], was planned to be released with Conquest, but was released with [[World Events]] instead.

title: Constellia
content:
{{cnp}}
== Description ==
The city of Constellia, once a gleaming City of Light, and the biggest of the Celestial Cities<ref name="Glossary">{{Ref/Glossary|Constellia}}</ref>, gifted to the [[Lightborn]] by the [[Celestial]]s as a last gift. Shortly after, the [[Celestial]]s abandoned the city to never return. The [[Surface]] folk referred to the city as "The Guiding Star" and used it to traverse [[Locations#Lumen|Lumen]].<ref name="Kaide">{{Ref/NPC|Kaide, the Drowned Light}}</ref>

Constellia was guarded by [[Stone Knight]]s created by the [[Celestial]]s, which appeared in [[Locations#Lumen|Lumen]] by falling from  [[Glossary#The Nightsea|The Nightsea]] in radiant meteors.

After the [[Celestial]]s fled the city, it was invaded by the [[Kyrsgarde|Kyrsans]] under [[Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron]]'s will, who destroyed the city and captured [[Kaide, the Drowned Light]], the last king of Constellia.<ref name="Kaide" />

==Notable Figures==
[[Spellhardt family]]: A noble and wealthy family, currently residing in [[The Floating Keep]]. Their keep was well-manned and the family had a lot of servants before the fall of Constellia, but afterwards it was left to be managed by the family itself. Every year they host a tradition, called [[Hallowtide]].

[[Kaide, the Drowned Light]]: The last king of Constellia, currently held captive by the [[Kyrsgarde]] in [[Second Layer/New Kyrsa|New Kyrsa, the Sleeping City]]. Provides lore on the [[Lightborn]] and the Fall of Constellia.

==Trivia==
*Currently, the only named Celestial City in [[The Heavens]].

The {{cl|alloyed|Broodalloy Cestus}} displays a telegraph alongside a sound effect. Coral Cestus' critical has a cooldown of '''6 seconds'''. Broodalloy Cestus' critical has a cooldown of '''9 seconds.''' ==Gallery== File:Coral Cestus Fist.png File:Coral Cestus Texture.png File:003 is releasing like july btw.png|Critical ===Enchantments=== File:Astral Coral Cestus.png|Astral File:Blazing Coral Cestus.png|Blazing File:Coral Cestus Chilling.png|Chilling File:Curse of NLK coral cestus.png|Curse of the No Life King File:Curse of Yun'Shul.png|Curse of Yun'Shul File:Deferred Coral Cestus.png|Deferred File:Detonation Coral Cestus.png|Detonation File:Elastic Coral Cestus.png|Elastic File:Coral Cestus Heroism.png|Heroism File:Coral Cestus Metal.png|Metal File:Grim Coralcestus.png|Grim File:Obfuscation Coral Cestus.png|Obfuscation File:Providence Thorns Coral Cestus.png|Providence's Thorns File:Sear Coral Cestus.png|Sear File:Solar Coral Cestus.png|Solar File:Storm Coral Cestus.png|Storm File:Stormbreaker Coral Cestus.png|Stormbreaker File:Umbral Knight Coral Cestus.png|Umbral Knight File:Vampirism Coral Cestus.png|Vampirism File:Wild Coral Cestus.png|Wild ==Trivia== *Coral Cestus originally had higher stats and a light weapon requirement of 75, but the stats and requirements were reduced when it received an alloyed variant. *The critical is based off of the Mudskipper Brute/Broodlord's smash attacks. *The critical did not work with Legion Kata on release, making the special critical exclusive to Way of Navae. This was fixed soon after the weapon was added. *Each gauntlet has a colored gradient under the "coral" texture. *The upper front of the fist resembles a brass knuckle, or a knuckle duster. *Coral Cestus is the only weapon to have an altered critical when alloyed. *Currently the only Cestus that can be alloyed. *The [[Fang and Coil]] running critical from [[Jade Vigil's Weave]] cannot be used on the Coral or Broodalloy Cestus. *The Talent Mudskipper Gripper could be a reference to ''Deepwoken'' content creator [https://www.youtube.com/@SkiperGripper Skipper Gripper]. *The Talent Mudskipper Gripper cannot proc from [[Thundercall|Lightning Clones]]. {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Criticals]] [[Category:Alloyable Weapons]] [[Category:Fists]] [[Category:Light Weapons]] [[Category:Weapons with Talents]]

==Description==
[[Council of the Moonlit Faith]] / [[Council of the Moonlit Faith|The Counsell]]<ref name="Glossary" /> is the highest form of government in the [[Lullaby Isles]]. They ensure all operations within the [[Lullaby Isles]] run smoothly. They work directly under [[the Lady Confessor]] and put all her decrees into action.<ref name="Glossary" /><ref name="Missives" />

The Council consists of a handful of philosophical, theological, and academic members of the [[Lullaby Isles]].<ref name="Glossary" /> All members of the Council are very religious and are apart of [[The Moonlit Faith]].<ref name="Missives" />

==Notable members==
[[The Lady Confessor]]: The mysterious leader of the [[Lullaby Isles]], where her word is law. Not much is known externally of her location, or condition, but interactions with scholars visiting the [[Luminants#Etrean and Eastern Luminants|East]] suggest a sense of great reverence and sincerity towards her decrees.<ref name="Glossary1">{{Ref/Glossary|The Lady Confessor}}</ref>

The Acolyte / [[Thal'assis Linnaes]]: The current Acolyte of the [[Lullaby Isles]]. A lead ambassador, leading groups of scholars to and from the [[Greathive Aratel]] in order to exchange knowledge, updates and information.<ref name="Missives" /><ref name="Glossary2">{{Ref/Glossary|The Acolyte / Thalassis}}</ref>

The Acolyte / [[Galvika]]: One of the previous Acolytes of the [[Lullaby Isles]].<ref name="Missives">[[Strange Missives]]</ref>

{{Monster Infobox |attacks=Double Strike |health=*150 *375 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |drops=[[Crustacean Meat]] |locations=[[The Diluvian Mechanism]] |image1=Crab.png }} ==Description== Crabs are a Monster that only appear in [[The Diluvian Mechanism]] and as a [[Bounty]] in [[Vow of Iron]]. They are small greenish - brown crabs, barely above knee height, with seven light green eyes and slit pupils. ==Moveset== Crabs only have one attack, listed below: {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Double Strike'''
(★☆☆) |The Crab will lift both of its claws in the air, striking you with its first claw and then quickly following up with the second. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |} ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Consume |Tears the victim apart with its claws, feasting upon them. |} ==Trivia== *Possibly the precursor to the [[Crustaceous Rex]] as its Double Strike attack resembles the Crustaceous Rex's Rising Smash attack. *Formerly cut content; they spawned on both the Surface and the Depths. Apparently, they were meant to exist as an easy method of getting meat. However, they were never truly deleted from the files, allowing [[The Diluvian Mechanism]] to spawn them in, culminating in their re-addition in the {{VersionHistory|2024|February 2nd}}. **Ironically, they cannot be used for their original purpose, as Crustacean Meat can only be used to cook [[Crab Pizza]], [[Seafood Boil]]s, and [[Seafood Surprise]]s all of which cannot be cooked in the Depths without leaving to the surface. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]]

title: Crafting Station
content:
{{Basic Infobox
|title1=Crafting Station
|image1=CraftingTable.png
|caption1=Crafting Station found in Temple of the Blade}}

== Description ==
Crafting Stations are a utility item that are used to craft more advanced recipes. They are typically found in larger settlements like [[Etris]] or the [[Isle of Vigils]].

Crafting Stations resemble typical tables with a large open space in the center.

== Usage ==
Crafting Stations can be used to build more complex items that can't be built in your hands.

To use the Crafting Station, you must click {{Input|keybind|interact}} within a certain proximity of it, causing you to bend over and it and start looking around, and use the crafting section in your inventory. To see recipes that the Crafting Station can be used for, see [[Crafting Recipes]].

You can avoid using the crafting station with the Talent "Master Craftsman", making it easier for you to craft without having to go to Etris or the Isle of Vigils.

A few items you build here must be learned with a Schematic.

== Locations ==

=== [[Etris]] ===

* Outside of the Fish Shop at [[Etris Docks]].
* Within the General Store.
* Within the [[Blacksmith]].

=== [[Isle of Vigils]] ===

* Inside the Inn.
* At the house with the [[Barber]].
* Nearby the [[Blacksmith]] at the [[Temple of the Blade]].

=== [[Guild Bases|Guild base]] ===

* Inside the Quarters roomo.

=== [[Summer Isle]] ===

* At Con's Pawn
* At the Inn.

=== [[Greathive Aratel]] ===

* Next to the [[Blacksmith]] in the Canopy Plaza.

==Trivia==
*Originally, you only had to stand near one to use it.

title: Crazy Slots
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Conjure an arsenal of weapons.|author=Crazy Slots description}}
{{Resonance
|effect=Pulls out a random weapon with a special ability.
|appearance=Summons a weapon from thin air into the user's hand.
|cooldown=2s (Weapon Pull), 15s (Special Move)
|image1 =<gallery>
File:Crazy Slots.gif|Crazy Slots
Crazy slots card.png|Card
Ccslots.png|Corrupt
</gallery>}}
==Description==
'''Crazy Slots''' is a [[Resonance]] that players can obtain and is uncommon to roll.

'''Crazy Slots''' does not have separate variants, but instead pulls out weapons from thin air that are completely unique to this Resonance.
===''Appearance''===
Once used, the user extends their right arm (and left arm if Soulwrought Gun), summoning a weapon from thin air.
== Usage==
Pressing {{Input|keybind|resonance}} will activate the '''Crazy Slots''' Resonance and its unique special skill.

'''Crazy Slots''' calls forth a randomly chosen weapon each time it is used, with [[Enchantments]] and stars being copied from your main weapon onto the summoned weapon. Each weapon scales with its respective stat and has a unique skill that can be used by re-activating the bell.

{{cl|corres|If Crazy Slots is corrupted, its cooldown is halved, rolls are further weighted towards your highest stat investment and the durations of the summons are increased. Additionally, your Soulwrought Weapons will be colored purple instead of gold.}}

===''Resonance Point usage''===
When obtained, Crazy Slots will spend its points on the following stats:

* '''Weapon Weight:''' Increases the likelihood of an individual Soulwrought weapon being summoned relative to its counterparts.
* '''Time:''' Increases the time for which an individual Soulwrought weapon lasts before dematerializing.
** Varies between 30 seconds to 150 seconds, in 15-second intervals (30s, 45s, 60s, 75s, etc.).
** Corrupted rolls may have higher maximum durations (requires more testing)

Crazy Slots will favour its point distribution towards weapons aligned with your highest WEP attribute.
==Weapons ==
These weapons are unique to the '''Crazy Slots''' [[Resonance]]. Notably, they have very high base stats, which helps to alleviate the potential loss of damage from using weapons outside of your main attribute. This also enables them to be viable even for builds which have no weapon investment (e.g. [[Hero Blades]]).

===Soulwrought Weapon Stats===
<center>{{AllCrazySlotsWeapons}}
</center>

==Special Abilities==
Upon reactivating your Resonance while your Crazy Slots weapon is active, perform a special attack. The special attack varies depending on your currently equipped Soulwrought weapon. Using this ends your resonance early, returning you back to your original weapon.

The special abilities deal physical damage and do not have any scaling.
===Soulwrought Dagger===
The user winds up before teleporting to the target with a flurry of Soulwrought slashes. Functions similarly to the "[[Rapid Slashes]]" Mantra. 

* Deals 22.5 damage on the initial slash followed by 2.7 damage over a flurry of slashes.
* Despite the bleed effects, it does not apply {{Cl|Bleed}}.
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazyDagger.gif
</gallery>
===Soulwrought Gun===
The user flips upside down and rapidly shoots at the target six times, finishing with a ranged shot that propels you backwards. 

* Deals 15 damage per shot.
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazySlotsGun.gif
</gallery>
===Soulwrought Longsword===
The user strikes forward with their elbow, followed by a [[Telegraphed Attacks#Red|red telegraph]] leading into three Soulwrought slashes, the final slash ragdolling. Functions similarly to the "[[Dark Blade]]" Mantra. 

* Deals 37.5 damage per hit.
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazySlotsSword.gif
</gallery>
===Soulwrought Spear===
The user rises into the air and fires three Soulwrought spears. Also used by [[Sworn Angel]]s, shooting up to a total of five spears.

* Deals 42 '''typeless damage''' per hit.
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazySlotsSpear.gif
</gallery>

===Soulwrought Greataxe===
The user rises into the air and plummet towards their cursor.

* Deals 75 damage.
* Large hitbox is behind the user; will not deal damage if you land on or in front of the target
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazySlotsAxe.gif
</gallery>
===Soulwrought Greatsword===
The user gains a brief speed boost before leaping into the air and crashing down at theircursor.

* Deals 37.5 damage.
<gallery widths="250px">
CrazySlotsGreat.gif
</gallery>

==Trivia==
*The Soulwrought weapons carry over the Quality Bonus (stars), [[Enchantments]], and if any, Special Effect from your main weapon.
*Soulwrought weapons '''cannot''' use [[Motifs]]
*The exceptionally high base damage for each weapon makes them especially powerful in PvE; it is a tried-and-true choice for M1 builds.
*The designs of the Soulwrought weapons were inspired by weapons from other media:
**The Soulwrought Longsword resembles the ''[https://typemoon.fandom.com/wiki/Excalibur_Proto Excalibur Proto]'' from the [https://typemoon.fandom.com/wiki/Fate_series ''Fate''] series.
**The Soulwrought Spear resembles the ''[https://genshin-impact.fandom.com/wiki/Primordial_Jade_Winged-Spear Primordial Jade Winged-Spear]'' from ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genshin_Impact Genshin Impact]''.
**The Soulwrought Greatsword resembles both the ''[https://typemoon.fandom.com/wiki/Clarent Clarent]'' and the ''[https://typemoon.fandom.com/wiki/Arondight Arondight]'' from the ''Fate'' series.
**The Soulwrought Greataxe seems to be derived from the weapon used by [https://shining.fandom.com/wiki/Lestin_Serra_Alma ''Lestin Serra Alma''] from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shining_Resonance_Refrain ''Shining Resonance Refrain''].
**The Soulwrought Dagger resembles one of Victor Swords from [https://store.steampowered.com/app/2221920/Immortals_Fenyx_Rising/ ''Immortals: Fenyx Rising''].
*This Resonance is inspired by a character from ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_%C3%97_Hunter Hunter x Hunter]'' named ''"Kite"'', whose special ability is to summon a random weapon from a selection of nine. This ability is also called "Crazy Slots".
*This Resonance may also be inspired by the "''Shardblades"'' from ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stormlight_Archive The Stormlight Archive]'', which are powerful summonable weapons that produce white mist when materialized.
*The Soulwrought Gun is one of the only three pistols in the game to play a unique sound on M1/crit, alongside the [[Iron Requiem]] and [[Rosen's Roscoe]].
*The Soulwrought weapons can actually be wielded without the Resonance, though whether or not there is a reason for this has yet to be explained.
**The [[Golden Warrior]]s found in [[Upper Erisia]] and the bouncer outside of the [[Rat's Den]] all wield Soulwrought Greataxes.
**The [[Sworn Angel]]s found in the [[Trial of One]] both wield Soulwrought Spears.
**The [[Immortal Guardians]], and by extension their Nightmare counterparts, in the [[Crypt of the Unbroken]] can wield either a Soulwrought Greatsword or Soulwrought Greataxe.

*The Crescendo may have been used or created by a [[Krulian]] due to it dropping from The Ferryman who is a Krulian along with its ends resembling [[Krulian Knife|Krulian Knives]].

==Description==
On the top left of your screen, next to the Help button, there will be an icon of three people, with an orange-ish background, labeled "Crews." Clicking this will allow you to create a Crew with any player in the server, as long as they do not have an [[Origin]] that [[:Category:Faction Origins|aligns them with a faction]]. *[[First Light]]|health=2800 7000 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |challenges= {{bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}}}} ==Description== The result of a rare case where a [[Megalodaunt]] gets exposed to '''The Vents''', the '''Third Layer''' of [[The Depths]], resulting in this unique species able to utilize [[Flamecharm]]. As their nature suggests, they feature a different, crimson-colored skin tone and the ability to utilize Flamecharm by invoking the Song through its roar, which causes flaming swords to rain down from the sky. Additionally, they are considered outcasts of [[Megalodaunt]] packs, as they will attack other variants on sight. These are the only notable differences that are associated with this unique mutation, but they behave no different than a regular Megalodaunt. They are a significantly rarer sight, and are only found in a few select locations of the [[Locations#East_Luminant|Eastern Luminant]], namely [[Songseeker Wilds]] and the [[Starswept Valley]]. The latter of which they can always be found on one of the bridges between Starswept Valley and [[Bluster Rift]], their only static spawn. They can appear anywhere with the use of a [[Megalodaunt Bait]], but as expected, they are a much rarer sight. {{clear}} ==Attacks== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description !Media |- |
'''Slash'''
(★☆☆) |A short range swipe using their arms. Can slash once or twice, and if once can be paired with '''Kick'''. *Heavy posture damage. Will commonly block break after two hits. *If the Megalodaunt slashes twice, it will take longer to attack again. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Crimson Megalodaunt Slash.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} will wind up its right leg back with a red circle effect before delivering a kick that ragdolls and sends the player flying. *Causes the player to be [[Status Effects#Dazed|Dazed]] if kicked into a wall. *It will take longer to attack again after using this. *Uses '''Bite''' instead if in water. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll.true |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Crimson Megalodaunt Kick.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Thousand Needles'''
(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} bends over and points its coral tubes towards an opponent, spewing a large and constant spray of coral shards at anyone in front of/around it for a second. *Lasts as long as auto-parry frames, meaning you can simply parry once to parry the whole attack. *There is a shorter-ranged AoE version and a longer-ranged single-target version. Both function the same. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y |type3_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Crimson Megalodaunt Thousand Needles.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Roar'''
(★★☆) |Lets out a roar at nearby targets, inflicting [[Insanity]] and [[Status Effects#Fear|Fear]]. *Usually used as the {{PAGENAME}}'s first move. *Blocking negates much of but not all the Insanity gain. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, debuff |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:CrimsonSharkoRoar.gif|centre|thumb|252x252px]] |- |

(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} turns invisible, with a white ring signifying where they are. After a moment, it turns visible again and appears over its target, grabs it, holds it up, and chews it down, before throwing it away and ragdolling it. *If its target is mid-air after it turns invisible, it will instead use '''Tacet Drop Kick'''. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, autogrip, teleport, grab, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Crimson Megalodaunt Tacet Hug.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Tacet Drop Kick'''
(★☆☆) |Starts out similarly to '''Tacet Hug''', but after it turns visible again, it will throw out its entire body in a drop kick, flinging and ragdolling targets hit. *Cannot be used on its own, and is only used as a variant for '''Tacet Hug'''. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, teleport, ragdoll }} |[[File:Crimson Drop Kick.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Pyroclastic Roar'''
(★★☆) |Similar to the standard '''Roar''', but the ring effects are colored orange and it doesn't apply any debuffs. Additionally, flaming swords will begin raining down that inflict Flamecharm damage on hit. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Crimson Megalodaunt Pyroclastic Roar.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Jump'''
(☆☆☆) |If the target is above it, the {{PAGENAME}} will jump in the direction of its opponent to close the distance. Often used after '''Kick'''. {{AttackTags |unharmful, movement }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Bite'''
(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} leans forward and bites down, ragdolling those hit. Only used while in water. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} | [[File:CrimsonSharkoBite.gif|centre|thumb|265x265px]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Thick Hide''' - {{PAGENAME}}s automatically extinguish [[burn]]. *Flamewreathed - Crimson Megalodaunts have approximately 80% flamecharm resistance ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Curb Stomp |The Megalodaunt ends its opponent's life by delivering a stomp onto their bodies with a gruesome crunch. This happens in less than a second. This attack has an AOE effect which can be parried similar to the [[Rock Golem]]'s stomp. |} ==Tips== The same knowledge you learned from the base [[Megalodaunt]] can be applied to the {{PAGENAME}}. ==Description==
The '''Crypt Blade''' is a Legendary [[Greatsword]] [[weapon]]; a stocky bull-necked hilt giving rise to an ominous blade serving as the crypt and final resting place of a previous generation, hence its name. The weapon itself is wreathed in waning shadow, and is made of a large and long forthright blade that is adorned in sharp symmetry and pallid patterns. The Crypt Blade scales off [[Shadowcast]] alongside [[Attributes|Heavy Weapons]]. 

The Crypt Blade comes with 2 passive abilities:

#'''Last Dead's Boon''' - M1 attacks drain 22.5 Ether from the target on hit.
#'''Shadow Affinity''' - Non-Mantra specific Shadowcast Talents proc on your basic attacks (e.g if the user has {{t|Sightless Still}}, their basic attacks will apply {{status|Obscured}}). This includes [[Talents#Wraith Path: Twisted Puppets|Twisted Puppets']] {{status|Shadow Burn}} status effect.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:Crypt Blade Critical.gif|Standing Critical
File:CryptChainBreak.gif|Chain breaking
File:CryptChainDrag.gif|Chain dragging
File:CryptRunning.gif|Running Critical
</gallery>
The Crypt Blade has two criticals.

For the standing critical, the user plunges the greatsword into the ground, releasing a eruption of darkness, inflicting Shadow and chaining everyone within it. This additionally drains 45 Ether from the target on hit, an additional 10 Ether when the chain breaks. The plunge attack deals '''0.8x scaled damage'''. The attack is avoidable by jumping.

If the user hits a chained target, the chain will break and the target receives three consecutive ticks of damage and Ether steal. This effect is applied when the target's chest is engulfed in shadow. Blocking and parrying will not cancel out this effect. If the target attempts to go beyond the length of the chain, they will be dragged back to center.

For the running critical, the user swiftly tears into the target two times before flashing with a red telegraph, unleashing a slashing cleave through them. The final slash ragdolls and dazes the target, and the first slash must be landed in order to progress through the other slashes.

Both criticals have a cooldown of '''10 seconds'''.

{{text|m1leg}}

==Trivia== 
*The original model for the Crypt Blade was a [[Darksteel Greatsword]] but slightly recolored and with black particles coming out of the blade. The weapon also used the same description as the Darksteel Greatsword.
*It used to be unobtainable, however, the update that introduced [[Chime of Conflict]] also [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YrCzjvKI6AI brought back the Crypt Blade].
*The original updated Crypt Blade contained 30k vertices. Following the 3/27/2023 update, this was reduced to a mere 2.5k vertices.
*The original Crypt Blade was able to proc Singularity and Fear on hit, essentially stunning the enemy in place on each hit, thankfully, this has since been removed.
*The YouTuber Nanoprodigy was the first to showcase the Crypt Blade in his video, where the title referenced it as the "[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x4Euw0kCQVs Shadow Greatsword]"
*During the original addition of this weapon before it's temporary removal, the scaling used to be unreasonably high at 20 SHW scaling and also had 0.7 swing speed (In Legacy swingspeed, translated to current swingspeed it would be around 0.93), without endlag.
*Despite being named '''Crypt''' Blade, it cannot be found at the [[Crypt of the Unbroken]]. The "Crypt" is likely metaphorical, representing how it's made from corpses.
*The first person to wield a Crypt Blade was the user Flashbacking during closed access.

title: Crypt of the Unbroken
content:
{{Location|name=Crypt of the Unbroken|area=Voidzone|caption=The dimly lit halls echo with voices of those who once walked.}}
[[File:Crypt or idk.png|thumb|900px|center]]

The '''Crypt of the Unbroken''' is a location in ''Deepwoken''. It is a [[Voidzones|Voidzone]] found at the top of [[Minityrsa]]. 

==Overview==
The Crypt of the Unbroken is a building in the highest part of [[Minityrsa]]. The inside is filled with tall, narrow intersecting halls inhabited by hostile enemies. Braziers are sparsely placed in the stone halls, and various humanoid statues are around the Crypt. 
==Points of Interest==

* On the 1st floor, there is a massive, library-like room with an Alpha Megalodaunt and four [[Immortal Guardian]]s in it.
* On the 2nd floor, the [[Deep Shrines|Shrine of Temptation]] can be found. For 5 knowledge, you may exchange one of your mantras for a hand of whispers.
** An opening in the wall will lead to the [[Glacial Remnant]] with the [[Frostdraw Obelisk]] inside, required for the [[Saintsworn#Obtainment|Saintsworn]] obtainment.
* The [[Gran Sudaruska]] can be found in the chests dropped by the [[Immortal Guardian]]s on the 1st floor. This is a very grindy way to obtain the weapon, but it is safer compared to [[Second Layer|Layer 2]] which most people are scared of. This is also why people can be found here so often.
**Farming [[Immortal Guardian]]s is also the only way to get the [[Immortal Helm]], which is one of the reasons why people choose to go here.

*Hellfire Lotuses and Skyvalor Lotuses can be found around the Crypt. Crafting 2 Hellfire Lotuses or 2 Skyvalor Lotuses together at a crafting table will yield a Strength attribute flask or a Willpower attribute flask respectively.
*There are 3 black flowers with the roman numeral 1 on top of the Crypt. They serve as a tribute to a player who passed away.

CryptStorage.png|A mysterious room that appears to serve as storage
</gallery>
==Maps==
A map can be found at [[Maps#Surface]]

==Trivia==
*The music for this area is [[Of Labours, Veiled]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]]
*The majority of images and information are taken from Xaslin's video (https://youtu.be/NkEiMJmvimU).
*[[Immortal Guardian]]s use the Divine Axe and Divine Greatsword from the [[Crazy Slots]] resonance, but they can't use the special abilities 
*Gripping an enemy will aggro a massive amount of the enemies in the dungeon nearby, even on the floor above, so if you can't autogrip or burn them, take enemies outside of the Crypt to grip them safely. (This still tends to aggro [[Carbuncle]]s, but they are a minor threat.)
* Good place to farm books, the library has tons of bookshelves.
*Characters with the Mute [[Regalias|Regalia]] are instead spared and insulted when knocked by [[Immortal Guardian]]s, similar to various town guards.
*If you are inexperienced with farming this dungeon, you can simply lure the [[Immortal Guardian]]s out of the dungeon to avoid going to The Depths because it is a Voidzone.
*Please note that the crypt entrance can be blocked and it cannot be broken, it will open after the server time has reached 15 minutes.
**If you however want to access the blocked entrance follow these steps:
**#Get two heavy weapons in your hotbar (unequipped)
**#Sprint to the entrance
**#Swap between the two heavy weapons, but don't equip
**#While you sprint and swap weapons, just wait and you should've glitched through the wall
**As of April 19th, the crypt entrance is open in all of Vow of Iron servers.
*Tip: With the assassin Talent (30 Agility or the [[Assassin's Hood]]), you can one shot the Guardians with an assassination, which makes the grind way easier.
**If they aggro on you go outside the dungeon and wait for them to de-aggro.
**Tacet and/or the Mute Regalia are extremely useful for assassination.
* The Crypt of the Unbroken may be the resting place of [[Gran Sudaruska|Sudaruska]], as her epithet was "the Unbroken," not to mention the fact that Gran Sudaruska can drop in the Crypt.
* You should always check your blood and food bars, because NPC's in Crypt of Unbroken will drain your blood very fast.
*[[Immortal Guardian]]s in the upper floor don’t give chests when they are gripped, making farming them less efficient as the ones downstairs as chests give a lot of exp.
*[[Immortal Guardian]]s are able to spawn on top of Crypt of the Unbroken, it can happen by de-aggroing the enemy or by natural causes.
*In the Vow of Iron gamemode, it's called The Crypt of the Forgotten.

title: Curse of Captain Greene
content:
{{Relic
|image=<gallery>
Enchant Curse of Captain Greene.gif|Enchantment
Curse of Captain Greene Enchant Stone.png|Enchant Stone
</gallery>
|desc=Known throughout the [[Summer Company]], many heard of the famous treasurer [[Captain Greene|Captrain Greene]]{{sic}}. You inherit his strange ability of gaining damage the more rich you are. However since you aren't Captain Greene himself, you lose notes whenever you get hit. A strange curse indeed...
|obtainment=
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' [[Enchant Stone]]:
*Trading an [[Exotic Hide]] to [[The Gaunt Man]]
|droppable=No
|pass down=Yes
}}

==Description==
{{PAGENAME}} is a damage buffing [[enchantment]] that increases your weapon's damage based on how many [[Notes]] you have.

==Effect==
{{PAGENAME}} increases your weapon's '''base''' damage by 0.001% for every {{c|notes|[[Notes|Note]]}} you have above {{c|notes|7,500}}. This caps at +7.5% base damage at {{c|notes|15,000}}. Because this increases your base damage, it is '''not''' affected by the damage multiplier caps and instead increases the effectiveness of them.

Upon landing a weapon attack, your opponent will lose {{c|notes|50}}.

==={{cl|lired|Curse}}===
If you are below {{c|notes|7,500}}, your weapon's base damage will be reduced by 0.001% for every Note you have below this threshold instead. This caps at -7.5% base damage at {{c|notes|0}}. Because this decreases your base damage, damage multipliers will be less effective.

Upon taking damage from a player, lose {{c|notes|100}}.

===Notes===
*'''If you have not completed [[The Gaunt Man]]'s trial on your character, this enchantment will not work, and your weapon's damage will be voided.'''
*While at {{c|notes|7,500}}, this Enchantment does not provide a damage buff nor debuff.
*This enchantment has a coin splash sound effect on hit and upon taking damage.
*This enchantment's curse functions somewhat similarly to, and stacks with, the [[Loose Change]] Echo Modifier.

==Trivia==
*This enchantment was originally a Developer Spec before it was made publicly accessible during the {{VersionHistory|2026|February 16th}}, as a part of Operation: Deep Healing.

content:
{{Relic
