title: First Layer
content:
[[File:Celtor Wastes.png|center|900px]] ==Overview== The '''First Layer''' of [[The Depths]], also known as '''Scyphozia,''' is the first of nine layers of The Depths, embodied with the long-lost sunken civilization of Celtor. Players are sent here after [[Death|dying]] while having a stained health bar, being sucked in by a Whirlpool, dying with the [[Hollow]] Echo Modifier, or dying in a [[Voidzones|Voidzone]] / the [[Voidsea]]. ==Points of Interest== *[[The City of the Drowned]] **Important NPCs: ***[[Nostor, Master of Shadow]] **[[Varicosa District]] **[[The Military District]] **[[District of Commerce]] **[[Cathedral of the Interstice]] ***Important NPCs: ****[[Shrine of Courage]] *[[Temple of Hearts]] **Important NPCs: ***All [[Deep Shrines]] ***[[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts]] *[[Castle Light]] **[[Light's Causeway]] **Important NPCs: ***Various town-NPCs [[Banker]], [[Antiquarian]], [[Blacksmith]], etc. accessible only to [[Deepbound]]s ***[[Klaris Llfiend, Mother of Lights]] *[[The Chariot's Spire]] **Important NPCs: ***Various town-NPCs [[Banker]], [[Antiquarian]], [[Blacksmith]], etc. accessible only to [[Ignition Delver]]s ***[[Hollow Forge]], accessible only to [[Ignition Delver]]s *[[The Forest of Lights]] **[[Marauder's Entrance]] ***[[The Diluvian Mechanism]] *[[Celtor Wastes]] **[[Brinepool Passage]] ***[[The Cold Forge]] **Important NPCs: ***[[The Gaunt Man]] ==Escaping First Layer== [[File:Depths map test3 two.png|thumb|300px|Outdated, detailed map of Scyphozia]] There are 2 ways of escaping the First Layer: *The first is through the [[Depths Trial]], a challenge where the player is faced with a [[Monsters|Monster]] befitting their [[Power]]. *The second is through a [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts#Wishes|Wish]], only granted once specific conditions are fulfilled. ===Depths Trial=== ''Main Page: [[Cathedral of the Interstice]], [[Depths Trial]]''
The main and preferred method to escape is by the [[Depths Trial]] through the [[Cathedral of the Interstice]] in the center of [[The City of the Drowned]]. You normally enter through one of the 2 gates present on the West and East sides of the city in the middle, and then go up the elevator to fight your trial. The trial itself changes its difficulty depending on various factors relative to the player. See the [[Depths Trial]] page for more specific information. ===Wishing to Yun'Shul=== '''This method can only be done once per character'''. This alternative method is limited to players with a [[Resonance]] and an eligible [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts#Wishes|Wish]] or an [[Idol of Yun'Shul]]. Talk to [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Yun'Shul]] and select the wish "'''The trials ahead of me fill me with trepidation, I wish to escape this place.'''" This method skips the trial altogether, but will only work in the [[First Layer]]. You can also achieve this with the use of an [[Idol of Yun'Shul]] relic by selecting the wish "'''Release me from the depths'''", which does not require a [[Resonance]] nor a [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts#Wishes|Wish]] from [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts#Wishes|Yun'Shul]]. Wishing to escape the Depths can only be done once per method, per character. For example, if you've already escaped the Depths by using an [[Idol of Yun'Shul]], then you will only be able to wish your way out again if you speak to the [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Shrine of Yun'Shul]] itself, and once both options have been exhausted, you will need to escape through the [[Cathedral of the Interstice]]. ==The Void== The void is an ever-present hazard in the First Layer, being large sections of the map that have been cut away to reveal an endless pit. Falling into the Void will mean '''instant death''', and your character '''wiping''', unless your current health is above the 'Void Threshold'. The Void Threshold is a percentage of your maximum health, showcased as a corroded section on your healthbar. As long as your current health is above this threshold, then jumping into the Void will send you to the [[Second Layer]] instead of wiping you. The Void Threshold is affected by many variables: #If you are below Power 3, your Void Threshold will be 0% of your maximum health. This means you will be sent to Layer 2 at any health. This is not affected by PvP or PvE combat. #If you are not in combat, are in PvE combat, or are in PvP combat while being '''below''' Power 16, your Void Threshold will be 50% of your maximum health #If you are in PvP combat while being Power 16 or higher, your Void Threshold will be increased, scaling on your level. This caps at a maximum of 75% of your maximum health at Power 20. #Your Void Threshold will be reduced by 5% for every player Combat Tag you have, capping at a minimum threshold of 40% of your maximum health. File:Void Threshold.png|Void Threshold outside of combat ==Farming in First Layer== Scyphozia, being a naturally hostile location, is intentionally difficult to survive in, from perpetual monster spawnage to the fast and easy to forget sanity loss. However, the benefits of EXP Gain and loot drops can far outweigh the dangers for players who are willing to risk wiping in seconds. Listed below are some things you may want to consider before heading down. These things will aid in your sustained survival in one of the most treacherous areas in Deepwoken. ===Talents & Equipment=== *'''''{{t|Carnivore}}''''', the Talent that makes up part of the '''Apex Predator''' Talent tree, is important if you plan to stay in The Depths in the long term. It removes the ability to consume plants (mutual exclusive with [[Vegetarian]] flaw), but in exchange, gripping Players, NPCs, '''AND''' monsters will replenish your HP, Hunger, and Thirst meters. With most food in the Depths being poisonous, the steady supply of [[Gigamed|Gigameds (electric jellyfish)]] are more than enough to keep you satiated. Requires '''5 Willpower''' and '''5 Strength'''. *'''''{{t|Conquer Your Fears}}''''', a Talent that makes up part of the '''Mental Fortress''' Talent tree, is a good way to combat the slow drain of Sanity that being within purgatory imposes. Though all Talents in the '''Mental Fortress''' Talent tree are beneficial inside The Depths, '''Conquer Your Fears''' is a surefire guarantee as, like '''Carnivore''', it replenishes your Sanity upon killing monsters of the Deep. Requires '''10 Willpower'''. *'''''{{t|Underdog}}''''' allows more damage to larger foes and opponents with higher health than you. Almost every Depths mob, especially since the second part of this Talent will almost always be active in PvE. Requires '''40 Willpower.''' *'''''[[Megalodaunt Coat]]''''' and '''''[[Pathfinder Elite]]''''', these are the only two equipment items with the Damage Vs. Monsters stat, increasing your damage dealt to all [[Monsters]]. *'''''[[Diver's Ring]]''''', this ring increases your damage dealt to Monsters in the Depths by 5%. ===Tips and Tricks=== Information to keep in mind. *'''''[[Insanity]]''''' will be your artificial timer for how long you can stay in Layer One. You start with 80 max sanity, and every point allows 30 more seconds before losing it. You can last approximately 40 minutes before your character gains maximum insanity. Although impossible to die to natural insanity in the depths, insanity can severely affect your combat abilities and having max insanity will make you '''die instantly when downed or below 10% health.''' Willpower, Talents, and equipment grant extra sanity. **Consider utilizing Flamecharm to cast Graceful Flame with Undying Flame. The Talent removes any risk of going insane in the First Layer as sitting by a campfire restores sanity. **[[Blindseer]] doubles or even triples the time you can stay in the Depths. **[[Deepbound]] players can rest in [[Castle Light]] at the campfire to restore sanity and craft food. Do note that only Deepbound players can use the campfire. **[[Ignition Delver]]s may use the campfire in [[The Chariot's Spire]], much like Deepbound. *'''''Corrupted Monsters''''' are the juiciest part of Depths Farming. Identified by the purple haze/mist surrounding them, these mobs act like their regular counterparts but have 2.5x HP and 1.5x damage. These grant [[Chests]] with even better loot. *On opposite corners of the map, two '''''Black Bells''''' can be found. They increase the odds of Corrupted Monsters appearing. [Citation needed] *The inability to create campfires means that healing methods are limited. Besides killing monsters, especially jellyfish, commonly nicknamed "Health Packs" (unless you engaged combat with a player), and Graceful Flame (with the Talent Undying Flame), you might want to consider bringing '''''healing potions'''''. *'''''Heartening Salves''''' are also a great idea to bring because of their special ability to get rid of insanity. They are a part of '''[[Alchemy]]''' and cost three Bluecaps to make the maximum effective version of the potion. *'''''Warrior's Respite''''' is an extremely useful Talent in The Depths, allowing you to heal without special abilities. Another good card is '''''Conditioned Runner''''', which allows you to heal while running. *'''[[Mute]]''' will be your best friend if you desire to farm in the Depths. However, due to being a [[Regalias|Regalia]], your character can only be born with it under certain conditions that are still unknown. The reason why Animal King will be very helpful in the Depths is because most, if not, '''all''' monsters in the Depths will be Neutral to you on sight. This will make farming mobs a lot easier, as they will also lose aggro to you if you do not attack them after 15 seconds, similar to guards in Etris or Isle of Vigils. Thanks to this, The Depths may be your best friend when you are in a pinch such as if you are attacked by a group of high levels, any group of mobs can aid your escape. Keep in mind that hitting a monster even once '''will''' make them attack you. *If you have the Deepbound origin, remember to regularly visit [[Castle Light]], as it will rapidly restore your sanity. *Seaweed is currently the only natural source of food for vegetarians in the Depths, although it will drain a sliver of your thirst. ==Quests== ===Finding Morning=== *An NPC named Raphael asks to find someone on the surface world named "Morning" and tell them that the preparations are almost complete. When questioned more about how to find "Morning", he replies with "How is a 150–200-year-old dead person supposed to remember what someone alive looks like?". **(As of now the quest is not done, which was started by Arch_Mage. Morning doesn't exist in-game at the moment and will stay so until the quest is finished by developers.) ===[[Oath: Visionshaper]]=== Deep southeast in the Depths, you can find a secret room located near the [[Deep Widow]]. Here, there is a 'man' named [[Surge]] who can teach you illusion magic (the Visionshaper Oath) in exchange for Void Feathers. Once you have spoken with [[Surge]], [[The Nestmind]] - a being that exists within a deeper layer of The Depths - will open their realm to you. It offers scraps of knowledge on about the [[Deep Owl]] and the Depths. *Void Feathers drop from corrupted [[Deep Owl]]s in The Depths, although they can also rarely drop from the normal variants as well. *This quest is '''very''' tedious and dangerous, so it is recommended you come with a group or to otherwise be prepared. ==Potential Enemies== {{EnemyGallery |File:MudskipperIcon.png|Mudskipper |- |} ==Tips from Experienced Depths Divers== *Adaptation to The Depths is '''mandatory and inevitable''' in Deepwoken. If misfortune on the surface proves unavoidable, then your ability to strive in The Depths has to be sufficient. Learning the ways of vanquishing each and every of the Depths' monsters, learning the layout of the terrain in general, learning how and when to avoid unwinnable conflicts, succeeding in the Trials 100% of the time and more are part of your adaptation to the Depths. It is one of the most important parts of Deepwoken and can be extremely rewarding so long as you can deal with the risks involved. *'''FIGHT OR FLIGHT? That is the question''' and most of the time, the answer is flight. Do not over-estimate yourself or under-estimate the mobs that spawn in the depths. Mobs spawn very often and very widespread down in the Depths, so don't be surprised if you're fighting one mob and another one spawns nearby. All of these mobs are passive towards each other and have a common target - you. (A preferred way to escape monsters is by learning how to scale walls, and eventually when you get more comfortable, run off a cliff while they follow you, and then climb up when they jump off with you: effectively dropping them off a cliff while keeping yourself alive) *The [[Trial of One]] provides an effective guide to some of the monsters that permeate the depths (the Megalodaunt, Thresher, and the Enforcer), increasing your survival rate once you can conquer them. *If you see a group of high-level people, log to the main menu using the leave button in deepwoken (turn off leave game prompt) Your chances of not combat logging are better than your chances of not getting gripped in The Depths. There is also certain quests such as obtaining [[Contractor]] that require the player to grip people in The Depths, which gives them an incentive to ambush what may seem like jaywalking freshies. *The same goes if there many people of the same guild flooding the server. It's not worth risking your chances to be caught in the crossfire of a depths gank, or a depths cleanse (killing anything that moves in the depths). **Certain guilds are known for purposefully wiping players in the depths, such as the '''Axius, Sirno Club, Anguish, Akers, Sakura, Akai, Unnamed, Eznore, Nightcrawlers, Sweeperstop, and Depths Gank Community.''' ***Do note '''this information is mercurial and may quickly become outdated'''. Regardless, it's advised to switch servers if you see a player from these guilds, as they are still (probably) on high alert. *Angels (Spawn due to getting spotted a watcher) are very easily avoidable through scaling buildings and fleeing on high ground. Hiding in the top of buildings until your combat tag goes away can be very easy to do in most situations. Fighting is not a bad alternative however, as they do not have any game breaking moves to destroy you with. Simply trade parries with them and follow your normal combat procedure until they are knocked, and try guard-breaking them every once in a while, as their posture is not remarkably big. *Having a sense of direction and environmental awareness is '''vital''' for your survivability and safety. Maximize the usage of your map (keybind 'M') if your're new to the depths. Falling into the void while your above 60% Health (only applies for characters power 3+, as lower power leveled characters '''will get wiped''') will send you to the Ethironal Shrine Outskirts in Layer 2, Floor one. In order to escape the floor unprepared, (Light Hook is not available) you will have to activate the Deepdriller or kill [[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract|Chaser]]. (rather difficult for a new player, try check out some guides) *Ringing [[Lost Celtor city bells|the bells]] (not corrupted bells) in the [[The City of the Drowned]] will restore some HP and sanity, equivalent to that of knocking an NPC or monster around your power. *If you find yourself in the Depths with very little health, there are some options for you. These options include standing still for 15 seconds, which allows you to heal pretty fast after the 15 seconds, killing a low-level mob (i.e a Jellyfish or a Mudskipper) for healthpack, or a friend that can place a Graceful Flame for you (A support flame mantra). *[[Castle Light]] contains a blacksmith in which you can repair your outfit if you have good or neutral reputation with the Divers, and if you entered the depths via whirlpool, as you can't get into the place if you entered the depths by dying) *Bringing high mobility mantras such as [[Strong Leap]], [[Flame Leap]], or [[Adrenaline Surge]] will be helpful in fleeing any unwanted fights and navigate the treacherous terrain. *'''AVOID''' fighting a [[Megalodaunt]] near pitfalls - getting kicked by a Megalodaunt will likely fling you off the edge, which may lead you to an unexpected wipe, or Layer 2 visit. If you do happen to fight one near a pitfall/cliff, and there is no chance of regaining flat ground with no risks of pitfalls, face your character towards the edge of the cliff. The Megalodaunt will '''always''' attack facing the characters front side. *'''AVOID''' the [[Nautilodaunt]] if you're unexperienced with it. The Nautilodaunt will make loud grumbling noises when in it's idle spawn state. Once spotted, it is extremely difficult to escape. Unlike any normal monster, they can spot you at unfairly long distances, even when you're not even in their line of sight. They're very tough but also highly intelligent in close combat, being able to skillfully parry, block and vent attacks and criticals which leaves you having a good chance of being wiped by them. If you are caught by a Nautilodaunt, try scaling the tallest building you can find in the city, and then log after your combat tag disappears. Because if you didn't know already, they will '''never''' stop chasing you. *Avoid any monsters you have little to no experience with, especially [[Deep Owl]]s, [[King Thresher]]s and [[Nautilodaunt]]s, which have comparatively high mobility and intelligence. Additionally, don't take fights you're uncertain you can win. If you are not prepared to wipe, this '''is not the place to learn'''. For many mobs, you can fight them somewhere else with less risk (Except for the Nautilodaunts since they spawn in the Depths, but [[the Diluvian Mechanism]] is a very unorthodox but available way to train). *If you see your character is becoming insane, such as shivering or scratching, it is best to leave the Depths as quickly as possible. If you use a Glider at this stage of insanity, you '''will''' fall off the Glider. *If you are experiencing severe lag on a particular server, consider switching to another one. (PLEASE CHOOSE ONE THAT IS IN YOUR REGION) A single lag spike can result in a wipe if not careful. *It is advised to carry a [[Repair Kit]] in case your armor bar is gone, unless you have graceful flames, or a campfire. *If within the vicinity of [[Castle Light]], it's not a bad idea to bring a mob that you're fighting to them. The Diver NPCS are rather competent and tanky, shifting the monster's aggro towards them, effectively protecting you. *If you plan on using [[Flame Ballista]] in the trial to get a hit, start conjuring it right when the voice of Odium says "Their" in "Just be quick about it will you? '''Their''' stench is already nauseating." Make sure to point at the right spot, as it will most likely not auto-target. Do know where the monster will spawn. *If [[Finnegan The Lost]] or [[The Fisherman]] randomly spawn upon you, and you are not powerful enough to defeat them, run. It is not worth risking it against an enemy that has too much HP for you to properly deal with, and they dont have a good arsenal of player-catching mantras with them - just try not to get stuck with the Fisherman's chains, or get caught by Finnegan's Metal Ball. *Stay aware of your surroundings. With the recent job updates, the presence of more players increases the likelihood of monster spawns, which could make your situation worse if you're fighting a monster or players. While it is good having players in a server which could potentially help you in sticky situations, its not always a guarantee that they are friendly or they are there within your vicinity. *If you are unfamiliar with monsters and the Depths in general, always try bringing another experienced and competent friend with you, as it will make learning the harrowing tribulations of the Depths slightly more easing for you. *If you are a new player, it is '''heavily advised to log''' if you hear cracking and rumbling randomly inside the Depths. This is the 'Depths Collapse' which spawns in a horde of dangerous and threatening monsters in 2-4 rocks that fall from the depths' ceiling. **If you're confident in killing these mobs, however, they will drop chests with enhanced loot. *With the recent changes to Watchers, it’s crucial to avoid being spotted by one. They can now inflict insanity and distort your vision, making it extremely difficult to fight or escape. Do everything you can to stay out of their sight, as their insanity effect builds up rapidly. You can do this by hiding behind or inside a building. *When you're in the Depths, assume every player is hostile. Keep your guard raised at all times. Never relax just because someone looks passive or isn’t approaching you immediately a lot of players wait for the perfect moment to ambush, especially when you’re distracted by mobs, looting, or navigating tight spaces. *When traversing inside [[The City of the Drowned]], try to stay on top of buildings or higher surfaces, as mobs spawn easier, and can attack you easier if you stay on the ground. ==Gallery== Depths.png|Concept art ==Trivia== *Scyphozia is a corruption of the word [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scyphozoa Scyphozoa], which is the marine class the true jellyfish are in. Meanwhile, Scyphozia's main enemies are [[Gigamed]]s. *The ability for monsters to spawn corrupted appears to be intrinsic to the First Layer rather than the monsters themselves, as monsters from the Second Layer can be corrupted if spawned in the First Layer. *[[Resonance]]s can resurrect a player one time when they are knocked in the Depths, once progress is sufficient (usually about power 16 by only staying in the Depths and killing mobs exclusively in the Depths.) *You can use 5 Umbral Obsidians to gain [[Shadowcast]] by talking to [[Nostor, Master of Shadow|Nostor]] found in Layer One. This permanently unlocks [[Shadowcast]] for the account. *Staying in The Depths for prolonged periods of time (from 20 minutes onwards with 0 Willpower) will drain your Sanity, causing your vision to become blurred and eventually causing you to slowly lose health via scratching yourself. You can be executed by insanity if you are low enough, but you can stay alive as long as you keep your health up. Max insanity will instantly kill you if you are using the Curse of the No-Life King enchant. *The instruments in the combat theme heard in this location are reminiscent of "[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yXX9gO56EXw void]," a theme within the Terraria Calamity Mod that is heard within the 4th layer of the similarly dangerous Abyss biome. *If you are facing against a player/mob in The Depths while you have your back facing the void, it is essentially guaranteed that you will most likely be launched into the void if you are not careful. Many players, '''experienced''' or '''not''', have fallen victim or '''will''' fall victim to the void at '''least''' once in their gameplay. *According to the "Munet Journal, XIV", it canonically takes 2 weeks for a being to escape the depths. *The Depths Collapse Event can spawn most monsters including 2 [[Thresher]]s, a [[Megalodaunt]], an [[Alpha Megalodaunt]], a [[King Thresher]], and a [[Nautilodaunt]]. Killing all of the Depths monsters it has spawned will reward you with multiple [[Hell Mode]] chests filled with highly valuable loot. The more meteors that fall, the more chests with more valuable loot there will be depending on how many meteors spawned, but there will be more monsters to fight. (About 2-4 boulders = 2-4 chests) *If you go into the Depths Trial arena solo, but your Difficulty Score is low enough for your trial to be Nothing, then the Voice of Enmity and Voice of Odium have special dialogue, and the Voice of Authority doesn't talk. *Previously, 4 bells located throughout the city were required to be rung in order to escape the Depths. **This was adjusted, likely because of how much time it took and how risky it was, causing players to use unintended but easier methods such as barrel stacking over the walls. **In the same update, one of the elevator entrances were replaced with the sub-elevator, with a risky approach. title: First Light
content:
{{Weapon Infobox |type=Greatsword |requirements=75 HVY |damage=23 |damage type=Slash |scaling=HVY: 8 |posture damage=9 |range=8.5 |range type=Sweep |swing speed=0.82x |attack duration=0.9s |endlag=0.1s |penetration=15% |obtainment=*[[Crimson Megalodaunt]] (Very Rare) *[[Merchant Ships]] (Very Rare) *Sold in [[Traan Zakshun|Traan Zakshun's]] black market for {{c|crowns|8}} |m.equip=Yes |m.extract=No |description=Blade of [[Venn Kaelhand]], a disciple of [[Amorus Pleeksty|Pleeksty]], who immersed themself much too deeply in the study of beasts altered by [[Korilfiend, the Inferno's Provenance|Korlfiend]]'s influence. Met their fate in the jaws of a [[Crimson Megalodaunt|unique specimen of Megalodaunt]] said to have been exposed to the vents of Korilfiend. |image=FirstLight2025.png|Current FirstlightDW.gif|Old |rarity=Mythical |special effect=On critical, summon a storm of fiery blades that hail down onto the field. |selling price=100 |oath=Silentheart }} ==Description== The First Light is a [[Weapons|Heavy Weapon]] obtained as a rare direct drop from slaying a [[Crimson Megalodaunt]], finding it inside a Merchant Ship, or buying it from [[Traan Zakshun]]. The weapon has unique animations and a unique critical. ==Critical== File:FirstLightPlunge.gif|Plunge File:First Light Critical .gif|Sword rain The user plunges the greatsword into the ground, similar to Flame Eruption, causing everyone near the user to be burned briefly. This is followed up with flaming swords raining from the sky, similar to the [[Crimson Megalodaunt]]'s Pyroclastic Roar. '''Both''' parts of this critical scale solely on your '''[[Flamecharm]] investment'''. The plunge deals 25 [[Flamecharm]] damage with 5 Flamecharm scaling (gains 0.125 damage per point in Flamecharm), 5 posture damage, and '''applies burn'''. The critical will end early if this attack is parried.
The swords from the sword rain deal 14 Flamecharm damage with 5 Flamecharm scaling (gains 0.07 damage per point in Flamecharm) and 3.5 posture damage. The swords '''do not apply burn''' and '''cannot proc any enchant or "on critical" Talent effect''' (like {{t|Manipulator}}). The swords are also 360 blockable. This critical is mostly used as a distraction or pressure as opposed to dealing actual damage due to the randomness of the swords and the large area it covers. The critical has a cooldown of '''25 seconds'''. ==Gallery== ===Images=== File:Ogfirstlightpic.png|A player wielding the old model of First Light File:First Light M1 Cycle.gif| M1 cycle File:FirstLightModelsNuts.png|Model File:FirstLightModelsNutsComparison.png|Comparison between old and current model ===Enchantments=== File:AzureflameFL.png|Azure Blazing File:Enhcant.png|Wild File:Stormfirstlight.png|Storm File:First light curse of repulsion.png|Curse of Repulsion File:FirstLightUMBK.png|Umbral Knight File:FirstLightVamp.png|Vampirism File:FirstLightUnbidden.png|Curse Of The Unbidden File:FirstLightTears.png|Tears Of The Edenkite File:FIrstLightSTMBK.png|Stormbreaker File:Sear First Light.png|Sear File:FirstLightProvidence.png|Providence Thorns File:FirstLightOBFSC.png|Obfuscation File:FirstLightNLK.png|Curse of the No-Life King File:FirstLightNem.png|Nemesis File:FirstLightMetal.png|Metal File:FirstLightHeroism.png|Heroism File:FirstLightHarrowing.png|Harrowing File:FirstLightGRIM.png|Grim File:FirstLightGluttony.png|Gluttony File:FirstLightDETO.png|Detonation File:FirstLightDeferred.png|Deferred File:FirstLightBlazing.png|Blazing File:Curse of Yun'Shul First light.png|'''Curse of Yun'Shul''' File:Solar First Light.png|Solar File:Image 2025-12-08 183741303.png|Astral ==Trivia == *Similarly to The Crimson Megalodaunt, the First Light's critical attack is a reference to Gilgamesh's Gates of Babylon from the Fate series. *The critical First Light uses was previously a flame mantra, called "Potato". It was shown in the Deepwoken Direct.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEaEzDO04aU&list=PLQPka5UlSn4jMYDSxZv9kYGwCoITvDHg0&index=7 Deepwoken Direct] *Compared to other greatswords, this one looks more modern as the design resembles a more modern-designed blade and handle with designs and patterns of edges and gold crafted into it, rather than a basic flat blade with some carvings scratched into it, like the [[Darksteel Greatsword]]. **The hilt and blade resemble the Medieval European sword design, meant to resemble a crucifix. This suggest a more modern but also Western origin. *Similar to a [[Flamecharm]] Mantra, both parts of First Light's critical will receive a damage debuff during the rain unless you have the {{t|Unyielding Inferno}} Talent. *First Light is one of two weapons to have a critical that scales solely on an attunement stat despite the weapon not requiring said attunement to wield, the other being the [[Krulian Knife]]. *The swords from the sword rain on the critical are not counted as "weapon attacks" for any effect in the game. This allows them to do things like not lose damage if you have a [[Ring of Casters]] equipped, but also not gain a damage buff from things like [[Shade Devour]]. *The weapon originally had its own unique M1 animations, but they were removed due to being "unfinished and buggy". **When a Visionshaper clone was spawned with a Railblade, their weapon utilized the old animations of the First Light. **It was given reworked animations in the April 24th, 2023 pdate, alongside a new critical attack. ***Two years later, it was then given a visual remodel on the April 26th, 2025 update. *First Light's critical does not change colors depending on if you have Azure Flames or Twisted Puppets. *While it has good stats and has no endlag, it is severely held back by its okay-ish critical that has an unnecessarily high cooldown, making players opt to use [[Nemesis]] instead. *During the Deepwoken Youtuber Battle Royale Tournament on July 1st, 2023, Youtuber "Trunks" used this sword to clutch out a victory during the 4th Round of the Tournament against "Floppingman" and "nogo" during the final circle. **This victory earned the necessary points for their duo to place second overall, giving [[Lightborn]] to both Trunks and Agamatsu. *With [[Warmaster's Medallion]]'s Talent, ''Actions Speak Louder'', the critical cooldown is reduced to 20 seconds. **If you add the {{t|Critical Engine}} Talent with [[Blessed Gem]] to your [[Warmaster's Medallion]], you can bring the First Light critical down to 10 seconds, as the Blessed Gem effect that halves your cooldown is applied '''after''' Warmaster's Medallion. *The model of the flaming swords that are seen in the critical are identical to the [[Worshipper Longsword]]. *The First Light's new model may take inspiration from the [https://www.roblox.com/catalog/93136746/Telamonster-the-Chaos-Edge Telamonster] ROBLOX gear. It shares multiple similarities with the gear, such as a red and gold color scheme, being a fire-based sword, and the two wing-like structures at both weapons' guards. ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Greatswords]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Criticals]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Animations]] [[Category:Weapons with Multi-Hit Criticals]] [[Category:Heavy Weapons]]

title: Fisher Hut
content:
[[File:MortusIsland.png|thumb|900px|center]]
The fisher hut is an location in the [[Luminants|Etrean Luminant]]. It can be found when sailing from [[Isle of Vigils]] to [[Erisia]]. The hut itself is on an small island with a [[Boats|boat spawner]]. 

== Overview ==
There's a hut and few palms on the island as well as an [[Boats|boat spawner]]. Inside of the hut, you can buy a [[Fishing Rod]] for 30 notes and [[Chum]] for 10 notes, also [[Mortus]] can be found here. Next to the hut is a [[Training Gear|Gear cabinet]]. If you go left from the hut, you'll pass trough a small alley and youl'll be at a [[Fishing|fishing spot]].

==Trivia==

* Generally, this place is good for [[Fishing]], because people don't come here often and if you fish at the fishing spot you're tehnically uninteruptable.
* You can set up to 3 [[Monster Bait|Monster Baits]] here alongside being able to buy them here.
* The place is in the open sea but still secluded by a mountain

title: Fishing
content:
{{InProgress|Body=Fishing was recently reworked, please allow for some time before changes are fully set.}} {{Quotes |quote=The depth of water you fish at affects what you'll catch. Some fish are best caught at the shore, and others far out on a boat! |author=[[Loading Screen]] tip }}
File:Fishing.png
__TOC__ ==Description== [[File:Fishingicon.png|thumb|link=Special:FilePath/Fishingicon.png]] '''Fishing''' is a mechanic in ''Deepwoken'' that allows players to catch seafood and other valuables from almost any body of water using a [[Fishing Rod]]. Fishing Rods can be crafted with two [[Stick]]s and one [[Fiber]] at a {{crafting|station}}, or purchased from select vendors for {{c|notes|30/35}}. To fish, cast a line into any body of water by pressing {{Input|keybind|M1}}, or hold {{Input|keybind|M1}} to cast if farther and higher. Once the bobber lands into water, it will take some to settle before a minigame pops up to fish. Once something is caught onto the line, reel in catches by pressing the displayed key (W, A, S, or D) while holding down {{Input|keybind|M1}} before the caught item gets loose. Lines can also be instantly withdrawn by pressing {{Input|keybind|M1}} while its being thrown. Fishing also grants experience toward all ''physical'' [[Attributes]]. ==Catches== Fishing can yield a variety of fish, creatures, and other items. Every possible catch has a unique chat message displayed by the player's character upon being reeled in, with most being fish-related puns or other wordplay. The longer it takes to successfully reel in a catch, the higher the quality of the fish and potential loot obtained. On rare occasions, a catch may be '''golden'''. With the sole exception of the [[Golden Swordfish]], golden catches are automatically converted into {{c|knowledge|1}} [[Knowledge]] instead of being added to the player's inventory, up to a maximum of five times per fish. The following are all possible fishing catches and their quotes: *[[Golden Swordfish]] (and any golden fish): "Huh?!" *[[Lamprey]]: It's a Lamprey... Gotcha, sucker!" *[[Leather Boots]]: "A pair of old boots..." *[[Lionfish]] (As an enemy): "A LIONFISH?!" *[[Mudskipper]] (As an enemy): "What the...?!" *[[Pufferfish]]: "A poisonous Pufferfish! Careful eating this one..." *[[Red Snapper]]: "A Red Snapper! Quite the sailor's mouth on this one..." *[[Sea Bass]]: "It's a Sea Bass! Where's its instrument?" *[[Seaweed Bundle]]: "It was stuck on some seaweed..." *[[Squid]]: "Cool Squid! No, I'm not squidding." *[[Swordfish]]: "A Swordfish! Too bad I can't wield it..." *[[Chests & Sacks|Treasure Chests]]: "Woah a treasure chest!" *[[Tuna]]: "Holy moly! A Tuna! I wonder what at-tuna-ment it is?" *[[Urchin]]: "Barely edible..." *[[Yellow Bass]]: "It's a Yellow Bass! What a coward!" Failing to reel in something that was caught can give the quotes: "It broke loose!" or "I didn't reel it in fast enough..." ==Bait== While bait is not required, attaching bait increases the chance of attracting nibbles and converting them into successful bites. Bait can be attached by holding out a Fishing Rod and clicking on the desired item to put on as bait. The following items are known to function as bait: *[[Arkasid Pupa]] *[[Ambrosial Chum]] (Extremely potent) *[[Browncap]] *[[Calabash]] *[[Canteen]] *[[Cheese]] *[[Chum]] *[[Crustacean Meat]] *[[Dentifilo]] *[[Dread Flesh]] (Extremely potent) *[[Fish Meat]] *[[Fish Stew]] *[[Glazed Fish]] *[[Gobletto]] *[[Latchgrain]] *[[Mushroom Bisque]] *[[Plumfruit]] *[[Pomar]] *[[Primal Slab]] (Extremely potent) *[[Pufferfish]] *[[Raw Heavy Meat]] (Extremely potent) *[[Raw Parasol Brain]] (Extremely potent) *[[Redd]] *[[Sap]] *[[Seaweed Bundle]] *[[Squelcap]] *[[Squid]] *[[Sushi]] *[[Urchin]] {| class="fandom-table" !Bait & Amount !Misses !Common Fish !Uncommon Fish !Rare Fish !Chests !Monsters ! Other |- |100 Pomars |0 |76 |0 | 1 |12 |0 |11 |- |100 Chum No lucky spot |0 |69 |7 |0 |9 |15 |0 |- |100 Chum Lucky Spot |0 |55 |17 |2 |16 |10 |0 |- | 100 Urchin | 0 |56 |10 |1 |17 |16 |0 |- |100 Fish Meat |0 |60 |19 |0 |9 |12 |0 |- |100 Seaweed |0 |62 |10 |0 |11 |17 |0 |} ==Fishing Spots== The depth and salinity of the water being fished in determine the possible catches. For example, [[Sea Bass]] can be found near shore but cannot be caught in deep oceans or rivers. Certain areas have higher fishing activity, resulting in more frequent nibbles. A select locations also contain designated fishing spots, which provide significantly better loot pools than regular waters. Fishing spots appear as small circular areas with water splashes emerging from them. They can be found naturally throughout the world or summoned by placing a [[Rain Spire]]. [[File:Screenshot 2024-05-17 183718.png|thumb|Visual effect for a fishing spot]] The following areas are known to have designated fishing spots: *[[Boatman's Watch]] *Behind [[Mortus]]' shack *[[Starfield Grove]] *[[Starfield Veldt]] *Near the [[Shrine of Division]] *[[Miner's Landing]] *[[Eastern Interstitial Lighthouse]] *[[The Entropy Catalyst]] *[[Beloved Zofia]] *[[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City]] *[[Minityrsa]] |-|Boatmans Watch= ===Boatmans Watch=== This spot is seen on the coast of Boatman's Watch to the right of the shipyard looking outward. Ferryman fish spot.png |-|Mortus= ===Mortus=== This spot is accessed by slipping through a crack past the left side of Mortus' shack. Mortis Fishing Spot.png Mortus spot on map.png |-|Starfield Grove= ===Starfield Grove=== This spot can be seen behind the Startree located in the [[Starswept Valley]]. Startree fishing spot.png Startree fishing spot location.png |-|Starfield Veldt= ===Starfield Veldt=== This spot can be seen behind the Startree located near [[Miner's Landing]]. Starfield veldt spot.png Fishing spot miners starfield.png |-|Shrine of Division= ===Shrine of Division=== This spot is located to the right of the [[Shrine of Division]] island when facing outward. Shrine of division fishing.png Shrine of Division fishing spot location.png |-|Miner's Landing= ===Miner's Landing=== This spot is located in a waterfall in a staircase on the path to the upper landing. Miners landing fishing spot.png Miners Landing fishing spot location.png |-|Eastern Interstitial Lighthouse= ===Eastern Interstitial Lighthouse=== This spot is located in the inner walls of the Lighthouse Lighthouse fishing spot.png Lighthouse location.png |-|The Entropy Catalyst= ===The Entropy Catalyst=== This spot is located at the entrance of [[The Entropy Catalyst]] Entropy catalyst fishing spot.png Entropy catalyst fishing spot location.png |-|Beloved Zofia= ===Beloved Zofia=== This spot is located around the rocks in front of the front of the [[Beloved Zofia]] Beloved zofia fishing spot.png Beloved zofia fishing spot location.png |-|New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City= ===New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City=== This spot is located in Kaide, The Drowned Light prison(Can be visited through one of the white clouds teleporter tower near Ethiron Chamber). Fish.PNG Fish minityrsa spot.PNG ==Talents== There are currently three Talents related to fishing, each automatically obtained after reaching certain milestones. {{TalentInfo |name=Proficient Baiting |icon=Claw |rarity=Quest |category=Angler |requirements=Get 10 Bites in fishing (given automatically) |description=Casting your line excites ocea life, reducing the chances of fishing up trash. |additional info=*Drastically increases the chances of catching fish instead of junk items. *This inadvertently reduces the chances of fishing up chests however, due to fish being more common. }} {{TalentInfo |name=Hook, Line, and Sinker |icon=Claw |rarity=Quest |category=Angler |requirements=Get 30 Bites in fishing (given automatically) |description=Once something's caught your line, it's much harder for it to get loose. |additional info=*Increases the amount of time provided to complete the fishing minigame. }} {{TalentInfo |name=Fisher's Lure |icon=Claw |rarity=Quest |category=Angler |requirements=Get 50 Bites in fishing (given automatically) |description=Fish are drawn to your line more quickly. |additional info=*Reduces the amount of time it takes to get a bite. }} ==Gallery== maximum of {{c|knowledge|45}} just from fishing. *The general format and delivery of the lines that your character speaks is a possible reference to the ''Animal Crossing'' series. *There is no height limit for fishing, allowing players to throw out their lines from the peaks of mountains. *Fishing used to contain every single item inside of its lootpool as long as it was in '''any chest pool''', this led to infamous incidents such as the '''Verse 1 Enchant Shard incident'''. After this happened, a quick patch was rolled out to allow blacklists to items and chest pools, such as the blacklisting of Enchant Stone chests. *During the [[Warring States Era]] fishing would give points to the aspect you had. *Fishing up a [[Golden Swordfish]] allows you to use it as a weapon. *[[Lionfish]] are able to be caught in the lake in [[Second Layer/New Kyrsa|New Kyrsa]], and will still be capable of using their Cero attack. ==References== [[Category:Fishing]] [[Category:Mechanics]]

The '''Fishing Rod''' is a tool used to cast lines into most bodies of water for fish, treasure, and even monsters.

== Obtainment ==
The Fishing Rod can be obtained in a few ways:

* Bought for {{c|notes|30}} or {{c|notes|35}} depending on the vendor.
* Crafted with two (2) [[Stick|Sticks]] and one (1) [[Fiber]].

== Uses ==
The Fishing Rod can be used for the following:

* [[Fishing]] up fish and trash.
* Fishing up Treasure [[Chests & Sacks#Chests|Chests]].
* Fishing up [[Mudskipper]]s and [[Lionfish|Lionfishes]].

title: Fists
content:
==Description== Fists are a unique type of [[Light Weapons|Light Weapon]], being a collection of multiple martial arts styles rather than solely being one weapon type with distinct animations. Fists can be equipped at any time (even during combat) by unequipping your current weapon or using one of the Fist Style Talent tools. These weapons are typically locked to the One Handed stance. ==Styles== Fist Styles are unlockable martial arts techniques that change the animations and criticals of your Fist weapons. Instead of stance swapping, the {{input|keybind|Y}} key will swap your Fist Style. Style swapping has a 8 second cooldown. Each style has a [[Outfits|Master Armor]] associated with it, granting additional unique benefits when using the respective style. The following is a brief overview of the styles and their Master Armors. For more information, please view their individual pages. |-|Fang and Coil= [[Fang and Coil]]; a serpentine Fist Style that has been adopted by a select few of [[the Vigils]]. Its critical is a leg sweep that ragdolls. Using the [[Jade Vigil's Weave]] Outfit will grant this style an additional unique critical, as long as you are using a weapon that does not already have a unique critical. |-|Imperium Kata= [[Imperium Kata]]; an advanced [[Hundred Legions]] martial arts. Its critical consists of two brutal kicks. Using the [[Legion Centurion]] Outfit grants this style, and its sister style, [[Legion Kata]] 4% more damage. |-|Jus Karita= [[Jus Karita]] is a unique fist style, created by the [[The Justicar|Justicars]]. Its critical is a spinning kick attack. Unlike all other styles, this Fist Style is a '''Kick Style''', meaning it cannot equip Cestus weapons. To make up for this, Jus Karita's bare hands has unique stats compared to all other Fist Styles. Additionally, Jus Karita has unique Talents and Mantras, something entirely unseen with all other Fist Styles. Using the [[Justicar's Armor]] Outfit grants a 10% damage buff to this style. |-|Legion Kata= [[Legion Kata]]; the standard martial arts of the [[Hundred Legions]]. Its critical is a grapple attack that ends with an overhead slam. Using the [[Legion Centurion]] Outfit grants this style, and its sister style, [[Imperium Kata]] 4% more damage. |-|Untrained Fist= [[Untrained Fist]]; an untrained Fist Style, consisting of general theatrics and weak blows. Its critical is a run-up into a haymaker punch. This style deals 50% less damage than all other Fist Styles. |-|Way of Navae= [[Way of Navae]]; a Fist Style used by the [[Children of Navae|Navaen Nomads]]. Its critical consists of a guardbreaking overhead kick. Using the [[Navaen War Chief]] Outfit will grant +10% PEN to Way of Navae M1s and criticals with the [[M1 tag]]. ==PvE Mechanics== While wielding a Fist Weapon, gain a 2.5% damage buff to all sources of Blunt damage, and a 5% damage buff to weapon attacks in PvE for every Fist Talent you have. This is dealt as a separate damage instance. This effect benefits from {{t|Chain of Perfection|r=quest}} separately. At maximum, gain +30% weapon damage and +15% Blunt Mantra damage. Eligible Fist Talents: *{{t|Bruiser's Mixup}} *{{t|Captain Etrea}} *{{t|Dirty Boxing|r=rare}} *{{t|Fists of Fortitude|r=rare}} *{{t|Fists of Navae}} Outfit Talent *{{t|Pocket Sand}} Ineligible Fist Talents: *Fist Styles (e.g. {{t|Way of Navae}} Talent) *[[Talents#Justicar|Jus Karita]] Talents *[[Justicar (Origin)|Justicar]] (Origin) Talents ==Default Animations==
The {{PAGENAME}} weapon class comes with a set of default weapon animations.
===General Animations=== File:Placeholder.png|Running File:Placeholder.png|Blocking File:Placeholder.png|Uppercut File:Placeholder.png|Aerial Attack File:Placeholder.png|Running Attack ===Style Specific Animations=== |-|Fang and Coil= ''Main Page: [[Fang and Coil]]'' FangAndCoilNewIdle.gif|Idle FangM1chain.gif|Basic Attacks |-|Imperium Kata= ''Main Page: [[Imperium Kata]]'' Imperium Kata.png|Idle Imperium Kata M1 Cycle.gif|Basic Attacks |-|Jus Karita= ''Main Page: [[Jus Karita]]'' JusKaritaIdleGuildArena.gif|Idle JusKaritaM1sGuildArena.gif|Basic Attacks Placeholder.png|Running Placeholder.png|Blocking Placeholder.png|Running Attack |-|Legion Kata= ''Main Page: [[Legion Kata]]'' File:Legion Kata.png|Idle Legion kata m1.gif|Basic Attacks |-|Untrained Fist= ''Main Page: [[Untrained Fist]]'' Untrained Fist.png|Idle Untrained Fist M1s.gif|Basic Attacks |-|Way of Navae= ''Main Page: [[Way of Navae]] Way of Navae.png|Idle Way of navae m1's.gif|Basic Attacks

Your blood needs iron to deliver oxygen to your organs. You need organs to live." **This still doesn't work, even if you have the {{t|Alloyblood}} Talent. *Ragoozer has an exclusive fist style for his spec. This fist style is very similar to that of an advanced fist form in Rogue Lineage. *When possessing all cestus styles, style swapping using {{input|keybind|Y}} repeats in this order: **(Way of Navae -> Imperium Kata -> Legion Kata -> Fang and Coil) ==Weapons== {{AllFistWeapons}} {{History}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Light Weapons]] [[Category:Weapons by Class]]

content:
{{IronVowEx}} {{Memento |image=Flame Worshipper Memento.png |description=Following in the steps of [[Pleeksty]], they swore themselves to the flame within. |starting attributes=*5 Flamecharm *4 Medium Weapon *2 Fortitude *2 Agility *4 Intelligence *4 Willpower |final attributes=*100 Flamecharm *80 Medium Weapon *40 Fortitude *35 Agility *70 Intelligence *70 Willpower |starting traits=*2 Songchant *2 Proficiency |final traits=*5 Songchant *4 Proficiency |locked armor=[[Flame Worshipper Armor]] |allowed weapons=Shield, Sword, Club |starting weapons=[[Worshipper Longsword]] |starting items=[[Simmerbloom Diadem]] |unlock=Unlocked by default }} ==Description== '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a playable [[Memento]] in the [[Vow of Iron]] gamemode. You also spawn with the [[Simmerbloom Diadem]] and can equip the [[Pleeksty's Inferno]] which you can find as a static spawn at [[Miner's Landing (Vow of Iron)|Miners Landing]]. Following the teachings of [[Amorus Pleeksty]], the Flame Worshipper does what their order do best: set their surroundings ablaze. With their empowered Flamecharm Mantras, the ability to rise again should they fall, and flame spirits, they leave nothing behind. {{clear}}
==Starting Abilities==
*{{cl|mementotlnf|Pleeksty's Inheritance}} [Memento Talent] - You inherit the teachings of Amorus Pleeksty, augmenting your flamecharm mantras. **Fire Blade now blockbreaks regardless of mantra level. **Burning servants now inflicts knockback on its hits. **Relentless flames gains 6 extra slashes and becomes much faster. *Flame Within [Common Talent] - An application of Pleeksty's concept of the inner flame, also known as the soul of man. Set yourself ablaze to gain more move speed and 10% extra damage. **Unlike normal burn, Flame Within's burn is not cleared by rolling/sliding. Flame Within will not stop until 30 seconds have passed or until Flame Within is reused. **Generally dangerous to use without multiple sources of burn damage reduction, most notably, Immolation. **8 second cooldown that starts when Flame Within is activated. Meaning if you let it burn for long enough, the cooldown will effectively be nullified outside of burn immunity. The Talent tool does not showcase this properly. **It is a general damage buff, and as such it'll affect all sources of damage that can be modified. **Flame Within can be enabled while knocked. **Deals self-damage on cast, separate from the burn damage. This self damage can be resisted with the [[Deepscorn Casque]], elemental resistance (it deals Flamecharm damage), and many other sources of damage reduction. **[[Parasol Planter|Grotesque Resilience]] reduces the damage taken from Flame Within's burn DoT by 25%. **[[Deepfire Ring]] will lower Flame Within's duration down to 25s without affecting the burn damage taken. This is a direct downgrade for Flame within. *Intrepid Flame [Equipment Talent] - Flames wear off twice as fast on you. **Halves the maximum duration of any Burn that is applied to you. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Fire Palm (★☆☆) |image=Fire Palm.gif |desc=Conjure a cone of flames in front of you. Pressing {{Input|keybind|parry}} during windup will release a wider but shorter flame. |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |reqs=N/A |mantratype=Combat Mantra |effect=User releases a burst of flame from their palm in a cone shape. *Has a base damage of 26{{tooltip3|[[Caster Fur Pauldrons|{{cl|equiptlnf|/27.5}}]]}} with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 5 posture damage. *Has a windup of 0.7 seconds with 0.2 seconds of endlag, and a 16 second cooldown. *Has 9.14x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.14 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s to increase size, every +1 in size makes it 10% bigger. **Size modifications will lower the damage, however. *Pressing {{Input|keybind|parry}} during the mantra's windup will release a wider but shorter flame. File:Fire-palm-alt1-2025.gif|Alternative Cast }}
==Deck of Recollection==
===Starting Deck===
*Agitating Spark [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - If you hit an opponent that you've lit on fire, it spreads to anyone nearby. Including yourself. **On proc, a small orange particle will trail between the burning target you hit and other targets nearby, setting them on fire. ***This visual effect will still happen when hitting a non-burning target with a burn-applying attack, granting Emperor Flame stacks without spreading burn. **Agitating Spark bypasses block and parry. **Agitating Spark procs caused by self damage will not apply burn. Flame Within is an exception to this. **Has a 1 second cooldown. **Can spread to allies. *Controlled Combustion [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Your Agitating Spark no longer spreads to your allies. **Your Agitating Spark no longer spreads to yourself too. **In some places, this Talent doesn't work well, spreading to your allies if they are too close to the target. *Corpse Explosion [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Your flames will incinerate unconscious Targets much faster and bodies that you burn to death immediately explode dealing massive damage. **Burn grip unconscious targets, even yourself, in 3.5 seconds instead of 7. ***The time it takes for burn to execute is very reliant on server performance, it may take longer than what is listed here. **The explosion does not work; you'll burn them to death without an explosion. *Hungry Flames [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - When you have no Ether, consume Stomach and Water to instantly cast your next fire mantra [15 second CD]. *Immolation [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Fire spells cost 70% less while on fire. If you hit someone while on fire, apply fire damage. You take 50% less damage from self-inflicted flames. (+8 Sanity) **"Self-Inflicted flames" include Flame Within, Agitating Spark you spread and environmental burns created by you. **"Apply fire damage" applies the burn status effect instead of adding Flamecharm damage. It also applies burn even if you have Eruption Path: Lava Serpent. ***Not all attacks proc this effect, unlike what the Talent description implies. Instead, all instances of Physical damage apply burn, even if the attack doesn't deal pure Physical damage. And all attacks that have the slash (blood particle) vfx on hit will also proc Immolation, applying burn. *Magical Resolve [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Being hit increases [[Ether]] regen for a short duration, the strength of the regen scales off your Willpower. (+7 Sanity) *Pleeksty's Faith [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - When on fire, automatically quench flames at the cost of some ether. **Does not proc with flames produced by the user with Flame Within or Agitating Spark. *{{cl|questtlnf|Pleeksty's Will}} [Quest Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - You gain significantly more ether from consuming elemental ingredients. **Consuming [[Gale Stone]]s, [[Heartstar]]s, [[Dying Embers]], [[Spark Gland]]s, and [[Frigid Prism]]s gives significantly more Ether. **Consuming elemental ingredients has a 20 second cooldown. *Swift Rebound [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Move faster after successfully dodging an attack. (+1 Passive Agility) {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Burning Servants (☆☆☆) |image=Burning Servants.gif |desc=Summon a legion of flaming spearmen that lunge inwards. |ethercost={{stats|ether|30 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |reqs={{c|notes|250}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |effect=User summons six blazing warriors armed with Halberds in a circle, attacking one after the other in quick succession at the position of the caster, before performing a synchronous strike and disappearing. *Has a base damage of 4{{tooltip3|[[Caster Fur Pauldrons|{{cl|equiptlnf|/4.4}}]]}} per level, per hit (6) with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 4 posture damage per hit with an additional 20 posture damage on the final hit. *Has a windup of 0.45s and a cooldown of 10 seconds. *The synchronous strike occurs 2.2 seconds after the mantra is cast. *Has 9.17x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.17 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone]]s and [[Stratus Stone]]s to add more warriors, capping at +9 Range. *Can be modified with a [[Reversal Spark]] to have the warriors attack outwards and ragdoll. File:Burning-servants-reverse-2025.gif|Reversal Spark }}
===Power 5===
*Cauterized Wounds [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Blood loss from all sources is lowered. (+1 Passive Agility) **Despite what the description states, this Talent only affects blood loss from directly taking damage. Blood drain effects (e.g. casting or being hit by [[Bloodrend]] Mantras, blood loss [[Potions]], the blood loss [[Resonance|Corrupt Resonance]] downside) are entirely unaffected by this Talent. **Effectiveness of this Talent is reduced if you are using the [[Curse of the No Life King]] enchantment. *Flamewalker [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - When Warding Radiance is active you leave trails of flame when you slide. (+1 Passive Agility) *Unyielding Inferno [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Your flames burn just as strong even in the fiercest of storms. **Negates the innate 10% damage debuff Flamecharm Mantras receive during the [[rain]]. **Prevents your burn from going out in rain. *{{cl|raretl|Evasive Expert}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Your speed boost granted from dodging is increased. (+1 Passive Agility) *{{cl|raretl|Observation}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Dodge frames are larger if you cancel your roll immediately. (+1 Passive Agility) **Cancelling your roll quickly will grant dodge frames equals to the length of a regular roll. Basically giving extra 0.1s dodge frames. *{{cl|raretl|Safety Dance}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Your base dodge frames are increased by 0.05s. (+1 Passive Agility) **You gain more invincibility frames while dodging, granting you longer immunity to damage. **Dodge IFrames increased from 0.3s to 0.35s. *{{cl|raretl|The Final Act}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Landing a fire mantra immediately after flourishing an opponent will cause them to explode. **Does not have a cooldown. **Deals 5 Flamecharm damage. **Will not proc on knocked NPCs/players and mobs. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Fire Blade (☆☆☆) |image=fire-blade-2025.gif |desc=Slicing blades of flame. |ethercost={{stats|ether|45 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |reqs={{c|notes|450}} |effect=User forcefully slams down their blade coated in flames. *Has a base damage of 18{{tooltip3|[[Caster Fur Pauldrons|{{cl|equiptlnf|/21}}]]}} per level with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 18 posture damage at levels 1-4, guard breaks at level 5. **At level 5, this Mantra takes 20 additional Ether on cast to retain its guard breaking property. This additional Ether cost cannot be reduced. *Has a windup of 0.7 seconds and a cooldown of 10 seconds. *Has 9.18x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.18 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Breaks destructible objects on hit. *Can be modified with [[Vibrant Gem]]s, causing the attack to destroy more environment. *While having [[Starkindred]] wings activated, Fire Blade now launches the user upward before releasing a large plume of flames after a long windup. **A [[Reversal Spark]] can be used to negate this variation, allowing you to use normal fire blade with wings. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Flame Leap (★★☆) |image=Flameleap.gif |desc=Leap up leaving behind a burst of flames. |ethercost={{stats|ether|35 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |mantratype=Mobility Mantra |reqs={{c|notes|450}} |effect=User emits a blast under them that propels the caster and nearby opponents up in the air. *Has 10 base damage (5 if Reversal Spark) regardless of Mantra level with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 10 posture damage. *Drops carried players/NPCs when used. *Has a windup of 0.5 seconds and a cooldown of 18 seconds. *Has 9.17x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.17 for PvE damage). *Flame Leap can proc '''Meteor Impact''', even without hitting an opponent. *Animation persists on feint. *Shares similar traits to the [[Strong Leap]] Mantra. *Significantly reduces in height as the player gets lower on health, similarly to the [[Strong Leap]] Mantra. *The Mantra will not deal damage if used in water. *Can be modified with a [[Reversal Spark]], delivering an explosive front flip instead of a vertical leap. **This variant negates fall damage for a small duration. It can also be used in midair but expect fall damage upon use. **This variant gets replaced with it's base variant when used in water. File:Flame Leap Reversal Spark.gif|Reversal Spark }}
===Power 10===
*Explosive Finish [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - If an enemy is on fire when you flourish, blast them away with a fire blast. **Deals 5 Flamecharm damage. **Upon proccing Emperor Flame, this Talent will be put on a 3s cd. *Flaming Flourish [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Set enemies on fire when you flourish or uppercut them. **You also apply burn on enemies by swinging uppercut nearby. Aka doesn't have to be a hit to apply burn. *{{cl|raretl|Warding Radiance}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Every fire mantra builds up one halo stack. At 3 stacks a halo appears that allows you to slide further. Hell's Partisan is also triggered passively while this is active. (+1 Passive Agility) **Allows you to proc Hell's Partisan on Flamecharm Mantras that aren't [[Fire Forge]] while you have the halo active. **This can be easily procced by landing a multi-hit fire mantra. **Doesn't have a cooldown, lasts for 60s, cannot be refreshed. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Relentless Flames (★★☆) |image=Relentlessflames.gif |desc=Bear down on your foes with repeated fiery slashes. |ethercost={{stats|ether|40 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |reqs={{c|notes|700}} |effect=User releases a flurry of seven slashes. *The damage reduces with each successive hit. *Each level increases the base damage by 10% of the level 1's base damage. Relentless Flames has 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. **At level 1, Relentless Flames has a base damage of 20 + 20 + 14 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 4. **{{tooltip3|[[Caster Fur Pauldrons|{{cl|equiptlnf|At level 2, Relentless Flames has a base damage of 22 + 22 + 15.4 + 8.8 + 4.4 + 4.4 + 4.4.}}]]}} *Deals 5/11/13/15/19 posture damage per level. *Has a windup of 0.9 and 0.25 seconds between hits, and a 10 second cooldown. *Cancels if the first hit does not land. Additionally, if any hit is parried, even if it isn't the first one, the Mantra will also cancel. *Has 17.2x PVE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 17.2 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Can be cancelled midway by feinting. *The Pleeksty's Inheritance talent makes this mantra significantly faster. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Flame Assault (★★☆) |image=Flame Assualt.gif.gif |desc=Dash forward in a spiral of flames. |ethercost={{stats|ether|40 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |reqs={{c|notes|700}} |mantratype=Mobility Mantra |effect=User propels and spins in a 360 motion forward coated in flames leaving a trail behind; hitting anyone in their path. *Has a base damage of 8{{tooltip3|[[Caster Fur Pauldrons|{{cl|equiptlnf|/16}}]]}} per level with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 1.5/3/4.5/6/7.5 posture damage per level. *Has a windup of 0.5 and 0.2 seconds before it hits, and a 10 second cooldown. *Has 9.17x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.17 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn and Ragdolls. *Its distance is reduced by 60% when used in water. *Can be modified with [[Crystal Lens|Crystal]]/[[Perfect Lens]]es to cause the Mantra to fly farther (at the same pace). *Can be modified with [[Glass Stone|Glass]]/[[Magnifying Stone]]s to increase the hitbox size. **This reduces the damage dealt however. }}
===Power 15===
*Azure Flames [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Many of your flames turn blue, signifying their increased intensity. **Increases burn damage by 12.5%. **Increases the radius and posture damage of your Eruptions. **Increases the uptime of your [[Flame of Denial]] by 25%, from 25 seconds to 31.25. *Scorching Decay [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - The wither dealt from your Emperor's Flame is massively increased. **Increases the Wither application from your Emperor Flame from 25 to 75. **NOTE: This Memento does '''not''' get the Emperor Flame Talent at any point, meaning the only way to proc this Talent is through using [[Pleeksty's Inferno]]'s critical attacks. *{{cl|raretl|Denial Repulse}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - You now emit a delayed burst of flames after coming close to death. **When [[Flame of Denial]] activates, release an explosion around you. **This explosion deals 20 Flamecharm damage with 5 Flamecharm scaling, adding up to 30 Flamecharm damage at 100 Flamecharm. **This cannot be parried nor dodged, but can be blocked, dealing 5 posture damage. **This has a windup of 0.6 seconds. **NOTE: This Memento does '''not''' get the Flame of Denial Mantra at any point, meaning this Talent will do '''nothing'''. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Hell's Judgement (☆☆☆) |image=HellsjudgementVOI.gif |desc=A vicious grasp of flames. Receive a damage buff if you land this attack. |ethercost={{stats|ether|90 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flamecharm|Fire}} |reqs={{c|notes|950}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |effect=''User propels themselves forwards and grabs their foes, immolating them. If this lands, the user gains a damage buff.'' *The damage buff granted by this mantra does not have a time limit and applies to all sources of damage, including each tick of burn. }}
==Boss Unlocks==
===Shogun of the Prophet's Guard=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Ascended Phoenix Flames}} [Memento Talent] - Once per fight, when an attack would down you immediately revive with 30% HP. **This talent doesn't work in [[Zi'eer, the Fourth Prophet|Zi'eer]]'s bossfight ===Dravik, The Rat King=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Pleeksty's Wrath}} [Memento Talent] - After dealing 500 damage with Flame Mantras, call forth a hail of firey swords. (+4 Sanity) **Spawns flaming swords that fall from the sky, similarly to [[First Light]]'s critical attack. ===True Heart of Enmity=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Flames of the Past}} [Memento Talent] - Your flamecharm mantras now call forth firey homing spirits. **Your Flamecharm Mantras now spawn Twisted Puppets' Puppets. *{{iv|i|{{cl|raretl|True Mirage Clone}}}} [Rare Talent] - Successfully dodging leaves behind a heat mirage clone that sets enemies that swung at you on fire. **Has a 20s Cooldown
== Tips == * As the final count of Flamecharm and Medium Weapons in this memento, are 100 and 80 points respectively, it is highly recommended to grab [[Pleeksty's Inferno]] in [[Saramaed Summit (Vow of Iron)|Saramaed Summit]]; especially since it's buffed by the innate talent of [[Simmerbloom Diadem]]. *When fighting the [[Shogun of the Prophet's Guard (Temple of Mur)|Shogun]] and [[Dravik, The Rat King|Dravik]] with the Pleeksty's inferno equipped, they will roll much more often due to each M1 applying burn on hit. Take this in mind when dealing with certain attacks as you must adjust the timing of your attacks for a successful connection. {{Nav|Mementos}} [[Category:Mementos]] [[Category:The Covenant of Flame]]

This Outfit additionally requires the player to be at least [[Power]] 5 to be crafted. ===''Armor Stats''=== This Outfit has 1000 durability, grants {{stats|phys|+10% Physical resistance}}, {{stats|elm|+5% Elemental resistance}}, and {{stats|flm|+25% Fire resistance}}. Additionally, it provides the {{t|Intrepid Flame}} and {{t|One With Flame}} Talents. *Due to resistances being combined multiplicatively instead of additively, the total resistances are: {{stats|phys|10% Physical}}, {{stats|flm|28.75% Flamecharm}}, and {{stats|elm|5% Elemental|flm=n}}. title: Flamecharm
content:
{{Quotes|quote=The inferno burns ever brighter. Have you come to fuel it?|author=Amashi, Master of Flame}}[[File:Flamecharm.png|thumb|Flamecharm Icon]] ==Description== '''Flamecharm''' is an [[Attunement]] that grants the user the ability to create flames using Ether.. These abilities are primarily focused on DOT and AoE effects, while still providing a notable amount of utility and mobility. This Attunement is ideal for new players, due to its innate ability to grip knocked humanoid NPCs with its DOT burn effect, alongside its superior utility in comparison with other Attunements, making progression and exploration much easier. As mentioned previously, Flamecharm focuses on DOT and AoE effects. This Attunement's mantras usually create a large hitbox either around the user or in front of them, making hitting your opponent incredibly easy at close range. To compensate, its mantras rarely propel the user horizontally, with most of its mantras either slowing the user down or preventing movement almost entirely. This makes builds with lots of movement options and range viable against this Attunement, as it limits the amount of mantras you have to worry about. Do note that it does have a couple of options in order to close the distance or deal damage at considerable range, namely Fire Palm, Flaming Scourge modified with Reversal Spark, and the Flame Dancer talents. ==Obtainment== The [[Attunement Trainers|Attunement Trainer]], [[Amashi, Master of Flame|Amashi]], can be located at the [[Songseeker Temple]] in [[Songseeker Wilds]]. Once you give Amashi two Dying Embers, he will hand you the [[Attunement Potions|Hearthblood Potion]] which you must drink in order to obtain the Attunement. Alternatively, you can simply pick the Attunement from Character Creation. ==Training== {{text|att-training |train=using the [[Hearthgem]] to increase the attribute after either landing {{PAGENAME}} Mantras or eating [[Dying Embers]] to gain enough EXP |trainer=[[Amashi]] at [[Songseeker Wilds]] }} ===Mantra Damage Calculation=== {{text|mantracalc}} ==Cantrip(s)== Cantrips are, often minor, passive abilities that are granted upon obtaining any Mantra from the respective Attunement. ===Produce Spark=== This Cantrip allows the player to light [[Campfire]]s without [[Flint]]. This Cantrip is shared with [[Thundercall]], though the sound effect differs based on the Attunement. Produce Spark.gif File:Flame Wisp Flint 1.mp3|Flamecharm Produce Spark SFX {{col|sec|

Mantras

}} ===Combat Mantras=== {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Burning Servants (☆☆☆) |image=Burning Servants.gif |desc=Summon a legion of flaming spearmen that lunge inwards. |ethercost={{stats|ether|30 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flm|Fire}} |reqs=1 Flamecharm |effect=User summons six blazing warriors armed with Halberds in a circle, attacking one after the other in quick succession at the position of the caster, before performing a synchronous strike and disappearing. *Has a base damage of 4/4.4/4.8/5.2/5.6 per level, per hit (6) with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Deals 4 posture damage per hit with an additional 20 posture damage on the final hit. *Has a windup of 0.45s and a cooldown of 10 seconds. *The synchronous strike occurs 2.2 seconds after the mantra is cast. *Has 9.17x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.17 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone]]s and [[Stratus Stone]]s to add more warriors, capping at +9 Range. *Can be modified with a [[Reversal Spark]] to have the warriors attack outwards and ragdoll. This additional Ether cost cannot be reduced. *Has a windup of 0.7 seconds and a cooldown of 10 seconds. *Has 9.18x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 9.18 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Breaks destructible objects on hit. *Can be modified with [[Vibrant Gem]]s, causing the attack to destroy more environment. *While having [[Starkindred]] wings activated, Fire Blade now launches the user upward before releasing a large plume of flames after a long windup. **A [[Reversal Spark]] can be used to negate this variation, allowing you to use normal fire blade with wings. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Fire Gun (☆☆☆) |image=FireGun.gif |desc=A bullet of flames shot through each hand. |ethercost={{stats|ether|10 Ether}} (per shot) |dmgtype={{stats|flm|Fire}} |reqs=1 Flamecharm |effect=Caster draws out and propels bullets of flames from their hands towards the cursor's location. Clicking again while firing will fire additional bullets, at the cost of more Ether. *Has a base damage of 6.5/8.5/10.5/12.5/14.5 per level, per hit with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *Has an initial starting windup of 0.375 seconds and no cooldown. *Deals 1 posture damage per hit. *Has 5.13x PvE scaling (multiply damage dealt by 5.13 for PvE damage). *Inflicts Burn. *Breaks tiles, including the [[Hidden Village]] Door & [[Pathfinder's Respite]] Barricade. *Lights campfires. *Propels the user backward if cast while jumping/walking backward or in water. *Can be modified with [[Drift Shard|Drift]]/[[Rush Shard]]s to make the bullets fly faster + farther. *Can be modified with a [[Round Spark]], causing the bullets to split into two, reducing the base damage by 45%. *Can be modified with a [[Blast Spark]], causing bullets to explode opponents after 6 hits, but reducing the base damage by 25%. Explosion auto grips if the opponent is low. *Can be canceled early through right clicking. If you take damage while charging, you repulse it back. |ethercost={{stats|ether|30 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flm|Fire}} |reqs=1 Flamecharm |effect=User charges up releases an explosion of flames around them. *Has a base damage of 16/18.4/20.8/23.2/25.6/28 with 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *The Spring Spark variant's projectile has a base damage of 14.4/16.56/18.72/20.88/23.04 per level, while the explosion always has a base damage of 17 regardless of Mantra level. Both hits have 2.75 Flamecharm scaling. *The base variant deals 15 posture damage, while the Spring Spark variant deals 6 + 10 posture damage. *The base variant has a windup of 0.7 seconds.
