A player's Mantras are tied to their character's stats - the higher a given stat, the more Mantras you can obtain from that stat. Much like weapons and armor, Mantras can also have 1-3 stars which correlate with their stat requirement and strength. Mantras with higher stars have higher stat requirements.

==Classification of Mantras==
Mantras are divided into various categories based on their general application. By default, you can have up to '''six''' Mantras equipped:

*Combat Mantra (3) - Mantras used for combat. These will be the Mantras you will mainly be using to deal damage to your opponent.
*Support Mantra (1) - Mantras used for utility. Can range from healing, making potions, and all sorts of other things.
*Mobility Mantra (1) - Mantras used for mobility. Your ability to move is increased with these Mantras, allowing you to dash distances, or jump very high.
*Wildcard Mantra (1) - A special slot that can be taken up by '''any other Mantra type'''- if you have an extra Combat, Support, or Mobility Mantra, it will go here.

There is a fifth category of Mantras called Wisp mantras. By default, Wisp Mantras go into your Support Slot, but by getting the Talent {{t|Will O' Wisp}} (Requirement: 25 Element and having any Wisp Mantra), you can slot Wisp Mantras into an unlocked Wisp slot.

It is possible to have more Mantras than Mantra slots, but you will not be able to equip and use all of them at once. Additional Mantra slots can be gained by obtaining an [[Oaths|Oath]], or by getting the Talent {{t|Neuroplasticity}} (for 35 Mind) for an extra Wildcard slot.

== Combat Usage ==
Mantras are a key aspect of combat, and it is incredibly important to master the usage of Mantras while fighting to get the edge over your opponent. You can't get very far with just a weapon and skill alone; Mantras can turn the tide of a battle easily and is what makes Deepwoken's combat very deep and engaging, with various mechanics to accompany them.

=== Mantra Cancelling ===
Mantra Cancelling is exactly what it sounds. You cancel a Mantra, which essentially feints the Mantra you used. Cancelling a Mantra will not put it in cooldown but will still take the Ether required to cast it. To cancel a Mantra, you need to click M2 as soon as you cast it. Mantra Cancelling is extremely effective for Mantras that have a loud SFX, or an obvious start-up, like Gale Lunge or Fire Blade. Most people will fall for it if they are not prepared. A well-placed Mantra cancel can allow you to initiate combos onto your opponent. Some Talents even grant the user certain advantages when cancelling Mantras, such as Galebreathe users being able to Inhale their Mantras for buffs.

=== Ranged Mantras ===
[[File:RobloxStudioBeta_YX0v7URqCG.png|alt=Ranged Mantra Resistance, Green is no scaling while red is where ranged resistance scaling starts and ends, past that, full resistance is applied.|thumb|Ranged Mantra Resistance; Standing from the center of the green circle, there is no scaling, while red is where ranged resistance scaling starts and ends, past the red zone, full resistance is applied.]]
Ranged Mantras are any Mantras that can deal damage from at least 30 studs away, these Mantras have their damage fall off, reaching fully ranged resistance past 60 studs, Certain enemies like the [[Scion of Ethiron]] do not have this resistance while other enemies such as the [[Megalodaunt]]s do have ranged resistance. Humanoid mobs such as the [[Bandit Leader]] can roll and block ranged attacks, but this does not apply to most monster mobs, like the Megalodaunt that cannot block or roll.

=== Ritual Casting ===
Numerous amounts of Support Mantras, namely every Wisp, will require the player to perform a Ritual Cast. When a player uses a Mantra that requires a Ritual Cast, a staff will appear on the screen, prompting the player to press keys that correspond with the current letter from the given list: {{Input|input=Z}}, {{Input|input=X}}, {{Input|input=C}}, and {{Input|input=V}}. Ritual keys added via modifiers will always have the 5th key highlighted in purple, signifying that the key will be randomized for every Ritual Cast.

==Upgrading Mantras==
''Main Article - [[Attunement Trainers]]''

All Mantras can be upgraded from their respective element and trainer or from a [[Mantra Lectern]] (at the cost of spending 50% more notes) as long as you have the points allocated into them. Each 20 points allocated in your element/attribute will allow you to upgrade your Mantra(s).

There are 5 Mantra Levels you can have, starting from Level 1 to Level 5:

*Level 1
*Level 2: (20 Stat points into the required stat) [Upgrade Cost: 100 Notes]
*Level 3: (40 Stat points into the required stat) [Upgrade Cost: 200 Notes]
*Level 4: (60 Stat points into the required stat) [Upgrade Cost: 300 Notes]
*Level 5: (80 Stat points into the required stat) [Upgrade Cost: 400 Notes]
*The total cost to get one Mantra from level 1 to level 5 is 1,000 Notes, but 1500 at the Songwright inside of any guild base.

Each Mantra level gives a damage boost and increases effects from modifiers. The damage boost per level entirely depends on the Mantra in question, and sometimes isn't a linear increase per level. Support Mantras often have their cooldown reduced and duration increased per level. Certain Mantras have different effects at level 5, such as Thunder Kick, Fire Blade, Ice Smash, Shadow Gun, Iron Slam and Champion's Whirlthrow becoming Instant Guardbreaks.

==Modifying Mantras==
''Main Article - [[Mantra Modifiers]]''

To modify a Mantra, the player needs to go to a Mantra Lectern, typically located on populated islands or inside your guild base with the given upgrades.

*At a Mantra Lectern, '''all''' Mantras the person has will be shown to them on a display that pops up.
*After picking a Mantra to modify, '''all''' usable modifiers in the user's inventory will be shown.
**Mantra Modifiers include the following:
***<u>[[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s</u> increase size at the cost of speed.
***<u>[[Crystal Lens|Crystal]]/[[Perfect Lens]]es</u> increase range at the cost of size.
***<u>[[Aeon Logstone|Aeon]]/[[Eternal Logstone]]s</u> increase duration at the cost of range.
***<u>[[Drift Shard|Drift]]/[[Rush Shard]]s</u> increase speed at the cost of duration.
***<u>[[Glass Stone|Glass]]/[[Magnifying Stone]]s</u> increase AoE at the cost of duration.
***<u>[[Vibrant Gem]]s</u>, increasing 'intensity'; this effect is largely regarded as useless and unnoticeable and typically is a waste of a modification.
***<u>Sparks</u>, providing effects to mantra, typically changing how it behaves:
****e.g. Fleeting Sparks with a Blast Spark changes the mantra to chase down and detonate on foes instead of shocking them from range.
**Mantra modifiers, except for Sparks, increase the Ether cost of a Mantra. It is possible for a Mantra to consume most of, if not all, of a players Ether upon one use.
**You can also change the name of a Mantra by clicking on its name while applying modifiers to the said mantra.
***The Talent [[Valikor|Spell Shout]] will make your character shout the name of the Mantra when you use it, or its new name if it was renamed.
**Mantras can also be modified with [[Deep Gems]] by left-clicking while holding the Deep Gem and selecting the mantra you wish to apply the Deep Gem to, providing new effects depending on the gem applied.
*You can identify what modifiers you have on your Mantra by hovering your mouse over it. Including its Ether cost in numbers & percentage, as well as how many signs on a ritual Mantra.

== Mantra Damage Calculation ==
The formula to calculate Mantra damage is as follows:
<math>BaseDamage \times (1 + (\frac{Scaling}{1000} \times Investment \times (1 + Songchant \times 0.075)))</math>

Base damage often increases per Mantra level. Use the Mantra's base damage at its current level in the equation.

*Example 1: Level 5 [[Strong Left]] with 95 Strength and 2 Songchant:
**60 × (1 + (1.65/1000 × 95 × (1 + 2 × 0.075))) = 70.82 damage.
*Example 2: Level 4 [[Gale Lunge]] with 60 Galebreathe and no Songchant:
**16.25 × (1 + (2.75/1000 × 60) = 18.93 damage.

Nearly all [[Attunement-less]] Mantras have 1.65 investment scaling, while most [[Attunement|Attuned]] Mantras have 2.75 scaling, although there are outliers to this.

This formula also works for non-Mantra things, such as Galebreathe Apparitions, granted Songchant only applies to Mantras, so that part of the equation should be left out. This cannot be used to calculate Weapon damage.

'''[https://www.desmos.com/calculator/xoovzbiltk Desmos calculator here].'''

===Oath Mantras===
[[Oath]] Mantras gain +2% damage per Songchant, changing the formula to the following:

<math>BaseDamage \times (1 + (\frac{Scaling}{1000} \times Investment \times (1 + Songchant \times 0.075)) \times (1 + 0.02 \times Songchant))</math>

Note that most Oath Mantras do not have scaling, making the formula as simple as Base damage * (1 + 0.02 * Songchant).

*Example: [[Celestial Assault]] with 80 Strength and 4 Songchant:
**20 × (1 + (1.65/1000 × 80 × (1 + 4 × 0.075)) × (1 + 0.02 × 4)) = 25.3 damage per hit (2), 50.61 damage total.

== Types of Mantras ==
=== [[Flamecharm|Flamecharm Mantras]] ===
Large and threatening fire-based spells. Excels in crowd control and area denial as many spells have large range.

*The Lava Serpent path can be unlocked at 40 Flamecharm, dealing flat damage and ragdolling instead of applying [[burn]].
*Can be further upgraded with the {{t|Azure Flame}} Talent for increased burn damage and larger Eruptions.
*Has a hybrid path with [[Shadowcast]] called "Wraith Path: Twisted Puppets". More info can be found [[Hybrid Abilities#Flamecharm|here]].
*Has a hybrid path with [[Frostdraw]] called “Flashboil,” or “Steam Path.”

=== [[Thundercall|Thundercall Mantras]] ===
Thundercall utilizes fast and quickly regenerating spells to take a fight at any desired pace. Has spells with somewhat small start-up for closing distance or keeping an opponent on edge.

*Surge path can be obtained at 40 Thundercall. This replaces your [[Shock]] with applying [[Status Effects#Overloaded|Surge Rods]], a stacking status effect that causes a surge overload once enough stacks have been applied, dealing Thundercall damage.
*The Set Talent ''Shock Trooper Specialist'' turns your Thundercall Mantras green, allowing them to strike lightning on your opponent by landing [[Galebreathe]] and [[Thundercall]] Mantras.
*Most Thundercall Mantras have spark variants.

=== [[Frostdraw|Frostdraw Mantras]] ===
Uses ice to freeze enemies and create physical obstructions, allowing the user to both navigate the world easier and create terrain in combat.

*Can slow opponents, temporarily freeze them, or make barriers forcing opponents to go around.
*Glass Path: Crystallization can be unlocked at 40 Frostdraw. This replaces your [[Chill]] with [[Status Effects#Crystals|Crystals]], a stacking status effect that causes a crystal detonation once enough stacks have been applied, dealing Frostdraw damage. Unlocks the use of the [[Crystal Impale]], [[Ice Lasers]], and [[Crystal Knee]] Mantras.
*Most Frostdraw Mantras have spark variants.
*Has a hybrid path with [[Flamecharm]] called Flashboil or “Steam Path.”

=== [[Galebreathe|Galebreathe Mantras]] ===
Galebreathe utilizes the elements for movement, defense, and offensive actions.

*It has a mix of close-range combo Mantras, along with multiple movement Talents for moving around the world.
*Haunted Path: Specter can be unlocked at 40 Galebreathe. Specter Path replaces your [[Suffocation]] procs with Apparitions and greater mobility.
*Applies [[Winded]], slowing the attack speed of your opponent.
*The Set Talent ''Shock Trooper Specialist'' turns your Galebreathe Mantras yellow, allowing them to strike lightning on your opponent by landing [[Galebreathe]] and [[Thundercall]] Mantras.
*Applies [[Suffocation]], disabling your opponent's ability to cast Mantras. Innately procs by landing the [[Wind Gun]] and [[Galetrap]] Mantras, though it can be procced through Talents such as {{t|A World Without Song}}.

=== [[Shadowcast|Shadowcast Mantras]] ===
Uses dark energy to siphon Ether from others into the user's own Ether.

*Excels in keeping your Ether bar up and making sure others have low Ether.
*Drains your opponent's Ether when you land Shadowcast Mantras.
*Applies [[Status Effects#Obscured|Obscured]] if you have the "Sightless Still" talent, obscuring the vision of the opponent.
*Has a hybrid path with [[Flamecharm]] called "Wraith Path: Twisted Puppets". More info can be found [[Hybrid Abilities#Shadowcast|here]].

=== [[Ironsing|Ironsing Mantras]] ===
Ironsing provides the widest ranged Mantras in the game and the best damage output based on your opponent's mistakes and missteps.

*Offers Mantras that favor the user, resupplying their armor durability during fights whilst reducing the opponents
*Applies metal rods on hit, which can be pulled to pull the target towards you. Several Talents augment the functionality of these rods.
*Gilded Path: Scrapsinger can be obtained at 35 Ironsing. This path allows you to consume your rods on flourish, siphoning your opponent's armor and proccing the Scrapsinger Talent tree.
*Tunes in well with the [[Metal]] enchantment, as Metal gives you benefits depending on how much armor your opponent has.

=== [[Bloodrend|Bloodrend Mantras]] ===
Harvest the blood of yourself and your enemies to hinder them and empower your mantras and abilities.

*Weaken your enemies with [[Blood Poison]], applying various debuffs and priming your opponent for your Talents.
*Can drain your opponent's blood, sometimes causing them to die before their health depletes.

=== [[Hybrid Mantras]] ===
Hybrid mantras are obtained upon reaching the required level in multiple Attunement attributes, they provide unique opportunities to mix the capabilities of multiple elemental effects.

*Can provide powerful synergies between Attunements allowing use of certain Talents and paths in unique ways.
*Versatility due to their ability to inherit the effects of two Attunement paths such as Surge and Wraith Path.
*Typically requires high investment into your [[Attunement]] attributes.

=== [[Attunement-less|Physical/Attunement-less Mantras]]===
There are Mantras that are based off of Core Attributes, rather than your [[Attunement]]. This includes Strength, Fortitude, Intelligence, Agility, Willpower, Charisma, and Weapon Mastery.

A Mantra's type generally corresponds to its respective stat. Weapon Mantras and Strength Mantras tend to have more offensive capabilities, while Charisma and Fortitude lean more towards debuffing and supporting. Intelligence, Agility, and Willpower Mantras are more or less split between the two roles.

=== [[Monster Mantras]] ===
Mantras you get by turning in monster parts to an NPC in Castle Light. To get the NPC to spawn you talk to "Strange Diver" in [https://deepwoken.fandom.com/wiki/Second_Layer/New_Kyrsa New Kyrsa] After that the NPC will spawn in the library in Castle Light. The monster parts are fairly rare. These are the monster parts, their respective monster, the name of the Mantra and what is the Mantra is based off of:

*Megalodaunt -> Megalodaunt Coral -> Coral Spear (Thousand Needles)
*Dread Serpent -> Dread Serpent's Tooth -> Dread Breath (Dread's Ice Beam)
*Thresher -> Thresher Talons -> Beast Burrow (Thresher's Dig)
*Bone Keeper -> Giant Femur -> Brachial Spear (Bone Throw)
*Enforcer -> Enforcer's Eye -> Enforcer Pull
*Mechalodaunt -> Broken Gatling Gun -> Mecha Gatling (Bullet Fury)
*Nautilodaunt -> Nautilodaunt Beak ->  Abyssal Ridge (Grand Stomp)
*Terrapod -> Terrapod Shell -> Whirling Blade (Original Mantra)
*Interluminary Parasol -> Charged Parasol Part -> Abyssal Tendrils (Pierce)
*Turn in the [[Kyrsan Necklace]] to [[The Gaunt Man]]-> Charged Bonecharm -> Bone Wisp (Original Mantra)

'''NOTE: MONSTER MANTRAS CANNOT BE TRADED AT THE SHRINE OF TEMPTATION'''

All Mantras gained from the npc are 2 star Mantras and some have special effects, for example, Dread Breath proccing Chill, and also proccing Crystals if you have the respective Frostdraw path. This also goes for Mecha Gatling, as it procs Fire and will proc Lava Serpent eruptions as a result if you have the respective path. Keep in mind that these are rare mob drops and may require alot of grinding to obtain some certain ones

===[[Oaths|Oath Mantras]]===
Mantras you obtained through your Oath. Although it lacks the trainers to help level your Oath's Mantras, its exclusive abilities and uniqueness makes up for it.

==Trivia==

*Mantras ''can'' be leveled beyond the normal limit of 5, but only via developer interaction.
*Many places refer to Mantras as the Song or fragments of the Song, i.e Orlandeau during the [[Tutorial]] or the description of the [[Songseeker Temple]].
**According to [[Kaide, the Drowned Light]], Mantras are "A cheap imitation of the power held within the Song that Drowned Gods wield as their birthright", implying that they are an inferior form of the song's true power, which aren't intended for humanity
*Elemental Intensity, a now removed stat, once affected the damage of certain Mantras.

These point out your current location, the location of allies, and most landmarks in the current map, as well as NPCs like Antiquarians or Smiths in your area. The map also shows cardinal directions. Some locations (e.g. [[Beloved Zofia]], [[Boatman's Watch]], [[Moon's Eyrie|Moons Eyrie]]) are in the [[Voidsea]] and thus not mapped at all. The [[Vow of Iron|Iron Vow]] gamemode has a separate [[Boundary|map]]. title: Marauder's Entrance
content:
{{Location|name=Marauder's Entrance|caption=Hewn into rock, the ritual mechanism shudders. Scattered papers and schemes flit by in the current.}}
[[File:MaraudersEntranceLarge.png|thumb|900px|center]]
'''Marauder's Entrance''' is a location in the [[First Layer]] of [[The Depths]]. It is one of the starting locations for the [[Deepbound]] origin.

==Overview==
Marauder's Entrance is a location in the [[First Layer]] of [[The Depths]],  located at a side of the map near the [[District of Commerce]]. The way to Marauder's Entrance has a small parkour section, which is quite simple. The kill-bricks/void are lowered, and there are places to soften your fall and help you get up if you make a mistake. However if you aren't hesitant you will either wipe or go to [[Second Layer|Layer 2]], depending on your power and level.

After entering, there is a hall inside which is where [[Diluvian Mechanism (NPC)|The Diluvian Mechanism]] is located, You can find training equipment here. Upon conversing with the mechanism, you'll go within it and [[The Diluvian Mechanism|face trials of strength and willpower]], that reward great amounts of treasure. 

== Contents ==

=== Main Entrance ===
* Houses two [[Training Gear|Gear Cabinets]] on both sides. 
* There are bookshelves at the right side, which can be inspected for [[Books]].

=== Large Hallway ===
* Going forward, the Diluvian Mechanism can be found within the center of the large hall.

==Gallery==
<gallery>
File:Marauder's Entrance's Entrance..png|The EX Resonance Door leading to Marauder's Entrance
File:Marauder's Entrance Parkour.png|The way towards Marauder's Entrance
File:ResonanceDoorOpenedMarauder's.png|The Resonance Door leading to Marauder's Entrance after being interacted with
File:Inside of Marauder's Entrance.png|Inside of the Marauder's Entrance
File:Aga doing boss rush inside marauders .png|Agamatsu doing a boss rush inside Marauder's Entrance.
</gallery>

== Trivia ==

* The Marauder's Entrance was one of the most abandoned places in the depths, with most players never coming close to it. It used to have a resonance door but now is replaced with a hallway to the Diluvian Mechanism. Allowing any level to test their strength.
* The parkour area used to be very buggy, and had the kill-bricks and void on the same height or even higher as the obstacles, which meant many players had void-snapped to [[Second Layer|Layer 2]] or wiped.
* Marauder's Entrance was a massive mystery, during verse one and (part of) verse two, until The Dilluvian Mechanism was added.

== Description ==
Marcus is inarguably the ''coolest'' [[Stonespark]], if not the '''coolest''' [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]] (apart from [[The Meat Lord]]), in this vast game of ''[[Deepwoken (game)|Deepwoken]]''. He is of a ''modest'' and ''small'' size, unlike his '''braggart [[Rock Golem]]''' cousins, and ''calm'' and ''collected'' compared to his '''belligerent [[Stonespark]]''' siblings, who prefer to attack you on sight. He prefers relaxing over a nice warm beverage.

The only entity that could surpass Marcus' incomprehensible power would be [[The Meat Lord]], as both have risen to levels '''above''' the powers of [[:Category:Drowned Gods|Drowned Gods]].

Although Marcus does not give any rewards, XP, loot or even gameplay advice to the player, it's always great to talk to him as he is '''undoubtedly''', '''hands down''', the  '''most chill''' NPC in '''all''' of Deepwoken.

==Location==
When entering [[The Hidden Village]], go to the right side and through a hallway to find a [[Campfire]] and [[Rotskipper]]. When reaching the [[Campfire]] spot, looking to your left; there will be a house that has a crawl space under it. Inside the space there will be a hole, jumping into the hole will take you to the humble cave Marcus lives in. 

Make sure to say hello, and give some company to such a [[Stonespark]]. What a great guy, '''right'''?

==Description==
Maria was an [[Etrean]] soldier who served alongside [[Arthur]] during an expedition to investigate unusual [[Megalodaunt]] activity in [[Erisia]]. She is described as exceptionally brave. <ref name="Gamma">{{Ref/NPC|Arthur|quote=My.. I was sent on an expedition. Myself and a team of other Etrean soldiers. There were reports of an unnatural number of Megalodaunts surfacing here, and we were sent, but.. It turned out too much for use to handle.}}</ref>

During the expedition, Maria was killed by [[Megalodaunt]]'s after the group was attacked. While she fought courageously, [[Arthur]] was unable to act due to fear, leading to her death and becoming the source of his deep regret. <ref>{{Ref/NPC|Arthur|quote=I unfortunately am. I was with a team of three, one of my members being.. someone close to me. A fellow soldier, always brave, Maria. S-She didn't make it. We were surrounded, and I.. I couldn't move an inch. I was frozen in terror.. I can't get her screams out of my head. It haunts me. I feel like a coward. I could've done something but..}}</ref>

==Description==
[[Markor]] is a savannah region in [[Luminants#The Central Luminant|the Central Luminant]], the homeland of [[Felinor]],<ref name="Studies">{{Ref/Book|Studies on Canticlysm, Vol. IV}}</ref> and currently a territory conquered by [[the Central Authority]].<ref name="ScimitarDesc">{{Ref/WeaponDescription|Scimitar}}</ref>

Along with the [[Felinor]] originating from here, Markor is also the origin of [[scimitar]]s and similar blades.<ref name="ScimitarDesc" /> The Sea Highways also come from here, made by a company of [[Thundercall]]ers, known as [[the Golden Link]].

==Contents==
[[The Citadel of Markor]]: One of, if not the most prominent research organization in all of the [[Lumen]], led by [[the High Convocation]]. With the funding of [[The Central Authority]], they pride themselves as the foremost keepers of knowledge, history, and research into [[Lumen]] and the surrounding [[The Depths|Depths]]. [[The Divers]] originally were a branch of the Citadel.<ref name="GlossCitadel">{{Ref/Glossary|The Citadel of Markor}}</ref>

[[Felinor fieldfolk]]: A kingdom of [[Felinor]] was once located in Markor. However, it is hinted that this kingdom is no more.

Retain the same swing speed and damage your Markor's Inheritor had. You gain more swingspeed the more Intelligence you have. }} ==Description== Markor's Inheritor is a [[Weapons|Heavy Greatsword]] that requires 30 HVY and 10 STR. This weapon showcases the user's martial arts prowess by allowing them to utilize their [[Fists|combat styles]]. ==Talents== {{text|wtal}} Upon landing your weapon critical, {{etal|weapon|Blade Scholar}} procs, swapping your weapon to [[Iron Cestus]]/[[Anklets of Alsin]] for 15 seconds. While active, your base damage will bet set to 24, and scaling to 7 Heavy Weapons and 2 Intelligence. The increased scaling from [[Alloyed Inheritor|{{cl|alloyed|Alloyed Inheritor}}]] does '''not''' apply. Additionally, your swing speed will be set to 0.85x, but you will gain +0.002x swing speed for every point in [[Intelligence]], capping at 1.05x swing speed at 100 Intelligence. All other stats will be the same as the Cestus. The stat changes are handled internally, and will not be displayed on your weapon tooltip. This effect is not refreshable, requiring you to land another critical attack ''after'' the effect ends to reapply it. However, using [[Blightsurger]]'s Sovereign State during the effect will extend the prolong the duration of Blade Scholar until your Sovereign State ends. Quality stars on your Inheritor do not carry over when Blade Scholar activates, but [[Enchantments]] do. This manually changes your weapon to Fists on proc. This has a few upsides and downsides; *'''{{cl|ligreen|Upsides}}''': **You'll be able to benefit from Fist and Light Weapon Talents while it is active, as well as the Fists PvE effect of increased blunt damage, scaling on the amount of Fists Talents you have. *'''{{cl|lired|Downsides}}''': **You cannot proc your Greatsword or Heavy Talents while active. **Your Range and other stats that aren't explicitly carried over by this Talent will be the same as the [[Iron Cestus]]/[[Anklets of Alsin]], being reduced compared to the Inheritor. **If you do not have a [[Fist Style]], you will equip [[Untrained Fist]], halving your weapon damage while active. *'''{{cl|liorange|Other}}''': **Your [[Silentheart]] abilities will change to the Light Weapon ones while this is active. This isnt inherently an upside nor a downside, but keep in mind that these abilities scale on the respective attribute. ==Critical== Markor's Inheritor will inherit the critical attack of your last used [[Fists|Fist Style]], allowing for a large amount of build diversity. If you do not have a fist style, then [[Untrained Fist]]'s critical will be used. {{DefaultCritFists|nh|Both}} ==Gallery== Markor's Inheritor Full View.png|Full view Alloyed Markor's Inheritor Full View.png|Full view (Alloyed) Markor's Inheritor Full.png|Full view (Old) Alloyed Markor's Inheritor Full.png|Full view (Alloyed) (Old) ===Enchantments=== File:Umbral Obsidian Nether Portal Markor.png|Umbral Knight File:Makror inehr.png|Metal File:Markoring Inerhriting I'md runk.png|Curse of The Bloodthirsty File:Sonic.exe fnf mod build roleplay.png|Detonation File:InheritorHeroism.png|Heroism File:InheritorNLK.png|Curse of the No-Life King File:Image 2025-12-24 151329037.png|Curse of Yun'Shul ==Trivia== *The [[Gatherhand]] inscibed on the Markor's Inheritor says "Ignorance be thy tomb. To wander without wit is to stray into a battlefield without blade" *Markor's Inheritor can use the [[Jade Vigil's Weave]] [[Fang and Coil]] critical, which is uncommon, even amongst fist weapons. *Markor's Inheritor is the only Heavy weapon that has an aerial kick as an aerial attack. Heavies used to have fist-style aerial attacks, until a unique heavy aerial was added. *It can proc Fist Talents on critical, even if Blade Scholar is not active. {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Criticals with M1 tag]] [[Category:Greatswords]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Criticals]] [[Category:Weapons of The Central Authority]] [[Category:Alloyable Weapons]] [[Category:Heavy Weapons]] [[Category:Authority Faction Item]] [[Category:Weapons with Talents]]

title: Marro
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{NPCInfobox
|title1=Marro
|image1=Marro.png
|name=Marro
|affiliation=[[The Moonlit Faith]]
|aspect=Chrysid
|pronouns=He/him
|location=[[Songseeker Wilds]]}}

==Description==
Marro is a [[Chrysid]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]] who resides on the islands of [[Songseeker Wilds]]. He is found sitting near the mine entrance trying to find something for his village's Elder. When talking to him, he tells us a little about the culture of his people and especially about the Chrysid Elders and their characteristics.

==Dialogue==
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="12" |Hum, hum...
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |What are you doing here?
|-
| colspan="12" |Ah! Excuse me. I'm simply looking for little knick knacks for my Elder. He requested, ah... something full of life.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Elder?
|-
| colspan="12" |Elder of our little community out here. Traditionally, elders are given their title once they're considered 'blessed with true wisdom', as evident by their neck manes - but we ain't really ones to stick to that tradition out here.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |What do you mean?
|-
| colspan="12" |You may have heard tales of the {{g|The Lullaby Isles|Lullaby Isles}}... the Moonlit Faith... all that sort. We're kinda like that, but we do things our own way. Every one of us from our little community hails from that place. Whether they left out of anger, sadness, or pure curiosity - they're all welcome.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Why did you leave the Lullaby Isles?
|-
| colspan="12" |Had a tiny spat with a scholarmate of mine. Nothing serious, just some choice words said. He absolutely did not take it well - threatened to name me a heretic! Blackmail me over ''nothing''! And well... If you don't know what happens to heretics... It ain't pretty. So, I hopped out. Decided to find my own way without fearing for my life, 'cause of some reckless idiot. Best choice I've ever made.
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|action}} |Have spoken to [[Lake]]
| colspan="6" {{cl|action}} |Have not spoken to [[Lake]]
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Was it your community that Lake spoke to?
| colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="6" |''He breaks into a guffaw, grinning.*'' That one won't survive a minute out here - I'm convinced she believes this is the {{g|The Lullably Isles|Lullably Isles}}, and that she's only a five minute walk from home. Don't think she really gets that she ain't seeing that family of hers again - they ''don't'' let people back in, unless your leave is sanctioned by the Faith, y'know?. And she didn't take nicely to us trying to help her out, either. But... I mean, not every Chrysid adapts well to the outside world. She's definitely that sort.
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

==Trivia==
*Marro's racial variant appears to be Seer.

Calling these 'comfortable' feels charitable. And yet, holding them, you cannot help but feel your bones itch, and the ground beneath you quiver... |pass down=No |enchantable=Only if the boss drops it enchanted.}} ==Description== The '''Marrowmade Boots''' are an '''unenchantable''' [[Equipment]] item under the "Legs" category. They are boots seemed to be made from the foot and head of a [[Bonekeeper]]. The {{t|Surestep}} Talent makes you immune to the ragdoll and flinging effect of the winds of the Second Layer. You are still affected by the harsh winds' movement debuffs. The {{t|Osseous Surge}} Talent make it so when flourishing an enemy enhances the boots for 10 seconds. During this time, the wearer can right-click to release a wave of bones forward damaging and ragdolling enemies upward infront of them (The boot's Osseous Surge talent deals 30 PvP damage and 180 PvE Damage). This attack is parryable and jumpable, but guardbreaks and is undodgeable. The {{t|Osseous Surge}} effect can be proc'ed via the mantras Razor Blitz, Master's Flourish(with vigil longsword), along with Executioner offhand gun shots so it's not exclusive to base flourishes. ==Gallery== File:Gif of boots.gif|Osseous Surge ==Trivia== *These boots have an extremely small chance to be [[Enchantments|Enchanted]] when obtained. *The damage increases by 50% going from 30 to 45 with the [[Bone Ring]]. *It's previous description read: "Boots crafted from what seems to be the foot and head of the [[Bonekeeper]]. {{History}} {{Nav|equipment}} [[Category:Equipment]] [[Category:Legs]] [[Category:Boots]] [[Category:Equipment with Talents]] [[Category:Equipment with Exclusive Talents]]

{{text|wtal}}

|death=Eaten by the parasites of the [[Second Layer]]<ref name="Journal III" />
|deathdate=1272 CE<ref>{{Deep dates|Verse2}}</ref>
|image1=Mauled Diver Corpse 2.png}}

==Description==
The Mauled Diver Corpse is an [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. It is the lifeless body of Apprentice Hero.

The player is able to pocket the [[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Hero]] left behind by the corpse.

Apprentice Hero was a [[The Divers|Diver]] participating in the third expedition to the [[Second Layer]], sent by [[Klaris]] to retrieve the [[Black Divers division|Black Diver]], [[Chaser]], and the original team.<ref name="Journal III" />

In [[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Hero|his Journal]] he wrote about his last experiences with [[Chaser]] cutting off any food supply for his expedition team and forbidding them from entering [[The Frontier Furnace|territory]] of [[the Ignition Union]].<ref name="Journal III" />

This resulted in Hero resorting to eating eggs of the [[Second Layer]]'s parasites. They knew what happens to those, who get infested with parasites, but couldn't help themselves. They wrote their last thoughts before they turned into a [[Diver Husk|husk of themselves]].<ref name="Journal III" />

They were later mauled by a Bounder.

==Dialogue==
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="3" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="3" |''*A lone body lays abandoned in the wasteland. Deep claw marks are seen on its back, and a journal is attached to the hip.*''
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |[Read the Journal]
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |[Investigate claw marks]
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |Secrets are best left to the dead
|-
| colspan="1" |''*You find only one legible entry among the tattered pages, and pocket it to read later.*''
| colspan="1" |''*Deep gashes creating elegant lines decorate the body. They're beast-like in nature, with an extreme depth to each cut. A sense of dread washes over you, almost as if you were in the gaze of a predator.*''
| colspan="1" |''*You leave the body alone*''
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], player obtains [[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Hero]]
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

==Trivia==
*The description of the corpse says it was slashed across the back, but the wounds are very clearly across the front.
*Despite all signs pointing to Hero being killed by parasites, the corpse doesn't show any symptoms of such. They instead appear to have been killed while running from a Bounder. This oddity was preserved even after the Diver Journals were rewritten into the Diver's Journals.

content:
'' This might have not been the page you were looking for, if you were looking for a different page, view the [[Megalodaunt_(disambiguation)|disambiguation]].'' {{Quotes|quote=*Kzzt!* This one's REALLY nicked. *Kzzt.*|author=Mechalodaunt}} {{Monster Infobox|title1=Mechalodaunt |image1=Mechalodaunt.png |attacks=*Slash *Kick *Blazing Kick *Jump *Roar *Thousand Needles *Bullet Fury *Laser Explosion *Finisher: Curb Stomp |locations=*[[Miner's Landing]] *[[Saramaed Crossing]] *[[Saramaed Hollow]] *[[Saramaed Summit]] |drops= *[[Umbral Obsidian]] *[[Ore|Erisore]] *[[Ore|Irithine]] *[[Worn Cog]] *[[Mantra Modifiers]] *[[Broken Gatling Gun]] *[[Megalodaunt Coat]] |health=3500 8750 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |challenges= {{bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}}}} ==Description== The Mechalodaunt is a weapon produced by [[The Ignition Union]] by enhancing [[Megalodaunt]]s with iron shells, machinery and a powerful shoulder-mounted gatling gun. They are found in [[Saramaed Summit]], later stages of the [[Saramaed Hollow]] and [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. They are unfinished and were activated prematurely by [[The Summer Company]], thus defaulting to their natural behavior, resulting in them attacking both "friend" and foe.[[Parsnip]] However, it seems that some Mechalodaunts have been brought back under control, as some can be seen communicating through some sort of radio speaker system when being [[Faction Ambushes|ambushed]] by one. ==Attacks== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description !Media |- |
'''Slash'''
(★☆☆) |A short range swipe using their arms. Can slash once or twice, and if once can be paired with '''Kick'''. *Heavy posture damage. Will commonly block break after two hits. *If the Megalodaunt slashes twice, it will take longer to attack again. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Normal sharko swing.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} will wind up its right leg back with a red circle effect before delivering a kick that ragdolls and sends the player flying. *Causes the player to be [[Status Effects#Dazed|Dazed]] if kicked into a wall. *It will take longer to attack again after using this. *Uses '''Bite''' instead if in water. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll.true |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Normal sharko watch your tone.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Blazing Kick'''
(★★★) |Starts similarly to '''Kick''', except it will start with a distinct whistle-like sound and it will hold its kick for about half an extra second, setting hit targets on fire. *Causes the player to be [[Status Effects#Dazed|Dazed]] if kicked into a wall. *It will take longer to attack again after using this. *Uses '''Bite''' instead if in water. {{AttackTags |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll.true |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Thousand Needles'''
(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} bends over and points its metal tubes towards an opponent, spewing a large and constant spray of bullets at anyone in front of/around it for a second. *Lasts as long as auto-parry frames, meaning you can simply parry once to parry the whole attack. *There is a shorter-ranged AoE version and a longer-ranged single-target version. Both function the same. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Normal sharko coral.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Bullet Fury'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} holds its shoulder-mounted cannon before rapidly firing it at an opponent. *Has very limited range. *It can sometimes turn around and miss it altogether. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, autogrip |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Furnace Explosion'''
(★★★) |The {{PAGENAME}} will spin around, marking a glowing round area around itself with a laser, creating a fiery explosion after a small delay. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.n, dodge.y, ragdoll }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Roar'''
(★☆☆) |Lets out a roar at nearby targets, inflicting [[Insanity]] and [[Status Effects#Fear|Fear]]. *Usually used as the {{PAGENAME}}'s first move. *Blocking negates much of but not all the Insanity gain. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, debuff |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Normal sharko rawr.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Jump'''
(☆☆☆) |If the target is above it, the {{PAGENAME}} will jump in the direction of its opponent to close the distance. Often used after '''Kick''', as well as frequently using '''Furnace Explosion''' after jumping. {{AttackTags |unharmful, movement }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Bite'''
(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} leans forward and bites down, ragdolling those hit. Only used while in water. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Fireproof''' - {{PAGENAME}}s automatically extinguish [[burn]]. ==Finisher== {|class="fandom-table" ! Name !Description |- |'''Curb Stomp''' |The {{PAGENAME}} ends its opponent's life by delivering a stomp onto their bodies with a gruesome crunch. This happens in less than a second. This attack has an AOE effect which can be parried similar to the [[Rock Golem]]'s stomp. |} ==Tips== The {{PAGENAME}}'s unique moves do a lot of damage, but are relatively easy to parry and dodge. The recommended Power for these is 15-20 due to the sheer damage output they can have, easily ending lower leveled players in a few attacks. It is important to know the distinction between '''Kick''' and '''Blazing Kick''', as missing either your dodge or your block can result in heavy unwanted damage. Mechalodaunts in the [[Saramaed Summit]] often spawn in groups of two, only spawning a chest after both have been defeated. Its recommended that you are careful when exploring the area as alerting both Mechalodaunts can make them significantly more difficult to kill off. They are relatively easy to deal with by going past doorways, which they are too big to pass through, and by setting up campfires to heal with when retreating. This can also be done in Saramaed Summit, however due to the fact that [[Voidzones]] cause all Campfires to last significantly less and reduce all healing, this strategy is much less effective. ==Trivia== *Mechalodaunts probably have a radio built into them, as if you were to get ambushed by one it can say "*Kzzt!* This one's REALLY nicked. *Kzzt.*" Alternatively, they could also have the ability to talk, although this is probably not true. *The machinery on them are references to themes of industrial machinery and steampunk. *They give 1 [[Knowledge]] the first time you defeat them. ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Ambush Enemies]] [[Category:The Ignition Union]] [[Category:Ignition Union Enemies]]

==Description==
Meemaw is a [[Felinor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. She is a miner and the grandmother of [[Lucien]].

==Location==
Meemaw is located at [[Songseeker Wilds]], standing outside of the mineshaft.
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
Meemaw Map.png
</gallery>

==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{{#tag:tabber|Quest Start=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Oh, blast it! Blast it!!! Those ''villains'', those... '''''brutes!''''' I can't believe this. Damn it all!
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What happened?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Those blasted mudskippers. Mm, no, worse yet! These... ''mineskippers'' barged into our operation, made a mess of things, settled in like they've been livin' here and paying rent for years, tore most of my crew to pieces... And now, everything's in shambles!
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Are they still there?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Gods, yes! Those varmints are still in there. They even took our hats! Can you believe it? Our hats!!! Who takes a person's '''hat''' like that?!? Oh, and, I guess all the killin' was pretty rude, too. I barely got out of the slaughter with my hide intact. This'll be my lucky hat, I reckon. Good heirloom, that!..
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I could clear them out for you.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Yeah? You've got some fightin' spirit, young'un! I appreciate the kind gesture, really, I do. Tell ya what - if you can clear out them there ''PESTS'' in the minds, I'll teach ya' one of my special recipes. ''*She winks.*''
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Sounds good.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She lets out a determined war-cry.*'' {{sh|Hawwww}}! Get in there, young'un! Come back to me when they're all {{sh|dead and buried}}! I'll have somethin' cookin' for ya by then!
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], quest begins

{{!}}-{{!}}Quest End=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Have ya done it? Have you cleared out this mines yet?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Mineskippers cleared
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Mineskippers not cleared
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I took care of the mineskippers.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}My apologies, ma'am. I am yet to purge the mineskippers.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She hoots and hollers with excitement.*'' {{sh|HAWWWWWW}}! Shucks, stranger, ain't you just sweet as molasses! Now, I'm a woman of my word, aren't I? So, here. My ''best and finest'' recipe: Iron Bombs! All it takes is two pieces of iron, and a piece of coal. Light the fuse, throw it at someone you don't like, and {{sh|BOOM!}} That kinda cookin' will blow anyone away. Literally!
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Shucks buster, young'un! Don't tarry now, y'hear? I've got somethin' special cooking for ya for all the trouble. Trust me, it'll be worth it!
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], [[Iron Bomb]] recipe learned
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
}}

title: Megalodaunt
content:
'' This might have not been the page you were looking for, if you were looking for a different page, view the [[Megalodaunt_(disambiguation) | disambiguation]].'' {{Topbuttons|p, [[Megalodaunt/Gallery|Gallery]]}} {{Quotes|quote=[...] There's something marvelous about these creatures, some sort of almost mankind-like understanding between each other. Yet, to us, they are simply considered 'monsters.' You all fail to see it's social prowess, without not even a consideration of the possibilities; what if we were able to exploit this hierarchy for our own purpose? [...]|author=Archivist Journal: 'Megalodaunt'}} {{Monster Infobox |attacks=*Slash *Kick *Jump *Roar *Finisher: Stomp |health=900
350 {{To1Color|(Trial of One)}}
2250 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |drops=*[[Megalodaunt Hide]] *[[Mantra Modifiers]] *[[Umbral Obsidian]] *[[Megalodaunt Coral]] (Rare) *[[Megalodaunt Coat]] (Rare) |locations=*[[Erisia]] *[[First Layer]] *[[The Aratel Sea]] *Using [[Megalodaunt Bait]] *[[The Diluvian Mechanism]] *[[Saramaed Hollow]] |challenges= {{Bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}} |image1=WitheraldSharko3.png}} ==Description== The Megalodaunt (also referred to as Sharko) is a giant humanoid shark [[Monsters|monster]] most commonly found in [[Erisia]], in burning boats on [[The Aratel Sea]], and in [[The Depths]]. {{Quotes|quote=While not appearing to be reasonably intelligent creatures, they have a strong sense of social hierarchy, and their place in their 'society,' if it could be called that.|author=Archivist Journal: 'Megalodaunt'}} Megalodaunts are particularly known for being social creatures, evident by how a Megalodaunt can become an Alpha within a pack, though they are more often observed to be alone rather than the contrary. They are bipedal creatures with pale skin and a set of corals growing on their back, which are observed to only be used for offensive purposes. Documented as Carnivores, they have traits that matches this nature, featuring two sets of sharp teeth in their mouth, as well as durable hides and impressive looking claws. They can also be seen eating the corpse of an Authority Soldier, solidifying the fact that it is a carnivore. There is a quest in Upper Erisia located at the entrance to the Garden Reservoir where you will be tasked with killing a Megalodaunt, which will reward you with two Talents, Engage at Power 3 and Critical Attack at Power 5. This quest can be completed/recompleted if you already have the Talents to receive 1-2 hands of cards. Seen mostly around the island of [[Erisia]], the Megalodaunt is one of the first monsters, along with [[Mudskipper]]s, that most new players will encounter. Players that are ill-equipped or lack insight on this monster are mostly likely going to succumb to it within seconds. Megalodaunts are naturally hostile to every other creature in ''[[Locations|The Etrean Luminant]]'', and will attack them on sight for purposes both survival and territorial. They are never observed quarrelling with each other as of yet, though curiously enough, treats the Crimson Variant of Megalodaunt with extreme prejudice, mercilessly attacking them as if they are an 'outcast'. Upon being slain, it drops [[Megalodaunt Hide]] and Mantra Modifiers, with a low chance of the modifiers being high-tier. It will also uncommonly drop [[Umbral Obsidian]]. On rare occasions, it may drop a [[Megalodaunt Coral]] or a [[Megalodaunt Coat]]. In addition to be found wandering around various places or loitering around in selected caves and locations, they can also be lured with the use of a [[Megalodaunt Bait]]. ==Attacks== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description !Media |- |
'''Slash'''
(★☆☆) {{AttackTags |slash }}
|A short range swipe using their arms. Can slash once or twice, and if once can be paired with '''Kick''', which counts as its own move. *Heavy posture damage. Will commonly block break after two hits. *If the Megalodaunt slashes twice, it will take longer to attack again. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} | [[File:Normal sharko swing.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★☆) {{AttackTags |blunt }}
|The {{PAGENAME}} will wind up its right leg back with a red circle effect before delivering a kick that ragdolls and sends the player flying. *Causes the player to be [[Status Effects#Dazed|Dazed]] if kicked into a wall. *It will take longer to attack again after using this. *Uses '''Bite''' instead if in water. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll.true |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Normal sharko watch your tone.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Roar'''
(★☆☆) |Lets out a roar at nearby targets, inflicting [[Insanity]] and [[Status Effects#Fear|Fear]]. *Usually used as the {{PAGENAME}}'s first move. *Blocking negates much of but not all the Insanity gain. *Dangerous in [[The Depths]]. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, debuff |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Normal sharko rawr.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Jump'''
(☆☆☆) |If the target is above it, the {{PAGENAME}} will jump in the direction of its opponent to close the distance. Often used after '''Kick'''. {{AttackTags |unharmful, movement }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Bite'''
(★☆☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} leans forward and bites down, ragdolling those hit. Only used while in water. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} | [[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Thick Hide''' - {{PAGENAME}}s automatically extinguish [[burn]]. *'''Monster Resistance''' - Has an innate ~25% resistance to physical hits. ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" ! Name !Description |- |'''Curb Stomp''' |The Megalodaunt ends its opponent's life by delivering a stomp onto their bodies with a gruesome crunch. This happens in less than a second. This attack has an AOE effect which can be parried similar to the [[Rock Golem]]'s stomp. |} ==Tips== *Most likely the first non-humanoid enemy you will encounter as a new player. They may appear menacing but they are easily learnable. *Though it may seem like they do, a {{PAGENAME}} is not and will never use any move twice in a row; the three variants of '''Slash''' (single swipe, double swipe, and swipe + kick) along with '''Kick''' all count as their own moves, even if they are all quite visually similar. By using this to your advantage you can accurately predict the {{PAGENAME}}'s attacks. ==Trivia== *Megalodaunts are able to swim, unlike most monsters which simply sink and despawn. **They perform ranged attacks more often and when they are in the water they perform an unique "bite" attack as opposed to kicks and slashes. *Megalodaunts can technically be set on fire but will visibly snuff the flames off from themselves whenever this happens. This tends to obscure its animations. *The Megalodaunt roars when it spawns in and periodically afterwards, revealing its presence. *Megalodaunts in general are a reference to the [[References and Easter Eggs#Enemies/Bosses|Shark Giant from ''Bloodborne'']], as they share many physical and behavioral similarities. **Megalodaunts are most likely named after the "''Otodus Megalodon,"'' a large prehistoric shark that went extinct about 3.6 million years ago. *Megalodaunts have 120 teeth, 30 on the upper front, 30 on the lower front, 30 on the lower back, and 30 on the upper back of their mouth. *In the Winter of 1291, an event transpired that was later officially dubbed the Sharko Rumbling. This was caused by the addition of [[Monster Bait|Megalodaunt Bait]]. This was uncapped, allowing players to flood servers with tens if not hundreds of Megalodaunts, which proceeded to kill an extreme amount of players and cause heavy lag. Since then, the item has been changed to prevent this. *From April 1st-3rd 2023, Megalodaunts were capable of spreading [[Destroyman III|Coral Fever]] by taking damage from their '''Slash''' or '''Thousand Needles'''. *Megalodaunts participated in the April 1st, 2024 event under the name of Red Daunts and won. *[[Destroyman III]] is a small, chibi Megalodaunt that can talk. *According to [[Mortus]], the flesh of a Megalodaunt is edible. That being said, the [[Megurger]] is said to be made out of Megalodaunt's flesh and is described to be rather foul food. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]]

==Mementos==
Mementos are an exclusive feature to {{Iv|Vow of Iron}}. Mementos are progressed with predetermined talents and mantras, and each Memento has unique restrictions. The player unlocks 6 mementos by default: Berserker, Flame Worshipper, Saint Jay, Sightless, Spear Dancer, and Rogue Assassin. Other Mementos can be unlocked through various challenges within Vow of Iron.

Mementos can use any weapon in their listed category regardless of stats but can only equip weapons of their categories and if their final stats meet the requirement. For example, Saint Jay can only use Shields, Greatswords, Greathammers and Greataxes, but cannot equip weapons such as the Kanabo.

Beating the {{Iv|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard (Temple of Mur)}}, {{Iv|Dravik, The Rat King}}, and {{Iv|Zi'eer, the Fourth Prophet}} adds completion marks to your Memento tag in the character creation menu.

In the menu, the Mementos are represented by an Iron Memento, a metal tag worn by certain members of the [[Circle of Honour]].

The Memorial Masons, coloquially known as the "Deathscribes", are a subdivision of [[The Divers]] consisting of stonemasons. Their job is to carve the names of retired or, more likely,
deceased Divers into stone monuments. They are led by a [[High Mason]], or "Head Deathscribe". The current High Mason is [[Horus Helsen]].<ref name=":0">[[The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation]]</ref><ref name="DJ">[[A Deathscribe's Journal]]</ref>

Their uniform is all black.<ref name="DJ" />

'''Memory Shards''' were a [[Relics|Relic]] given to you when you spawned in the {{iv|Vow of Iron}} gamemode to restart the fight against the mode's mandatory [[Bosses]].
== Usage ==
When you would get knocked in a Memory Boss fight, you would be given 25% [[Status Effects#Wither|Wither]] and a full heal up to 75% and the Memory Boss would fully heal as well, along with setting your [[Etris Flask|Etris Flasks]] to 1 and doubling its healing percentage. 

== Trivia ==
*On release, you had to manually pull out and use a Memory Shard in order to restart the fight against a Memory Boss when you were knocked, and you could only use it if you had been combat-tagged by them.
**Some days after the release of Vow of Iron however, this was changed and they were automatically used whenever you would get knocked, even if you didn't have any in your inventory.
***Memory Shards themselves were removed from being given out to {{iv|Mementos|Vow of Iron characters}} on spawn shortly after this change, and their description was changed to ''"Useless"'', but they were not removed from existing characters' inventories. Their description previously read ''"Use these as you're fighting a Memory Boss to restart the fight when you're knocked. For each use of these however, gain increasing amounts of Wither when the fight is restarted."''

title: Mendacia
content:
{{PathfinderEx}} {{NPCInfobox |title1=Mendacia |name=[[Ethiron]]Mendacia is refered to as the Voice of Ethiron. Using an [[Idol of Yun'Shul]] has you interact with Yun'Shul, during which they are refered to as the Voice of Yun'Shul. This precedent confirms that this Voice is indeed Ethiron. |location=[[Ethironal Shrine Outskirts]]
[[Firfire Caverns]]
[[Kyrsan Wilds]]
[[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City]] |alias=Mendacia |aspect=Tiran |pronouns=She/her |image1=Mendacia.png}} ==Description== Mendacia is a [[Tiran]] with the [[Black Diver]] outfit who tasks you with the quest of saving her in the [[Second Layer]]. She claims to be an Arch-Diver in charge of the Interstice Skies, and upon completing her quest you are awarded with 2 [[Knowledge]] and some questionable information. You can find her in the [[Ethironal Shrine Outskirts]] once you spawn in [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|the Second Layer]]. She remains invisible near some rocks until the player comes close enough to interact with her. When the player interacts with Mendacia, she manifests in a ghostly form, saying that you need to free her from the second floor of [[Second Layer/New Kyrsa|New Kyrsa]] and that she is being imprisoned by the Kyrsgarde. Once you complete her quest and "free her," she will unmask herself as the Voice of [[Ethiron, the Eye of Calamity|Ethiron]] and mock you. Here, it's revealed that she, or rather he, tricked you into awakening the Scion of Ethiron, saying that he was holding a form of "A scum meat bag of your foolishness." ==Quest== After interacting for the first time with her in the 1st floor, near the spawn, you'll need to interact with her once more in the [[Firfire Caverns]], between the entrance and the fake floor hole between some spikes of stone. She'll tell you to go to the [[Cathedral of Ethiron]] to enter the city of New Kyrsa. Upon arriving to New Kyrsa she will be in front of the first obelisk near the spawn of Floor 2, she will tell you to activate the 5 Obelisks in New Kyrsa to "free" her from her prison. Upon activating the 5 Obelisks she will be near the entrance to the Scion of Ethiron boss fight (near the long tunnel) revealing herself and her true intentions, calling you a "LITTLE GODSEEKER." == Dialogue == |-|First Encounter= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Wait.. ==Description==
Mercille is a [[Vesperian]] NPC that's part of [[The Summer Company]]. They're on a team mission with [[The Guy]], [[Sierra]] and [[Prentis]]. They shares a common dislike for The Guy with Prentis and Sierra.

You can turn sacks found in [[Starswept Valley]] and [[Bluster Rift]] to them for a chest, much like the Summer Company's explosive crates found on [[Summer Isle]] that can be delivered back to [[Scope]]. Doing so will grant a normal Starswept Valley chest as well as some Summer Company reputation.

==Location==
Mercille is located in [[Bluster Rift]], standing in front of a small mine inside a little fort built next to [[Meteor Isle]].

title: Merit Detainment Core
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=Merit Detainment Core|caption=Deep below the fortress, all that the Authority wishes to extinguish are buried.}}
[[File:Meritcore.png|thumb|900px|center]]

== Overview ==
The '''Merit Detainment Core''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a complex prison below [[Fort Merit]] that you can enter without any requirements. It's controlled by [[The Central Authority]], containing only the most dangerous people. 

This dungeon is recommended for a party of people preferably [[Power]] 20.

== Mission ==
Upon entering the dungeon, the player must defeat numerous Authority related enemies riddled throughout the entire prison. Three keys are able to be dropped: Override, Release, and Master. Using the Override or Master key will disable the laser defense system in the right corridor. Using the Release or Master key is needed to reach the control room and to open the prisoner cells. Released prisoners will become hostile. 

To speak with [[Titus Fulminus Destellus]], you must release him and have the [[Legion Intelligence]] from [[Caitus]] at the [[Viper's Jaw]] camp.

== Points of Interest ==

=== Cell Block ===
* A large cell block filled with Authority guards is the first room the player will encounter. 
* These cells hold [[Prisoner]]s and a [[Friendly Prisoner]], including [[Titus]], who is contained in a larger cell than the rest. 
* A ventilation shaft is located on the top floor of the cell block, which can be broken to enter the library.

=== Library ===
* The library hosts around 5 Authority guards, including [[Captain Solaire]]'s Warden Ceremonial Sword variant, as well as a [[Hector|disinterested guard]] polishing his own blade. 
* Uniquely, each bookshelf can be searched up to 5 times.
* The large doors on each side can be broken, leading to the laser corridor.
* There is a breakable door that will lead to an L-shaped hallway containing 3 [[Authority Chainwarden]]s, which serves as an alternative route rather than navigating through the laser corridor.
<gallery>
File:PrisonLibrayr.png
File:Hector.png|[[Hector]]
</gallery>

=== Laser Corridor ===
* A large hallway that leads to each system, and is heavily filled to the brim with lasers.
* Standing in a certain spot will trigger a large metal ball to fall down onto the player, dealing '''great damage''' if they are struck by it.
* A single laser can deal '''high enough damage to knock you instantly''' while standing over one.
* If the player is above the laser corridor, they will be targetted by the cannons, additionally dealing '''high enough damage to knock you instantly''' on top of '''autogripping''' as well.

=== Laser Control System ===
* Located near the library is a small platform guarded by lasers that leads into a small room hosting one of the generators.
* This room contains 3 Authority Chainwardens.
* A generator where the Override Key can be used disables the laser grid system.
<gallery>
File:PrisonLaser.png|Location
File:LaserRoom.png|Interior
</gallery>

=== Cannon Control System ===
* Atop the platform is a large hallway that leads to a breakable door. Captain Solaire's Sovereign's Punishment variant can be found in this room, as well as hosting a generator.
* The generator where the Master Key can be used replaces the player's taunt with a whistle blow, causing the cannons to lock onto a nearby target. This disables the cannons located around the prison.
* Below the grated floor is a lava pit filled with spikes.
<gallery>
File:CannonRoom2.png|Location
File:Cannon.png|The hallway
File:CannonRoom.png|Interior
File:MasterKey.gif|A player using Taunt after using a Master Key
</gallery>

=== Cell Control System ===
* After navigating through the laser corridor, there is a bridge that leads to a wide room guarded by [[Captain Marley]] and Captain Solaire's Adretian Axe variant. 
* A panel can be interacted with using the Release Key to open every cell.
* The Prison Crafting Station can be found here, which is unlocked after defeating Titus.
<gallery>
File:PrisonBridge.png|Location
File:PrisonRoom.png|Interior
</gallery>

Merryweather is a [[Canor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. She is a member of [[The Ignition Union]].

==Description==
The Messer is an early-game sword that can be found in chests in [[Lower Erisia]], as well as in the [[Etris]] weapon shop for {{c|notes|16}}. Due to its nature as a very early game weapon, it is quickly overshadowed, even by weapons with the same requirements.

The Messer can be [[Pluripotent Alloy|Alloyed]], increasing its stats and requirements to make it a viable lategame weapon. The Messer gains a purple hue to indicate this change.

==Talents==
{{text|wtal}}

On critical, consume all of your {{t|Chain of Perfection}} stacks to proc {{etal|weapon|Finishing Slay}}, adding a secondary damage instance to your attack. This secondary damage instance deals 7 damage per {{status|b=y|Perfection}} stack you had (166 damage per stack in PvE).

The first 5 hits that normally do not grant Perfection stacks contributes to this damage bonus, stacking up to 150 PvP damage or 3.5k PvE damage at max stacks.

This effect can be procced on [[Motif]] and [[Enchantments|enchant]]-granted criticals and has no cooldown.

*For PvE, it is recommended to use the [[Motifs|Saber Motif]], as you'll get an additional 300 damage from Finishing Slay.
**Additionally, it is not recommended to use Alloyed Messer over the base variant for PvE, as Finishing Slay does not change when alloyed, and the damage increase from going for the alloyed variant is not that large. Saving points and investing them elsewhere is much more effective than going for the alloy upgrade.
*Finishing Slay can be buffed through damage modifiers, but it is not counted as weapon damage, so things like [[Astral]] or {{t|Manipulator}} will '''not''' affect it.

==Description==
{{PAGENAME}} is a sustain/debuffing [[enchantment]] that steals your opponent's armor durability on hit.

==Effect==
On weapon attack, {{PAGENAME}} drains your opponent's armor durability and restores your own. These effects scale on your weapon's scaled damage.

The armor drain and armor restoration are entirely independent effects and are calculated independently from each other.

===Notes===
*Metal's armor drain formula is as follows: 0.0021 × weapon's scaled damage × target's armor durability × armor drain modifiers ([[Steadfast]], {{t|Bulletproof}}, {{t|Armor Conserver}}, & [[Armorer's Ring]])
**Armor drain resistances are combined multiplicatively.
*Metal's armor restoration formula is as follows: 0.0021 × weapon's scaled weapon damage × your armor durability.
*Metal will still restore your armor on hit even if your opponent doesn't have any left.
*[[Monsters|Non-humanoid NPCs]] get staggered when their armor value reaches 0%. Because of this, this enchant allows you to stagger them '''faster'''.

==Description==
The Metal Greatsword is a Heavy Greatsword exclusive to the {{t|Rending Needle: Augmenter|r=rare}} Talent. After applying 5 Iron Rods and then pulling them with {{Input|input=X}}, Metal Greatsword will be equipped for 10 seconds, overriding your previous weapon.

{{t|Rending Needle: Augmenter|r=rare}} requires 90 Ironsing and 90 Weapon (90 LHT // 90 MED // 90 HVY) to obtain. Additionally, it is mutually exclusive with {{t|Gilded Path: Scrapsinger}}.

==Talents==
{{text|wtal}}

{{etal|weapon|Forced Fulfilment}} replaces your critical attack with [[Metal Fakeout]]. When landing a critical attack using your Metal Greatsword, attaching a heavy rod onto your opponent and reducing their movement speed by 70% for 15 seconds. This slow is reduced to -52.5% movement speed due to the innate slow resistance players have. This Talent has no cooldown.

Additionally, your [[Metal Armament]] damage is increased by 50%.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="250" position="center">
File:Metal Fakeout.gif|Metal Fakeout
File:BasicGreatsword.gif|Default Heavy
</gallery>
While inside [[Metal Fakeout]]'s targeting range, your critical attack will be replaced with the Mantra, teleporting behind your target while leaving behind a metal clone before immediately stabbing the target. This attack has innate {{status|Bleed}}, and counts as a weapon attack, '''not''' a Mantra. Attempting to use this critical while it's on cooldown will cause you to lose Ether.

If you aren't within Metal Fakeout's targeting range, your critical attack will be the default [[Greatsword]] critical, an overhead swing. It has a scaled damage multiplier of '''1x'''. Grants {{status|b=y|Hyperarmor}} for the first 1 second of the attack's windup, ending just before your weapon comes down. On hit, it applies {{status|b=y|Knockdown}} and will insta-guardbreak opponents who attempt to block it.

Both criticals have a cooldown of '''8 seconds'''.

==Trivia==
*The Metal Greatsword has the highest base damage of any weapon in the game.
*Like all other ability-bound weapons, the [[Enchantment]] and quality star bonus from your main weapon carries over to the Metal Greatsword.
*Pairs really well with light weapons, due to the sheer contrast in swing speed.

title: Meteor
content:
[[File:Erisia_meteor.png|Meteor Fortuna|thumb]] These purple meteors are found in random locations around the map, although generally spread out. They're meant for people with the [[Oath: Linkstrider|Linkstrider]] Oath; A Linkstrider can teleport to any meteor that they've interacted with, but they must be sitting at a campfire. The first usage always costs one [[Stardust]] Interacting with a meteor without the Linkstrider Oath, will give you the message: "''I feel connected to this somehow... but There's something I'm not grasping...''" Only Linkstriders are currently known to be able to utilize these meteors, although we could find more uses in the future. == How to Use == '''*You must have the Linkstrider Oath for this to work.*''' Upon interacting with a meteor, it will give you a message: "''Deep within your soul, '[Name]' calls out to you. Call it's name upon the flame, and embrace Entropy.''" Each meteor has a different name. You can teleport to each meteor by calling out its name whilst sitting at a campfire, "campfires" such as [[Flamecharm#Graceful Flame (★☆☆)|Graceful Flame]] do not count (guild base campfires do work however). You can also rest at a meteor site as if it were a campfire (Note: you cannot cook food on meteors) The currently known meteor names and locations are as follows:
== Etrean Luminant ==
Ceres (In [[Etris]], across from the 90° angled bridge, on the edge of a cliff) Fortuna (On a cliff above the [[Erisor's Church|Church]] in [[Erisia]]) Europa (In [[Minityrsa]], near [[Valley of Heroes]], if you walk over the bridge and go forward a bit) CeresMeteor.png|Ceres FortunaMeteor.png|Fortuna EuropaMeteor.png|Europa
== Eastern Luminant ==
Hygiea (Near [[Songseeker Wilds]], by the sea gate going towards [[Summer Isle]]) Pallas (Near [[Miner's Landing]], on a tiny island in front of the [[Oath: Oathless|Oathless]] trainer, [[Cerulean]], next to the sea gate to the [[Locations|Etrean Luminant]]) Eunomia (Near the [[Lifevents|Lifevent]] that allows you to glide to [[The Starswept Valley]]) HygieaMeteor.png|Hygiea PallasMeteor.png|Pallas EunomiaMeteor.png|Eunomia

==Description==
'''Meteor Isle''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is an island that can be found in the [[The Aratel Sea|Aratel Sea]]. It can be easily found by going to Fort Merit, where the Etrean Rescuer is.

==Points of Interest==
*[[Ata]] - Mantra Spark Vendor
*[[Beiruul]] - Fort Merit Raid quest
*[[Cestis]] - [[Murmur: Tacet|Tacet]] Obtainment
*[[Eres]] - Etrea Lore
*[[Exter]] - Speaks of the first Deepwoken Direct
*[[Sekh]] - Meteor Isle Lore.
*[[Blacksmith]]
*[[Saffron]] - [[Oath: Oathless|Oathless]] quest requirement
*[[Sev]] - Dye Packets & Manycolored Equipment in exchange for [[Crowns]]

==Events==

==Trivia==
*The music for this area is [[The Sun, Gleaming]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]].
*The combat music for this area is [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jEufEiXyuxU&list=RDjEufEiXyuxU&start_radio=1 Thrill of the Hunt] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]].
*This island was previously cut from the game before initial release but was since added back in the Verse 2 update.
**It is well known for featuring prominently in the first ever [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dGBOkpheY70 Deepwoken Direct].
***This is referenced by Exter, who notes how familiar the area where the direct took place is.
*During early testing, the isle was Territory of [[Etrea]].
*[[Cestis]], who was previously located in [[The Hidden Village]] was moved here in the Verse 2 update.
*Meteor Isle is a unique piece of land; rumored to be an Oasis of greenery and peace. Meteor Isle is a "neutral" location due to the equilibrium of Hivekin, Etreans and Gremors. 
**Although there ''are'' mixed relationships between each other, they refrain themselves from violence in Meteor Isle.
*You cannot set a spawn point in the Inn as they will tell the player that they are closed.

content: {{ItemTemplate |image=Might Gem.png |value=200 |weight=1 |stack=25 |type=Deep Gem |rarity=Legendary |desc=A sign of strength... ---- Increases a Mantra's posture damage by 10%. |obtainment=*[[Titus Fulminus Destellus]] (guaranteed) {{iv|Vow of Iron}}: *Found in {{iv|The Depths (Vow of Iron)|The Depths}} *{{iv|The Depths (Vow of Iron)|The Depths}} chests}} ==Description== The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an orange diamond-shaped [[Deep Gem]]. ==Effect== Grants a +10% posture damage modifier to the Mantra it is applied on. ===Notes=== *This Gem is best used on high posture damage Mantras, due to it being a percentage increase in posture damage. *If you have the {{cl|brain|Brain}} {{status|Food Buff}} from the [[Grilled Parasol Brain]], {{PAGENAME}}'s posture damage modifier will be increased from +10% to +15%. *The Might Gem can gain additional effects and more potency on its posture damage buff through the equipment Talents on the [[Ascended Outlaw Hat|Ascended Outlaw Set]]. **The {{t|Mass Effect}} Talent from the [[Ascended Outlaw Hat]] increases the posture damage buff from Might Gems by +2.25% for every Might Gem you have equipped in your arsenal. For example, if you had the Might Gem equipped onto 10 Mantras, your Might Gem's would grant +32.5% posture damage instead of the default +10%. ***With 14 Mantra slots, your Might Gem will increase your Mantra posture damage by 41.5%. This can be increased further, to a maximum of +46.5% posture damage if you have the {{cl|brain|Brain}} {{status|Food Buff}}. **The {{t|Ether Pinpoint}} Talent from the [[Ascended Outlaw Robes]] allows your Mantras with Might Gems equipped to ignore the posture bonuses from [[:Category:Shields|shields]]. **The {{t|Stronger Under Pressure}} Talent from the [[Ascended Outlaw Breeches]] additionally applies a slowing debuff to your opponent when you land a Mantra with a Might Gem equipped. The effectiveness of the slow scales on the amount of player combat tags you have. **The {{t|Offensive Recovery}} Set Talent from the [[Ascended Outlaw Hat|Ascended Outlaw Set]] restores a percentage of your posture if a Mantra with a Might Gem equipped hits your opponent's block. This Talent will only work if every Mantra in your arsenal has a Might Gem equipped. *A 10% or 15% increase in posture damage is a very low amount, as even high posture damage Mantras that deal 30 or more posture damage will only have their posture damage increased by around 3. Because of this, this Gem is not recommended for usage unless you're using the [[Ascended Outlaw Hat|Ascended Outlaw Set]]. *You are guaranteed to get 1 Might Gem (and [[Wrath Gem]]) for every time you defeat Titus Fulminus Destellus. ==Crafting== This Gem can also be used to craft a variety of items. *[[Equipment]]: [[Ascended Outlaw Hat]], [[Ascended Outlaw Robes]], [[Ascended Outlaw Boots]], and [[Ascended Outlaw Mask]]. {{History}} [[Category:Treasures]] [[Category:Mantras]] [[Category:Deep Gems]]

{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="12" |Happy Hallowtide, land dweller! Enjoy your stay in our Keep. We hope you enjoy our hospitality.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Are you a cook?
|-
| colspan="12" |I'd like to consider myself skilled in the culinary arts, yes. Make ''no'' mistake though, surface dweller -I am no servant. I am Mikhail, a Spellhardt. We divide housekeeping work among ourselves based on our skills. I just so happen to be the best cook of the lot. Besides... If I'm being honest? Everyone else's cooking is ''inedible''. It's a miracle how some of my kin have survived for so long without knowing how to cook properly.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |You guys look like nobility, I thought you'd have... I don't know - servants?
|-
| colspan="12" |''*He brushes a tuft of hair away from his eyes.*'' Oh, we used to have some, yes. Plenty, in fact. The Keep was once very well-manned, before the fall of {{g|Constellia, the Guiding Star|Constellia}}... But, that's that, and today's today. If you want to wax sentimental about the past, you should go talk to Galpin... I don't mean that as a dig, mind you. He's actually great company.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |The old guy?
|-
| colspan="12" |Tsk, show some respect, land dweller. He's one of the oldest among our kin. Generations of your own kind came and went in the blink of his eye... But yes, him. He loves reminiscing about the past. He misses the homeland dearly. I don't think he enjoys all this travelling - though, he's happy the family's still together, despite the circumstances.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Are the other Spellhardts much younger than Galpin?
|-
| colspan="12" |Lysander is around his age, if not older... ''*He pauses thoughtfully.*'' ...I suppose it's natural to your kind, but for us {{g|Lightborn}}, the passage of time isn't really a concern . We don't age quite like your lot do, and we appear ageless. But Galpin, well... Lysander says that if something weighs heavy on the heart and soul of one of our kind, their appearance changes to reflect their feelings.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |So, what you're saying is... He looks old because he *feels* old?
|-
| colspan="12" |''*Mikhail ponders for a second.*'' I guess you ''could'' say that, yes. Were it not for the near-centennial Hallowtide celebrations, I'm not sure how he'd cope with the heartache from the homeland. But whenever Hallowtide swings around, it gets a lot more lively in here. And despite what Lysander might say - snobby as he can be, -we do enjoy the visitors.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Is that why you keep the Hallowtide tradition going?
|-
| colspan="12" |In part, sure. But it's also a way to keep everyone together. Most of the other high {{g|Lightborn}} families have scattered to the winds. But the Spellhardt endure. Sure, we have our differences, and we have our fights - all families do. But at the end of the day, that's exactly it, isn't it? We're ''family''. ''*He smirks, wistfully.*'' And nothing brings the family together like a good holiday tradition.
|-
| {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

content:
{{Topbuttons|p, {{iv|Miner's Landing (Vow of Iron)}}}}
