[[File:Miners Landing good.jpg|thumb|900px|center]]

'''Miner's Landing''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is found in the Eastern Luminant.

==Overview==
Miner's Landing is the [[The Ignition Union|Ignition Union]]'s base of operations in the East, situated on a large island that houses a volcano.

It contains a Voidzone, the [[Saramaed Summit]]. It also contains a dungeon, the [[Saramaed Hollow]], which is the main way of progression for people with the [[Ignition Delver]] [[Origins|origin]] (who subsequently spawn here as well.) 

==Contents==

===Docks===
The Docks has a guard and a shipwright.

Past the gate, [[Tolkat]], the [[NPC]] who unbounds the player's [[Strength]], can be found.

To the right of the Docks, the NPC for the [[Oath: Oathless|Oathless]] [[Oaths|Oath]] quest is in a cave.

[[File:Miner's Landing Docks.png|250x250px|thumb|center|Miner's Landing's Docks.]]

===Town===
The town is one of the main parts of Miner's Landing. Buildings throughout the town are the Pub, [[Antiquarian]], [[Inn]], and an unnamed building. A blacksmith and a well are found in the town. No monsters or enemy factions spawn in the town. There's a bank where you can turn in [[artifacts]] and buy the [[Ignition Union Uniform]] for 50 notes. 

Behind the water wheel there is a room that contains a few NPCs that give quests, and [[Delta]] who gives the [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arcwarder]] [[Oaths|Oath]]. Taking an elevator up, you can find [[Calypso]]. The area ahead of this part is the Upper Landing.

In the same room as [[Delta]], there is an NPC next to a large drill called [[Deepdelver Tau]] who allows you to enter [[Saramaed Hollow]], a floor-based dungeon that takes place deep under the [[Saramaed Summit]] (See [[Saramaed Hollow]] for more).  

You are able to buy all necessary training gears from Miner's Landing. Along with that, you can buy [[Cloth]], [[Fiber]], an [[Lumber Axe|Axe]], and [[Pickaxe]].

===Upper Landing===
High above the Town of Miner's Landing is the upper areas. Here, the entrance to the Boiler Room can be found. Past the Boiler Room's entrance, there is a long mountainous bridge that eventually leads to [[Starfield Veldt]]. This mountainous bridge is littered with [[Brainsucker]]s and one [[Mechalodaunt]].

===Boiler Room===
The Boiler Room is an area where [[Summer Company Guard]]s and [[Ignition Union Fighter]]s are constantly fighting.

The Boiler Room contains two entrances into [[Saramaed Summit]], one of which is located to the right behind the vault door. The other entrance is located down the left hallway, up the left slope and in a room with an NPC.

===Saramaed Summit===
''Main page: [[Saramaed Summit]]''

==Points of Interest==
Miner's Landing contains a variety of locations containing chests. These chests contain loot from the Miner's Landing loot table. 

The Chests are in the following Locations: 

(Photos to come in future) 

# The "pub" near the blacksmith.
# Behind the water wheel next to the NPC with the dialogue mentioning the Summer Company causing trouble on the second floor.
# In the rooms to the right of the water wheel there can be up to 5 chests.
# Behind the window on a ledge near where the [[Darksteel Greatsword]] is sold and where the NPC tells you about delivery sabotage.

==Quests==
====Orion Quest====

* Speak to [[Orion]], a Celtorian Ignition Union Member. Located in the next room behind the waterwheel, or next to [[Oath: Arcwarder|Delta]].
* [[Orion]] offers you to help handle the conflict (Getting rid of a few [[Summer Goon|Summer goons]]) in the upper level's reactor room; next to (but not inside) the [[Saramaed Summit]] Voidzone.
* Neutralize the conflict and return to [[Orion]] for the reward, which is both Ignition Union Reputation, unlocking [[Origins|Ignition Union origin]] and an alternative access to [[Saramaed Summit]] (Iron Door connecting between the Voidzone to outside).
*Note: this quest is repeatable.

====Alpha's Quest====
''Main Page: [[Oath: Arcwarder]]''

*After finishing Alpha's questline, talk to Delta to receive the Arcwarder [[Oaths|Oath]].

==== Ironsing Quest ====
* To start, you need to have a [[Pluripotent Alloy]] in your inventory. 
* Speak to the Blacksmith. He will mention a friend who is interested in Alloys.
* Head up to the bridge overlooking Miner's Landing, go to the second pair of pillars, and go through the window on the left one.
* Talk to [[Adar, Master of Metal|Adar]]. He will ask you to bring him the following [[Ore]]s: '''Iron, Gold, Erisore, Irithine, Astruline,''' and '''Umbrite.'''
* Once you have all these ores, go back to Adar. He will give you an Alloyed Elixir.
* Drink the potion to unlock [[Ironsing]].

==Overview==
Miner's Landing is a mostly uninhabitable island covered in lava with small [[Ignition Union]] settlements. It is pretty much a construction site for the [[Miner's Landing]] the player can see in the [[Pathfinder]] version of the game.

It contains the static spawn of [[Prototype Railblade]].

==Contents==
===Docks===
The docks of Miner's Landing are identical to the ones of the [[Pathfinder]] version of the game, with the removal of the [[Ignition Union Guard|guard]] and [[Tolkat]].
[[File:MinersDocksVOI.png|thumb|center|500px]]

===Town===
The biggest [[Ignition Union]] settlement on the island. Here alongside an empty Pub, where in the [[Pathfinder]] version of the game the [[Barber]] would be located, the player can find the [[Innkeep]] and the [[Blacksmith]].
[[File:MinersTownVOI.png|thumb|center|500px]]

They can be found by using [[Talents|Shadow Travel]]/[[Shadow's Flight]] near [[Silhuett]], who spawns randomly around the [[First Layer]] or at chance by using [[Talents|Shadow Travel]]/[[Shadow's Flight]] on an area that is glowing with an ominous purple light. If you have Ally reputation or higher with [[The Ministry]], they will hand over the [[Deepspindle]], a [[Deepscorn Casque]] and the [[Darkened Bastion]] without a fight. This only applies via [[Silhuett]] encounters, however. Repeat encounters with the ally method via Silhuett will only grant one of the items from the set instead of all three. ==Dialogue== |-|First Encounter= {| class="fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" |- | colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} |Begin (>Ally Reputation) |- | colspan="12" |Who Told you of this place? Of the Gateway? |- | colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Easy friend, I'm on your side. |- | colspan="12" |Phew, you had me startled for a moment there, anyway, this place isn't safe anymore. You and I must leave. Until next time, friend. |- | colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} |End, the agent gives you the three items and leaves.
Begin
Who told you of this place? Of the gateway?
A Diver told me they were tailing some sort of Ministry Agent. Doesn't matter. Give up.
Did they now? Looks like I have one last loose end to tie up for good. Hah! I'd love to see that attitude after I'm finished tearing you limb from limb.
==Dialogues when you grip== * Curse you! * You slugs! ==Moves== The Agent wields the [[Deepspindle]] along with a variety of [[Shadowcast]] Mantras. {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |

(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |

(★★☆) |Lunges forward, marking an enemy before dealing damage multiple times. This critical attack applies true stun, preventing any and all actions while being hit. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.n, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Rising Shadow'''
(★★☆) |User moves their hands outward, creating a black tendril that chases nearby enemies. When connecting with an enemy, they will be lifted into the air and smashed into the ground, dealing damage and stealing ether. *This attack can summon multiple tendrils to grab multiple people simultaneously. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Revenge'''
(★☆☆) |A quick dash signified by a red-line effect, the mantra teleports him forward upon hitting the player or the player's block. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, teleport }} |- |
'''Shadow Assault'''
(★★☆) |Windup before turning into shadows and dashing forward, dealing very minor damage to anyone in your way while applying darkness. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |- |

(★★☆) |The user performs a slow axe kick, causing nearby opponents to be ragdolled and flung back. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |- |

(★☆☆) |An explosion of blue ether around the user that pushes opponents away. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, unharmful }} |- |} ==Trivia== *You must beat them within 5 minutes, otherwise you will be teleported out of the Understrand. *Burning the Agent to death will cause nothing to drop, instead after four sorry seconds you will be sent back. **Strangely enough, burning the Agent with Twisted Puppets causes them to get up, supposedly with half their health back, like how Phoenix Flames works. *The Agent is also a [[Celtor]], as markings can be observed on their face. ==References== {{History}} [[Category:Individuals with They/them pronouns]] [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Ministry Enemies]]

title: Ministry Bloodrender
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}{{EnemyInfobox |image1=MinistryBloodrender2.png |health=~1800 |weapon=[[Krulian Knife]]|caption1=Name: Bloodedge the Apprentice|drops=[[Heartstar]]|moves= *Assault *Critical *Crucifixion *Scarlet Cyclon *Razor Blitz}} == Description == The Ministry Bloodrenders are a tri-group of blood cultists, working under the second prophet of [[The Ministry]]. They utilize [[Bloodrend]] Mantras and their [[Krulian Knife|Krulian Knives]] to defeat their adversaries. They can spawn in the [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|Floor 1]] of the [[Second Layer]] if the player has hunted [[reputation]] with [[The Ministry]], or near the entrance to the [[Derelict Highchurch]] if the player takes [[Vyrelda, Master of Blood|Vyrelda's]] quest, as an alternative to descending to the [[Second Layer]] and killing [[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract|Chaser]] for [[Heartstar|Heartstars]] in order to get [[Bloodrend]]. (Do note that she only shows up there after obtaining [[Bloodrend]].) Defeating one of them rewards the player with 1 [[Heartstar]] and bad [[The Ministry|Ministry]] [[reputation]]. Defeating all of them rewards the player with a [[Chests & Sacks|chest]] containing [[Second Layer]] loot. ==Moveset== A Ministry Bloodrender uses [[Bloodrend]] Mantras and the [[Krulian Knife]]. {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Assault'''
(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Critical'''
(★★☆) |The Ministry Bloodrender enters a stance before unleashing a flurry of slashes. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Crucifixion'''
(★☆☆) |The Ministry Bloodrender conjures a cross, ragdolling and throwing enemies back. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll }} |- |
'''Scarlet Cyclone'''
(★★☆) |The Ministry Bloodrender conjures a tornado of blood where they're facing and sends it out. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Razor Blitz'''
(★★☆) |The Ministry Bloodrender creates a scythe out of their own blood and swings it. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |} ==Trivia== *Strangely enough, they don't wear [[Blindfold|Blindfolds]] like their colleagues. *They also are said to monitor Chaser and give him orders, meaning they have some sort of power over him, it just isn't seen or stated. *According to [[Vyrelda, Master of Blood|Vyrelda]], they are hunting her under the [[Lore#The Second Prophet|Second Prophet's]] orders, due to having left the Ministry. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Ministry Enemies]] [[Category:The Ministry]] [[Category:Enemies that can wield Enchantments]]

They wear a Vagabond's Bicorn, either a [[Blindfold]] or Crimson Blindfold and a [[Prophet's Cloak]] outfit. ==Moveset== Their arsenal consists of a [[Krulian Knife]] and the [[Shadowcast]] attunement: {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |

(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |

(★★☆) |Windup before turning invisible and dashing forward, dealing very minor damage to anyone in front of caster while applying darkness. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |- |

(★☆☆) |The caster dashes forward and does 3 shadow infused slashes with their weapon. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |

(★☆☆) |The caster raises their their hand and lifts one target in the air, then proceeds to slam them in the ground. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, knockdown }} |- |
'''Encircle'''
(★☆☆) |The caster conjures shadows around the enemy that deals damage and teleports the caster towards them. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, teleport }} |} ===Boons=== *Third Eye - A Ministry Captain cannot be assassinated under any circumstances. === Talents === * Finishing Touch - Instantly execute enemies finished with the critical attack of your dagger. * Successive Throw - When you successfully flourish an enemy, you throw out a dagger afterwards * Pressure Detonation - Block breaking an opponent with a shadow mantra generates a small vacuum that suffocates those hit. * Dark Hours - Shadowcast mantras deal more damage at night. * {{cl|raretlnf|Dark Rift}} - Enter a rifted state when you successfully dodge, where you can't be damaged until its duration ends. Can be cancelled with feinting or attacking. * Dark Synergy - Engulf your enemy in shadows when flourishing them. * Singularity - Enemies will briefly hang in place when hit by a shadow move. * Blackhole - Your singularity pulls everyone nearby in. ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Execute |Pins down opponent and slices their throat with the Krulian Knife. |} ==Trivia== *Ministry Captains are identical in appearance to [[Ministry Scout]], yet hold a higher rank. **This trend can also be seen with [[Apprentice Diver]]s and regular [[Diver]]s. **They are NOT to be confused with their scout variant, as using a light approach on them will almost always result in death for their higher HP pool and their variety of attacks along with them spawning in packs of 3. **The only way of telling them apart is seeing if they use shadow roar or not. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Ministry Enemies]]

content:

They will either spawn in groups of three or only one of them will spawn alongside two [[Ministry Footpad]]s. ==Moveset== Their arsenal consists of the [[Way of Navae]] along with the [[Shadowcast]] attunement and [[Contractor]] Oath: {| class="fandom-table" |+ !Moves/Danger !Description |- |
'''Assault'''
(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |

(★★☆) |Raises right leg before firmly slamming it down into the ground below. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.n, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Shade Devour'''
(★☆☆) |Gorge on your own health to push away opponents and grant a damage bonus to melee attacks. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Shadow Assault'''
(★★☆) |Windup before turning into shadows and dashing forward, dealing very minor damage to anyone in your way while applying darkness. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |- |
'''Encircle'''
(★★☆) |Conjure shadows around your enemy before warping to them after a delay. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, teleport }} |- |
'''Eclipse Kick'''
(★★★) |A slow axe kick that ragdolls and flings nearby opponents on contact. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |- |
'''Judgement'''
(★★☆) |Summons a black casting circle before enveloping your target in black tendrils and tearing them apart. *The move will instantly execute if it brings HP to 0. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |} ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Execute | Pins down opponent before firmly bashing their face. |} ==Tips== * Their quick, powerful attacks with their fists paired with their abilities will easily overwhelm the less-skilled player and directly counter their mantras. ==Trivia == *Rather ironically, the stronger variants use [[Way of Navae]], despite the Ministry engaging in an ethnic cleansing of Navaen Nomads, as can be observed during their battles around [[Summer Isle]]. However, they may be using it as a way to enhance their Shadowcast, as there are implications Navae may also be the pioneer of Shadow, similar to how Expert Galebreathers use Legion Kata. *The reward chest for the Ministry ambush has a small chance of yielding a [[Gran Sudaruska]]. *They can use Judgment, from the [[Oath: Contractor]]. Despite this, they lack the strings or red eyes that indicate the presence of the Oath. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Ambush Enemies]] [[Category:Enemies with Oaths]] [[Category:The Ministry]] [[Category:Ministry Enemies]]

title: Ministry Heartspiller
content:
{{EnemyInfobox |image1=Heartbleeder.png |health= 10000 |moves=*Assault *Critical *Rising Shadow *Crucifixion *Veinbreaker *Eclipse Kick |drops=*[[Red Death]] *{{iv|Ministry IOU}} |caption1=Count Dracula's secret cousin |weapon=*[[Red Death]] |title1=Ministry Heartspiller }} ==Description== Ministry Heartspillers are [[The Ministry|Ministry]] agents under the Second Prophet that specialise in information gathering via torture. They wield [[Bloodrend]] and [[Shadowcast]] in order to torture and then erase their victims. They can be found spawning at [[Minityrsa]], within [[First Layer|The Depths]], or rarely at [[Starswept Valley]]/Lower Erisia(towerstruck lands). They can be found interrogating a pathfinder hostage. In [[Vow of Iron]], they can rarely appear to ambush the player after completing a job. Their moveset remain the same between both modes. Ministry Heartspillers wear a [[Vagabond's Bicorn]], a [[Blindfold|Crimson Blindfold]], a [[Prophet's Cloak]], and a dark red [[Ministry Cloak]] with three medals on attached to the left breast. The 3 medals on their chest signify their rank as a Heartspiller, with the one we fight likely being a high rank.[[File:HeartbleederMedals.png]] As stated by Arch Mage, you don't have to meet any requirements for the NPC to spawn.[[File:No_REQS.png|none|thumb|243x243px|Arch Mage Statement]] == Dialogue == |-|On spawn= * Speak worm. Tell me what you know. * What did you see? Well? * Tell me. Who did you meet with? ** Pathfinder: I'd die before I told you! *** It's all the same to me. |-|On Aggro= * Oh well, another one for the pyre. * More for the pyre. Oh well. * Tch. Loose ends. |-|On Grip= * Far too late. * Do you think what you're doing means anything? * Be seeing you soon. Additionally, if the pathfinder hostage is still alive when the agent is gripped, they will say "Thank you...", "Please, you have to get away from here. Please." or "Stranger. You don't know what you stepped into, I'm sorry." == Moveset == A Ministry Heartspiller wields a [[Red Death]] alongside a mix of Shadowcast and Bloodrend Mantras. {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |

(★★☆) |The Heartspiller moves their hands outward, creating a black tendril that chases nearby enemies. When connecting with an enemy, they will be lifted into the air and smashed into the ground, dealing damage and stealing ether. *This attack can summon multiple tendrils to grab multiple people simultaneously. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Eclipse Kick'''

If fully charged, this move gains the ability to guardbreak. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y |type2_color = DarkRed }} |} == Tips == * If you're having trouble with spawning the npc, using Ring of Curses is a good way to increase the chances of the event from spawning. ** Combining this along with Hell mode, you'll get an even more increased rate of the event from spawning (Risky). * Does not attack you if you have Neutral or Positive reputation with the Ministry but it can still spawn.

What a cruel, cruel world… 😔 |affiliation=[[The Ministry]]}} ==Description== Ministry Scouts are enemy NPCs that can be found in [[Minityrsa]], patrolling [[Outpost Antumbra]]. There are about nine Ministry Scouts: four patrolling outside, five inside. Curiously, they also gather around [[Summer Isle]], whether to murder members of [[The Children of Navae]] or massacre [[Bandit]]s. A Ministry Scout's appearance consists of a [[Vagabond's Bicorn]], either a [[Blindfold]] or Crimson Blindfold and a [[Prophet's Cloak]]. ==Moveset== A Ministry Scout's arsenal consists of a [[Krulian Knife]] and the [[Shadowcast]] attunement: {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Assault'''
(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Critical'''
(★★☆) |User unleashes a quick flurry of slashes. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Shadow Assault'''
(★★☆) |Windup before turning invisible and dashing forward, dealing medium damage to anyone in front of caster while applying darkness. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |- |
'''Dark Blade'''
(★☆☆) |The caster dashes forward and does 3 shadow infused slashes with their weapon. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Shadow Eruption'''
(★☆☆) |The user makes a swipe with their right hand before releasing a large sphere of shadow. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Clutching Shadow'''
(★☆☆) |The caster raises their hand and lifts one target in the air, then proceeds to slam them in the ground. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, knockdown }} |- |
'''Vent'''
(★☆☆) |An explosion of blue ether around the user that pushes opponents away. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, unharmful }} |} ===Passives=== *Third Eye - Ministry Scouts cannot be assassinated under any circumstances. ===Talents=== *Blackhole - Your singularity pulls everyone nearby in. *Dark Hours - Shadowcast mantras deal more damage at night. *{{cl|raretlnf|Dark Rift}} - Enter a rifted state when you successfully dodge, where you can't be damaged until its duration ends. Can be cancelled with feinting or attacking. *Dark Synergy - Engulf your enemy in shadows when flourishing them. *Finishing Touch - Instantly execute enemies finished with the critical attack of your dagger. *Pressure Detonation - Block breaking an opponent with a shadow mantra generates a small vacuum that suffocates those hit. *Singularity - Enemies will briefly hang in place when hit by a shadow move. *Successive Throw - When you successfully flourish an enemy, you throw out a dagger afterwards ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Execute | Pins down opponent and slices their throat with dagger. |} ==Trivia== *Every NPC except the other members of [[The Ministry]] are hostile towards them. *When gripped by a [[Gran Sudaruska]], the spirit of Sudaruska will speak. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:The Ministry]] [[Category:Ministry Enemies]]

'''Minityrsa''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is an island found in the [[Luminants|Etrean Luminant]].

==Descrption==
Minityrsa is a mostly uninhabited island perpetually blanketed in snow. It can be found to the right of the Luminant Gates. Despite being mostly uninhabited, there are remains of buildings and structures scattered around. 

==Points of Interest==
*[[Valley of Heroes]]
*[[Trial of One]]
*[[Crypt of the Unbroken]]
*[[Starfield Tundra]]
*[[Outpost Antumbra]]
**A stronghold inhabited and guarded by [[Ministry Scout]]s.
**The [[Trial of One]]'s entrance can be found here underneath the back right hatch.

==Maps==
A map can be found at [[Maps#Surface]].

==Trivia==
*The music for this area is [[A Waltz Of Snow And Knights]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]].
*Minityrsa is also called "Mini" by other players.
*During the Winter, the entirety of Minityrsa is covered in snow. The mix of both sheets of white and permanent snowfall makes the island tedious to traverse.
*Enemy NPCs here cannot be assassinated, much like the Songseekers in the [[Songseeker Wilds]].
*Since it is constantly snowing in Minityrsa, it is best to place [[Campfire]]s beneath shelter or use one of the set spawn campfires.
*Wiping for the first time unlocks the ability to spawn here as an origin ([[Trial of One]])
*If you are ineligible to start the Trial of One, (either you've already attempted it, aren't power one, or are [[Deepbound]]), you can slam yourself into the trial door and it will bounce you back and ragdoll. When bouncing yourself back, you will gain exp for Fortitude. Use this to your advantage. Make a wall with Frostdraw and bounce yourself into the door and repeat until max fortitude.
*Many players struggle with the pronunciation, calling it names such as "Ministrya" or "Minitrysia," but the actual pronunciation is "Mini-tear-sa."
*Strangely, despite the fact that there are many Ministry Scouts and Ministry Necromancers here, Minityrsa is not considered to be territory of the Ministry in-game, as it doesn't say "TERRITORY OF THE MINISTRY" under its name. However, this DOES apply to [[Outpost Antumbra]], which is located in Minityrsa.

title: Misérables
content:
{{PathfinderEx}} {{Quotes|quote=Is that all? A dull life. Dull choices made by dull humans, befit of only the dullest minds. You should seek peace of mind. Peace of mind, mouse.|author=Misérables}} {{NPCInfobox |name=Misérables |species=??? |affiliation= |location=[[Second Layer/New Kyrsa|New Kyrsa]] |image1=miserables.png}} ==Description== '''Misérables''' is an enigmatic avian entity located at the outskirts of [[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City|New Kyrsa]] in the [[Second Layer]], found in a valley behind a fence near large shrine-activated door. Upon interaction with the player, Misérables has the ability to grant wishes to the player, similarly to the [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|Shrine of Yun'Shul]] inside [[First Layer|Scyphozia]], indicated by two dialogue options: * '''I seek power in my upcoming battles.''' ** Grants additional 30% damage boost towards [[Scion of Ethiron]] for the duration of the run at the cost of 5 [[Kyrsan Medallions]]. '''Lacking these funds and agreeing to the trade will kill you instantly.''' *** Doing this transaction multiple times in the same run does not yield any additional damage. * '''I seek clarity.''' ** Grants a Yun'Shul wish and removes the [[Boons and Flaws|Tarnished]] flaw from the player at the cost of 15 [[Knowledge]]. *** If you already have a wish, you can hold multiple at the same time. The transaction costs 5 more Knowledge for each wish you already have; it will cost 30 Knowledge for the 4th wish if you have 3. Players can choose any amount of wishes per expedition. Misérables ONLY kills you if you lack the medallion funds for his power boost. ===Wish Knowledge Calculator=== If you want to calculate the Knowledge you'd need for a certain amount of wishes, use this [https://www.desmos.com/calculator/mftmw3nwvo Desmos Calculator]. Remember, 1 Kyrsan Medallion = 1 Knowledge when exchanging at Klaris. ==Dialogue== |-|First Encounter= {| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" | colspan="24" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue |- | colspan="24" |{{sh|A rose, a cornflower, and perhaps a hyacinth appear to me in a dream. Amidst the field, only one can bloom to its fullest. What shall I pick?}} |- | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Rose | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Cornflower | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Hyacinth |- | colspan="24" |{{sh|What a charming choice. With this flower, what shall I do?}} |- | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Relax | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Frolic | colspan="8" {{cl|reply}} |Eat |- | colspan="24" |''*The sharp blue eyes narrow, glaring at you coldly. An unnerving sensation crawls up your spine, as your mind twists and turns.*'' {{sh|Is that all? A dull life. Dull choices made by dull humans, befit of only the dullest minds. You should seek peace of mind. Peace of mind, mouse.}} |- | colspan="24" {{cl|reply}} |Peace of mind, friend. (Takes up 50 choices) |- | colspan="24" |''*Their expression relaxes, as if the tension has been released.*'' {{sh|That's the spirit, my dull, dull friend. Now, tell me. What do you seek? Surely, my new friend wouldn't have come here just to check in on me? I think we both know just how selfish your kind are. Tell me, what are you here for?}} |- | colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |I seek power in my upcoming battles. | colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |I seek clarity. |- | colspan="12" |{{sh|Power, you say? I can only offer it toward a great foe, one much larger then yourself. For the price of, hm.. let's say, 5 {{g|Kyrsan / Kyrsgarde|Kyrsan}} Medallions.}} | colspan="12" |{{sh|Ah... Clarity. Yes. The most selfish of desires... To reorder all within your perspective. Very well.. perhaps for a splinter of that perspective, I can resolve the conflict in your soul. Perhaps then your deepest desires will be clear to you once more?}} |- | colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |I'm interested. | colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |Why Kyrsan Medallions? | colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |I'm interested. |- | colspan="6" |{{sh|Very well. Show me your bounty then, friend. '''Five will do.''' If you lack the coin, or claim to, I'll simply search for it within your dear spine. Pray, you wouldn't want that, no? Show me your bounty.}} | colspan="6" |{{sh|My kind. We have need of these perspectives. The products of mind. These medallions... You could think of them as the crystallisation of the Kyrsan perspective, no? Truly fascinating. Are you interested?}} | colspan="12" |{{sh|Do you have the knowledge within you then, my dull friend? [15 Shards + 5 for each additional Wish] shards will do. My kin grow hungry...}} |- | colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} |Nevermind, maybe later. | colspan="3" {{cl|reply}} |Here are the coins. | colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |I'm interested. | colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Take it. |- | colspan="3" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue] | colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Sufficient Kyrsan Medallions] | colspan="1" {{cl|action}} |[Insufficient Kyrsan Medallions] | colspan="6" |[See first instance] | colspan="6" {{cl|action}} |[Sufficient Knowledge] | colspan="6" {{cl|action}} |[Insufficient Knowledge] |- | colspan="3" | | colspan="2" |(A surge of strength enters your mortal vessel.)
{{sh|Wise friend.. Cleanse their bones with this strength.}} | colspan="1" |{{sh|I shall search your spine, rat.}} | colspan="6" | | colspan="6" |{{sh|Now... Good. The veil is placed over your eyes once more. You will see things as you wish. Perhaps with a clearer mind, you might again request deals with those beyond you...}} | colspan="6" |{{sh|Ah. I pity you. You lack the perspective. I pity you, little one. Poor dull little mouse. Is it not the proper thing for me to take mercy on one as pathetic as you? It is.}} |- | colspan="3" | | colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], player gains 30% increased damage against the [[Scion of Ethiron]] | colspan="1" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], player is instantly killed | colspan="6" | | colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue], player receives a Wish and removes the Tarnished Flaw if possible | colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue] |} |-|Subsequent Encounters= {| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" | colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue |- | colspan="2" |Hello once more, my dull friend. Tell me your selfish desire. |- | colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |I seek power in my upcoming battles. | colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |I seek clarity. |- | colspan="2" |[See first instances] |} ==Gallery== File:Miserables Death Message.png|Misérables Death Message File:Lol he doesnt die.gif|Misérables not killing when choosing "Nevermind, maybe later." ==Trivia== * Misérables' name may be a reference to 19th century novel ''Les Misérables'', a story which touches on the topics of moral philosophy and the nature of human society. The word "Misérables" directly translates to wretched. And of course, Misérables is a cognate for Miserable. * He is theorized to be related to Deep Owls; both are familiar with the concept of deals and treat humans as small boring creatures like mice. Misérables especially has the power to back up his threats, whereas you can fight off a Deep Owl. ** This difference in strength between Misérables and other Deep Owls may stem from Misérables' differing choice of prey. Feeding on Kyrsgarde, as opposed to humans, likely yields a far superior meal, as shown by the Kyrsgarde's overwhelmingly superior technological innovation and splendor. Misérables himself speaks on this when asking why he seeks Medallions. * As a friendly reminder, Misérables won't kill you if you're in combat, if you select any of the [End Dialogue]'s, or lack the knowledge for Clarity. He exclusively kills you if you ask for Power without the necessary Medallions. * You can empower yourself with Medallions as many times in a row as you wish despite having no effect. * If you still have your Light Hook active, you can make your deal with Misérables and then Light Hook out. This method will still count your Echo task completed. * You can use the Medallions from your Inventory to Power up against Ethiron. * The maximum amount of Wishes a player can carry at any given time is 197. Due to the price ramp up, Wish 198 would require you to bypass the Knowledge cap. ** This would require a combined total of ~99,485 Knowledge. {{History}} [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:NPCs located in the Second Floor of the Second Layer]]

Mofisu Clan Informant is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]].

[[The Inheritor]] is able to speak to them once they defeat the [[Shogun of the Prophet's Guard (Temple of Mur)|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard]] in the [[Temple of Mur]]. They send messages for {{iv|Clan Mofisu}} and speaks of the {{iv|Dravik, The Rat King|Rat King}}, who can penetrate [[The Lord Regent]]s barriers.
{{clear}}
==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Shogun defeated]
| colspan="2" {{cl|action}} |[Shogun not defeated]
|-
| colspan="2" |Good work... Had that beast not caught me off guard, I too would have made quick work of him...
| colspan="2" |Focus on your own life...
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |[Memory] I'm here for the information we agreed upon.
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|-
| colspan="2" |I don't have much time, it seems... So, I will make this quick. The clans have no way of approaching the Regent. As I'm sure you know, the barrier surrounding the royal palace is impenetrable.
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Is there nothing we can do?
|-
| colspan="2" |My kindred, Clan Mofisu, as well as the other great Etrean noble families that resist the Regent, have gathered at the Golden Rat. Rumors have spread that the 'Rat King' is in possession of a technique capable of piercing the barrier. Unfortunately, that is all we know for now...
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Where can I find the Golden Rat?
|-
| colspan="2" |Make for the Etrean side of the {{g|The Luminants|Luminant}}, through the easternmost waterlock. Pass it, and, facing east, and you'll find a small verdant shore adjacent to the mountain wall. Head inland... And you will find the Golden Rat.
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |I'll make way for the Golden Rat.
| colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} |Do you need help?
|-
| colspan="1" |Hear my advice, before you go... The 'Rat King' was formerly one of the Blade Temple's most exceptional instructors, before his fallout with Maestro Alkhurst Legato regarding the temple's standards... Approach the man with extreme caution.
| colspan="1" |Simply leave me to rest, for now... Merciful {{g|Mur of Light|Mur}} will watch over my fate, whatever comes...
|-
| colspan="2" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

|-|Subsequent Encounters=
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
| colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="1" |Make haste. There is no telling how long the 'Rat King' will be willing to give you his aid...
|-
| colspan="1" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

title: Monster Bait
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Winter 1291 marks that fateful night, when the rumbling of a million Megalodaunts thundered in our ears. They laid waste to our homes... And what little lands we had left to squabble over.|author="The Dangers of Overfishing," page 42}}[[File:Monster Bait.png|thumb|Monster Bait]] ==Overview== Monster Bait are craftable items in Deepwoken. It costs Chum to craft, and prior knowledge of the recipe from [[Mortus]], housed in a shack a ways away from the alternative shore of [[Lower Erisia]]. Like the name suggests, it is used to spawn monsters. The three craftable baits can be used to spawn [[Megalodaunt|Megalodaunts]], [[Thresher|Threshers]] and [[Terrapod|Terrapods]] respectively. Megalodaunt and Thresher Bait costs 3 [[Chum]], and Terrapod Bait costs 2 [[Chum]]. ==How to Use== To use Monster Bait, it has to be placed near the sea (in both elevation and proximity to the water). Terrapod Monster Bait, however, also allows being placed near a "temperate woodland," which seems to refer to anywhere on [[Lower Erisia|Erisia]]. It must not be within a certain radius of another Monster Bait and has a 30 second cooldown before you can place it again. Then, you must wait a varying amount of time for it to spawn. Times can range from nearly half a minute to upwards of 5 minutes for the monster to spawn in the place of the bait. Monsters spawned through bait ''do not'' give chests. ==Trivia== * On the 13th of March, 2022, Megalodaunt Bait was added into the game. However, due to improper testing, the item wouldn't be removed from the player's inventory upon use, and there was nothing to stop players placing large amounts of bait in the same place, causing comically large numbers of Megalodaunts to spawn at once and also causing most of the resulting Sharkos' animations to break, so servers were filled with many, especially in Etris.
It caused the developers to shut down servers and disable the item, and the contents of Chests were doubled for 3 days to commemorate this event. This is now considered lore as "Sharko Day," as said by the developers, trying to cover up the mistake. ** There were even entire gangs of high levels server-hopping and beelining to Megalodaunt-infested hotspots to try to protect freshspawns and kill the Megalodaunts. ** Many refer to the event as 'The Sharko Rumbling,' a reference to the rumbling from Attack On Titan, which happened to be airing around that time. The latest version log in the wiki reflects this disastrous event as '''"The Dreaded Winter of 1291."''' ** One of the shutdown warning notes read "Shutdown at XX:57, good night to sharkos across the world" * Monsters spawned through bait seem to give less EXP than their naturally-spawning counterparts. * Megalodaunt Bait is easily the most sought-after bait as they can rarely spawn their Crimson counterpart, which in and of itself can drop the incredibly sought-after [[First Light]], although at a very low rate. * [[Destroyman III]] mentions that taxes are worse than the Sharko Rumbling, implying that the Internal Revenue Sharkos are ruthless when it comes to tax collection. * Though Monster Bait was heavily nerfed, it is still possible to spawn essentially infinite mobs as long as you have the [[Chum]] and the patience to do so. This is especially true with Terrapods at Erisia, since no shore is necessary, as most of Lower Erisia counts as "temperate woodlands." ** Furthermore, due to the cheaper cost of Terrapod Bait and an infinite source of Chum from Mortus's shack nearby, if you have the patience and want to spam mobs everywhere, you can flood Lower Erisia with ease. == Bugs == * Sometimes upon use of bait, the item will be removed but the bait won't be placed. ** You can avoid this by always placing beneath your character in first person mode *Occasionally, after a mob spawns on bait, the bait will remain in place, though this is only visual (this does seem to affect the ability to place more bait near it, however) and no extra mobs will spawn. It will despawn on its own eventually. [[Category:Items]]

title: Monster Mantras
content:
File:Alchemy GFX.png
==Description== Monster Mantras are [[Mantras]] that players are capable of obtaining which mimic a specific move from a [[Monsters|monster]]. Obtaining the monster drops required to acquire the [[Mantras]]. It can be difficult to obtain, although most, if not all of the [[Mantras]] are considered worth the requirements. Having the ability to throw bones like a [[Bone Keeper|Bonekeeper]], shoot coral as if you were a [[Megalodaunt]], pull enemies as though you were an [[The Enforcer|Enforcer]], monster mantras allow the player to have more versatility within combat. These mantras do not belong to any [[Attunement]], being their own category of abilities. This means the Mantras are not upgradable, retaining the [[Combat Mechanics|damage]] from obtainment. ==Obtainment== Talk to [[Carrion|Carrion, Father of Evolution]] at the end of the maze in Layer 2: Floor 2, after which he appears and stays at [[Castle Light]], allowing you to speak with him and obtain the mantras. Monster mantras are obtained by talking to Carrion and giving him rare drops from certain monsters. The drops follow: [[Enforcer Eye]], [[Thresher Talon]], [[Megalodaunt Coral]], [[Dread Serpent's Tooth]], [[Giant Femur]], [[Broken Gatling Gun]], [[Terrapod Shell]], [[Nautilodaunt Beak]] and [[Charged Parasol Part]]. ''For a more in-depth walkthrough, consider watching [https://youtu.be/pEgA0zXlJsk this video].'' ==Mantras== ===Combat Mantras=== {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Abyssal Ridge (★★☆) |image=Abyssal ridge.gif |desc=Send a cascading eruption towards your foes, forcing them to react. |ethercost={{stats|ether|55 Ether}} |dmgtype=Typeless |reqs=[[Nautilodaunt Beak]] |effect=''The caster stomps into the ground and sends out a eruption that can automatically targets the nearest opponent, knocking them upward. This mantra is based on the [[Nautilodaunt|Nautilodaunt's]] ''''Grand Stomp'''' attack.'' *Deals 38.25 damage and 15 posture damage *Has a windup of 0.9 seconds *This Mantra has two hits. The first one scans for if it touches the opponent and the second deals the damage. *The wave tracks and follows the opponent. Because there is a slight delay, if your opponent is running from you, Abyssal Ridge may miss. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Abyssal Tendrils (★★☆) |image=Abyssal Tendrils.gif |desc=Create tentacles and pierce multiple opponents at once. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype=Typeless |reqs=[[Charged Parasol Part]] |effect=''4 large tentacles protrude outward from the user and quickly stab the nearest opponents within a '''large radius'''. Based on the [[Interluminary Parasol]]'s ''''Pierce'''' attack.'' *Deals 15 typeless damage and 4.75 posture per tentacle, bypassing armor resistances. Damage decreases the further away the opponent is. *Targets up to 4 people. If there are less than 4 people, the tendrils will allocate randomly. If there are no targets in range within its short timeframe of activation, tendrils will not attack. Opponents using {{t|Murmur: Tacet}} will still be targeted. *Does not target allies, making it useful in ganks. *Targeting is automatic within a large radius - not manual - and can target opponents behind the player. *Up close, tendrils will hold the opponent in place for 0.5s. *Further away, tendrils will knock the opponent away in a random direction and apply Dazed. *Is able to be feinted instantly. *You're able to move and attack during the Mantra. *Consecutive hits have no "auto-dodge" frames, allowing them to hit after dodge invincibility runs out and bypass abilities like {{t|Risky Moves}}. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Brachial Spear (★★☆) |image=Brachial Spear.gif |desc=A javelin of jagged bone. |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs=[[Giant Femur]] |effect=''The user digs into the ground, pulling out a comically large bone, and throwing it for hefty damage. This move has a large startup and is based on the [[Bone Keeper]]'s ''''Femur Throw'''' attack.'' *Deals about 100 damage. **Landing direct hits with this Mantra deals less damage than landing the AoE. *Applies HEAVY posture damage, almost always guardbreaking. *Grants hyperarmor during startup. *{{status|Ragdoll|Ragdolls}} the opponent and flings them on hit. *Has 9.18x PvE scaling. *The damage of this Mantra can be improved by equipping the [[Bone Ring]], granting it 30 additional damage. *The range can be compared to a little less than twice the distance between [[Das]] and [[Maestro Evengarde Rest]] in the [[Temple Sparring Hall]] }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Coral Spear (★★☆) |image=Coral Spear.gif |desc=... |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|slash|Slash}} |reqs=[[Megalodaunt Coral]] |effect=''The user grows coral on their back and sprays coral in every direction. Based on the [[Megalodaunt (disambiguation)|Megalodaunt]]'s ''''Thousand Needles'''' attack.'' *This Mantra has ~4 damage per hit with 8 hits, totalling for ~32 damage. *Deals 90 damage to ships. *This Mantra has 9.18x PvE scaling. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Dread Breath (★★☆) |image=Dread Breath.gif |desc=... |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ice|Ice}} |reqs=[[Dread Serpent's Tooth]] |effect=''The user shoots out a devastating beam of compressed ice, based on the [[Dread Serpent]]'s '''Ice Beam'''. This move stuns and procs ice, slowing enemies.'' *Inflicts {{status|Chill}}. *It will change color to pink and apply {{status|Crystal|crystals}} if the user has {{t|Glass Path: Crystallization}}. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Mecha Gatling (★★☆) |image=Mecha Gatling.gif |desc=... |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|flm|Fire}} |reqs=[[Broken Gatling Gun]] |effect=''Pull out a Gatling gun, mowing down the enemies in your way. This mantra is based on the [[Mechalodaunt]]'s ''''Bullet Fury'''' attack.'' *The bullets do not stun, dealing minuscule damage with a short range of fire. *Inflicts {{status|b=y|Burn}} and sets the user {{status|Burn|on fire}}. *Will proc eruptions instead of applying burn if the user has {{t|Eruption Path: Lava Serpent}}. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Whirling Blade (★★☆) |image=Whirling Blade.gif |desc=A chitinous scythe to cut through your foes in a whirl. |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|slash|Slash}} |reqs=[[Terrapod Shell]] |effect=''The user grows a [[Terrapod]] claw from their left arm and begins to spin forward after a short windup.'' *Deals ~6 damage per hit with innate {{status|Bleed|bleed}} damage and a total of 6 hits, totalling to 36 + bleed. *Deals about 10 posture in total. *Cancels if parried. The movement speed increase will be retained after it has been parried, lasting until the Mantra would have ended. *Can be modified with Aeon and Eternal Logstones to increase the number of times it hits *Can be modified with Drift and Rush Shards, but it doesn't seem to do anything (needs testing) }} ===Mobility Mantras=== {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Beast Burrow (★★☆) |image=Beast Burrow.gif |desc=... |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs=[[Thresher Talon]] |effect=''Burrow into the ground, giving invincibility for its duration. Click to cancel the Mantra and hit anybody above, knocking them upwards. Based on the [[Thresher]]'s ''''Burrow''''.'' *Deals 35 damage. *The burrow has a duration of 3 seconds, ending early if you get close to a player/NPC. **Unlike [[Sanguine Dive]] and [[Shade Step]], this cannot be manually deactivated early by pressing {{input|k|M1}}. *Can be enhanced by using the [[Thresher Charm]], increasing the burrow duration by 30%, and reducing its cooldown by 25%. *Shares a cooldown with [[Shade Step]] and [[Sanguine Dive]]. }} ===Support Mantras=== {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Bone Wisp (★★☆) |image=Bone Wisp.gif |desc=A servant of bone, powered by the Eternal Gale. |ethercost={{stats|ether|100 Ether}} |dmgtype=Typeless |reqs=[[Charged Bonecharm]] |effect=''Summon a wisp that shoots an undodgeable bone on uppercut and flourish. Based on the [[Scion of Ethiron]]'s ''''Bonestaves of Eld'''' attack.'' *Deals 15 typeless damage on proc, bypassing armor resistances. *Alternatively procs on all uppercut Mantras, such as Skyshatter Kick and Celestial Assault. *3 charges unmodded (5 with [[Bone Ring]]) *5 second cooldown (1s cd with Bone Ring) *Bone Wisp has various inconsistencies on what can or cannot proc it. Below is a list of all things that are confirmed on whether or not they proc it. **The following abilities {{cl|ligreen|can proc}} Bone Wisp: ***Base combat: Uppercuts, Flourishes, and Offhand [[Pistols|Pistol]] shots (even if you do not have {{t|Execution}}). ***Talents: Air Counters with {{t|Cut to the Chase}} and {{t|Emperor Flame}}. ***Mantras: [[Celestial Assault]], [[Crimson Surge]], [[Crystal Knee]], [[Onslaught]], [[Palm Strike]] (in True Strength), [[Razor Blitz]], [[Rising Flame]], [[Rising Wind]], [[Shade Step]], [[Skyshatter Kick]] (Round Spark), and [[Wind Blade]] (slide jump variant). ***Weapon Criticals: [[Ysley's Pyre Keeper]], and[[Rimebreakers]]. **The following abilities {{cl|lired|do not proc}} Bone Wisp, despite uptilting: ***Mantras: [[Abyssal Ridge]], [[Flame Leap]], [[Lightning Impact]], [[Rising Frost]], and [[Updraft]]. ***Resonances: [[Portals]] (Dive Variant). }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Enforcer Pull (★★☆) |image=Enforcer Pull.gif |desc=A powerful gravitational pull. |ethercost={{stats|ether|40 Ether}} |dmgtype=N/A |reqs=[[Enforcer Eye]] |effect=''Create a vacuum of space from your hand, auto-tracking enemies and pulling them in. Based on the [[The Enforcer|Enforcer]]'s ''''Space Pull'''' attack.'' *Missing still takes Ether and does not put this mantra on cooldown. *The set Talent "'''Enforcer's Pull'''" from {{iv|Reinforced Enforcer Plate}} and {{iv|Reinforced Enforcer Boots}} all-but removes the windup of the pull after landing a flourish. *Can be modified with Crystal and Perfect lens to slighty increase range. }} ==Trivia== *For unknown reasons, Abyssal Ridge was originally a Mobility Mantra. *Monster Mantras are somewhat similar conceptually to Blue Mages in the Final Fantasy Series; Blue Mages are able to acquire enemy abilities (Monster Spells) through various means in encounters, somewhat echoed in Monster Mantras and their obtainment methods. *The maximum stack size of monster mantra ingredients is 6. ==Navigation== {{Attunements}} [[Category:Mantras]]

title: Monsters
content:
{{Stub|Body=There is little information about [[Vow of Iron]]-[[:Category:Vow_of_Iron_Exclusive|exclusive equipments]]. Please help us improve the page through editing, or wait for an updated version of the page to release.}} ''This page is for Monster enemies. For humanoid enemies, see '''[[Enemies]]'''. For Bosses, see '''[[Bosses]]'''''.
003 Teaser.png
'''Monsters''' are inhuman NPCs who are almost always hostile to Players at all times. The main factors that set a Monster apart from [[Enemies]] is both thematic and model-wise. Monsters include non-humanoid NPCs (anything with a custom model), and also humanoid NPC's who are clearly some types of creatures, beast, or automaton. ==Description== One of Deepwoken's finest, and arguably primary focuses, are the Monsters. Monsters consist of a wide array of threats, ranging from beasts, zombies, cyborgs, constructs, aliens, inter-dimensional entities, and even worse. They are embedded to the game as a multi-purpose tool, being a roadblock to better gear, armor, [[Mantra Modifiers]], new areas, but most importantly: being a fundamentals check. They can tear players apart if they're unprepared, unlucky, or unskilled, and cannot be beaten without proper skill and technique. In addition, they serve as a way for a player to gauge their skills; if a player can't even beat an NPC Monster, what makes them think they can beat a boss or an entire dungeon? While each Monster has unique attacks, behaviors, traits, and patterns, they all share one thing in common; '''They can be overcome.''' Every monster, even the strongest ones such as the Dread Serpent can be beaten with enough memorization and skill. (However, do note certain monsters have unique traits such as a Time Limit or Health Regeneration which actually does make them impossible without enough damage.) The vast majority of non-humanoid monsters encountered in-game have hyper armor, meaning most, if not all of their attacks cannot be interrupted from being hit by a player. ===Scyphozia=== In '''Scyphozia''', monsters have differences from their Overworld counterparts, ranging from small effects to gigantic differences in how they fight, their danger level, and how they must be dealt with. *No longer attack each other based on species, instead '''completely focusing''' on players. *Benefiting from the lower gravity of The Depths, being able to '''jump much higher''' to pursue players. '''[[Megalodaunt]]s''' especially benefit from this, as their jump is already high to begin with. *Being '''much more aware''', noticing players from further away, or even behind them in '''certain''' cases. *Gaining '''new behaviors/abilities''', such as Lionfish Cero. *Becoming '''much more persistent in chasing,''' almost never stopping their pursuit until the death of themselves or their target. Depending on your position in the depths, you might have an easier chance of escaping a life or death situation. Additionally, {{cl|corrupted|Corrupted}} Monsters are able to spawn. They are virtually identical to their normal counterparts behavior-wise, however visually they have a large, persistent purple smoke aura around them, along with dealing roughly 50% more damage, having two and a half times the health, and moving more quickly compared to their normal counterparts. It's easier to see the aura on high graphics. On very low graphics, some monsters such as [[King Gigamed]] can be mistaken as not being corrupted. Ringing one of the 'Corrupted Bells' (black colored bells) in the Scyphozia increases the chance of monsters being corrupted by a heavy margin. ===Attuned Monsters=== Every time a monster spawns, it has a chance to spawn in with an attunement, giving it 50% resistance to its respective attunement but making it take 2x damage from its opposing attunement. ====Attunement Types/Effects==== *{{cl|Flamewreathed|nl}} - Applies [[Burn]] on hit, can additionally proc [[Talents#Lava Serpent|Lava Serpent]] effects. Weak to [[Galebreathe]], resists [[Flamecharm]]. *{{cl|Frostmantle|nl}} - Places Ice and applies [[Chill]] on hit. Weak to [[Flamecharm]], resists [[Frostdraw]]. *{{cl|Galeforce|nl}} - Applies [[Winded]] and/or [[Suffocation]] on hit, deals Extra Knockback, and has Increased Movement Speed. Weak to [[Thundercall]], resists [[Galebreathe]] *{{cl|Thunderstruck|nl}} - Applies [[Shock]] on hit. Weak to [[Frostdraw]], resists [[Thundercall]] *{{cl|Shadowmeld|nl}} - Steals Ether on hit. 50% Resistance to Physical damage. Weak to attunements, resists basic attacks. Humanoid monsters can be attuned, but only in [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. Mini-Boss and Boss Monsters like the [[Deep Widow]], [[The Enforcer]] and even [[Primadon]] can also be {{cl|Attuned}}, albeit, very rarely. Certain uncommon-rare variants of monsters thematically already have an attunement tied to them (such as [[Fury Nautilodaunt]]s or [[Crimson Megalodaunt]]s. In these cases, they are only able to become attuned with that type of Attunement effect. Certain Monsters have unique visual effects when attuned. *{{cl|Thunderstruck|nl}} [[Gigamed]] (Lightning is blue as opposed to yellow.) **{{cl|Thunderstruck|nl}} Gigameds have almost full immunity to [[Thundercall]] Mantras *{{cl|Corrupted}} and {{cl|Attuned|nl}} Monsters are fairly common (and in later waves, almost guaranteed) in [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. ==Humanoid Monsters== ===

|FuryNautilodauntIcon.png|Fury Nautilodaunt |ParliamentIcon.png|Parliament |Prime Megalodaunt.png|Prime Megalodaunt }} ==Tips / Monster Hunting Advice== As most Monsters behave differently from each other, the ways to fight them are unique to themselves. However, there are some general rules of thumb that can be applied to most if not all of them. *'''Most''' Monsters will '''never''' use the same attack twice in a row. **For example, this can be observed with Monsters such as the [[Megalodaunt]], who - if you can recognize their attacks - will never use the same attack back-to-back, making their behavior almost predictable. *If an attack has a colored glyph indicator or a colored outline over the Monster and a distinct sharp sound effect, the attack '''cannot''' be completely defended against normally and must be avoided accordingly. **These attacks are generally slower than regular attacks (with the exception of some attacks such as [[Stone Knight]]'s Kick), giving the player more time to react. **For more information and a comprehensive list on these telegraphed attacks, click [[Combat Mechanics#Telegraphed_Attacks|here]]. *Take extreme caution if attempting to flee from a Monster, especially at low health. **Most Monsters have abilities specifically designed to catch players running away, such as the [[Megalodaunt]]'s Thousand Needles, which slows you down when hit. If running is your last option, you must be smart about it. You should abuse buildings, terrain, and other obstacles to your advantage or defend against such long ranged attacks. *Practice makes perfect. **The player should try and fight Monsters in situations where they have little to no risk of dying, such as against the Megalodaunts found in [[The Viper's Jaw]].(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WZD9Akn0gjM) Being unprepared is worse than fighting the Monsters themselves. The absolute '''worst''' thing for the player to do is to jump into a fight with a Monster they’ve never fought, or even worse, never even seen before. While many Monsters are indeed weaker than they look, '''others are the opposite and are deceptively strong.''' ***For Example: Despite [[Blizzard Knight]] looking somewhat spindly and identical to their much weaker [[Stone Knight]] counterpart, they actually boast one of the highest amount of hit points out of any Non-Boss Monster. On the other hand, [[Deep Owl]]s may look ginormous and intimidating, but only have roughly 30% more health compared to a [[Thresher]], a weaker mob. *Monsters are affected by most things a player would be affected by including: **Potions **Status/Elemental Effects **Flinging **Grabbing Mantras/Crits (e.g. [[Legion Kata]] Crit or [[Jolt Grab]]) *Most monsters can be staggered. **While humanoid NPCs can be Posture Broken, most Monsters can be Staggered (on rare occasion, some can both be Staggered and Posture Broken). Depending on the player's ability to deal '''ARMOR DAMAGE''', hitting a monster drains their armor bar (Ironsing works to drain their armor, Metal enchant increases damage to armor, but due to the draining effect you could say it also drains their armor). When the armor bar is empty, the monster will be stunned for around 4 seconds, unable to do anything. This is represented by the red spark that appears on them, a noticeable sound effect, and them becoming motionless. During this time, they lose all their resistances and cannot attack or defend themselves, but once they wake up from stun their armor is fully regenerated. *All monsters have 25% physical armor and in some cases up to 50%. However humanoids don’t have any armor and are tanky by their hp.[[File:Archmagefrrrrrrr.png]] ==PvE Scaling== If you have looked at Monster's health on their pages, you might have noticed how they have absolutely '''absurd''' health, like how the [[Megalodaunt]] apparently has 1000 health. What's happening here? At max, a weapon does, like, 30-50 damage, why doesn't it take a max power player 20 to 34 hits to kill one?. When you level up, you automatically gain bonus damage during PvE, know as "PvE scaling", This is why even when someone doesn't upgrade their weapons damage, they still are able to kill Monsters much faster than a lower level with the same weapon damage. This scaling very quickly becomes crazy in its own right, (to cope with the Monster's crazy health, of course), and towards the endgame, people can kill monsters with thousands of health in a few hits. Calculating how much health a Monster has from just your damage alone won't be correct, you need to factor in your Power. The Mathematical formula used to find the DMG multiplier for PvE scaling is (2.7+( (Power-1)/19) * 4.86) ===Formulas=== The formulas that you need to calculate how many hits are required to kill a monster are the following: DamagePerM1 = (3(Power + 3.33)) \times (WeaponDamage \times (\tfrac{DmgVSMonsters\%}{100} + 1) \times 0.089)
Hits = \tfrac{MonsterHealth}{(\tfrac{100 ~ - ~ Resistance\%}{100}) ~ \times ~ Damage} Example: If you were to fight a a Stone Knight with 9000 health and 55% resistance to slashing, using a weapon that does 40 damage per hit, while having 10% Damage VS Monsters and being at level 20, you would do: DamagePerM1 = (3(20 + 3.33)) \times (40 \times (\tfrac{10}{100} + 1) \times 0.089) = 274.12 Hits = \tfrac{9000}{(\tfrac{100 ~ - ~ 55}{100}) ~ \times ~ 274.12} = 73 (72.9607471181) {{MonsterCalculator}} ==Trivia== *Some Monsters will fight each other; multiple can fight at the same time. These can be either intentional through events like the [[Random Encounters|Megalodaunt vs. Rock Golem event]] in [[Upper Erisia]] or if the Monsters just happen to find each other. See this in action [https://youtu.be/01uQchtfUvw here] and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Su6IU88g7PM&t=37s here]. *Some variants of some Monsters are limited to certain [[Locations]], such as the [[Fury Nautilodaunt]] being found only in The Depths *Prior to an update that reworked the telegraphing of attacks, most unparryable (red flash) attacks of monsters were accompanied by a red flash and the [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5YzN2bPgjB0 Perilous attack sound] from ''Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice''. *There's a rare easter egg with an unknown chance that a [https://streamable.com/ul7sv3 Metal Gear solid alert sound] will play when a Monster notices a player. ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Mechanics]]

For other uses, see [[Moon (disambiguation)]].'' {{Location|name=Moon's Eyrie|area=Voidzone|caption=A beacon calling out from the Void to the Old Dead above. Dreams are so frequently dragged neath the mires of time.}} [[File:Moon's Eyrie.png|thumb|900px|center]] Moon's Eyrie is a non-static Drifting Island type [[Locations|Location]] in Deepwoken found in the [[Voidsea]], located in the [[Luminants|Eastern Luminant]]. ==Overview== Moon's Eyrie is a mysterious island found within the Voidsea, potentially made as a sort of vault for the Celestials' weapons. It has strange architecture, many evident ties to the [[Moonseye (symbol)|Moonseye]], and is guarded by several [[Moon Knight|Moon Knights]]. [[File:Moon's eyrie location.png|center|frameless|360x360px|Moon's Eyrie's location on the minimap]] ==Points of Interest== ===The Moonseye Sigil=== *At the top of the island, a very large [[Moonseye (symbol)|Moonseye]] symbol can be found, with a beam reaching skyward. *Below the [[Moonseye (symbol)|Moonseye]] symbol, accessible through a door on the cliff beside it, is an arena with a [[Moon Knight]] that drops a chest, including unique drops [[Soulthorn]] and [[Nocturne]], as well as other various Moonseye-related drops, including the [[Moonseye Tome]]. **To open the door, attack the stone pillars with a twisting white glow around them. Once deactivated, they will no longer glow. Do this for all three pillars to gain access to the door. ==Description==
'''The Moons Blades are reskinned Flareblood Kamas. It does not have unique properties, only a unique model & effect.'''

The Moon Blades are a weapon skin for the [[Flareblood Kamas]] that was given to Team Supekis (ValekisYT & s_supaa), the first place winners of the second Deepwoken YouTuber Tournament.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
MoonBladeCrit.gif
</gallery>
The critical unleashes an explosion of purple energy around the cursor, launching the target into the air and ragdolling them for a short duration.

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
Moonblades runes better.png|The runes on the blade
</gallery>

==Trivia==
*It is based on a design from Pinterest named [https://www.pinterest.com/pin/639863059567923776/ 'Fantasy Swords' by Wakfu Sins].
*The Critical Attack is a purple recolor of the Flareblood Kamas’ crit.
*The Elder Futhark runes present on the swords translate to "Supaa Valekis" (though Valekis' name uses the Latin alphabet V).
*The weapon had a bug that made all scalings to the weapon void in PvE, causing a 20 minute solo Chaser fight in the Dev Spec Progression Finale by Supaa.
**This was fixed almost on the spot.

content:
::''This page is about the [[Monsters|Monster]]. For other uses, see [[Moon (disambiguation)]].'' {{Topbuttons|[[Stone Knight]], [[Star Knight]], [[Moon Knight]], {{iv|Moss Knight}}}} {{Monster Infobox |title1= Moon Knight |image1=Moon Knight.png |health=15,000 |drops= *[[Ore#Astruline|Astruline]]
*[[Astral]] [[Enchant Stone]] |attacks= *Slash *Kick *Wind Cutter *Terra Eruption *Moon Rain *Finisher: Death by Thousand Cuts |locations=[[Moon's Eyrie]] |challenges={{bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}} }} =='''Description'''== Moon Knights are monsters that spawn exclusively on [[Moon's Eyrie]]. They are similar to other [[Stone Knight]] variants, but with a black torso hole and a Moonseye aura. They have only a '''''chance''''' to drop an Astral Enchant Stone upon death unlike their [[Star Knight]] counterpart. Knights spawned within the catacombs of the Eyrie will drop a chest that has a chance of dropping the Astral Enchant Stone in addition to sought-after items like the [[Moonseye Tome]] and [[Soulthorn]]. '''Knights will respawn every 2 minutes.''' Some Moon Knights may spawn clipped inside of a rock near the center of the island. Getting it to kick can help clip it out. {{clear}} =='''Moveset'''== {| class="sortable fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |
'''Slash'''
(★☆☆) |Swings its sword at the opponent once or twice. *'''Insta-executes the player if health is low.''' {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★★) |Deftly kicks the opponent with added momentum from its body. *Deals extra damage and dazes if the player is slammed against a wall. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |- |
'''Energy Wave'''
(★★☆) |Slashes at the air with its sword, creating a crescent-shaped projectile aimed at the opponent, identically to [[Wind Blade]]. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Maledicta Terra'''
(★★☆) |Punches the ground, causing a pillar to erupt below the player. *The next attack from the Moon Knight is usually guaranteed if this lands. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.fyw, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |- |
'''Moonscorched Blades'''
(★☆☆) |Causes a rain of white flaming javelins from the sky, similar to the critical attack of the [[First Light]]. *Strangely enough, these deal wind damage. *Moon Knights will not do any additional attack while this one is active. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y }} |} ====Passives==== *'''Celestial Stone -''' Has 55% Slash Resistance. *'''Artificial Construct -''' Bloodless Gems do not work against Moon Knights. == Tips == * Moonscorched Blades do a decent amount of damage, but mostly serve as a distraction. Pay attention to the Moon Knight itself even if you take a few hits. * Moonscorched Blades cannot pierce through terrain, meaning it does nothing in the "arena" of Moon's Eyrie. * The Moon Knight spawn in the catacombs requires moving within a certain area near the entrance going until the front of the arena in order to actually trigger the spawn, simply waiting for the respawn timer won't respawn the Moon Knight leading to the misconceptions around the respawn time. == Trivia == *Moon Knights are recolored Star Knights. *The [[Star Knight]] is probably the newer and stronger design of the Moon Knight, which is why the Star Knights protect the Resonant Dawn meteor while the Moon Knights stay on their home island. *Strangely, the Moon Knight has more HP than the Star Knight. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Knights]]

==Description==
The Moon Ring is an [[Equipment]] item under the "Rings" category.

It conceals your character's age, making you appear under 40 (pre-Stage 1 [[Age]]). It is a somewhat rare drop from many sources, most notably [[Aelita]], [[The Ferryman]], [[Duke Erisia]], [[The Depths]], and [[Moon Knight]]s.

==Trivia==
*[[Evengarde Rest]] canonically wears a Moon Ring, which was sold to him by [[Traan Zakshun]].<ref>[[Traan Zakshun#Black Market|Traan Zakshun]] black market dialogue</ref>
*For a long period of time, this ring did not work properly. It was fixed in May of 2022.
*The Moon's Ring is in a category of "Moon" weapons, equipment and relics, other "Moon" items are the [[Moonseye Tome]], [[Moon Blades]], [[Moonlit Earrings]], [[Moonseye Gauntlets]], [[Moonseye Scalpel]], and the [[Moonseye]]. All of these items are commonly found at [[Moon's Eyrie]] from the [[Moon Knight]]s.
*This ring is the opposite of the [[Waning Ring]], which visually increases your character's age
**When both are equipped, you appear as if you are over 40 (Stage 1 [[Age]]).

title: Moonseye
content:
::''This page is about the celestial object and its symbolism. For other uses, see [[Moon (disambiguation)]].''
{{Cleanup}}{{InProgress}}
[[File:MoonseyeNight.png|center|thumb|449x449px]]

{{Quotes|quote=AH! ALL SO CLEAR! THE MOONSEYE! NOT A REFLECTION, NO - ITS OWN LIGHT! NO WONDER IT IS SO COVETED!|author=Soothsayer}}

==Description==
The Moonseye is one of the two celestial objects between the Surface and the Heavens - standing as Deepwoken's equivalent of the Moon and the counterpart to the [[Suncross]]. Unlike the Suncross, it is suspended between the surface and the Heavens at an equal distance.

It is a recurring symbol across Deepwoken, being referenced in items, locations, and aspect descriptions.

The Moonseye is a small hollowed circle with two vertical protrusions and has a smaller white circle within, hence giving it the "eye". A swirling vortex and a faint ray of light surrounds it.

== Cultural aspects ==
The people of Lumen have taken to unique perceptions about the Moonseye. Generally, it is viewed as a representation of life, death, and rebirth.<ref>[[Moonseye Gauntlets]]</ref> 

=== Religion ===
In Capran tradition, Jurik is often associated with the Moonseye, viewing it as an observer and an embodiment of the material forces of the world.

[[The Moonlit Faith]] is a religion dedicated to the worship of the Moonseye, believing that it is the gateway to the afterlife. In turn, sacrifice is needed for an entry into the afterlife.

The Starkindred Faith see the Moonseye as a gate to a promised land that they will journey into following the banishment of the Deep and the revival of Celestials. They also believe that the souls of deceased Celestials make their way into the Moonseye for a promised day.

== Notes ==

* The Moonseye projects a Light that is believed to be the same as a Lightkeeper's.
* The Celestials, namely [[Zhatarn]] had siphoned souls out of the Moonseye for power, causing said souls pain as they are ripped away from their eternal rest.<ref>[[Soulthorn]]</ref>
* A wide amount of evidence supports the idea that the Moonseye contains a mass of souls, and if proven true, may hold the souls of the [[Glossary#The_Old_Dead|Old Dead]].
** Following the Tides, the Moonseye no longer pulls souls of the departed into it, but rather the Depths.
*** The Depths has a stronger pull on souls than the Moonseye. Even so, the Moonseye's pull is still noticeable, given the swirling vortex that surrounds it.
** The mural when reading the [[Moonseye Tome]] depicts souls floating towards the Moonseye.
* The Moonseye also has an abundant relation to [[insanity]]. This can be seen in the Moonseye Tome, which is a [[Prophet Pariah|prophet-turned-insane]]'s dream, and the Blessing of the Moonseye Talent in [[Vow of Iron]].

==Trivia==
*A majority of the relation to the Moonseye involves Celestials, which is reasonable, considering they live among the stars.
*The Moonseye at [[Moon's Eyrie]] is a beacon calling out to "the Last Dead," which, as the [[Crypt Blade|Crypt]] [[Crypt Blade|Blade]] description states, are "the last fortunate souls at the end of the Canticlysm to be spared the Drowning."
*The Suncross and Moonseye are comparable to the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yin_and_yang Yin and Yang], with one representing the darkness and another representing the light. Additionally, the Moonseye is circular, the Suncross is spiked, furthering the Yin and Yang analogy.
*The player's cursor whilst in shift-lock can actually be seen as a tiny Moonseye.
[[File:Suncross Orbit, drawn by ArchMage.png|center|frameless|273x273px|The orbit of the Suncross, maybe the Moonseye orbits the same? Confirmation needed.]]

This Outfit also requires the player to be at least [[Power]] 15 to be crafted. ===''Armor Stats''=== This Outfit has 40000 durability and grants {{stats|phys|+55% Physical resistance}}, {{stats|elm|+35% Elemental resistance}}, {{stats|sdw|+25% Shadow resistance}}, and {{stats|elm|+200% Ether Regen}}. Additionally, it provides the {{t|Crippling Darkness}} Talent. *Due to resistances being combined multiplicatively instead of additively, the total resistances are: {{stats|phys|55% Physical}}, {{stats|sdw|51.25% Shadowcast}}, and {{stats|elm|35% Elemental|sdw=n}}. The {{t|Crippling Darkness}} Talent gives the user 20% PEN to any non-weapon attack, such as Mantras and Talent abilities. Additionally, because [[Reinforce|Reinforce's]] general resistance is affected by PEN, Crippling darkness allows your typeless damage attacks (e.g. {{cl|bleed}}) to deal more damage against Reinforce users than you would otherwise. ==Trivia== *This Outfit reuses the [[Darkened Bastion]]'s appearance and [[Prophet's Cloak]]'s Talent. {{History}} {{Nav|Outfits}} [[Category:Outfits]] [[Category:Outfits with Talents]] [[Category:Outfits with Exclusive Talents]]

==Description==
The Moonseye Scalpel is just a [[Rifle Spear]] with a fancy name and description, that's it.

==Trivia==
*This item was originally a spec for Doctor "Doc" Carrion, the user whom [[Carrion, Father of Evolution]] was based on.<ref>[[File:CarrionScalpel.png|200px]]</ref><ref>[[File:CarrionScalpel2.png|275px]]</ref>
** As such, this is arguably the only spec in the game that was ever publicly available, excluding the [[Railblade]], as it was always intended to be released and NanoProdigy simply received it early.
**The item was released early, and thus its stats were changed to be identical to the Rifle Spear, including Doc's own version of the weapon.<ref>[[File:CarrionYouFool.png]]</ref>
*Despite being an unobtainable weapon, the Moonseye Scalpel doesn't actually come with any defining features that sets it apart from the average Rifle Spear, other than its unique name and description.
*The description of the Moonseye Scalpel was added after the weapon had accidently been added into the game, which mentions how the owner of the weapon had essentially won the lottery, due to how hard it was to obtain inside the short timeframe of it being added.
*This weapon was only obtainable for around an hour, making it one of the rarest weapons in all of Deepwoken.
*It was eventually replaced with a normal Rifle Spear in Version PV_JAN_19_22:13, with all copies turning into regular Rifle Spears.<ref>[[File:Intended.png|frameless]]</ref>
*[[File:Moonseye Scalpel banked (8-28-2024).png|thumb|Moonseye Scalpel banked as of August 28th 2024]]If your rifle spear was in your bank at the time of the revert, then it remains visually untouched.

== Description ==
The Moppet is a [[Weapons|Light Weapon]] in the Dagger category, appearing as an old doll with a crudely-stitched frown alongside a large sewing needle on the offhand.

The Moppet's basic attacks will deal no damage, rather storing the damage dealt towards the target hit. The Moppet will also gain increased PEN per stored M1 with no cap, eventually reaching 100%. On hit, the Moppet will take the appearance of the opponent, copying their hair and [[Aspect]] features, such as a [[Gremor]]'s horns or a [[Vesperian]]'s mask.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="250">
File:MoppetUnmarked.gif
File:MoppetMarked.gif|Target marked
</gallery>The user impales the doll with the needle. If the Moppet has stored damage on an opponent through landing m1s, the opponent will be impaled as well, taking all of the stored damage at once.

The damage this critical deals cannot be directly increased; you must increase the damage of your M1s to increase the damage output of the critical. "On-critical" Talents proc on Moppet's critical, but as you cannot directly increase the critical's damage, your options will be limited.

This critical cannot be parried, blocked, or dodged, but it can be avoided via gaining iframes (e.g. [[Vent]]ing). You cannot deal more than 70% of a player's maximum health with one usage of your critical. See [[Stored Damage Mechanic]] for more info.

The critical has a cooldown of '''3 seconds'''.
