 == Kyrsan Names == Kyrsan names are the custom names that are given by [[Erosius Amaltus Urivortus Alistus Casius Walistoshus]] after collecting the spear at the bottom of [[Firfire Caverns]]. These names are randomly generated and are accountwide instead of per slot. They can also have different names depending on your dialogue choices with [[Aeroaseluniris Oricalum Forentus]] if you didnt call him the right name. The amount of words you get in your kyrsan name seems to be based upon how old the slot was when it retrieved the spear. (This list is highly incomplete so please add any information if you have any) * Amogu * Casius * Craic * Twilight * Ifan * Busko * Booyah * Brabzon * Brumbpus * Bungus * Swallyhoo * Scrimble * Solid * Steve * Fiddlesticks * Holy * Costeau * Humbus * Mulvortus * Morph * Biggs * Eagle * Mud * Burmpo * Ekuvarius * Vexadodecahedron * Dirt * Dedue * Dizco * Drats * Chordles * Quesotericus * Tungus * Boxer * Jubilee * Relarius * Mustadio * Mustard * Mingus * Real * Sunset * Tschwibb * Tsktsk * Tumbus * Tungus * U'Don * Ultra * Twinkletoes * Yr'dum [[Aeroaseluniris Oricalum Forentus|Aero]] Names * Squibby * Bigcheese
==Trivia== *The name "Meliodas" is a reference to [https://nanatsu-no-taizai.fandom.com/wiki/Meliodas Seven Deadly Sins]. * The names "Edward" and "Alphonse" are references to the anime and manga series [https://fma.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Page Fullmetal Alchemist]. *The name Adolin was removed due to its similarity with [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler a certain Austrian painter in the 1940s]. *The name "Hawk" was removed due to being used to reference "Hawk Tuah". * Most names added after the release of the game are available in all three gender categories. This is likely a bug. *If you don't have a valid aspect, you don't have a last name. If you have a valid aspect but it doesn't have any last names, it defaults to Spellhardt, the [[Lightborn]] last name. *Random name generation will occur upon clicking [The End] in [[Fragments of Self]]. The name will be applied to your next character. *The surnames of Ganymede and Vesperian are the same, only with different suffixes (-e and -i). **This hints at the two species being of the same genetic origin, and is confirmed by the Ganymede model under the vesperian mask (viewable through clipping). * The surnames of Felinors are, of course, relating to cat species. *The names "Omar" and "Olie" are references to community members omar_io and Olieware respectfully, the latter of whom suggested the idea of the [[Flamecharm]] Mantra Flame Ballista. *The name "Vergil" is a reference to the [https://devilmaycry.fandom.com/wiki/Vergil storm that is approaching]. *The name Dante is a reference to Vergil's brother and the main character of Devil May Cry. *The names "Usopp", "Luffy" and "Alvida" are references to the anime and manga series, [https://onepiece.fandom.com/ ''One Piece.''] **While various characters from ''One Piece'' were personally suggested as names to developer ragoozer, only Usopp and Kaido were added initially.[[File:Olie.png|250px]] Alvida and Luffy were added much later. *The names "Solaire", "Ornstein", "Smough", "Seath", "Patches", "Artorias", "Gwyn", "Wolnir", "Aldrich", "Oceiros", "Lorian", "Lothric", "Midir", "Halflight", and "Gael", are references to various characters from the ''Dark Souls'' series. **Initially, the name "Ornstein" was '''''incorrectly''''' spelled as "Orstein." **The names Shabriri, Vyke, Maliketh, Godrick, and Godfrey are references to ''Elden Ring'', a spiritual successor to ''Dark Souls''. **The name "Halflight" could also potentially a reference to a skill in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco_Elysium Disco Elysium] which shares the same name, very disco. *The name "Kamina" is a reference to the popular [https://gurrenlagann.fandom.com/wiki/Kamina Gurren Lagann] character of the same name. *The names "Tanith", "[https://skulduggery.fandom.com/wiki/Cadaver_Cain Cadaver]" and "[https://skulduggery.fandom.com/wiki/Skulduggery_Pleasant Skulduggery]" are in reference to characters from the ''[[wp:Skulduggery Pleasant|Skulduggery Pleasant]]'' franchise. **Funnily enough, Cadaver and Skulduggery are technically the same person. *The name "Inari" is a reference to Monad Studios previous game ''[https://rogue-lineage.fandom.com/wiki/Rogue_Lineage_Wiki Rogue Lineage]'' where the races ''[https://rogue-lineage.fandom.com/wiki/Vind?so=search Vind]'' and ''[https://rogue-lineage.fandom.com/wiki/Fischeran Fischeran]'' share that name''.'' *Names such as "Adolin," "Hoid", "Kaladin", "Moash", "Szeth", "Renarin", "Teft", and "Dalinar" are references to the book series "The Stormlight Archive" by Brandon Sanderson. *Names such as "Kelsier", "Vin", "Marsh", and "Wax" are references to the book series ''[[wp:Mistborn|Mistborn]]'', also by Brandon Sanderson. **The series also supposedly influenced the creation of the [[Adret]]. *The names "Zote", "Ogrim" and "Isma" are a reference to the indie game ''[https://hollowknight.fandom.com/wiki/Hollow_Knight_Wiki Hollow Knight]'' by Team Cherry. *The name "Link" is a reference to - [[wp:The Legend of Zelda|wait does this one really need explaining?]] *The names "Angela," "Binah," "Chesed," "Gebura," "Hokma," "Netzach," "Roland," "Tiphereth," "Xiao", "Zena", "Iori", and "Argalia", are references to the games ''[https://lobotomycorp.fandom.com/wiki/Home Lobotomy Corporation]'' and ''[https://libraryofruina.wiki.gg/ Library of Ruina]''. This is likely not all of them. **The name "[https://library-of-ruina.fandom.com/wiki/Angela Angela]" was heavily requested due to the [[Etrea]] "Coral" variant heavily resembling her due to its pale skin and light blue hair. **Coincidentally, "Xiao" is also the name of a ''[https://genshin-impact.fandom.com/wiki/Xiao popular character from Genshin Impact]'', with several names originating from Genshin Impact being suggested at the same time as those originating from ''[https://libraryofruina.wiki.gg/ Library of Ruina]'' and ''[https://lobotomycorp.fandom.com/wiki/Home Lobotomy Corporation].'' **"Binah", "Chesed", "Gebura", "Hokma", "Netzach", "Tiphereth" can also be reference to [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_of_life_(Kabbalah) the tree of life] which the said characters from ''Library of Ruina'' and ''Lobotomy Corporation'' are based on. But "Malkuth", "Yesod", and "Hod" are not added as names. **"Roland" and "Argalia" can also be reference to characters from [https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Innamorato Orlando Innamorato] which the said characters from ''[https://libraryofruina.wiki.gg/ Library of Ruina]'' are based on. * Additionally, the names "Ishmael", "Ahab", "Heathcliff", "Catherine" and "Gregor" are references to ''Limbus Company'', a game created by the same studio as ''Lobotomy Corporation'' and ''Library of Ruina.'' **These names, like most from Limbus Company, are derived from classic literature. Ishmael and Ahab are from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moby-Dick Moby-Dick], Heathcliff and Catherine are from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuthering_Heights Wuthering Heights] and Gregor is from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metamorphosis The Metamorphosis.] **Faust may be an exception due to said name existing since release, unlike the others mentioned from above, and is a commonly used name in real life. *The names "Chert", "Esker", "Feldspar", "Gabbro" and "Solanum", are references to the game ''[https://store.steampowered.com/app/753640/Outer_Wilds/ Outer Wilds]''. *The names "Luka", "Yugo" and "Faris" could be references to ''[https://steins-gate.fandom.com/wiki/Steins;Gate_Wiki Steins; Gate]''. *Various names reference the works of William Shakespeare: **Claudius, Polonius, Horatio, Laertes, Ophelia, Gertrude, Osric, Cornelius, and Marcellus, are from ''[[wp:Hamlet|Hamlet]]''. **Romeo, Juliet, Mercutio, Tybalt, and Balthasar are from ''[[wp:Romeo and Juliet|Romeo and Juliet]]''. **Agrippa and Demetrius are from ''[[wp:Antony and Cleopatra|Antony and Cleopatra]]''. * The name Sashenka may be a reference to a novel of the same name by Simon Sebag Montefiore. *The names Frieren, Stark, and Fern are a reference to the manga and anime series, ''[[wp:Frieren|Frieren: Beyond Journey's End]]''. * The name Wanderer is a reference to the [https://genshin.hoyoverse.com/en/ Genshin Impact] character, Scaramouche. *The names 'Chilchuck', 'Falin', 'Izutsumi', 'Laios', 'Macille', 'Senshi' and 'Thistle' are all references to the main party and antagonist of the manga and anime series, [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicious_in_Dungeon Dungeon Meshi]. *The names Mycen, Shinon, and Raigh are references to game series [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_Emblem Fire Emblem]. **The name Kelik may be a reference to the (notoriously poorly written) character from a 2013 Fire Emblem mod, [https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/TheLastPromise The Last Promise]. *The names [https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Radovan_Slobasch Radovan] and [https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Ifrit Ifrit] are references to the game series, [https://www.finalfantasyxiv.com/ Final Fantasy]. Furthermore, the name "Clive" is a reference to the Protagonist of Final Fantasy XVI, Dominant of [https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Ifrit_(Final_Fantasy_XVI) Ifrit, the Dark Eikon of Fire], [https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Clive_Rosfield Clive Rosfield]. *The name Basil is a reference to the game [https://www.omori-game.com/ OMORI]. *The name Samwise is a reference to the series Lord of the Rings. *The name Tharson may be a reference to the game Risk of Rain. *The name Tristram may be a reference to a location in the game Diablo. *The name Alvida is a reference to the anime and manga series, One Piece. *The name Azula is a reference to the animated series, Avatar: the Last Airbender. *The name Kiyoko may be a reference to the anime and manga series, Haikyu. *The name Sisyphus is a reference to the ancient Greek myth of Sisyphus, who was doomed to forever train FTD using a Boulder *The name Minos is also a reference to Greek mythology. * Thoth is the Egyptian god of knowledge. *The name Kronk is a reference to Kronk's New Groove. *When in character creation and loading, the randomized name will be displayed as "John Doe" instead of what it's supposed to be, before loading in. John Doe is a placeholder name when the true name of a person is unknown or purposefully hidden. *"Yakub" is either reminiscent of the real-life Arabic name, or the famous tale of the creator of all white men commonly believed by the Nation of Islam.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakub_(Nation_of_Islam) *The name Albion is an alternative name of Great Britain. It may also reference the island of Albion in Warhammer Fantasy universe. It may also be referencing Albion, one the Fallen of Albaz's dragon forms, a character from Yu-Gi-Oh! *The neutral first name Anubis is most likely a reference to the Egyptian God of the same name. * The name Corvo could be a reference to Corvo Attano, the protagonist of Dishonored. *The name Dogbert is a reference to [https://dilbert.fandom.com/wiki/Dogbert a megalomaniacal dog] *The names Phos, Cinnabar, Rutile, Antarc, and Padparadscha are references to the anime and manga series, [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_the_Lustrous Land of the Lustrous]. *The names Montresor and Fortunato are a reference to The Cask of Amontillado, a story by Edgar Allan Poe. *The name "Orpheus" is a reference to the "Master of Strings" of the same name from Greek Mythology, and could possibly be a reference to [https://megamitensei.fandom.com/wiki/Orpheus Orpheus from the Persona series] *The names "Maras" and "Nosfa" are references to Fallen World; a game being created by InnerTenacity *There are repeatable names, due to the same name being a selectable first and last name. Something like Regulus Regulus or Marius Marius. *The name "Crona" might be a reference to Crona from [https://souleater.fandom.com/wiki/Crona Soul Eater]. *The names "Teshin", "Incarnon", and "Lotus" are references to [https://www.warframe.com Warframe]. *The name "Ohma" might be a reference to Ohma Tokita from Kengan Asura. *The name "Arthas" is a reference to [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Arthas_Menethil Arthas Menethil] from [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_The_Frozen_Throne Warcraft 3]. *The names "Jinshi" and "Maomao" are in reference to the protagonists of The Apothecary Diaries. *The name "Atreus" could be a reference to the son of Kratos in God of War. ==References== [[Category:Character]] [[Category:Creation]] [[Category:Mechanics]]

==Description==
Nanji is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. Upon speaking to them, they task the player with finding the whereabouts of [[Ilji]], their brother through the "Wandering Blade" [[Quest]].

==Quest details==
Completing their sidequest will reward you with EXP, positive [[Etrea]] reputation, Compassion, and the {{t|Nanji's Training}} Talent, granting +1 Posture.
#Go to the [[Isle of Vigils]].
#Find the Well-Preserved Grave near the attunement training gear shop.
#Use the zipline on the left of the grave.
#Once on the other side of the zipline, head towards the tree and turn right after passing the cliff corner.
#Interact and inspect the [[Katana]] until it only gives you the option to end dialogue.
#Return to Nanji and interact with them.

File:Chipped Sword Dialogue.png|An Etrean interacting with the sword
Screenshot 2026-07-27 152229.png
</gallery>

==Location==
Nanji is located at the bridge heading towards the [[Barber]] and [[Nerin]] at [[Etris]].

==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{{#tag:tabber|Quest Start=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="12" style="color:#32CD32;" {{!}}Begin
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="12" {{!}}I don't know what to do...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}What's wrong?
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}We can play catch with a Gobletto?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}I haven't seen my little brother for days. I've asked everyone, looked everywhere. I can't find a single trace of him.
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}Uh... Yeah, no.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}Maybe I've heard something. What's his name?
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#D2042D;" {{!}}End
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}Ilji, and I'm Nanji. We're travellers who set off from here a year ago, and we've now returned home. We agreed to meet at this point two days ago.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#00FFFF;" {{!}}[Haven't found the sword]
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#00FFFF;" {{!}}[Already found the sword]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}I'm sorry. I haven't heard a thing.
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}I found his sword at the bottom of a cliff.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}*''Sigh.''* I shouldn't have gotten my hopes up. If you happen to see him, please come and let me know.
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}No... His sword..? Ilji and I... were eachother's closest rivals in the way of the sword. We both trained to best eachother constantly. If there's one thing Ilji would never allow himself to be separated from... It's this.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}I'll keep an eye out.
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#D2042D;" {{!}}End, Quest Complete
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" {{!}}If you end up finding him, I'll be grateful.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="3" style="color:#D2042D;" {{!}}End
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Quest End=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="12" style="color:#32CD32;" {{!}}Begin
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="12" {{!}}You're back... But he's not with you.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#00FFFF;" {{!}}[Sword Found]
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#00FFFF;" {{!}}[Sword Not Found]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}I found his sword at the bottom of a cliff.
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#E4D00A;" {{!}}I haven't been able to find him.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}No... His sword..? Ilji and I... were eachother's closest rivals in the way of the sword. We both trained to best eachother constantly. If there's one thing Ilji would never allow himself to be separated from... It's this.
{{!}} colspan="6" {{!}}No? Please, keep looking for him... I have to remain here. Just in case he shows up.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#D2042D;" {{!}}End, Quest Complete
{{!}} colspan="6" style="color:#D2042D;" {{!}}End
{{!}}}

title: Nautilodaunt
content:
''For the stronger variant that utilizes Thundercall, see [[Fury Nautilodaunt]].'' {{Topbuttons|p, [[Fury Nautilodaunt]], {{iv|Nautilodaunt Officiate}}}} {{Quotes|quote=...Denizens of Scyphozia, Nautilodaunts are a chilling reminder that those of the Deep are not simply mindless monsters, but can possess startling intelligence.|author=Odd Tentacle description }}Mostly referred to as "Squibbo". {{Monster Infobox|title1=Nautilodaunt |image1=SQUIBBO.png |health=900
2250 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}}
|drops=[[Odd Tentacle]]
[[Pathfinder Elite]] (Very Rare)
[[Martial Artist]] (Semi-Rare)
[[Nautilodaunt Beak]] (Extremely Rare)
[[Black Diver]] (Very Rare)
[[Cala-Mariner]] (Very Rare) |locations=[[First Layer]]
[[The City of the Drowned]]
[[The Diluvian Mechanism]]}} ==Description== The Nautilodaunt is a bipedal monster found in the [[The Depths|Depths]]. It exclusively spawns during the Depths Collapse event, when you are doing the "Nautilodaunt Extermination" job or within the marketplace in the [[The City of the Drowned|City of the Drowned]] (except for [[Hell Mode]]), rummaging through some wares. When killed, it will drop either an [[Odd Tentacle]] or in much rarer cases, a [[Pathfinder Elite]]. The Nautilodaunt can also spawn from [[Chests & Sacks|Mimic Chests]] after opening at an extremely rare chance. It will spawn with feathers and smoke erupting from the chest and attack you. Nautilodaunt has a chance to be summoned by [[Interluminary Parasol]]. While a Nautilodaunt is rummaging in the marketplace, it creates easily distinguished noises, making them especially easy to detect and avoid. However, if they are no longer rummaging through the marketplace, said noise will not be created, it will simply stand in silence until another player approaches and is spotted. {{Quotes|quote=...They do not take a liking to human flesh, tending instead to experiment upon the fallen, inserting parasites into their victims.|author=Odd Tentacle description }} There are no existing records of research done on Nautilodaunts, and their origins and life cycle are largely unknown. However, it is observed that they are highly intelligent creatures, evident by their sheer combat prowess and their exceptional ability to utilize the motor functions their anatomy would allow to the fullest extent. In addition to their impressive intelligence, it is also observed that they are capable of turning humans into Mudskippers, their preferred way of finishing off prey, for the purpose of experimentation, displaying a chillingly human natural curiosity. Their skill and strength are even recognized by the [[Voices of the Depths]], using them as secret weapons against the especially powerful. They are true menaces, with the one at the marketplace even rewarding positive reputation with the Divers upon defeat. ==Attack Patterns== {| class="fandom-table article-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Punch'''
(★☆☆) |The Nautilodaunt attempts to punch their prey with a variety of different punches. *These have long hitstun with very little delay between each hit, '''do not''' attempt to retaliate or parry immediately after being hit, as you will only be interrupted again. Instead, let the Nautilodaunt hit you two more times before attempting to parry its next punch. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★☆) |Nautilodaunt's punches randomly lead into a kicking flourish, forcing the opponent backwards. They typically close the distance created for another attack by powerwalking, sliding towards you, or using '''Flip-Kick'''. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Flip-Kick'''[[File:Blunt.png|frameless]]
(★★★) |Nautilodaunt flips into the air and attempts to strike their prey with a kick. *This is most commonly used to close the distance between targets that are at a higher elevation than it; often being used after Grand Stomp. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |- |
'''Drop-Kick'''[[File:Blunt.png|frameless]]
(★★★) |Nautilodaunt initiates a full sprint before committing to a drop kick on its prey. {{AttackTags |indicator = parry |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Grand Stomp'''
(★★★) |Nautilodaunt stomps the ground, sending rubble powered by geysers hurtling towards you in a straight line. *This is most commonly used against distant prey for a variety of functions such as giving chase, or to take the initiative. *This insta-grips, sparing you from becoming a Mudskipper but still wiping you all the same. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Feint'''
(★★☆) |The Nautilodaunt halts their attack mid-way in an attempt to mixup their opponent and create an opening. *If the Nautilodaunt feints and you whiff your parry, '''dodge''' the next attack instead of attempting to parry it. {{AttackTags |misc, unharmful }} |- |
'''Vent'''
(★☆☆) |If hit by any move that utilizes the Song (such as a Mantra, certain Resonances, or a Vent from the player), the Nautilodaunt will near-completely negate the damage of said Mantra. This can happen even during other moves. {{AttackTags |misc, unharmful }} |} ===Finisher=== == Finisher == {| class="fandom-table" ! Name !Description |- |'''Mudskipperification''' |Punches the victim's head with a parasite in it's hand, inserting it into their skull and turning them into a Mudskipper. |} ===Talents=== *'''Monster Resistance''' - has 70-80% elemental reduction. =='''Combat / Tips'''== While this mob has the health equivalent to a [[Megalodaunt]], making it the weakest of the endgame tier mobs, it's unique in the fact that it has a much smarter AI along with the ability to '''Block''', '''Parry''', and '''Dodge'''. While this mob '''cannot''' be power checked, most strategies that work on [[The Enforcer]] will also work on the Nautilodaunt, aside from its much higher damage. Even with its near immunity to [[Attunement |Mantras]], it can still be posture broken quickly and easily with mantras such as [[Galebreathe |Tornado]] or [[Ironsing |Caltrops]]. Keep in mind that standard humanoid boss PVE tactics such as stacking attacks, grouping up, and running to heal can still work against this mob, and that due to its incredibly low health of 1000 (which can reach numbers as small as 200 with PvE Scaling), it will die incredibly fast. It also cannot reliably parry Critical Attacks if a feint is used beforehand, making instant guardbreaks such as the [[Pernach]] and a majority of [[Weapons |Heavy Weapons]] turn this mob into a far easier challenge. With such a weapon, simply block 2 or 3 attacks, then feint-critical to blockbreak him. Do this until he dies. This is still a very risky strategy, especially if you run out of posture to block with. Keep in mind that using the One-Handed stance with a [[Weapons|heavy Weapon]] makes you deal less posture damage, allowing the Nautilodaunt to safely block one Critical swing, so be sure to swap back to the Two-handed stance if you encounter one. However, without a "cheese weapon," each of the Nautilodaunt's attacks can prove difficult, so they will be gone through in order: *The Nautilodaunt has a wide variety of punch variations, which all possess their own speed and animations, throwing off any players who believe to have hit a rhythm. Their animations are desynced, so what could be a Parry ends up as a Block, usually with the hit coming before the animation finishes. After a punch, it can follow up with any of its other punches instead of pausing like the Enforcer would, this can be chained infinitely leading to infamous "Infinite Combos," especially from the Fury variant. *Nautilodaunt's kick is basically identical to The Enforcer's. It will usually use it as an extension of his other attacks, placing it after his normal or double punches. While dealing less damage than its punches, it is painfully quick and the second hit will low profile. * Attempting to Vent to disengage, or use any mantras, will proc its Vent regardless of what action its doing, leading to incredibly heavy Mantra resistance but not Immunity. This action is not considered an attack and as such can be "movestacked" with. *Flip-Kick and Drop-Kick share many similarities. Normally, Nautilodaunt power-walks towards its targets. But right before it uses these two attacks, it will perform a much different "Naruto-Run" towards the opponent. Flip-kick is used when the Nautilodaunt gets somewhat close, rapidly closing the gap in the air with a kick. This is INCREDIBLY fast, but also somewhat delayed for when the attack actually lands, being an easy source of whiplash. Alternatively, it will plow right into the player with a sliding Drop-Kick, dealing high damage, and also being rather fast. However, these moves will only be used at a distance. ** In theory, it should be easy to avoid these attacks as it clearly telegraphs them with the sprint, but in practice, both of the attacks have radically different executions, speeds, and delays, basically forcing you to have to react fast enough. If it keeps running towards you after a distance it WOULD HAVE flipped from, it's almost certainly a Drop-Kick. * Its third attack is made when distance is made that's too far for a Flip or Drop-Kick, the Nautilodaunt instead stomps the floor with a loud audio cue. Depending on your distance, it can either be highly telegraphable as the pillars go progressively, or nigh unreactable if it is incredibly close to you. While this move is the most dangerous, realistically you should not be seeing this attack outside of being on top of a building. Always keep calm while fighting the Nautilodaunt, and rely on parries before doing a Critical Attack to break their posture and kill it in one or two guardbreaks. If you have an incredibly high damage mantra (such as Tornado or Caltrops), instead those may be used as the Nautilodaunt will choose to ignore them in order to vent, which leads to a Posture Break that will allow you to kill it while having only blocked or parried and using one move. On a final note, you '''cannot''' sneak attack the Nautilodaunt while it is burrowing at the spawn, as it will consistently dodge the first attack. Its aggro range is pretty big so be cautious if you are entering on its side of the city, listen out for the digging because it's loud enough for you to be able to hear it from outside the agro range. '''The best way to beat it is by having an insta-guard break weapon'''.
==Gallery== File:Nautilodaunt Model Render.png|Model Render File:Nautilodaunt Idle1.gif|Nautilodaunt Idle File:Squibbo2.png|Eyeview File:Squibbo naruto run.png|Nautilodaunt Chasing File:Squid victim.png|A victim being jumped File:Squibbo killing somebody.png|A victim of the Mudskipper parasite File:Nautilodaunt Rummaging.gif|Nautilodaunt Rummaging File:Squibbo Back.png|Nautilodaunt Back File:Squibbo Sideview.png|Nautilodaunt Sideview ==Trivia== *The Nautilodaunt cannot vent in [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. *The Nautilodaunt is likely inspired by the Mind Flayers from ''Dungeons & Dragons'', which similarly implant parasites into humans. [https://jujutsu-kaisen.fandom.com/wiki/Dagon Dagon] from ''[https://jujutsu-kaisen.fandom.com/wiki/Jujutsu_Kaisen Jujutsu Kaisen]'' also bears similarity to the Nautilodaunt in terms of appearance. *The Nautilodaunt is one of two monsters that can be both guard broken and posture stunned, the other being [[The Enforcer]]. *When it isn't in combat, it will automatically begin healing, going from 250 to full health within a matter of seconds. *It spawns roughly every 18 minutes. *[[Mortus]] mentions his wife was killed when they fished up an octopus. Since no octopuses are present in Deepwoken, he may have been referring to a Nautilodaunt. He also says that he no longer fishes up octopuses, indicating that there won't be a Nautilodaunt bait in the game anytime soon. *The Nautilodaunt cannot vent when its attacking. * The vent it uses was the old vent before Deepwoken's release. *If encountered in the overworld, it has the ability to swim. However, it does not possess a swimming animation. *It is named after the Nautilus, a family of shelled cephalopods. *Despite being nearly impossible to see the Nautilodaunts armor can be broken *It is internally referred to as ".squidward."[[File:.squidward.jpg|250px]] *May spawn Frostdraw attuned ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]]

title: Nautilodaunt Officiate
content:
{{Topbuttons|[[Nautilodaunt]], [[Fury Nautilodaunt]], {{iv|p}}}} {{IronVowEx}} {{InProgress|Body=Gifs needed for Attacks}} {{Monster Infobox |title1=Nautilodaunt Officiate |health=400 |attacks=*Punch *Kick *Flip Kick *High Flip Kick *Electro Stomp *Furious Stomp *Combo Slam *Feint *Vent|drops=*[[Odd Tentacle]] *[[Pathfinder Elite]] (Very Rare) *[[Stormseye]] *[[Nautilodaunt Beak]] *[[Justicar's Armor]] *[[Cala-Mariner]] *[[Martial Artist]] *[[Astruline]] |locations={{iv|The Depths (Vow of Iron)|The Depths}}
|image1=Nautilodaunt Officiate.png|caption1=The '''TRUE''' incarnation of pure fear.}} == Description == The {{PAGENAME}} (also known as Enforcer Squibbo) is a mix of a [[Fury Nautilodaunt]] and an [[Enforcer]], creating the abominable weapon seen in the Depths Trial of {{iv|Vow of Iron}}. They have the body shape and fighting style of a [[Nautilodaunt]] but the shell of an Enforcer, as well as a few new attacks that make it a foe fitting of its position, making quick work of unfortunate souls. {{clear|right}} == Attacks == {|class="sortable article-table" !Name/Danger !Description !Media |- |
'''Punch'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} punches their prey with a variety of different punches. *These are similar to a [[Nautilodaunt]]'s Punches, the difference being theyre slightly slower, enough to throw off those accustomed to the regular Nautilodaunt's pace. *Works similarly to a humanoid enemy's Assault, finishing off with '''Kick''' after enough Punches have been thrown out. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Kick'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} performs a kick, knocking the opponent away. *Usually uses another attack to follow-up after, meaning you must stay on guard. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Flip Kick'''
(★★★) |The {{PAGENAME}} initiates a full sprint before flipping into the air and descending down towards their prey with a kick. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, movement }} |[[File:officiatedropkck.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''High Flip Kick'''
(★★★) |Starts similarly to '''Flip Kick''', but is instead done in place and the {{PAGENAME}} jumps much higher, as well as being only dodgeable. {{AttackTags |indicator = guardbreak |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Drop-Kick'''
(★★★) |{{PAGENAME}} initiates a full sprint before committing to a drop kick on its prey. {{AttackTags |indicator = parry |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Electro Stomp'''
(★★★) |The {{PAGENAME}} stomps the ground, making geysers of rubble and lightning burst from the ground in a straight line, knocking upwards those hit. *Rolling to the side makes avoiding this attack more consistent, as each geyser has its own hitbox. *However, effectively avoiding this attack is not guaranteed, as it comes out very fast and deals dangerously high damage. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, autogrip }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Furious Stomp'''
(★★★) |Starts out similarly to '''Electro Stomp''', but the animation is much slower, and the geysers are instead colored red. *This attack can be avoided by rolling or simply walking to the side as it cannot change directions when using this attack. {{AttackTags |indicator = skull |parry.n, block.n, dodge.n, jump }} |[[File:officiatewhiteslam.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Combo Slam'''
(★★★) |The {{PAGENAME}} lets out a roar and performs two back-to-back punches, after which it will raise both of its arms up and slam down with them, creating a large white crater on the ground. *The two punches before the slam come out relatively fast, but do not do too much damage, most of the damage comes from the following slam. *It can move while using this move, often causing it to miss the slam entirely as it keeps walking past you. *It will gain its green indicator on the last attack of the sequence. *You can jump to avoid the final slam which allows you to get a free aerial attack in. {{AttackTags |indicator = parry |parry.y, block.y, dodge.n, jump }} |[[File:officiatepunchpunchslam.gif|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Feint'''
(★★☆) |The {{PAGENAME}} halts their attack mid-way in an attempt to mix-up their opponent and create an opening. *It can only '''Feint''' its '''Punch''' attack. {{AttackTags |unharmful, misc }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |- |
'''Vent'''
(★☆☆) |If hit by an elemental move, the {{PAGENAME}} will gain a blue aura and near-completely negate the damage of said attack. *This move seems to activate passively. {{AttackTags |unharmful, misc }} |[[File:Placeholder.png|centre|thumb]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Thunderstruck Fury''' - All of the {{PAGENAME}}'s attacks apply [[Status Effects#Shock|Shock]], stunning you and interrupting your attacks, even through [[Status Effects#Hyperarmor|Hyperarmor]]. **This passive makes the {{PAGENAME}} ''significantly'' more dangerous than its default counterpart, as you cannot hyperarmor your way through its attacks. *Hardened Guard - The {{PAGENAME}} has significantly more posture than its counterparts. ==Tips== *Stay close to the {{PAGENAME}}, and '''DO NOT VENT'''. Venting will usually result in the {{PAGENAME}} using Electro Stomp which is essentially a guaranteed hit due to vent endlag. *Try to "statcheck" and focus more on attacking than parry trading. It may sound counter intuitive, but once you get about 2-3 trades on the {{PAGENAME}}, fishing for more leaves you vulnerable to feints or other attacks whereas attacking will usually connect as long as you fully commit. == Trivia == *This [[Nautilodaunt]] variant seemingly breaks the lore associated with the [[Enforcer|Enforcers]], as Enforcers are the souls of those who have failed to beat the Depths Trial, morphed into the Enforcers we know today, and it doesn't seem very plausible that a Nautilodaunt would not only have a soul, but to have fought - and failed to survive - the Depths Trial. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:The Depths]]

title: Navaen Hostage
content:
{{EnemyInfobox|image1=File:Navae Front1.png|health=1200|drops=None|weapon=N/A|moves=N/A}}
==Description==
Navaen Hostages hail from the [[Children of Navae]]. They appear exclusively as [[Gremor]]s wearing the [[Navaen Nomad Robes]]. The hostages are often accompanied with 3 [[Knife of Eylis|Knives of Eylis]]. A Navaen Hostage is required for the obtainment of the [[Way of Navae]] fighting style.

The best way to find them is through the [[Job_Boards#Erisia|Knife To Antler]] Job, as it guarantees that they will spawn.

They are found in a prisoner pose, kneeled down on both knees and having their arms behind their backs, though they are forced into a standard pose when being knocked back. They usually randomly spawn in [[Erisia]], most commonly upper parts such as [[Towerstruck Lands]], [[The Garden Reservoir]], and [[The Birdcage]].

Navaen Hostages can be picked up by pressing {{Input|keybind|V}}. Dropping them will cause them to be knocked for a bit before returning to their original stance. Unlike any normal NPC, you can carry the hostage anywhere and everywhere, and will not despawn unless you travel to a new Luminant.

Bringing a Navaen Hostage to the [[Eastern Nomad Leader]], [[Beiruul]], or the [[Eastern Camp Master]] will give you the [[Way of Navae]] fighting style prompting a dialogue that will be shown below. This will also allow you to choose the style in [[Character Creation]] on subsequent characters.

== Gallery==

File:FunnySAD Hostage.png
</gallery>
[[File:Navae dialogue.PNG|center|thumb|500x500px|Giving back what is rightfully theirs.]]

==Trivia ==
* [[File:Trial hostage combat tag.png|thumb|Being combat tagged by ".hostage_nomad1".]]For some strange reason, there is a brick that spawns a single Hostage above the [[Trial of One]]. If you are hit by the first parry-check orb and you hover over the combat tag skull, you'll find yourself combat tagged by ''".hostaage_nomad1"''; apparently, the Nomad is the one attacking you. Should it be thrown off the cube the dungeon takes place in, the Parry Check orbs will be incapable of dealing any actual damage.
**This can actually be done by using the [[Providence's Thorns]] Enchantment on your weapon, and parrying enough of the orbs, which will knock the Navaen Hostage, dropping them off the brick.
*Despite popular belief, you do not need any Light Weapon points to equip Way of Navae, nor any of the other fist styles. You only need points in Light Weapons to equip a Cestus, but even then, the [[Iron Cestus]] only needs a fist style.
*They can be turned in to [[Alastir]] for a chest.

title: Neatly Embelished Notebook
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
Neatly Embelished Notebook
===
This notebook is neatly bound, embossed with rich iconographies of the Moonseye. [The pages are packed to the brim with scruffy diary entries, doodles, and administrative jargon, written in an almost-indecipherable script. Sheets of crumpled iridescent paper with aggressively slashed-out paragraphs bookmark the pages. Intrigued, you flip to one of the most recent entries, hoping to find something legible. It seems to be a brief list, hurriedly jotted down. You imagine it must've been misplaced, considering it was just lurking upon a shelf.] ---- - Week's s'pply of rations for the j'rney. {{g|The Moonseye|Moonseye}} knows how long it'll take. - Make sure Konrad r'quests his new unif'rm upon arrival. He will forget. - {{g|The Counsell|Counsell}} doc'ments. MAKE SURE THEY'RE ORGANISED. Liviu has the right crates and bindings. Ens're the job is done. - Have the rest pr'pare the cargo at LEAST two days b'fore. We will not be forg'tting half our doc'ments again like last year. - Aud'ence with our {{g|Confessor}}. Perhaps He will let us in to speak with her this time. [Turning to the next page reveals a short diary entry, scribbled furiously.] ---- Not allow'd in. Again. Act'ng as if the Central Chamber is some exclus've little suite for Him and our {{g|Confessor}} only. OUR {{g|Confessor}}, Not his. Must be spectac'lar comp'ny, that damn'd sarcoph'gus. (Forgive me.) {{g|The Counsell|Counsell}} still trying t' appease me with some sec'nd-hand 'Good lucks' and 'May She prot'ct your j'rneys', but they know how much it'd mean to these new scholars t' receive her own pers'nal bless'ng b'fore this trip. Especially consid'ring that we're lik'ly to have those Author'ty terrors breath'ng down our necks. Those scholars don't ev'n have a clue that there's ev'n a risk of our ship being pumm'lled by those barb'rous brutes as soon 's we leave the archipelago. They've no idea what an 'Author'ty is! W'ldn't it be nice to put th'm in a good mood? Instill th'm with good morale? No. Th' Vox refus's to see a soul. Some oracle! Insists th' {{g|Confessor}} keeps her words f'r 'Nostri Eclipse or any oth'r grand ev'nt where he can preach to her public. {{g|The Moonseye|Moonseye's}} sake. He bar'ly even allows the {{g|The Counsell|Counsell}} in! They're flounder'ng without any substant'l decrees on the progress of th' Isles this year, but it seems the Vox is content with that. Or, well, it seems th' {{g|Confessor}} is content with that. I'm not sure wh'ch. Some oracle, hm? Perf'ct at whipp'ng up tired crowds at the end of their pilgr'mage, but not at deliv'r'ng the most import'nt of advices? Or when he does, it's some impassion'd and nonsens'cal garble on "Th' danger of her'tics!! No! We need this year's harv'st dates, not paranoid rambling! Gah! What mess. I can only pray our j'rney is uninterrupted. May th' {{g|Confessor}} prot'ct us, whether we hear it from her or not. From all this examination of our own past, th' Acolyte has always been entitled t' receive an aud'ence with the {{g|Confessor}}, and her Vox. And now it's all d'fferent. Everything's d'fferent. I'm convinced s'mething's awry. With the Vox, that is - I daren't quest'n our {{g|Confessor}}, I pray th' {{g|The Counsell|Counsell}} checks on that man's tinn'd brain, or whatever's left behind that clamp of a mask. Or perhaps this is just th' {{g|The Lady Confessor|Confessor's}} will, and we ought t' follow it. Perhaps time will just need to tell. I've my own probl'ms at hand.
[[Category:Books]]

==Description==
Needle's Eye is an endgame [[Weapons|Rapier]] that require 75 Light Weapon to use.

Being a refined rapier made for nobility, its ornate design highlights its deadly capabilities. A Needle's Eye has a similar stat lineup to other endgame rapiers, albeit being on the lower end in terms of raw statistical values. While very powerful in the right hands, this weapon's strength lies in its unique critical.

Needle's Eyes are replicas of the former Duchess [[Thera Erisia]]'s famed personal rapier. Thera bore the title of the Needle's Eye.<ref>[[Pathfinder's Respite]]</ref>

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:NeedlesEyeCrit.gif
</gallery>
The user winds up before stabbing the opponent 5 times and lunging forwards to unleash a sixth strike. Each hit applies Daze and has 35% chip damage. Upon critical activation, gain a 1 second long speed boost (this will last for the first four hits).

The critical has the following stats and modifiers: 0.9x (first hit) + 0.5x * 5 (last five hits). The first five strikes deal 4 posture damage each, the final one guard breaks.

The critical has a cooldown of '''5 seconds'''.

{{text|slowturn}} {{text|m1tag}}

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
Needle's Eye Full.png|Full view
</gallery>

==Trivia==
*Needle's Eye is the slowest rapier in the game, having a swing speed of 1.05x.
*Needle's Eye and the [[Golden Swordfish]] are the only two non-legendary rapiers to have a unique critical attack. 
*This rapier has the same name as the [https://rogue-lineage.fandom.com/wiki/Whisperer Whisperer's] skill from ''[https://www.roblox.com/games/3016661674/Rogue-Lineage Rogue Lineage]''.

Well, at least for us historian types, not so much the looters.|author=Neero}} {{NPCInfobox |image1= neero2.png | Current neero.png | Old |name=Neero |aspect=Celtor |location=[[Temple of the Forgotten Flame]]}} ==Description== Neero is a [[Celtor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. They are a [[Pathfinder]] wearing an [[Iron Mask]] along with the [[Pathfinder Cloak]]. They are investigating the disappearance of the [[Relics|Forge of Sin]] and provides speculation about [[Duke Erisia]]'s actions prior to the events of the [[The Lord Regent|Lord Regent's]] questline, as well as lore about [[Erisia]] and the Forge itself. ==Location== Neero is located in the [[Temple of the Forgotten Flame]], leaning against the wall. File:NPC Map Neero.png ==Dialogue== {| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" | colspan="8" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue |- | colspan="8" |Ah, another {{g|Pathfinders|Pathfinder}}? |- | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |Yep. | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |What's a Pathfinder? |- | colspan="4" |Oh really? Are you one of those self-professed {{g|Pathfinders}} who make a living peddling stolen artifacts to the petty aristocracy? ''*He adjusts his mask and sighs.*'' Sorry. I apologize for being so crass, I tend to only run into those who tarnish our reputation simply by breathing. | colspan="4" |I don't have time for questions of philosophy, you nit-wit... Oh, you really don't know? A {{g|Pathfinders|Pathfinder}} is someone who explores these {{g|Driftlands}}. Some of us are scavengers, some are historians, and some are bounty hunters. |- | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |What're you doing here? | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |What do Pathfinders do? |- | colspan="4" |I've been searching this Temple for the 'Forge of Sin'. It was written to be in the peaks of Erisia, but someone or ''something'' seems to have dragged it away... The marks don't seem fresh though, it must've been pulled away some time ago, perhaps during the last time the island drifted into one of the {{g|The Luminants|Luminants}}? | colspan="4" |Our job is to make sense of the world left behind in these time-adjacent places. Well, at least for us historian types, not so much the looters. Although, I think the disappearance of the Forge here is not due to a {{g|Pathfinders|Pathfinder}}. I believe this island fell to great tragedy the last time it washed into the {{g|The Voidsea|Voidsea}}. |- | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |The last time it drifted? | colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Great tragedy? | colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |The Forge? |- | colspan="4" |These islands are known to drift in and out of the {{g|The Voidsea|Voidsea}} over the years. {{g|Pathfinders}} have been looking for Erisia for decades. Though, all of that time spent searching just for the Forge to be missing? Maybe this coincides with the great tragedy that befell this place. | colspan="4" |[See first instance] |- | colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |Great tragedy? | colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} |The Forge? |- | colspan="2" |Yes... From what I can see, the golems function as a sort of ''security system''. They're able to discern man from monster, but they aren't powered by {{g|Thundercall}}. Something else makes them function - as if the stones themselves have been given life. | colspan="2" |Better known as the Forge of Sin... An artifact once dredged up from the deep and kept in this temple. Legends say the Forge enabled its wielder to shape not only metal, but the ''souls of men''. |- | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |Any ideas what it could be? |- | colspan="4" |Well, it's not {{g|Lifeweave / Lifewoven|Lifeweaver}} tech, that's for sure. The main thing that catches my eye is that purple flame... Something caused the golems to start killing the inhabitants of the island. Or seemingly, ''capturing'' them. |- | colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} |Capturing them? |- | colspan="4" |Yes, there would be signs of bloodshed otherwise. I find it hard to believe that such advanced constructs run wild on their own, someone must have given them the order, no? It all comes back to that strange flame... |- | colspan="4" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue] |} ==Trivia== *Neero wears the old model of the [[Iron Mask]], along with the [[Pathfinder Cloak]]. *Using shiftlock to see inside of his mask shows that Neero is a Celtor, based upon his facial markings. {{History}} [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:NPCs located in the Etrean Luminant]]

You must drink it. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] }} ==Trivia == *Both they and [[Funke]] don the [[Black Diver]] [[outfit]]. According to Arch_Mage, they are most likely Black Divers.[[File:Nellfunkebd.png]] ** If they are indeed [[The Divers|Divers]], this would make then and Funke two of the oldest, physically, known Divers, as they are the only Divers with [[Age|wrinkles]], excluding [[Coldheart Fortinbras]]. *Their eyes are unique, having a dark blue sclera similar to that of the [[Hallowtide]] variant of the [[Adret]] aspect.[[File:Nell's pretty face.png|frameless]]Close-up of Nell's face and eyes. The only ottheirNPC that shares these eyes is [[Coldheart Fortinbras]]. *Nell is equipped with a Gran Sudaruska. As there was only one Sudaruska, only one Gran Sudaruska exists, seemingly implying Nell wields ''the'' Gran Sudaruska. In reality, this is a case of Gameplay and Story Segregation, having it for the games' sake; being so they have a unique, legendary weapon when they're fought.[[File:Nellgransuda.png]] *Nell used to have [[Rapid Punches]] before the NPC Mantra changes. *Unlike most [[Attunement Trainers]], they can be aggroed, seen during the [[Etris: Siege|Etris Raid]] event occasionally fighting off Authority troops if they somehow get to her. ==References== {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Attunement Trainers]] [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:Diver Enemies]] [[Category:NPCs located in the Etrean Luminant]] [[Category:Individuals with They/them pronouns]]

|droppable=No
|pass down=Yes
}}

==Description==
{{PAGENAME}} is a damage dealing [[enchantment]] that replaces your critical with a teleporting slash.

==Effect==
{{PAGENAME}} changes your weapon's critical attack to resemble that of the [[Katana]]'s, though this attack will not have hit registry unless you've applied the {{status|Nemesis Mark}}.

Upon landing an M1, {{PAGENAME}} applies the {{status|Nemesis Mark}} status effect, priming your target for your critical attack. When using your critical attack on a marked target, teleport to them and slash them, dealing 25 slash damage or 18 posture damage if blocked.

If you've marked multiple targets, you will teleport to each of them on critical and hit them in quick succession.<gallery widths="200">
Nemesismark.gif|Nemesis Mark
</gallery>

===Notes===
*Nemesis' critical '''cannot''' be buffed through damage modifiers.
*Nemesis' critical '''can''' proc "on critical" Talents, but as it cannot benefit from damage modifiers, certain Talents may not benefit it.
*Nemesis' critical has a range limit of 65-70 studs.

==Trivia==
*This Enchantment's visuals and sound effects are based off the cursed status from ''Spiral Knights''.

==Description==
The Nemit's Sickle is a dagger that boasts a 30% penetration against armor and an extremely high swing speed like most of the other daggers. It does less damage than few other daggers, however its high penetration and high scaling make up for it.

==Talents==
{{text|wtal}}

{{etal|weapon|Curved Edge}} grants +30% chip damage to all [[Attunement-less#Light Weapon Mantras|Light Weapon Mantras]].

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:Nemit.gif
</gallery>
The user winds up for 0.45 seconds and then unleashes a quick upward slash before unleashing a strong side kick, dealing high damage and high posture damage on block. This knocks the target back, even if the move is blocked and deals about 16 posture damage.

The first hit has a 1.2x scaled damage multiplier and applies {{cl|bleed}}. The second hit has a scaled damage multiplier of 0.65x.

The critical has a cooldown of '''4 seconds'''.

==Trivia==
*This weapon serves as an alternate for [[Alloyed Tanto]], which is often used as a pseudo medium weapon.
*Remodeled on {{VersionHistory|2024|December 24th}} as a part of the World Events update.

[[File:Nest Corridor.png|thumb|900px|center]]
==Overview==
The Nest Corridor is a location located between [[Firfire Caverns]] and [[The Maw of Ethiron]]. Stepping foot into the corridor prompts waves of multiple Bounders to spawn, and is one of the requirements to spawn the [[Chaser, Scholar of the Burning Blood|Chaser]] boss fight. At the end of the corridor, opposite of a fenced ledge is the [[Ignition Deepdrill]], which will only spawn if you got [[Llevyn]] to call it beforehand. If you are feeling very confident, killing four of the six bounders rewards you with a chest that has the same amount of items and drop rates as the one that drops from Chaser (if not better), as the bounders are not meant to be killed, just evaded and ignored.

Keep in mind that leaving Layer 2 through the Deepdrill will ''not'' let you keep the loot that you gathered while there, unless it's equipment that you already have equipped.

*[[Ignition Deepdrill]]

==Trivia==

==Description ==
The Night Axe is a [[Weapons|Heavy Weapon]] in the Greataxe category. It can be obtained from [[Ministry Necromancer]]. Its defining trait is having 80% chip damage, making blocking almost completely useless against it. 

== Critical ==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:Night axe crit.gif
</gallery>
The user performs a Shadowcast-empowered upwards swing that guard breaks and steals Ether on hit. The critical is compatible with Shadowcast talents that '''do not''' specify Mantras, like {{t|Sightless Still}} and [[Talents#Twisted Puppets|Twisted Puppet's]] Shadowcast burn for example.

The critical deals '''1.25x scaled damage''', and deals Slash and Shadow damage. It has a '''windup of 0.6s''' and '''0.3s of endlag'''. 

The critical has a cooldown of '''3 seconds'''.

title: Nightwish x Deepwoken Promotional Event
content:
{{EventContent}} {{Event|image1=Yesterwynde tavern1.png|effects=|items=* Gilded Instrument Skins|type=Promotional Event|date1=1522|date2=9/20/2024}} == Description ==
''• To celebrate the release of Nightwish's new album "Yesterwynde", a promotional event will be available this weekend!
• Doorways leading to the [[Yesterwynde Tavern]] have emerged across Lumen, with the tavern itself tended by the Ferryman of all people...
• Search Lumen for the three missing Yesterwynde Vinyls from the Ferryman's collection and earn yourself exclusive skins for your instruments ingame!"''
''- The Deepwoken team'' This is a promotional event for Nightwish, a Finnish metal band. By finding and entering one of the many tavern doors scattered around the map, the player will be able to speak to [[The Ferryman]] and pick up the event quest in which the players must retrieve the Krulian's music collection. The event quest requires the player to collect 3 records across Lumen, giving the following cryptic hint at the end of the dialogue:
''"One lurks over the machinery threaded through the caldera of a volcano, another lies within a nestled spot of nature within a frozen waste, and the final record can be found in a land lost to time, yet familiar all the same."''
''- The Ferryman'' The hint indicates towards each record being located at [[Upper Erisia]], [[Minityrsa]], and [[Miner's Landing]]. Upon collecting all three and returning to the Ferryman, the player will be rewarded with gilded [[Instruments]]. This reward applies to all slots on the account. Additionally, the Ferryman provides free [[Redd Juice]] to the player, only if they don't already have one. More about the [[Yesterwynde Tavern]] can be found in its respective page. ==Obtainment== *Begin the quest as instructed above, the tavern doors can be found tucked away at almost every major island in the game. Note that you do not need to accept the quest first before finding the Vinyl records *The first record can be found in [[Upper Erisia]]. Go past the [[Mudskipper|Mudskipper Knights]] and down through the rock passage as you would do for the [[Temple of the Blade|A Lost Sibling]] quest. As soon as you exit the rock passage, head left and search for the record. It can be found atop a few small rocks. *The second record can be found in [[Minityrsa]]. Climb your way up the island to the [[Golem Constructs|Hive Construct]] mini-boss, then climb up the right hand wall towards the abandoned church. Keep walking until you see the campsite, then turn right and climb the icy wall next to the stone ramp. Inside a hollowed out log, you can find the next record. *The third and final record can be found in [[Miner's Landing]]. Make your way through [[Saramaed Summit]] and keep progressing through the volcano until you have almost reached the top and are met by two large stone statues against the walls. Climb up the one on the right, and near its head on a ledge you can find the final record. *Return to the tavern and claim your reward from the Ferryman. *For a visual guide, consider watching [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lCMQHCUhL5E this video]. File:Disk Erisia.png|thumb|Vinyl in Upper Erisia File:Diskityrsa.png|Vinyl in Minityrsa File:Saramaed Diskit.png|Vinyl in Saramaed Summit File:Door Fishing.png|thumb|Tavern Entrance door on island between Lower Erisia and Isle of Vigils. File:Isle Door.png|thumb|Entrance at Isle of Vigils. Behind the food stand down to the left. ==Gallery== File:Gilded Accordion.png|Gilded Accordion File:Gilded Violin.png|Gilded Violin File:Gilded Drum.png|Gilded Drum File:Gilded Trumpet.png|Gilded Trumpet File:Comparison of Trumpet.png|Comparison of Trumpet File:Comparison of Violin.png|Comparison of Violin File:Comparison of Accordion.png|Comparison of Accordion File:Comparison of Drum.png|Comparison of Drum ==Trivia== *When approaching each record, they will play their respective song. Make sure your music volume is up! *The Yesterwynde Tavern will play Nightwish songs, indicating which song is playing on the left of the screen. *This confirms that [[The Ferryman]] has access to vinyl records, means to play them, and is therefore a fan of metal. *Every tavern door leads to the same instance of the Yesterwynde Tavern, meaning it can get quite overpopulated and dangerous. You can always exit by walking up to the tavern doors again. *The shortest event in the game's history, lasting only a few days. {{Nav|Events}} [[Category:Events]] [[Category:Promotional Content]]

content:

==Description==
Nimea is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. She is on [[Erisia]] to investigate [[The Hidden Village]].

She provides insight into the [[Lightkeepers]], offering background on the situation in the Hidden Village, the condition of its civilians, and possible explanations for their fate. She also discusses her personal connection with Viqh, the Lightkeeper of the [[Eastern Interstitial Lighthouse]].

Nimea is a File Etrean wearing the [[Pathfinder Arch-Sorcerer]] [[Outfit]] and [[Leather Boots]]. Based on her visible wrinkles, she appears to be in Stage 2 of [[Age|Aging]], likely placing her between 50 and 59 years old.

==Location==
Nimea is located inside a house at [[The Hidden Village]].
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
Nimea Map.png
</gallery>


==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|Base Dialogue=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin 
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Heavy is the burden of the {{g|Lightkeep|Lightkeeper}} for the world rests on their shoulders.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What is this place?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}That's a curious saying.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}That's what I'm trying to figure out. It contradicts the other architecture of this {{g|Driftlands|Driftland}} - as if this village was constructed by a completely different culture. 
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*She smiles.*'' It's an old one.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Why do you think that is?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What exactly is a Lightkeeper?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}The way the people of this village lived seems to suggest that they were salvagers. Presumably, they came here the last time this {{g|Driftlands|Driftland}} appeared and made a living salvaging what they could from the ruins, much like how {{g|Pathfinders}} today search for objects of interest here. 
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}A {{g|Lightkeep|Lightkeeper}} is someone who radiates 'Light' from their soul. They're responsible for maintaining the system of travel between {{g|The Luminants|Luminants}} - the Interstitial {{g|Lighthouse|Lighthouses}}.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What happened to them?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I assume you don't mean the light you get from a lamp?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}There are no signs of a struggle. It's as if they vanished overnight when this place drifted. One day, they were in the Light. The next... Not.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}The Light of a {{g|Lightkeep|Lightkeeper}} is to Void as paint is to a canvas - it draws out substance. Or, I suppose you could say it's like peeling back the paint of a whitewashed wall to expose the wallpaper, but that's not quite as poetic. It can illuminate things that have long since faded. Although, these effects are quite temporary. {{g|Lightkeep|Lightkeepers}} must constantly draw upon their own soul to project this Light, and it takes quite the toll.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}You seem pretty knowledgeable on these things.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*A wistful expression plays upon her face.*'' A childhood friend of mine was born with the Gift. The first in the {{g|The Luminants|Luminant}} in decades, so they said. ''*She sighs.*'' I had only ever wished that we could have both lived a normal life together; that they had never found her Gift.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Duty calls, I suppose.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'm sorry.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Naturally. What use is a normal life to a world fading away? What would an idle experience grant to its memory? ''*She stares at the table, lost in her thoughts with a pained expression.*''
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}There's no need. She still lives, I'm sure of it. They wouldn't let her Light drown.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What is this place?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}}

|-|Spoken to Klaris=
These dialogues play instead if the player has spoken to [[Klaris Llfiend]] about [[Viqh]].
{{#tag:tabber|First Encounter=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}What's the matter? You look as if you've something to say.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I spoke to Klaris Llfiend. She says Viqh is doing okay.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*Her eyes widen in surprise, her face turning pale.*'' H-how... How do you know Viqh?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I asked Klaris about a Lightkeeper from the Etrean Luminant and she remembered her.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*Tears start welling up in her eyes.*'' How... How is she coping? After all these years?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}She's writing poetry.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}She's too busy to do anything.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Oh Viqh... You purehearted fool... ''*She smiles despite her tears.*''
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Oh... Yes, I suppose that's right. They wouldn't squander her Gift... Tell me. Does she... Does she remember me?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], "Poetry" ending
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'm not sure, sorry.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Well, she's writing poems.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She holds her head in her hands and shakes, sobbing.*'' I... I need a moment...
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Oh Viqh... You purehearted fool... ''*She smiles despite her tears.*''
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], "Forgotten" ending
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], "Poetry" ending
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Subsequent Encounters=
{{#tag:tabber|Poetry Ending=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Thank you for giving me some peace of mind, friend. It lightens my heart to know that she still lives. And that she still writes those soppy poems, even if I'm not there to receive them. ''*She smiles wearily, her mind in other places.*''
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What is this place?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Sorry for asking, but how exactly do people know if they have this 'Gift'?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She eyes you for a moment, then sighs.*'' You've done good for me, so I'll share a little. Those with the Gift... are somewhat ironically incapable of using the {{g|The Song|Song}}. Almost everyone has a little potential for it, right?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Not Viqh though?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}No. Not Viqh. Poor thing couldn't muster a single word of it. As a child, I simply thought she hadn't got the knack for it yet. We must've sat there for hours - just reciting the same {{g|Mantra|Mantras}} over and over again. ''*She smiles, reminiscing. Seems like a pleasant memory for her.*''
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}And then...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}And then they took her. We were out in the boonies, so when an {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}} ship suddenly appeared at our shore there wasn't much we could really do about it. So many soldiers - all filtering out of that hideous ironclad of theirs.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Was there no chance of hiding her?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She shakes her head.*'' Only reason she was out in the sticks like me is because her parents realised keeping her in Etris would be bad news. The {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}} are monsters, the lot of them. But what do you even ''call'' something that monsters fear?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'm sorry. About all of this.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She eyes you once again, measuring your sincerity. Her face cracks into a smile.*'' I know you are. But what is one to do? I can only hope that love can reach where the {{g|The Song|Song}} never could.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Forgotten Ending=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="12" {{!}}Thank you... For at least letting me know that she still lives. I only hope that her heart remains strong after all these years, despite her impronm- ...despite her Gift.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What is this place?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="12" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}}
}}}}

title: Notes
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Delicate shells with a distinct shape, Notes are the default currency of commerce within Lumen, Though their value may vary from shore to shore, few fail to recognise them.|author=Notes' description}}
{{CurrencyInfo|title1=Notes|
image1=NotesLargeNew.png
|usage=Used for buying almost everything
|obtainment=*Selling items
*Completing [[Job Boards|Jobs]]
|caption1=Delicate shells with a distinct shape, Notes are the default currency of commerce within Lumen, Though their value may vary from shore to shore, few fail to recognise them
}}
==Functions==
Notes are the main currency used within the Lumen and can be used for a variety of things, such as [[Mantra Modifiers|modifying]] and leveling [[Mantras]], making [[Outfits]], purchasing [[Item Bank|Bank]] slots, upgrading [[Guild Bases]], buying items and paying [[Reputation|bribes]].

===Dropping===
Upon clicking your Notes on the bottom right, you can choose to drop any amount less than or equal to 1000. 

===Obtaining===
The max amount of Notes you can carry at a time is {{c|notes|15,000}} in [[Pathfinder]] and {{c|notes|50,000}} in [[Vow of Iron]].

* Asking the helper at [[Etris]] or the [[Isle of Vigils]] will give you {{c|notes|25}} or {{c|notes|20}} respectively. Only one can be interacted with per character.
* Selling various things to an [[Antiquarian]] (weapons, gems, ores, etc.)
* Turning in an [[Artifacts|Artifact]] at a [[Banker]].
* Turning in [[Knowledge]] at the [[Soothsayer]].
*Completing various [[quests]].
*[[Echoes]] can grant a miniscule amount of starting Notes to a character.
*Mugging a downed player with the [[Talents#Thief|Pickpocket]] Talent.
*Doing [[Job Boards|jobs]].
*Turning in [[Crowns]].

=== Bank ===
At the [[Banker]] you can access your account, a shared storage of notes '''between all Slots''', which allows you to bank your notes up to a max of 100,000. However the transaction of notes between slots depend on your level and trading cap (at level 1 you cannot accept 1000 notes from someone, with the cap being around 900). The banker will inform you of the notes that you have, and will ask if you want to deposit or withdrawal.

== Grinding ==
There are many means to obtain Notes, with some being better than others.

===== Most Efficient =====

* 1 [[Knowledge]] is worth 300 Notes at the [[Soothsayer]], so the [[Moonseye Tome]] or [[Klaris Llfiend, Mother of Lights|Klaris]]' [[Knowledge]] for [[Kyrsan Medallions]] exchanges can give a lot of notes in the long run.
* [[Maestro Evengarde Rest]] drops a good amount of items and is very close to an Antiquarian.
* [[Saramaed Hollow]] drops items at a very fast rate and the dungeon itself contains an Antiquarian. You can either wait until the last few chests of the dungeon in order to pick up more valuable loot, or extract immediately after reaching max Carry Load from picking up all items.
* [[Voidwalker]]s specifically benefit from being able to access [[Antiquarian|Antiquarians]] faster than other [[Origins]] if farming [[Primadon]] or [[The Ferryman]] due to others being unable to access [[Guild Bases]] directly at their locations. The former drops a massive amount of items and the latter drops many high-value items. Bear in mind the Voideye cooldown, however. The Voideye can also be substituted with the Ouroboral Husk as it allows unlimited access to an Antiquarian without a cooldown or being a Voidwalker
* [[Crypt of the Unbroken]] can be farmed extremely quickly, especially using an assassination-based build. Getting all 5 chests can take as little as 2 minutes if you know what you're doing. However, the rate you get items at is too fast for the [[Voideye]] cooldown, so unless you have a [[Guild Bases|Guild Base]] with an [[Antiquarian]] or an [[Ouroboral Husk]], it won't be as effective.

===== Somewhat Efficient =====

* Farming as a [[Deepbound]] varies in pace and danger, but the undesired contents of chests are frequently left alone and chests drop a good amount of items. Call of the Deep can be used to return to [[Castle Light]] if farming elsewhere in [[the Depths]], but you can also farm near [[Light's Causeway]].
** [[Ignition Delver]]s can access jobs from anywhere in [[the Depths]], making [[Random Encounters|events]] even easier to encounter.
** Experienced players with a good route and sufficient Carry Load can obtain many [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|Second Layer]] chests on their way to [[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract|Chaser]].
* The following are only accessible for those who can access the [[Voidheart]]'s [[Antiquarian]] as a [[Voidwalker]], the [[Saramaed Hollow]]'s [[Antiquarian]] via the [[Ouroboral Husk]], or a [[Guild Bases|Guild Base]]'s [[Antiquarian]].
** Reaching an area where [[Guild Bases]] can be placed does not take too long after fighting [[Duke Erisia]].

===== Not Efficient =====

* [[Random Encounters#Sea Events|Sea Islands]] drop a lot of items, but are often slow to reach and clear.
* If not a [[Deepbound]] or [[Ignition Delver]], farming in [[the Depths]] for Notes is not worth it due to the time it takes to enter and leave [[the Depths]] to access an [[Antiquarian]].
* Even at high Carry Load and with proper [[Origins]], doing [[The Diluvian Mechanism]] for Notes takes too long compared to the Notes received and the time traveling takes.
** The [[Moonseye Tome]] and [[Knowledge]] that can be provided by the Mechanism can help offset this, but is highly variable in nature.

title: O Pardoner of Mine
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
O Pardoner of Mine
===
Sincerely, Eneka's Heir O pardoner of mine, I seek your guidance. Upon this moonlit faith, I seek not the future ahead, but solutions for the past. Within my dreams, I see only reflections of those distant memories, scattered upon the nightflowers of which my kin has grown fond of. These flowers guide me, they guide me so, so far toward the ideology you impose upon us, devouring my family in the name of faith. Connecting each flower to a name, a story, a burnt piece of Chrysid so familiar to my touch. A life ripped away, in the name of pardoning Sin. ---- O pardoner of mine, I seek your answer. To the questions I wail hopelessly into the night, clawing at the walls for why, oh why, why Pardoner must it be given up? To the countless Eneka before myself, generations of blood, all deemed too sinful to live, why must we be sacrificed? When will my flesh be spared? When will my father be spared? Upon this {{g|The Moonseye|Moonseye}} we pray to, upon these stars you will see our demise. Upon this star, this {{g|The Luminants|Luminant}}, we become night flowers not from our own sin, but inherited sin. My mother’s mother may have acted wrongfully so, but I am not her, pardoner of mine. When I look toward you, I am trapped inside the glass your fingers clasp upon, and within its reflection I see two of me. It’s the very thing that made me believe, pardoner. ---- O pardoner of mine, your Lachrymosa is the cancer that keeps me up at night. We pray, only for the Lady {{g|The Lady Confessor|Confessor}} to reap our kin in return. Her fingers are wrapped around our society, toying with the souls of those who only possess hope in their hearts, yet she still mercilessly plucks it out, to replace it with devotion. Pardoner, is it devotion you seek? Is it devotion that the Lady {{g|The Lady Confessor|Confessor}} seeks? When you promise us the stars, I promised my heart. When she takes your family too, promising you not only the stars, but the {{g|The Moonseye|Moonseye}} too, do you accept? When you watch your own kin burn, is devotion truly worth it? ---- O pardoner of mine, you are a fool. This faith toys with us, it enchants us, it pulls us closer towards a demise we can never crawl out of. Your devotion to the slaughter of ourselves is not the future for us, my Pardoner. I seek light, just as you. But, oh pardoner of mine, why must we light ourselves ablaze?
[[Category:Books]]

title: Oath: Arcwarder
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Look at that! Seems like it fits you just fine. Why not go put it to practice? Hm... Although, it doesn't seem quite attuned to you yet. Nothing you can't figure out, I'm sure.|author=Delta}} {{Oath |title1=Oath: Arcwarder |image1=Arcwarder Card.png |oath_req=*20 Fortitude *20 Flamecharm *20 Thundercall *Completing [[Alpha]]'s Quest |effects=*+5% PEN *+1 Wildcard Mantra *+2 Combat Mantra }} == Description == '''[[Oath]]: Arcwarder''' is one of the {{text|oathnumber}} obtainable Oaths in ''Deepwoken.'' It heavily focuses on defense; four of its passives are defensive, and the other two are mobility. It still allows for a fair bit of offensive play however as dash allows the user to close gaps and maneuver around opponents, and both combat mantras are as effective if not more in aggressive play. {{Quotes |quote=Unlike the Central Authority, the Union's identity is not defined wholly by internal hierarchy, lingering military traditions, and loyalty to power. Instead, it is rooted in the solidarity of toil - a sense of kinship among those working for the same goal. |author=The Hammer's Call}} The Arc Suit is a defence orientated piece of semi-sentient armour that [[The Ignition Union]] bestows upon their most trusted. It fuses with the soul of those who swear the oath, allowing them to manifest it around them at will. Arcwarders are sworn to become a conduit of protection to their fellow Union mates and do whatever it takes to defend them. Notably, Arcwarders are the only people known to utilize Plasma in their attacks, likely from a result of the [[Flamecharm]] and [[Thundercall]] being combined within the suit. == Obtainment == #Go to [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|Layer 2]] and Complete Alpha's quest. ##Activate the Generator. ##Talk to [[Alpha]]. ##Retrieve injured [[Epsi]]. ##*Choose option 2 when you talk to Epsi. ##**Option 1 causes [[Epsi]] to perish due to the parasites. Epsi will always be outside of [[Firfire Caverns]] when you repeat [[Second Layer|Floor 1]], so you may go back and choose the right option if you messed up the first time. #Talk to Alpha again. #Have at least 20 Fortitude, 20 [[Flamecharm]] and 20 [[Thundercall]]. #Return to surface and talk to [[Delta]] at [[Miner's Landing]] inside the lower-mountain part of the town, specifically behind the water mill located right where the waterfall is. In order to progress the Oath, you must kill [[Chaser]] or [[Scion of Ethiron]] ''For a more in-depth walkthrough, consider watching [https://youtu.be/joHZD3rZVkM this video].'' {{text|oathreobtain|no}} == Progression == Arcwarder Passives and Mantras are obtained via defeating either [[Chaser, Scholar of the Burning Blood|Chaser]] or the [[Scion of Ethiron]] AND taking Klaris' light hook a total of 4 times (Killing the bosses does not grant progression, taking the light hook Klaris' spawns after killing them (not the one in your inventory) does. So killing chaser, going to floor 2, and using inventory light hook will not grant progression) granting one passive Talent/Mantra per kill until the Oath is fully progressed. Mantras are received every 2 kills in addition to the talents. If you have progressed Arcwarder before, you can skip Arcwarder's progression with 10 knowledge by speaking to Delta again after obtaining the oath. ==Effects== This Oath grants +1 Wildcard Mantra Slot and +2 Combat Mantra Slots. When casted, a suit of hulking armor appears around the user. The visor and breastplate both glow yellow, also functioning as a dim source of light. The Arc Suit gives complete immunity to [[Parasites]] in the [[The Ethironal Shrine]], allowing the player to walk over Parasite pools and preventing them latching on by the gales. ==Abilities== ===Talents===
    *'''Arc Module: Dash''' - [In Arc Suit] Your dashes become Jet Dashes, allowing you to attack while dashing. **Jet dashes go much further than regular dashes. **Also allows the user to M1 while performing a dash, ending their dash early. *Obtained with the Oath File:Arc Module Dash.gif|Ground Dash File:Arc Module Dash Air.gif|Air Dash
    *'''Arc Module: Eject''' - [In Arc Suit] When blockbroken, eject from your suit. **If your posture would reach 100% while in the Arc Suit, you instantly eject from it instead of being guard broken, launching yourself backwards and preventing stun. **Upon ejecting from the Arc Suit, your posture will be set to 50%. *Obtained after first [[Chaser]] / [[Scion of Ethiron]] kill. File:Arc Module Eject.gif
    *'''Arc Module: Enhance''' - [In Arc Suit] Your Arcwarder Mantras deal increased damage. **Increases Arc Wave's base damage by 25%. **Increases Arc Beam's base damage by 50%. **Because Enhance increases your Mantra's base damage, it bypasses the damage modifier cap and increases the efficiency of your damage multipliers.
