title: Stored Damage Mechanic
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Damage done with a Katana isn't received until the user sheathes their weapon.|author=[[Poser's Ring]] description}}
{{Oath|image1=PosersRing.png}}<!-- this uses the Oath template because it doesn't have any evergreen things that are always present even if there's no data, like "droppable", "bankable", etc. -->

==Description==
These abilities suspend and store the damage your light attacks deal, until you perform a specific action, releasing all of the stored damage at once.

The term "'''Suspended Hit'''" refers to the release of the stored damage; [[Poser's Ring]] and {{tv|Gathering Storm}}'s sheathe or [[Moppet]]'s Critical Attack.

==Mechanics==
===General Mechanics===
*'''The Suspended Hit {{cl|lired|cannot}} be directly buffed by any means.''' You must buff your light attacks if you wish for the Suspended Hit to deal more damage. Mechanically, the Suspended Hit deals true damage, though in practice this isn't necessarily the case. See [[#Damage Shapshotting|Damage Snapshotting]] for more info.
*Suspended Hits '''{{cl|lired|cannot}}''' be blocked, parried, or dodged, though being attacked during the Suspended Hit's animation will cause the stored damage to '''{{cl|lired|void}}'''.
*The Suspended Hit effectively has infinite range, and triggers "on hit" effects.
*You cannot exceed 70% of a player's maximum health with the Suspended Hit. By using {{status|Wither}} application or any damage source, you can reduce your opponent's health below the 70% threshold.
*Effects that trigger based on scaled damage (e.g. {{status|Bleed}}) will function like normal on weapons with this mechanic. These effects will be triggered when you land your basic attacks, and '''not''' when you trigger the Suspended Hit.
*All abilities with the Stored Damage mechanic share stacks, meaning you can deal damage on a [[Poser's Ring]] [[Katana]], then swap to the [[Moppet]] and critical attack to release the stored damage.
*The Stored Damage mechanic applies an 8% damage buff to the Suspended Hit in PvE. This is believed to be attributed to the general 8% PvE damage buff.
*The stored damage is amassed on the target, and is not recorded per player. The damage credit goes to the player who triggers the Suspended Hit first. For example: If two people are fighting an enemy with Stored Damage mechanic weapons, and person B sheathes ([[Poser's Ring]]), then all of the stored damage applied by both players will be dealt at once. This credits the damage to Player B, regardless of how much Player A contributed.
*The stored damage on each target you've damaged will be dealt simultaneously on Suspended Hit; hitting enemy A, then enemy B, and then proccing the Suspended Hit will cause both of them to take their respective stored damage.
*Chip damage and the damage from damage-dealing enchantments are not stored, and deal their damage normally.
*Player clones do not store their damage, and will instead deal their damage normally. In the case of [[Moppet]], they also cannot use its critical attack.

====Damage Snapshotting====
The damage that each hit deals is calculated and stored, accounting for the effects of damage buffs and resistances. Conditional effects, positive or negative, that are active when your attacks land will still be considered for the damage of those attacks, even if the effects are not active by the time you trigger the Suspended Hit. The [[Viscosity]] and [[Deferred]] Enchantments function very similarly.

To prevent damage buffs or resistances from double-dipping, the Suspended Hit deals '''true damage''', meaning it cannot be directly buffed or resisted. In practice, however, this does not necessarily deal true damage, as the resistances and damage modifiers are taken into account for each hit landed. To reclarify: it deals true damage to fix fringe cases where something would buff or resist the Suspended Hit specifically, and in practice, the hits are still resisted.

Example scenarios:
#While [[Taunt]] is active (20% damage modifier), you land three basic attacks that normally deal 10 damage each. Once Taunt runs out, you land three more basic attacks and then Sheathe ([[Poser's Ring]]). In total, you've dealt 66 damage, as the first three hits received Taunt's damage buff, but the last three didn't.
#You land six basic attacks that deal 10 damage each, then apply [[Taunt]] (20% damage modifier) and Sheathe ([[Poser's Ring]]). In total, you've done 60 damage, as Taunt was not active for any of the hits landed, and the Suspended Hit cannot be directly buffed.
#You land three basic attacks that deal 10 damage each, then your opponent afflicts {{status|Charm}} on you (10% damage debuff), and you land three more basic attacks and Sheathe ([[Poser's Ring]]) while you are still Charmed. In total, you've done 57 damage, as Charm was only active for the final three hits, and the Suspended Hit cannot be directly resisted.

==Individual Abilities==
The differences and individual mechanics of each ability that uses the Stored Damage mechanic.

==={{tv|Gathering Storm}}===
Exclusive to the {{iv|Flashing Thunder}} [[Memento]], the damage your weapon attacks deal is stored, and is triggered upon sheathing the weapon.

This plays an animation and applies an extended true stun to the target. During this stun, the user and the target gain damage immunity to outside damage.

Unlike the others, this effect has a visual component; as you store damage, lightning orbs will form and orbit your character's head. More orbs will appear the more damage you store, capping at 8, visually, and the orbs are fired on sheathe. These orbs have various effects, given to them by the other [[Flashing Thunder]] Talents. See [[Flashing Thunder]] for more info.
<gallery widths="250" position="center">
Gathering Storm.gif|link=Flashing Thunder|<center>{{tv|Gathering Storm}} Sheathe
</gallery>

===[[Moppet]]===
Exclusive to the [[Moppet]], a [[Hallowtide]] dagger weapon, your damage of your M1s is stored, with the Suspended Hit being triggered by performing a critical attack. Moppet will lose the Stored Damage mechanic if you replace its critical attack with a [[Talent]]-given critical attack; enchant-given criticals will retain the Stored Damage mechanic, despite not having a way to deal the stored damage.

For every stored attack the Moppet gains increased PEN. This can scale up to 100% PEN after enough hits.

Because Moppet's Suspended Hit is on a critical attack, Moppet is a great catalyst for any "on critical attack" Talents. With that being said, due to the Suspended Hit not being directly buffable, some of these Talents may not work fully, or at all.
<gallery widths="250" position="center">
MoppetMarked.gif|link=Moppet|<center>[[Moppet]] Critical Attack
</gallery>

===[[Poser's Ring]]===
Exclusive to the [[Poser's Ring]] equipment, the weapon damage of the [[Katana]], [[Alloyed Katana]], [[Palace Tachi]], and [[Shattered Katana]] weapons is stored, and is triggered when sheathing (unequipping) the weapon.

This plays an animation and applies an extended true stun to the target. During this stun, the user and the target gain damage immunity to outside damage.

The damage will remain stored if you swap weapons, but sheathing will only cause the Suspended Hit if your equipped weapon is one of the above.
<gallery widths="250" position="center">
Poser's Ring Sheathe.gif|link=Poser's Ring|<center>[[Poser's Ring]] Sheathe
</gallery>

==Description==
{{PAGENAME}} is a damage dealing [[enchantment]] that applies [[Shock]] to your opponent.

Having the {{t|Adept Thundercaller}} Talent turns this enchantment yellow. Having the [[Talents#Unstable Capacitor|Surge Path]] gives this enchantment a blue hue, overriding the previous yellow recolor.

==Effect==
On weapon hit, {{PAGENAME}} adds a secondary damage instance to your attacks, dealing 16.5% of your weapon's damage, before modifiers, but after resistances as [[Thundercall]] damage. This has a 5 second cooldown.

If it is raining, then a lightning strike will hit your opponent, dealing 33% of your weapon's damage instead, before modifiers, but after resistances as [[Thundercall]] damage in an AoE. This has a 5 second cooldown.

Additionally this applies [[Shock]] or one {{status|Surge Rod}} on proc.

Similarly to a [[Thundercall]] Mantra, landing a Storm basic attack on an armor-broken [[Monsters|Monster]] will increase the duration of the stun by 25%. This also changes the color of the armor broken visual effect to match the Storm enchantment.

===Notes===
*Storm's secondary damage instance cannot be buffed.
*Because Storm's secondary damage instance deals Thundercall damage, you can use this enchantment to change your opponent's {{t|Everchanging Aegis}} type to Thundercall resistance, allowing the first hit of your non-Thundercall attuned attacks to deal 10% more damage against players using this Talent.
*Because Storm deals a percentage of your weapon's damage '''after''' resistances, it can be double resisted.
**For example, if you deal 100 damage with your weapon hit, then Storm will deal 16.5 damage. If your opponent has 50% physical resistance, your attack will deal 50 damage, meaning Storm will deal 8.25 damage. If your opponent also has 50% Thundercall resistance, then Storm's damage will be reduced further down to 4.125 damage.
**This also applies to general resistance sources. If your opponent has a general resistance, then your weapon damage will be reduced, and Storm will deal damage based on that reduced damage, before being reduced itself. For example, if your opponent has [[Reinforce]] with no other resistances, and you have 100 scaled damage, your Storm proc will only deal 13.365 damage.
*Storm's effect is essentially a worse version of [[Stormbreaker]]'s base effect, as Stormbreaker's effect does not get double resisted.
**It is highly recommended that you build for high (general) PEN, or use {{t|Berserk}} if you wish to utilize Storm over Stormbreaker to try to adjust for this mechanic.

==Trivia==
*The lightning strike caused from proccing this enchantment while it is raining grants [[Thundercall]] experience.

If it is raining, then a lightning strike will hit your opponent, dealing 33% of your weapon's damage instead, before modifiers as [[Thundercall]] damage in an AoE. This has a 5 second cooldown.

Additionally this applies [[Shock]] or one {{status|Surge Rod}} on proc.

Stormbreaker additionally replaces your critical attack with a cursor-aimed weapon throw that ragdolls and strikes your opponent with lightning on hit. You cannot attack or move until your weapon has returned to you.

Stormbreaker's critical deals 40 flat typeless damage on throw and 30 flat typeless damage on return. This can hit the same target twice. Stormbreaker's critical deals 1 posture damage if blocked.

===Notes===
*Stormbreaker's secondary damage instance cannot be buffed.
*Because Stormbreaker's secondary damage instance deals Thundercall damage, you can use this enchantment to change your opponent's {{t|Everchanging Aegis}} type to Thundercall resistance, allowing the first hit of your non-Thundercall attuned attacks to deal 10% more damage against players using this Talent.
*Stormbreaker's base effect is essentially a better version of [[Storm]]'s, as it does not get double resisted.

==Description==
The '''Stormseye''' is a Legendary [[Weapons|Rifle]] powered by a [[Kyrsan Medallions|Kyrsan Medallion]] that sits in the center of the Stormseye. This invention functions by utilizing the power of Thundercall to better hit foes with charged ammunition and sharp, sudden strikes, fitting of its deliberately deadly design. It scales from Medium Weapons and the [[Thundercall]] Attunement.

The Stormseye comes with 2 passive abilities:

*'''Medallion Shockwave''' - Every third flourish creates an explosion that knocks people away and applies {{status|Shock}}. This has a 10 second cooldown. If the user has Surge Path: Unstable Capacitator, the passive applies a surge stack with this flourish instead.

*'''Rosen's Fakeout''' - At close range, aerial M1s teleport you behind the enemy.
**Due to how weapon passives work, this is one of few passives that can be transferred to another weapon equipped by abnormal means.
***This includes all Soulwrought weapons from the [[Crazy Slots]] Resonance, the Sovereign Bangle from [[Blightsurger]], and the Saintsblade from [[Saintsworn]].
**This passive has a similar behavior with the Static Fakeout Talent, in terms of visual effects.

This weapon procs all static and electrified Talents as well as all [[Thundercall]] status effects, including Interrogator, proccing Surge stacks, Static Blade, and the Stratoshock buffs.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:StormseyeGIF.gif
File:Surgecrit.gif|Stormseye critical with Surge Path
</gallery>
The user winds up before beginning to circle the opponent in form of electricity, appearing in short flashes to fire shots at them, the last shot applying Shocked. The user will be locked in the air and has I-frames during the critical. The critical has a scaled damage multiplier of 0.74x per shot, totaling up to 2.22x scaled damage.

If the user has Surge Path: Unstable Capacitator, the last shot will apply a surge stack instead.

The critical has a cooldown of '''10 seconds'''.

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:StormseyeConceptArt.png|Concept art
File:StandardStormseye.png|Normal thundercall
File:OverloadedStormseye.png|Surge path
File:MedallionShockwave.gif|Medallion Shockwave
File:RosensFreakout.gif|Rosen's Fakeout
</gallery>
==Trivia==
*The Stormseye was inspired by the [[w:c:destiny:Touch of Malice|Touch of Malice]] from the ''Destiny'' franchise and the [[w:c:callofduty:Wunderwaffe DG-2|Wunderwaffe DG-2]] from the ''Call of Duty'' franchise.<ref>[[File:StormseyeInspo.png]]</ref>
*Elaborated on in its description, the Stormseye is the combination of the technology of guns and the energy of [[Kyrsan Medallions]] stolen from the Ignition Union, channeled using Thundercall.
**The object in the middle of the gun has a [[Kyrsan Medallions|Kyrsan Medallion]], furthering its connection to the Second Layer.
*The bullets shot from the Stormseye took on a yellow color, which would additionally turn blurple if the user had the Surge Path prior to its removal from rifles.
*Originally, [[Funke, Master of Thunder]] did not use this weapon and instead used the [[Hero Blades|Hero Blade of Lightning]].
**According to Arch_Mage, NPCs were not coded to use rifles at the time, despite [[Summer Dragoon (NPC)|Summer Dragoons]] existing.<ref>[[File:Funkestormseye.png|325px]]</ref>
*Contributor HorrorTM uses this weapon as an offhand.
**Considering the nature that the average player cannot use rifles as an offhand, it is simply known that whatever twisted hubris's man has wrought may be belonging to Witchcraft.
*The previous description stated "Pilfered from Union shipments" instead of "Union expedition party".

title: Strange Merchant
content:
{{IronVowEx}} {{Quotes|quote=Spend an exorbitant amount of notes at a box most mysterious.|author=Strange Merchant obtainment hint}} {{Memento |image=Strange Merchant Memento.png |description=A strange being hailing from a time that no longer exists, they hauled a strange relic everywhere. |final attributes=*50 Shadowcast *100 Light Weapon *100 Medium Weapon *100 Heavy Weapon *10 Fortitude *75 Intelligence *100 Charisma |final traits=*8 Proficiency *7 Songchant *6 Dexterity *6 Erudition *1 Vitality |starting armor=[[Strange Merchant (Outfit)|Strange Merchant]] |allowed weapons=Dagger, Fist, Rapier, Sword, Spear, Club, Twinblade, Bow, Greataxe, Greatsword, Greathammer, Greatcannon
Essentially any '''{{cl|lired|except}}''' Pistols, Rifles, and Shields |starting weapons=[[Vortex Echo]] |starting items=[[Warlock's Mantle]] |unlock=Spend up to 16,000 [[Notes]] at various [[Mystery Boxes]]. |aspect=[[Levit]] |starting attributes=*3 Shadowcast *75 Light Weapon *75 Medium Weapon *75 Heavy Weapon *1 Fortitude *4 Intelligence *5 Charisma|starting traits=*1 Proficiency *1 Songchant *2 Dexterity *1 Erudition *-3 Vitality}} ==Description== '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a playable [[Memento]] in the [[Vow of Iron]] gamemode. This Memento forces your race to be [[Levit]]. This Memento's core ability is the Magic Coffin; a [[Mystery Boxes|Mystery Box]] that costs Notes to use. Strange Merchant can ignore all requirements (stat and otherwise) on equipment, weapons and outfits (with a few exceptions). Wiping as a Strange Merchant unlocks the {{t|Enrage}} talent on [[Pathfinder]].
==Starting Abilities==
*{{cl|mementotlnf|Magic Coffin}} [Memento Talent] - A jack of all trades, all attribute requirements are ignored. Activate your Coffin with {{input|keybind|resonance}}. **Activating your Coffin takes {{c|notes|50}}. This Note cost will increase by 50 per Power, costing {{c|notes|1,000}} at Power 20. The price increase mechanic needs further testing. **When used, the Coffin acts like a loot box, randomly rolling an item to give you. **There is a relatively high chance to get {{cl|mementotlnf|Skull}} (previously known as the Enforcer Labubu)December 24th Update Log [[File:Enforcer Labubu Update Log.png|300px]] , which can either be a blank that doubles the cost of the next roll and laughs at you or gives a rare item. **You can use any weapon or equipment item without meeting their '''attribute''' requirements. This also applies to Outfits (with some exceptions). *Benefactor: [Equipment Talent] - Gain reputation for selling goods to Antiquarians within faction territories. **Grants faction [[reputation]] when selling items to their respective Antiquarian. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Radiant Kick (☆☆☆) |image=radiant_kick6915.gif |mantratype=Combat Mantra |desc=Kick your foes at the speed of light. |ethercost={{stats|ether|70 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} |reqs=N/A |effect=''Teleport to your opponent with a flashing kick.'' *Has 0.45s windup *Deals a base of 19.5 Oath damage twice. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Sing (☆☆☆) |image=Sing.gif |mantratype=Support Mantra |desc=Charm those around you with your powerful voice. |ethercost={{stats|ether|100 Ether}} |dmgtype=N/A |reqs=N/A |effect=''User creates a tune with their voice that charms nearby opponents'' *Inflicts Charm on nearby entities for 10 seconds. *Sing cannot be parried, but will not apply Charm if it is blocked or dodged. Sing deals 0 posture damage. *Can be modified with cloud and stratus stones to increase range, but increase the cooldown. (1 Cloudstone = +2s CD, 1 Stratus stone = +3s CD) *Shares a cooldown with [[Glare]]. *Can be upgraded with the '''Encore''' Talent, applying '''true stun''' if you land Sing on a Charmed opponent. *Can be upgraded with the '''Propagandist''' Talent, granting your allies [[Status Effects#Overcharm|Overcharm]] for 15 seconds. }}
==Deck of Recollection==
===Starting Deck===
*{{cl|mementotlnf|Compelling Offer}} [Memento Talent] - Any charmed enemy below 50% hit with your mantras or critical will mysteriously begin attacking everyone but you. [{{status|ncl=y|Madness}}] Your [[taunt]] also now functions as a counter that stacks damage multipliers with every successful taunt. **Madness from this Talent procs when attacking charmed enemies who are below 50% health. **Madness prevents non-boss enemies from dealing damage and hitstunning you. **Using Taunt as a counter displays [[Prediction]]'s visual effects but with a dark purple color. This also plays a laughing sound effect and reduces Taunt's cooldown to 1 second. **Taunt counter does not deal damage but instead stacks Taunt's damage buff effect. *Cornered Fool [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Blockbreaking a Charmed opponent procs Taunt for 5s, making them take and deal more damage. 15s CD **Despite what the description states, this applies Taunt for 6 seconds. **The Taunt damage buff is also applied to the attack that guard broke. *Off Your Game [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - You now slow Taunted enemies when you hit them. *Tough Love [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Deal 10% more damage to enemies {{status|b=y|ncl=y|Charm|Charmed}} by you. Mantras deal +5% instead. Being hit by someone the same Aspect or Oath as you apply {{status|b=y|ncl=y|Charm|Charmed}} briefly. **Charms for 2 seconds with a 1 second cooldown. **If attacked while on cooldown, the cooldown timer resets and you have to wait another second again to be able to proc Tough Love's Charm. **The damage increase affects '''all''' forms of Charm, not exclusively Tough Love's. **Procs its charm through block, parry, and dodge. **This damage buff is only applied if '''your''' Charm is applied to the target. Due to how Charm works, it is highly recommended that you have a high Charm duration from Lasting Charisma if you wish for this Talent to function in large-scale ganks. **Instead of your charm debuffing affected players and making them take more damage, it actually applies an on-hit buff when attacking someone affected by your charm, granting a damage buff to that attack. This means Tough Love '''is''' affected by the damage modifier cap. *{{cl|mementotlnf|Deal Maker}} [Memento Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Your rapport with merchants allows you to attach a flat fee of 20 notes to all your sales. **Increases the sell price of all items by 20 notes. **This is applied '''after''' Snake Oil. *{{cl|raretl|Observation}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Dodge frames are larger if you cancel your roll immediately. (+1 Passive Agility) **Cancelling your roll quickly will grant dodge frames equals to the length of a regular roll. Basically, giving extra 0.1s dodge frames. *{{cl|advancedtl|Dazing Finisher}} [Advanced Talent] '''{{c|notes|350}}''' - Flourishing enemies that are charmed by you cause them to not be knocked back and dazed instead. **Prevents you from knocking back charmed players with flourishes, instead, dazing them. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Taunt (☆☆☆) |image=Taunt.gif |mantratype=Support Mantra |desc=Taunt those around you, causing them to be unable to jump and to take 20% more damage. However, they deal +10% more damage. |ethercost={{stats|ether|100 Ether}} |dmgtype=N/A |reqs='''{{c|notes|250}}''' |effect=''User taunts their opponent, signified by red particles.'' *Inflicts Taunt for 11/12/13/14/15 seconds per level. *Affected entities receive 20% more damage, but deal 10% more damage to the caster. **This is applied as a damage modifier to the person hitting the Taunted player. Meaning that Taunt is affected by the damage modifier caps. *Affected entities become unable to jump. *Taunt deals 0 Posture dmg and doesn't go through block, parry or dodge. *Can be upgraded with the '''Off your Game''' Talent, allowing you to slow Taunted opponents when hitting them. *Using Taunt on any humanoid [[Bosses|boss]] (excluding [[Titus]]) will instantly start the fight, skipping all dialogue. }}
===Power 5===
*Critical Engine [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - You gain the ability to use Deep Gems on your critical attack. Hold out the Deep Gem you wish to apply to your crit then use the tool to enhance your critical. **Equipping a Deep Gem to your critical will not consume the Deep Gem. **Proccing this Talent will put the respective Deep Gem on cooldown if it has one. **See info on specific [[Deep Gems]] on their individual pages. *Dragon's Song [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Using a mantra after an uppercut grants ether. 2s CD *Target Switch [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Parrying an opponent then hitting someone else makes your next mantra free. **This effect is signalled by a yellow halo. **Has a 4 second activation window with a 10 second duration. **This talent will still proc if you hit a knocked enemy. *{{Cl|oathtl|Absolute Radiance}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Dealing damage with Dawnwalker mantras briefly makes you immune to all elemental effects for a short period. **All elemental status effects cannot be applied to you during Absolute Radiance. *{{cl|mementotlnf|Sweeten the Deal}}[Memento Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - {{status|ncl=y|Madness}} can now be applied to enemies at 80% health or lower. *{{cl|raretl|Encore}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Your sing will stun opponents who are already charmed. **On proc, apply 0.4s of "full stun". This can interrupt enemy attacks. **Doesn't affect allies. *Cornered Fool [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Blockbreaking a Charmed opponent procs Taunt for 5s, making them take and deal more damage. 15s CD **Despite what the description states, this applies Taunt for 6 seconds. **The Taunt damage buff is also applied to the attack that guard broke. **This talent is also present in the Starting Deck shop and disappears upon you purchasing it there. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Radiant Dawn (☆☆☆) |image=Radiant Dawn.gif |mantratype=Combat Mantra |desc=Strike down your foes with your blinding light. |ethercost={{stats|ether|100 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} |reqs='''{{c|notes|450}}''' |effect=''User leaps into the air and then comes back down with an unparryable slam.'' *Deals 46.5 base Oath damage. *Takes 1.45s (to hit), 0.45s (to jump in air) + 1s to land. *This Mantra is '''unparryable''' and guardbreaks if anybody attempts to do so. *This move has an early hitbox. It registers a hit before the attack hits the ground. Make sure to dodge '''before''' the move is going to land. *Requires the player to actually hit the floor after the initial leap for the explosion to go off in a certain timeframe. **This means that in low-gravity environments such as [[Scyphozia]], this mantra is very inconsistent in combat use. }}
===Power 10===
*Charismatic Cast [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Landing a hit with a mantra on an enemy applies {{status|b=y|ncl=y|Charm|Charmed}}. Allies recover from being knocked twice as quickly when {{status|b=y|ncl=y|Charm|Charmed}} by you. **This charm lasts 10s (5s against Disbelief Talent). **Targets ''you've'' Charmed will deal 10% less damage to you. **When applying Charm to an already Charmed target, if the new Charm's ''total duration'' is longer than the current Charm's ''remaining duration'', the original Charm will be replaced. If not, nothing will happen. *Manipulator [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Deal 20% more critical attack damage to charmed enemies, but the effect is removed on impact. **10 second cooldown. **Works insanely well with Unnecessary Theatrics and {{status|Overcharm}} as they reapply the charm after the charm is removed on the same hit. ***Will not allow you to proc Manipulator twice as it has a cooldown. **Tough Love and Manipulator proc at the same time, allowing for a 30% damage bonus. **Manipulator is inherently weaker on multihit criticals, but that doesn't mean it's always bad. ***For example, a 5 hit multihit critical will only gain the 20% damage bonus from Manipulator on the first hit as it only procs once and then goes on cooldown. ***The effectiveness of Manipulator on multihitting criticals depends entirely on the critical itself, with its hit count and scaled damage multipliers being very important factors, as well as whether or not you expect to even land the whole thing. Sometimes front loading the critical proves more effective than having a more consistently applied damage multiplier. *Narcissist [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Charming an already Charmed opponent Overcharms you briefly. Guess you really were always that great. **Overcharms yourself for 4 seconds. **Charms yourself for 8 seconds (halved to 4s if you have Disbelief). ***The self Charm proc reduces self damage taken by 10% and allows you to benefit from Charismatic Cast's secondary effect, which reduces your time knocked by 50%. **Landing M1s and criticals while Overcharmed charms your opponent for 5 seconds (halved to 2.5s if they have Disbelief). Additionally, Overcharm grants a 10% damage bonus to melee attacks when hitting charmed opponents. *Snake Oil [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Okay, the amount you're charging people for your items is getting downright criminal. But I'm just a Talent description, I can't stop you. **Gain 40% more notes from selling items. *{{cl|oathtlnf|Protagonist Syndrome}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - The grasp of shadow is meaningless in the face of your blinding light. Your Dawnwalker mantras are empowered after getting hit by Shadowcast. **Increases your Dawnwalker Mantra damage by 30% after being hit by Shadowcast damage. *{{cl|raretl|Golden Tongue}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Typing or using a gesture gives a random buff to you and those around you. (60 second cooldown) **Sending a message in chat or using an emote will proc this Talent. **Can either restore 30% of max ether or grant 10% damage reduction for 30 seconds, similar to [[Reinforce]] (does not stack). **The buff is random for each person affected. **For every point in Charisma above 40, the cooldown will be decreased by 0.25 seconds, having a 45 second cooldown at 100 Charisma. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Blinding Dawn (☆☆☆) |image=blinding_dawn6915.gif |mantratype=Combat Mantra |desc=Spin rapidly to unleash powerful rays of light. |ethercost={{stats|ether|55 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} |reqs='''{{c|notes|700}}''' |effect=''User stands on their hands and spins, shooting beams of light out of their feet.'' *Has 1.2s windup, takes 2.1s to land all hits. *Deals 18 total hits of Oath damage, with 9.333 base damage per hit. }}
===Power 15===
*Unfazed [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - You are more resilient to the side effects of going insane. You no longer Shiver and you Panic with less severity. **Contrary to the card's description, effect of insanities are delayed by a full tier. ***You now Shiver at Tier 2 insanity instead of Tier 1. ***Shiver slows movement but does not cancel M1/Mantra. ***You now Scratch yourself at Tier 3 insanity instead of Tier 2. *{{cl|oathtlnf|Luminous Flash}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - After dealing a certain amount of damage in Absolute Radiance, gain a chance to empower your strikes with pure light. **During Absolute Radiance, your M1 attacks have a chance to proc Luminous Flash, increasing their damage by 75% (the damage modifier hardcap). In PvP combat, this is lowered to 50% instead (the damage modifier hardcap).
===Power 20===
*Jackpot [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Charmed enemies now have a chance to be hit critically, multiplying the damage. **There is a ?% chance that your hits against a Charmed target will be a critical hit, dealing significantly more damage
==Boss Unlocks==
===Shogun of the Prophet's Guard=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Stack the Deck}} [Memento Talent] - Charmed enemies will grant you even more damage multipliers on your Taunt counter. ===Dravik, The Rat King=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Know When To Run}} [Memento Talent] - Your magic coffin has a higher chance to draw depths loot, but the price is increased. **Increases the price of your Magic Coffin by 50%. **Adds the entire Depths lootpool to the coffin. **Rat King is currently accessible without fighting Shogun first, allowing you to fight him at lower power and get the benefit of the Depths lootpool and the reduced price of the Coffin, due to your low power. ===True Heart of Enmity=== *Voice of the Mad God [Common Talent] - Any time you apply [[charm]] it now applies "[[Status Effects#Madness|Madness]]" to enemies directly.

title: Strange Missives
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
Strange Missives
===
A collection of mysterious letters [The book itself is littered with pages of letters and notes, some stray sheets within in an unintelligible language, scrawled in an unknown print. Some documents are easy to make out - archived correspondence.] ------------ [From the wear and condition of the first letter sheaved in the book, this is old. Most certainly written several generations ago.] Th'armati, most hold greetings from the {{g|The Echelon|Echelon}}. The {{g|The Counsell|Counsell}} has decre'd it! Nostri eclipse is upon us once again, and we send out tidings and caution to our distant kin. As our {{g|The Moonlit Dialect|aecti}} surge below the surface into our ossuaries, we urge your kin to avoid trespassing upon our festivities, and keep their craft clear from our islands - the all-too-familiar matercrypt will receive those who do not heed this warning into its sunk'n shores. As always, we send our kindest tidings from our Lady, for th'armato will be glad to know of the peace we have enjoyed since her sacrifice long since. Have faith in our practices - her guidance continues to crade our isles well. True faith survives such troublesome events - there is peace as she had promis'd, we have rebuilt plentifully since our most worrying ordeal, our crypts have expanded greatly to all reaches of the archipelago. We pray for the safety of your own and th'ambulo living your protection. - Galvika, our confessors' Acolyte. ------------ ---- [Rifling through, a sleeker page appears - almost pearlescent in contrast to the previous letters' wear. It's silk to the touch. Part of the letter is again in the obscure language, yet it seems that there is a translation neatly printed beneath.] Th'armati of Aratel, most insistent greetings from the {{g|The Echelon|Echelon}}. We regretfully have to inform of a mishap with your academics you have entrusted us with. The consell assures you that it was nothing of malicious practise - it seems that one, when being blessed with an exploration within our most belov'd crypts, has run astray. We intend this to be received in the most comforting sense - one individual intended to make a 'souvenir' of our heritage laid upon our walls, and henceforth shall not be returning to your Greathive. For their trespass against our most sacred space, the Lachrymosa waits their attendance, and their repentance will be witnessed. We have since sent the other ambassadors onto their return, and they have been equipped with the requested copies of our archives - we hope the reminder of our common ancestry contained within them will kindle our distant friendships. We ask for more caution when selecting those to represent the beest of th'armati. - {{g|Thalassis}}, our confessor's Acolyte. ------------ [The other documents do not pique your interest - more unintelligible jargon and bizarre utterings. Certainly this was not intended for your hands.]
==Appearances== *[[Thal'assis Linnaes]] *[[Galvika]] *[[The Lady Confessor]] {{Mo}} [[Category:Books]] [[Category:The Moonlit Faith]]

==Description==
Stratos is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. They are the second-in-command of the Blade Temple, behind [[Evengarde Rest]].

To speak with him normally, players must have good [[Reputation]] with [[Etrea]], around 75 reputation, between neutral and ally status. If the player does not meet this requirement, Stratos will refuse to speak to them unless they are carrying his [[Lance's_Brother#Crate_Delivery_Quest|delivery]]. If the player has the delivery, he will reward them with 25 Notes. After speaking with him, Stratos says he will teach the player once they feel the "essence of the wind", starting his [[#Windwaker Quest|quest]].

===Quest===
To complete Stratos' quest, the player must meet the following requirements:

*Have 15 points in [[Galebreathe]].
*Have "Ally" [[Reputation]] with Etrea.

Once these requirements are met, speaking to Stratos again will grant the {{t|Windwaker}} talent and 10 full training points. This Talent appears as an ability in the player's inventory and can be activated while on any boat.

==Location==
Stratos can be found meditating in front of a fountain at the [[Temple of the Blade]] at the [[Isle of Vigils]].

title: Studies on Canticlysm
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Books|Book Collection]]. ==Vol. IV== ===
Studies on Canticlysm, Vol. IV
===
compiled by Steward Amross, Steward Bridges, et. al Perhaps there are those who, in their own perspectives, see the {{g|The Canticlysm|Canticlysm}} as something wholly detrimental to our civilisation, to our way of life. That the idle decadence and reckless inquiries into the Song of our forefathers could only have ever brought ruin, devastation, to the soul of our culture and our world. As scholars we must look past our desire to condemn the actions of those who came before us, as though we live through the consequences, they were not privy to the knowledge that is now tacit to our generation. To them, it was a renaissance born from the advent of their greater understanding of the surrounding planes. The very powers of creation seemed only a hair's breadth away, a tantalisingly small gulf for them to cross. Were we in the same position as they, I’m sure that we would not hesitate to make use of the powers that it brought. And even in our current era, many do not grasp the correlation between the state of the world now and the unmistakable effects of the {{g|The Song|Song}}. To truly appreciate the world that our forebearers damned, it seems pertinent to set the scene. From what we know, the {{g|The Old World|Old World}} took the form of five major landmasses. In those days, the {{g|The Luminants|Luminants}} were mostly contiguous, with what was known as the World’s Edge delineating its circumference. The World’s Edge, of course, is what we now call the {{g|The Voidsea|Voidsea}}, and from their histories we can attest that it was equally impassable in their day as it is in ours. The skies are also said to have been clearer, seemingly devoid of the outstretched fingers of {{g|The Voidfod|Voidfog}} that have blotted out our stars and confounded our instruments for centuries. The {{g|The Voidfog|Voidfog}} is, of course, one of many lesser-known effects of the {{g|The Tides|Tides}}. With the naked eye, they appear merely as clouds. Any observer who paid enough attention would realise that these formations are fixed in relative space, moving across our skies in a cycle. When observed through a telescope, the lensing effect becomes apparent, the light seeming to bend and distort around it. In these broad and interrupted lands, its people lived lives of plenty, well-fed from their expansive farmland and connected by a flourishing network of trade. Many comparisons can be drawn between their way of life and that of the Felinor fieldfolk of Markor - a topic that has been well documented by our cousins at the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel}}. And far beneath these plentiful lands, deeper in those days, lurked the danger that we know now to be the source of our maladies - the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. What little accounts we have dredged up of these outer planes in the times before the threat became apparent seem to have largely persisted in the realms of folklore and mythology - tales of sea monsters emerging from the depths of the ocean were often recanted on dark stormy nights, some having more foundation than others. Furthermore, though the {{g|The Song|Song}} had not yet been discovered, its effects could still be seen. In the years before the {{g|The Canticlysm|Canticlysm}}, strange creatures would sometimes be found on the shores. Pale gelatinous flesh stretched over their bones, seemingly due to decompression. Bearing no visible relation to any of the animal life they had yet documented, these creatures were kept for research and dissected. Those that lived were unresponsive and did not last long in captivity, seeming to lack some form of nutrition. With the creatures often came strange curios and trinkets; artifacts of civilisations that did not belong to the surface world. It is thought it is through the nobles’ fascination with these artifacts that the {{g|The Song|Song}} was first discovered. What began as a faint whisper heard only by those attuned soon grew into an enthralling melody that was never far away. Even the mere snippets of it that the researchers had retrieved were potent and intoxicating, seeming to promise something ever deeper and ever greater than what they had ever known. And in capturing the {{g|The Song|Song}} and trying to replicate its melodies, strange phenomena began to occur. In the dingy basement of a tavern, a practising musician’s viola burst into flames. A temple erected in service to the growing religion surrounding this newfound {{g|The Song|Song}} has its steeple struck by lightning in the middle of their morning prayers. Those that memorised more and more of its tones seemed to gain an ever greater understanding of the world around them and the powers that drove it. It took a mere generation after its discovery for a renaissance of technology and culture to blossom forth. This great era became known as the {{g|The Canticlysm|Canticlysm}} - the advent and heyday of the {{g|The Song|Song}}. With an easily accessible source of power that came at seemingly no cost beyond one’s stamina, mundane tasks were swiftly trivialised. As with early man’s discovery of the means to start a fire, the discovery of its manipulation through the {{g|The Song|Song}}, known as ‘Flamecharming’, was similarly fundamental in uplifting the world’s technology. Contraptions and new technologies could be fueled simply by the energy of its user, and the greatest asset to mankind’s progress soon became so-called Songwork. Songworkers were instructed in the use of a limited subset of {{g|Flamecharm|Flamecharming}} and were put to work powering machines and foundries. Concentration was vital, and safety was often cast aside in favour of greater efficiency, costing many Songworkers their lives. As new processes were developed to advance technology, Songworkers were saddled with ever-increasing workloads. The dissent of the labourers grew with every passing day - given a taste of the {{g|The Song|Song}}, the very powers of creation were dangled like a carrot on a string in front of them. Labourers began to gather in secret in the few hours they were afforded to rest a day, pooling their experience together and furthering their understanding of {{g|Flamecharm|Flamecharming}}. It’s sometimes mused that in these times, the lowliest Songworker had a better grasp of the {{g|The Song|Song}} than the loftiest academic did. While scholars lounged and ruminated on its potential, the labourers were made to use it every minute of every day, coming to know it through intuition. With a growing network of support among the labourers, talk of an uprising soon spread across the factories of the world. Unable to hide their anxiety, the ruling class sought to make an example of the dissidents, and with the execution of a prominent labour activist they lit the spark that would soon ignite revolution. Armed with the Song, many Songworkers soon earnt their rights through fire and blood. Those governments unable to smother the embers of rebellion were toppled and replaced, though not always for the better. Wise to the power the workers held, the long-forgotten arts of {{g|Vows}} were resurrected by the surviving powers, now forcing the Songworkers of many nations into lifelong servitude. With the widespread devastation exacted on the world by the wars waged through the {{g|The Song|Song}}, many did not fully realise the changes that were coming to it. The creatures that emerged from the seas were no longer pallid comatose things, and were now presenting a growing threat to the peoples of seaside settlements. In time, this threat spread even further inland. Year after year, record flood highs were reached. Mass evacuations sparked across the world, its people frantic to escape a catastrophe they hadn’t foreseen. But in their flight, they did not abandon the {{g|The Song|Song}}. As the tides drew in ever closer, they held it as tightly to their chests as a prayerbook. Seeking the fabled mountaintops of the world’s spine, the {{g|The Song|Song’s}} {{g|The Tides|Tides}} carried the people higher and higher. Where pastures and orchards had once sustained a vast population, the mountain peaks could never sustain nearly enough. Mankind’s understanding withered as its population dwindled. Without fervent research into the {{g|The Song|Song}} and its applications, technological advancements ground to a halt. Despite the relative abandonment of the {{g|The Song|Song}}, the {{g|The Tides|Tides}} never stopped rising, and the Edge of the World hemmed itself inwards. This Edge, the {{g|The Voidsea|Voidsea}}, soon extended its fingers into the oceans - no longer seas - that parted the continents of the world. Where once the {{g|The Voidsea|Voidsea}} had been a border between the known and the unknown, it now drew its borders between the nations of the world, a seemingly insurmountable obstacle to cross.

Your Knife's Journey procs do 2x Armor damage * Swift Rebound - Move faster after successfully dodging an attack. * {{cl|raretlnf|Evasive Expert}} - Your speed boost granted from dodging is increased. * {{cl|raretlnf|Risky Moves}} - When you successfully dodge, you'll automatically dodge the next attack. * Finishing Touch - Instantly execute enemies finished with the critical attack of your dagger. * Matador - Deal +20% more damage to human enemies with hyperarmor. * ==Finisher== A Subtle Knife of Eylis executes it's opponent after knocking them: {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description |- |Execute |Pins down opponent before slicing their throat with their blade. |} ==Tips== * If you don't have any ranged mantras, you'll have to get up close to them since a single hit from any attack will cancel their time bubble. *They'll use their Time-Slowing Bubble much more frequently if fighting a player who has negative reputation with [[The Knives of Eylis]] instead of an npc, so it's recommended to stay their enemy if you're trying to obtain the '''Voidwalker''' origin. ==Trivia== *It is required to enter their time bubble to obtain Voidwalker. *Their time bubble will still affect players who have the [[Voidwalker]] origin on their character. *The only characters in the game to have the Voidwalker Oath. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Enemies that can wield Enchantments]] [[Category:Enemies with Oaths]] [[Category:Knives of Eylis Enemies]]

==Description==
Sudaruska, known as the Unbroken, was an inhabitant of [[Minityrsa]] prior to it's colonization by [[Etrea]]'s [[Clan Kobura]]<ref>{{Deep dates|Iron}} This places it only a few decades before the events of the main game, where the forces who invaded Minityrsa are described as ancient. Thus, Minityrsa was invaded by the Ministry prior to becoming a territory of Clan Kobura.</ref> and the [[The Ministry]].<ref name="Gran" />

When the island was [[Invasion of Minityrsa|invaded]] by the Ministry, Sudaruska fought to protect her homeland from them and eventually found herself as the island's last defender. However, she was mortally wounded in the process. Sudaruska made the choice to imbue her being into her greataxe, giving her the necessary strength to cut down hundreds of the invaders, but ultimately died in the process. In her place, her self and the axe became one, turning it into the [[Gran Sudaruska]].<ref name="Gran" />

Tragically, Sudaruska's death proved to be in vain when the Ministry eventually settled into Minityrsa 38 years after the [[Etrean Civil War]].<ref>{{Deep dates|Verse1}}</ref><ref>[[Outpost Antumbra]]</ref>

The tale of Sudaruska's fate spread beyond the shores of Minityrsa. [[Deirdre]] looked up to Sudaruska and hoped to possibly replicate the process, but her untimely death made such a task impossible.<ref>{{Ref/Book|Coldheart's Journal}}</ref>

==Trivia==
*Give the similarity between its name and her epithet, the [[Crypt of the Unbroken]] may have been made for Sudaruska after her death. This adds an extra layer of sad irony due to its later perversion by the Ministry.

title: Summer Isle
content:
{{Location|name=Summer Isle|territory=The Summer Company|caption=The smell of gunpowder blankets this tropical paradise.}}
[[File:Summer Isle Main!.jpg|center|thumb|845x845px]]

'''Summer Isle''' is a populated island in [[The Aratel Sea]], it is [[The Summer Company]]'s headquarters and is the only location with access to firearms and Hunter's Braces for sale.

One of the most eventful populated islands in the Eastern Luminant, having basically the essentials of starter islands: an inn, guards, training gear along with nice additions, those being ores, more sources of food and NPC events you wouldn't find at Etris, Isle Of Vigils or Greathive Aratel. A good place to quickly resupply your rations and repair/gather equipment, and enjoy the tropical scenery. 

==Points Of Interest ==
=== <u>The Castle</u>===

====Gunsmiths====
Main Article - [[Guns]]
The Summer Isle's main attractions are the firearms, which can be found inside the main building at the gunsmith, the prices being:

* [[Flintlock]]s - 100 Notes. The first guns the player to access early-game, dealing 11 damage on hit.
* Req: 20 LHT.

* [[Repeater]]s - 200 Notes. Similar to the flintlocks with a slight increase in damage (14) and a massive increase in swing speed. (M1's flow into each other, spammable)
* Req: 65 LHT.

* [[Dragoon]]s - 500 Notes. Similar to the flintlocks with a massive increase in damage (16), but cooldown increased. (M1 spam combo cannot be used)
* Req: 65 LHT.

Notes:

* [[Bullet Casings|Bullets]] can be purchased for five notes each, or they by crafted anywhere with one iron, creating 20 bullets per iron.
* Firearms also come with an off-hand variant allowing you to dual wield firearms, or use a different weapon with one.
* Firearms can be parried, blocked, and dodged like all normal attacks.

====Funke, Thundercall Trainer====
On the second floor of the Summer Company's castle, the [[Thundercall]] trainer [[Funke, Master of Thunder|Funke]] can be found.

* To unlock Thundercall, the player must bring 5 [[Spark Gland]]s (2 if previously obtained) to the trainer to be crushed into a vial, obtaining a [[Sparkblood]] potion.
* You can upgrade your Thundercall mantras for 100 notes each, the price increasing by 100 notes with each upgrade on the specific mantra.
* Funke wields the [[Stormseye]] when encountered in the [[Oath: Silentheart|Silentheart]] progression.
* Summer Isle's [[cauldron]] is located in the same room as Funke.


====Blacksmith====
Within the tower on the right side of the castle's entrance stairs.

* Works like any other blacksmith, won't communicate with you if you have negative rep.

====Antiquarian====
Within the castle's ground floor, situated in the same room as the Gunsmith.

* Works like any other antiquarian, won't communicate with you if you have negative rep.

====Modifier Trader====
Within the castle's ground floor, on the opposite side of where the Antiquarian/Gunsmith are.

* You can talk to them even as an enemy of Summer Company.

====Scope====
[[File:ScopeLocation.png|thumb|300px]]Within the tower on the left side of the castle's entrance stairs, Scope needs to recover crates filled with explosives that have been stolen by the bandits/Ignition Union, and what other better way to retrieve the crates is there than just sending you to do it.

These boxes of explosives can be found all across Isle, usually being tended to by Summer Company guards post offscreen battle. Returning to Scope with one of these boxes in hand, will net you a chest that will have loot from the item table below, and a small amount of positive reputation with the Summer Company.
[[File:ExplosiveCrateEvent.png|thumb|300px|Explosive Crate Event]]


====Shipwright====
The Shipwright is located on the rocky beach within a castle like structure.

* Works like any other shipwright, won't communicate with you if you have negative rep.

===Inn===

====Innkeep====
* Allows you to set your spawnpoint at Summer Isle for 5 notes.
*Won't communicate with you if you have negative reputation AND you will be kicked out if you set your spawnpoint at this inn and then get negative reputation.

====Kujae====
* Can be found outside the Inn
* Will give you something random out of his sack for 350 notes.

====The Guildmaster====
*Allows you to make a guild/leave an existing one.

====Trig====
[[Trig]] is an NPC at the entrance of the Guildhall/Inn (if you have interest points on, it's marked as Guildhall). His quest sends you to find [[Asius]], a merchant who hasn't been paying his dues to the Summer Company. Asius can be found behind the Inn if you follow the path leading away from the Inn, in an alcove facing the hive. 

You will be given two quest dialogue options after answering why you're meeting him:  

#I'll see what I can do.
#No you bottom-feeder, hand over the money now or you'll be sinking to the 3rd layer.
#[ End Dialogue ]

# Answering with the first dialogue option and returning to Trig will cause him to send three Summer Company guards after you. The {{t|Bulletproof}} Talent will be added to your Talent pool, and you will lose Summer Company reputation.
#*You can apologize to Trig after completing the quest, and for {{c|notes|2,000}}, he will add {{t|Armor Piering}} to your Talent pool, along with rewarding you with positive Summer Company reputation.
# Answering the second dialogue option will have Asius reluctantly hand you an invisible stack of ship documents, his vessel sunken at sea and the documents the final few things to show for it. Returning to Trig will have him reward you with positive Summer Company reputation, EXP, and the {{t|Armor Piercing}} Talent will be added to your Talent pool.
#*Unlike the opposing quest ending, there is '''{{cl|lired|no way}}''' to obtain {{t|Bulletproof}} if you initially sided with Trig.

===Reputation Reset===
* Nepo, an NPC found on a bridge can reset your reputation with Summer Company.

===The Furnace===
[[File:The furnace.jpg|center|thumb|854x854px]]''Main Page: [[The Furnace]]''

This place contains [[Jarvis]], a NPC who allows you smelt two equipments into one, and an Arena.

===Cave===
[[File:The cave summer isle.jpg|center|thumb|724x724px]]
A cave opening facing the Shipwright's building, easy to spot.

===Circular Structure===
* A circular building located outside of the castle, near the Inn.
* In the circular structure, there is a [[??? (Blindseer Glyphs)|Blindseer Glyphs]], hinting towards how to progress and unlock [[Oath: Blindseer|Blindseer]] mantras.

===Castle Ruins===
*A castle-like building in ruins. Inside, in the room to the left of the entrance, a small crack in the floor can be found, allowing you to drop into a hidden basement containing barrels and, occasionally, chests.
* You can get there by taking the zipline on the main castle, and continuing forward.
* Additionally, the [[Chained Captive]] can be located here if you have spoken with [[Vice Warden Morredh]].
[[File:Summer Cannon.jpg|thumb|The Summer Company cannon|504x504px]]

===Summer Isle Cannon===

* An enormous cannon lying on the cliffs on the Summer Isle. If a player has negative reputation, the Summer Company will aim the cannon at them, and fire. It fires a hit-scan projectile, that launches players far away, deals a large amount of damage. A horn will play before firing, alerting the player to their imminent demise. The cannon will NOT fire if the player is swimming. If the player is sailing or on the island in front of summer isle, it will fire.
* The cannon also serves as a fast travel point to the Songseeker Wilds. Provide 3 [[Spider Egg]]s to [[The Guy]] in the cave across from [[Meteor Isle]] at Hive, and then interact with the door at the base of it, and it shoots you over to the Songseeker Wilds. Upon interacting you will fly across the luminant with fire surrounding you as if you were a meteor.

title: Suncross

{{Cleanup}}{{InProgress}}[[File:Suncross.png|thumb|476x476px|center]]{{Quotes|quote=THE WANDERING STAR! ITS MOVEMENTS SO CALCULATED! ITS WARMTH - ITS LIGHT! SUCH BEAUTY - SUCH INTENT!|author=Soothsayer about the Suncross}}

== Description ==
The Suncross is one of the two celestial objects that orbits between Lumen and the Heavens - standing as Deepwoken's equivalent of the Sun and the counterpart to the [[Moonseye]]. Orbiting around Lumen in an elliptical path, the Suncross is partly responsible for Deepwoken's day/night cycle. 

The Suncross is always seen as a white star with six distinct points. The Suncross can only be seen during the daytime, and cannot be witnessed during nighttime, retreating into the Voidfog - during which the Moonseye becomes more visible in the night sky. 

== Cultural aspects ==
Although it is an infrequently-used symbol in Deepwoken compared to the Moonseye, it is generally viewed as the embodiment & bringer of life by both Man & Celestial.

=== Religion ===
The Kyrsans have a unique depiction of the Suncross, which is referred to as Ameda. Within [[Old Kyrsa]] is the Amedan Temple which still stands amongst the ruins of the city, but none make their pilgrimage to to the temple.

The Starkindred Faith shows followers who view the Suncross as a Celestial, while others do not. As a whole, it remains as a sacred object to the Faith.

==Description==
Sunway is a Plackart [[Vesperian]] working for [[The Ignition Union]] in [[The Ethironal Shrine]]. Speaking with Sunway reveals that the 'snow' that the player has building up on them are actually parasites, which if left unchecked to build up will kill the host (the player, too). From there, victims turn into [[Diver Husk|husks]], and finally, [[Carbuncle]]s.

From speaking with Sunway, it is implied that the Ignition Union created the black and yellow variants of the lanterns as a way to prevent parasite buildup. These are not to be confused with the white and blue variant seen in the [[Galewax]] area of the [[Ethironal Shrine Sanctuary]]. 

==Dialogue==
{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|begin}} |Begin Dialogue
|-
| colspan="12" |Eh? You look, hm... ''*He tilts his head to the side, puzzled.*'' Unfamiliar. I'm guessing you're the one who turned on the generator?
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |That's me.
|-
| colspan="12" |Gods below, you did us a big favor with that. You should go see Alpha, I'm sure he could work out something for you to reward your efforts. In any other case... do you need anything from me?
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |What is going on with the snow?
|-
| colspan="12" |''*The man presses his thumb against the bottom of his mask in thought for a moment.*'' Well, despite describing it as 'snow', it is anything but that. Have you noticed how tricky it is to brush off yourself? Well, to be short... ''it's alive''. Some form of parasitic organism, it seems.
|-
| colspan="12" {{cl|reply}} |Parasitic?
|-
| colspan="12" |Aye. Have you, by any chance, seen what happens after a sufficient nest of them inhabits a body long enough? They end the incubation phase, and start taking control of the host. All of them burst out of their snow-like eggs through the host at once, killing the host in the process.
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |That sounds quite morbid.
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |How do the lamps work, then?
|-
| colspan="6" |Once the host's body is dead, the parasites start taking control of the husk left behind. It grows additional limbs, contorting into an awful shape, and the face... ''ugh''. It's not a pretty sight. Those husks slowly become ''Carbuncles'' over time, and the host's body is left a mere puppet.
| colspan="6" |Ah, that is quite simple! These are no ordinary lamps! ''*He taps on the side of the lamp's glass proudly.*'' Think of it as... hm, blasting the eggs with an absurd level of heat enough to shock it, forcing it to let go of your body. The small sting of the lamp is worth it, better than the cruel fate that the parasite hosts go through...
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |How do you know so much about this?
| colspan="6" {{cl|reply}} |What happens to the host?
|-
| colspan="6" |''*He looks down to the ground contemplatively for a moment, before returning his gaze to you.*'' This base used to have a lot more people wandering these halls, friend...
| colspan="6" |[See "That sounds quite morbid."]
|-
| colspan="6" {{cl|end}} |[End Dialogue]
|}

title: Surface
content:
{{gaa}}
__TOC__

==Description==
'''The Surface''' is the half of [[Lumen]], in which the player resides in-game, unless they are in [[the Depths]]. The surface is made up of different [[Luminants]] and the [[Voidsea]] which surrounds them.

[[Voidsea|The Voidfog]] surrounds the skies of the Surface, resembling the clouds. The [[Suncross]] lights up the day, while the [[Moonseye]] and the other [[Stars]] of the [[Nightsea]] light up the night.<ref name="Glossary0">{{Ref/Glossary|The Voidfog}}</ref>

==Contents==
[[Luminants]]: Akin to continents, the [[Luminants]] are the remaining regions of Lumen that haven't been claimed by the [[Voidsea]]. In order to secure safe passage through the [[Voidsea]], the work of a [[Lightkeepers|Lightkeeper]] is required.<ref name="Glossary">[[Glossary#The Luminants|Glossary entry for the Luminants]]</ref> Currently, there are only 2 [[Luminants]] in-game: Etrean and Eastern, which are actually a singular [[Luminants|Luminant]], since they are only separated by the Sea Gates.<ref name="Ploom">[[Ploom#Dialogue|Ploom's dialogue after completing his quest/passing the stat check]]</ref><ref name="Citation Needed">Citation needed</ref>

[[Voidsea|The Voidsea]]: An anomalous and near-insurmountable stretch of water that represents the gradual dissolution of Lumen into [[the Depths]]. Conventional laws of time and physics do not work fully in the [[Voidsea]].<ref name="Glossary1">{{Ref/Glossary|The Voidsea}}</ref><ref name="Glossary0" />

__TOC__

==Description==
Suri is a [[Vesperian]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]].

Talking to him will start the Grave Tending [[Quests|quest]] where he asks you to bring a flower to his [[Well-kept Gravestone|brother's grave]].

==Location==
Suri is located in [[Greathive Aratel]] beside the stairs leading to the heart plaza and the R&D entrance.
<gallery widths="300px">
Suri's Location in Hive.png|The room Suri's in
Suri's Location.png|Suri's Location
</gallery>

==Quest==

Completing his quest will grant the player 1 [[Vibrant Gem]], EXP, positive [[The Hive|Hive]] reputation, Compassion, and the {{t|Careful Handling}} Talent, reducing the chance that you drop [[:Category:Ingredients|Ingredients]] on death.

#Finishing Suri's dialogue will start the quest.
#You will be given a [[Delicate Flower]], if you take certain forms of damage it will break and turn into a Ruined Flower (If it breaks you'll have to go back to Suri to get a new one)
#After taking the flower you need to head to [[Isle of Vigils]] and find his [[Well-kept Gravestone|brother's grave]].
#Interact with the grave and finish it's dialogue.
#Then head back to Suri to complete the quest.

Suri's brother's grave is located near the barber at [[Isle of Vigils]]
<gallery widths="300px">
Well-kept Gravestone.png|Suri's brother's grave
Well-kept Gravestone Location.png|The location of the gravestone
</gallery>

==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{{#tag:tabber|Quest Start=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*He mutters to himself.*'' I don't have any spare time to leave town, but I can't just leave my brother's grave unkept...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Need help?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Were you eavesdropping? Well, in any case, yes. Can you take this flower to my brother's grave? It's on the Isle of Vigils.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What's in it for me?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Me? Eavesdropping?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}It's not much, but I inherited some ''rare {{g|Mantra}} ingredients'' from my brother when he passed. If you do this for me, I can give you a few.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*He knits his brow and gives you a look of consternation.'' So... Can you help or were you just winding me up?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'll do it.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}No. I hate mantras and doing jobs for people.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}What's in it for me?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}One thing before you leave, thought. The flower I'm giving you is very delicate, and is easily ruined. It would be best for you to take the safest route you know.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Is there something wrong with you?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], Quest Accepted
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Quest End=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="3" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}[Delicate Flower destroyed]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}[Delicate Flower placed]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}[Delicate Flower not placed]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}What's that look on your face?... Did you lose it?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}You're back... I can tell that you placed the flower. Thank you.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Good luck, I appreciate you doing this for me.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I need another flower.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}No problem.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*He sighs.*'' Try not to damage it this time, okay? Here you go.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}I hope these items will compensate you well enough.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], player is given another Delicate Flower
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], player earns reputation with The Hive, a Vibrant Gem, and EXP
{{!}}}
}}

|-|Subsequent Encounters=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Thank you for delivering my flower safely...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}
</tabber>

==Trivia==
*When damaging a flower and receiving a new one, or when changing luminants with the flower, the new flower will NOT be destroyed by any sources of damage. These interactions can be abused to get a durable flower when doing the quest.
* His quest is likely a reference to Hollow Knight, which has a similar quest in which you are tasked to deliver a flower to a grave and lose it if you take damage.

==Description==
Suyuan is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]].

They give the quest "Ghost Hunting," asking [[the Pathfinder]] to seek out a [[Beloved Zofia|Ghost Ship]]. Upon completion, the Pathfinder earns XP, a Compassion [[Talent]] hand, and the {{t|Supernatural Sense}} Talent, providing +10 Sanity.

==Location==
Suyuan is located in the library of the [[Temple of the Blade]] at [[Isle of Vigils]].
<gallery>
Suyuan Map.png|Suyuan's location
</gallery>

{{clear}}
==Dialogue==
<tabber>
|-|First Encounter=
{{#tag:tabber|Quest Start=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Hey, you! Ever seen a ghost? Or perhaps.. a ghost ship?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Player has already interacted with a Ghost
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Player hasn't interacted with a Ghost
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Ship?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Yeah.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}No.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}You haven't heard the rumors? They say there's an abandoned, haunted ship off in the {{g{{!}}The Voidsea}}, not far from here... with a ''Depths-sent'' spirit corrupting it.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Wow, really? What was it like?
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}That's disappointing... If you can tell me what they're like, I'll give you a gift!
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}That sounds interesting.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}It's not fresh on my mind...
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'll let you know if I see a ghost.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Honestly, it scares me. A few Vigil initiates here went to investigate, but each one had a different story. One said to have seen the spirit, while the others saw nothing. They said it only appeared to those who ''believed'' in it.. I'd never go! But.. if you do go, can you tell me if you see any ghosts there?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See "No."]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Really? Thanks! I'll be waiting right here. Get searching!
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'll let you know if I see a ghost.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}[See first instance]
{{!}}}

{{!}}-{{!}}Quest End=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Have you found a ghost ship yet? Or perhaps.. a ghost ship?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Player has found Ghosts
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Player has not found Ghosts
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Yeah. I saw one.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Ship?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}You saw one? What was it like?
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}[See Quest Start]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Ghosts attacked the player
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}Ghosts didn't attack the player
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}There were more than just one - they stabbed me!
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}It smiled, and asked me to remember the dead.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}That's quite the experience... Thanks for sharing! In return, here's somethin' small.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], Player gains XP and Compassion
}}

|-|Subsequent Encounters=
{{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;"
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}What you told me about the ghosts sure was scary...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}So what exactly do you do here?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Oh! My apologies. I was so caught up in my ghost stories that I forgot my manners. I'm Suyuan, my father was a friend of the Maestro's so I'm allowed to flick through the books here.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Who was your father exactly?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Vigil Kiriban. One of the best, they say. We weren't very close in life, so I guess that might explain to you why I'm a little obsessed with ghosts...
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}}
</tabber>

title: Sworn Angel
content:
{{Monster Infobox |image1=Sworn Angel.png |attacks=*Assault *Critical *Feint *Glare *Gaze *Exhaustion Strike *Dash *Light Piercer |health=900 200 {{To1Color|(Trial of One)}}
2250 {{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}} |locations=[[Trial of One]]
[[The Diluvian Mechanism]] |drops=[[Sworn Angel Mask]] |challenges= {{bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}} }} '''Note: Not to be confused with the weaker [[Hollow Angel]].''' == Description == '''Sworn Angels''', previously known as '''Angels''', are white and dull-yellow humanoid creatures with wings. They wield the Soulwrought Spear from the [[Crazy Slots]] [[Resonance]] and use Crazy Slots' Soulwrought Spear light shots ability. Sworn Angels can either be spawned as the fifth challenge in the [[Trial of One]] by the Voice of Solitude, by the [[Watcher|Watchers]], or from the 10th wave of [[The Diluvian Mechanism]]. Sworn Angels can also spawn with enchants which differentiate them from their [[Hollow Angel|Hollow]] counterparts. ==Moveset== {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Assault'''
(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Critical'''
(★★☆) |Enters a stance before performing a quick swipe, will perform an additional short lunge if the first hit lands. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Feint'''
(★★☆) |Performs a fake attack, before pulling back and committing to a thrust. {{AttackTags |unharmful }} |- |
'''Glare'''
(★☆☆) |The Angel's eyes light up, stunning anyone facing them if it isn't parried/blocked. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Gaze'''
(★☆☆) |A swirling symbol appears around the Angel's eyes, causing a insanity shiver effect while they look at you. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Exhaustion Strike'''
(★★☆) |Quickly performs a medium ranged jab that transfers all of their posture damage onto the target. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Dash'''
(☆☆☆) |Quickly dashes a long distance, purely for mobility. {{AttackTags |unharmful, movement }} |- |
'''Light Piercer'''
(★★☆) |Rises into the air and shoot 5 spears of light that slow those hit. *Deals typeless damage. *Has autoparry frames. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |} ==Passive== *'''Bear Trap''' - Getting hit with Angel's critical will disable your jumps and slow you down for a duration ==Gallery== Sworn Angel Wide.png|Full Wingspan SwornAngelIcon.png|Sworn Angel Mask ==Trivia== *Sworn Angels are prone to retreating/dodging by moving backwards from you, making it sometimes frustrating to fight them. *In the Trial of One, Sworn Angel's Gaze can affect each other Angel if they walk in front of the other while it's active, allowing for a chance to strike. *In the Trial of One, executing one of the Sworn Angels will cause the other to automatically despawn, passing the trial with less effort. *They '''CAN''' be spawned by [[Watcher|Watchers]] when you are above [[Power]] 8-10(testing needed), so being below that will spawn a [[Hollow Angel]] as usual. *Activating {{etal|weapon|True Seraph Slash}} with a [[Sworn Angel Mask|Sworn]] or [[Hollow Angel Mask]] while having [[Oath: Starkindred|Starkindred]] wings out will allow you to spawn an allied Sworn Angel. {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Enemies that can wield Enchantments]] [[Category:Humanoids with Unobtainable Outfits]] [[Category:Humanoid Monsters]]
