|image1=Silhouette.jpg
|goals=
*Saving [[Lumen]].
*Sealing their souls in [[Saintsworn Obelisks|obelisks]] to immortalize themselves.
|territory=[[Saintsworn Obelisks]]}}

__TOC__

==Description==
The Five Heroes were a team consisting of Heroes, each one wielding their own respective element's [[Hero's Blades|Hero's Blade]].<ref name="Obelisks" />

At some point of their lives, they all bound their souls to their [[Hero Blades]]. After their deaths, their souls now live in the [[Saintsworn Obelisks|obelisks]] scattered all around the [[Luminants#Etrean and Eastern Luminants|Etrean and Eastern Luminants]].<ref name="Obelisks" />

The Five were:

*'''[[Jace|{{cl|fir|Jace, The Hero of Flame}}]]:''' A [[Khan]], who wielded [[Flamecharm]] and the [[Hero's Blade of Flame]]. His soul is sealed in the '''[[Flamecharm Obelisk|{{cl|fir|Flamecharm Obelisk}}]]''', located in [[Saramaed Summit]].<ref name="Obelisks">[[Saintsworn Obelisks]]</ref>
*'''[[Faust|{{cl|ice|Faust, The Hero of Frost}}]]:''' A [[Capra]], who wielded [[Frostdraw]] and the [[Hero's Blade of Frost]]. His soul is sealed in the '''[[Frostdraw Obelisk|{{cl|ice|Frostdraw Obelisk}}]]''', located in the [[Glacial Remnant]] in a small opening in the [[Crypt of the Unbroken]].<ref name="Obelisks" />
*'''[[Urek Felhand|{{cl|sdw|Urek Felhand, The Hero of Shadow}}]]:''' A [[Kiron]], who wielded [[Shadowcast]] and the [[Hero's Blade of Shadow]]. His soul is sealed in the '''[[Shadowcast Obelisk|{{cl|sdw|Shadowcast Obelisk}}]]''', located on the [[Moon's Eyrie]]. At some point of his life, he was betrayed by, or betrayed the other heroes.<ref name="Obelisks" />
*'''[[Trinity Galenwarde|{{cl|wnd|Trinity Galenwarde, The Hero of Wind}}]]:''' A [[Tiran]], who wielded [[Galebreathe]] and the [[Hero's Blade of Wind]]. Her soul is sealed in the '''[[Galebreathe Obelisk|{{cl|wnd|Galebreathe Obelisk}}]]''', located in the [[Burning Stone Gardens]].<ref name="Obelisks" />
*'''[[Tessa|{{cl|ltn|Tessa, The Hero of Lightning}}]]:''' An [[Adret]], who wielded [[Thundercall]] and the [[Hero's Blade of Lightning]]. Her soul is sealed in the '''[[Thundercall Obelisk|{{cl|ltn|Thundercall Obelisk}}]]''', located on the [[Boatman's Watch]].<ref name="Obelisks" /> At some point of her life, she fell in battle and was forever immortalized in her [[Thundercall Obelisk|obelisk]].<ref name="Tweet">https://fxtwitter.com/Deepwoken/status/1801820070403772727</ref>

==Description==
Twin spatulas somehow used as a weapon.

The Flippers of Fate can be upgraded with the [[Chef's Toque]] equipment, granting it a 35% chance to drain to steal 1.95 * ln(D) + 1.075 hunger and thirst from your opponent on weapon hits, where D = scaled damage dealt (calculator [https://www.desmos.com/calculator/yktgme7xnc here]). This has a 3 second cooldown per proc attempt, going on cooldown even if it didn't proc. This stacks additively with [[Gluttony]].

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:Warden Sword Crit.gif|Critical
File:WardenCeremonial.gif|Critical + Follow-up
</gallery><!---temporary file due to identical criticals--->
The user dashes forward and performs a 360° horizontal slash. Landing the first part of the critical will clear its cooldown. Using the critical after the initial hit performs a second 360° horizontal slash that hits twice.

The critical has a cooldown of '''6 seconds''', even after the follow-up critical is landed.

Notably, this attack is shared with the [[Warden Ceremonial Sword]].

title: The Floating Keep
content:
{{EventContent}}
{{Location|name=The Floating Keep|caption=The awe-inspiring moving keep of the mysterious Spellhardt family.}}
[[File:TheFloatingKeep.png|900px|center|thumb]]

== Description ==
The Floating Keep is a temporary location in Deepwoken. (only found during Hallowtide) It appears to be a medieval keep, and very grand in appearance. The entire island is floating in the air next to the the Isle of Vigils. You can reach this place by interacting with the Jack'o Lantern in the [[Isle of Vigils]] near the building that sells attunement training items or at [[Greathive Aratel]] near the entrance. It is inhabited by [[Lightborn]]s of the Spellhardt family. Here players can interact with members of the [[Spellhardt family]] and participate in the Halloween Event.

===Cathedral===
In the Cathedral, you can talk to [[Lysander Spellhardt]] to start the quest to craft yourself [[Hallowtide Mask|a mask]]. To create [[Hallowtide Mask|the mask]], you need a [[Hallowtide Mask Ingredients|Shell Stock]], a [[Hallowtide Mask Ingredients|Paperette]] and a [[Hallowtide Mask Ingredients|Fine Ink]]. When creating [[Hallowtide Mask|the mask]], there is a chance for it to be of a Mudskipper, Primadon, or an Owl. Once you put on a mask, you can speak to NPCs and scare them (there are at least 87 NPCs you can scare, 13 in the depths and 74 in the overworld), which gives you Hallowtide Joy, which is a form of currency that can be exchanged with [[Lysander Spellhardt|Lysander]], [[Glaive Spellhardt|Glaive]], and [[Galpin Spellhardt, Musicologist Extraordinaire|Galpin]] for items. [[Joy]] can be exchanged for:

*[[Books#Eggs In A Basket|Eggs In A Basket]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel)|Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel)]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#Tale of the Storm|Tale of the Storm]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#The Ferryman's Lullaby|The Ferryman's Lullaby]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#The Gideshu March|The Gideshu March]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#The Hammer's Call|The Hammer's Call]] [20 Joy]
*[[Books#The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation|The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation]] [20 Joy]
*[[Outfits#Master|Random Master Schematic or Familiar Schematic]] [20 Joy]
*[[Familiar Priest's Helm]] [35 Joy]
*[[Familiar Heretic's Helm]] [35 Joy]
*[[Familiar Knight's Helm]] [35 Joy]
*[[Pumpkin Head]] [50 Joy]
*[[Books#A Light In The Sky|A Light In The Sky]] [50 Joy]
*Hallowtide Variant [70 Joy]
*[[Relics|Random Relic]] [100 Joy]
*[[Gourdguard|Gourdguard (Shield)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Mushroom Costume]] [100 Joy]
*[[Skyreap Blade|Skyreap Blade (Greataxe)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Hallowscleave|Hallowscleave (Sword)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Skull Piercer|Skull Piercer (Rapier)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Putrid Edenstaff|Putrid Edenstaff (Greathammer)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Bloodtide Trident|Bloodtide Trident (Spear)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Drakemaw Gauntlets|Drakemaw Gauntlets (Fist)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Wretched Mawblades|Wretched Mawblades (Greatsword)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Death's Reverie|Death's Reverie (Twinblade)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Spectral Grasp|Spectral Grasp (Dagger)]] [100 Joy]
*[[Enchantments|Harrowing Enchant Stone]] [150 Joy]
*[[Instruments#Spectral_Instruments|Galphin's Spectral Instrument Set]] [200 Joy]
*[[Pumpkin Pitch]] [300 Joy]
*Hallowtide '24 Medal [300 Joy]

===General, Weaponry and Mantra Shop===
*Players can buy several things here:
**Players can purchase a Lumber Axe for {{c|Notes|3}}, and a Pickaxe for {{c|Notes|3}}.
**Players can purchase a Dumbbell for {{c|Notes|25}}, Ankle Weights for {{c|Notes|25}}, and a Training Vest for {{c|Notes|25}}.
**Players can purchase a Self-Conducting Loop, Hermafrost, Hearthgem, Pure Heart and Gale Kata for {{c|Notes|25}}.
**Players can purchase a [[Parry Dagger]] for {{c|Notes|16}}, a [[Messer]] for {{c|Notes|16}}, a [[Tanto]] for {{c|Notes|100}}, an [[Apprentice Rapier]] for {{c|Notes|100}}, a [[Trident Spear]] for {{c|Notes|100}}, a [[Vigil Longsword]] for {{c|Notes|100}}, and a [[Darksteel Greatsword]] for {{c|Notes|200}}.

===Exclusive NPCs and Variants===
====Lightborns====
*[[Everis Spellhardt]]
*[[Brasidas Spellhardt]] 
*[[Louie Spellhardt]]
*[[Leaf Spellhardt]]
*[[Green Spellhardt]]
*[[Tundra Spellhardt]]

====Unknown/Exclusive====
*[[Hallowtide (Event)|Hallowtide Caller]]
*[[Suspicious Skeleton|Suspicious Skeleton (Bone Rattler)]]
[[File:Dining hall.png|thumb|The Dining Hall.]]

===Food===
*Players can buy several [[food]]s here from an NPC called Mikhail.
**Glazed Fish for {{c|Notes|15}}.
**Sushi for {{c|Notes|20}}.
**Mushroom Omelette for {{c|Notes|15}}.
**Mushroom Bisque for {{c|Notes|20}}.
** Fish Stew for {{c|Notes|15}}.

===Library===
*Players can purchase a Weapon Manual for {{c|Notes|25}}, [[How to Make Friends]] for {{c|Notes|25}}, and an Encyclopedia for {{c|Notes|25}}.

==Maps==
A map can be found at [[Maps#Surface]]

==Trivia==
* The music for this area is [[A Light In The Sky]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]]
*The combat music for this area is [[A Darkness Beneath]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]]
*Initially, there was a bug where the Void Feather cost 5 Joy instead of the required 15. This was patched quickly.
*The Familiar Priest, Heretic and Knight helmet are direct references to their counterparts from ''Rogue Lineage'', being the Church Knight Helmet, Dark Sigil Helmet and Sigil Helmet respectively.
*Whenever you try to spook Glaive Spellhardt with a Hallowtide Mask, he doesn't get spooked and instead says: "Oh please."
*This location appears in the Battle Royale mode as an "intermission" before the game starts, but there are no Lightborn NPCs
*On October 17, 2023 there used to be a floating gate above the castle. However, it was presumably removed during one of the bug fix updates following the release of Hallowtide.
**For some reason, the floating gate is back in Hallowtide 2024, it's unknown if it will get removed yet.<gallery>
File:Floating gate floating keep.png|Removed Floating Gate
</gallery>
*There was a bugged version of the Floating Keep in certain servers where if someone with [[Lightborn]] in the [[Vow of Iron]] joined in [[Pathfinder]] it would spawn the Keep, only accessible by gliding from a high point or with Ad Astra. In this bugged state, some interactables, like the wells, stop working, and [[Lysander Spellhardt]] is replaced with one of [[Vow of Iron]]'s [[Chest Master|Chest Masters]]. This was the only [[Chest Master]] accessible outside of [[Vow of Iron]].<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:KeepChestMaster.png|A [[Chest Master]] in [[Pathfinder]] mode, found in the bugged Floating Keep.
</gallery>

title: The Frontier Furnace
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=The Frontier Furnace|caption=The hiss of steam and roar of engines grant a strange comfort amidst the wind-swept land.}}
[[File:Frontierfurnace.png|center|thumb|900px]]

==Overview==
The Frontier Furnace is [[The Ignition Union]]'s main base of operations in the [[Second Layer]], and is opened after turning on the Generator, guarded by a [[Bone Keeper]].  

==Contents==

*[[Alpha]], who you can talk to and acquire the Union Hook Talent as well as starting the quest that lets you obtain [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arcwarder]].
*[[Llevyn]], who activates the Union's Elevator, the [[Ignition Deepdrill]]. 
*[[Sunway]], who explains [[Second Layer#Dangers|Parasites]], lanterns, and the existence of [[Carbuncle]]s.
*A lantern right next to [[Sunway]].
*[[Epsi]], who only appears after choosing the apply heat option at the [[Firfire Caverns]].

==Trivia==
*In [[Diver's Journal: Apprentice Hero]], some of the Divers in [[Chaser, Scholar of the Burning Blood|Chaser's]] expedition got fed up and assembled an attempt to take shelter inside the furnace, but were most likely killed by him.
*You can enter here by breaking through the door with destructive Mantras, however you won't be able to pick up the Arcwarder quest, obtain the Union Hook, or call the Deepdrill without the generator.
*Attempting to speak with Alpha or Sunway before turning on the generator will prompt the dialogue: "You get that generator working?"
**Llevyn has unique dialogue if you entered this way, saying "I know what you are." in shaky text.

*[[Dockson]] allows players to duel in a more controlled fashion above the steaming vents below the Summer Castle.

'''The Garden Reservoir''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a sub-location found in [[Upper Erisia]].

==Description==
The Garden Reservoir is a location directly underneath the [[Burning Stone Gardens]]. It seems to hold a resemblance and possibly be connected through unreachable tunnels to [[The Viper's Jaw]], possibly from underneath the acid. It is a gloomy area covered with pillars of stone, [[Ore|Irithine]] deposits and acid running along everywhere, possibly the main cause of acid in [[Burning Stone Gardens]]. Going into the acid will end up with you taking damage and being put into combat.

There is a small cave within the Reservoir that contains multiple Soul Hearthgems, which are a necessary part of the [https://deepwoken.fandom.com/wiki/Attributes_Unbound?so=search#Intelligence_Unbound Intelligence Unbound] process.

==Description==

The Gaunt Man is a slender and pale Krulian NPC that resides in [[The Depths]] that gives access to some endgame content and items. 

The Gaunt Man will task you with taking on [[The Vat]], a dungeon that contains 3 dangerous mobs the player will be tasked with fighting; [[Fury Nautilodaunt]], [[Prime Megalodaunt]], and [[Parliament]]. Upon completing this experiment, the Gaunt Man will grant you access to his shop, containing exclusive enchants, an exclusive Deep Gem, and a highly-valued [[Monster Mantras|Monster Mantra]] ingredient.

==Trivia==
*All items sold by the Gaunt Man ([[Curse of Void]] Enchant, [[Rain (enchantment)|Rain]] Enchant, [[Curse of Captain Greene]] Enchant, [[Parasol's Blight]] Enchant, and the [[Aegis Gem]]) will be inactive if you have not completed his experiments on that character.
**This also applies to the [[Nightbringer]] Enchant, even though he doesn't sell you this item.
*Providence Thorns does not work in the Gaunt Man's Trial.
*Though it appears that the Gaunt Man is offering you the [[Kyrsan Necklace]] for the [[Charged Bonecharm]], it is actually the opposite.
*If you've beaten [[The Ferryman]] during Spring and have asked what he is, a new dialogue option for The Gaunt Man will appear after his experiment, in which he confirms that he's a [[Krulian]].
**This may mean that Krulians are made up of more than just souls, as in a previous dialogue line, he uses an analogy to compare the player as a single stalk of wheat, but himself to bread. This can be inferred to meaning the stalk wheat = a singular soul, but as bread is made up of more than just wheat, Krulians may be made up of more than just souls. Though, given both how bread is made in gameplay and the Gaunt Man's lack of knowledge, he may well really just mean that he's multiple people.
*When you die in the experiment, he states: "Ah. I was hoping to learn more from that one. Oh well." he is very likely referring to the player character here, not the monsters. This theory is reinforced by his dialogue when you complete the experiment being "Hm. I have much to learn about your kind. Please do return for more experiments."
*The Gaunt Man may be a young/recently formed Krulian. This is evident by his sense of self not being completely there, stating "Yes, some portion of me knows this to be true" when asked if he's a Krulian. On top of this, he has unnatural speech and is "still learning the interplay of muscle groups required for speech" - akin to a child learning how to speak. Him experimenting on the player characters and monsters could also tie into this theory, being similar to a childlike hunger for learning or sense of curiosity. Furthermore, his guise does not resemble any aspect on Lumen, showing he still has an imperfect grasp of humanity, though this may be more due to personal preference as well.
*He is an obvious reference to the [https://half-life.fandom.com/wiki/The_G-Man G-Man from the Half Life series.]

title: The Gideshu March
content:
::''Not to be confused with [[The Gideshu March (OST)]], which this book is based on.'' ==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
The Gideshu March
=== from Vincent Zeneke's monograph cycle 'Songs of the Sea' We're masters of the oceans wide, Custodians of relentless tide! For the {{g|Authority}} we fight - Within this dark a blazing light. Hurrah, hurrah, three cheers for the cause! We truth uphold, and also laws! For the many, the few, the big, the small - We would give our lives for the cause! We would give our lives for the cause! We're wardens of the valiant dead, From shore to shore our boots will tread! The furthest reaches we shall tame, Bring order, peace, {{g|Adretian}} fame! Hurrah, hurrah, three cheers for the cause! We truth uphold, and also laws! For the many, the few, the big, the small - We would give our lives for the cause! We would give our lives for the cause! ----
The Gideshu March is a popular marching song of the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}} - the iron-fisted guardians of the {{g|The Central Luminant|Central Luminant}}. Written in the year 1227 CE by August Gideshu, an {{g|Authority}} officer, the march quickly became popular among the rank and file soldiers, with many regiments choosing the song as their marching tune. Some even consider it to be the {{g|The Central Authority|Authority's}} unofficial anthem - though the {{g|Authority}} elites' stance on this is not entirely clear. Not much is known about First Lieutenant August Gideshu, the author of the song, himself. Supposedly an {{g|Adretian}} in origin, his unusual surname seems to indicate an older lineage, likely one reaching back to the Pre-Tidal epochs, when the {{g|Adretian}} peoples were contained within their mountain homelands, squabbling as scattered tribes. The Gideshu family name appears several times in various historical {{g|Authority}} records, though never in a rank higher than First Lieutenant. {{g|Authority}} records indicate that August Gideshu served aboard the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}} Sailing-Ship (or CASS) 'Zephyr', under Captain Hector Corbet. Little else is known about this ship's crew or specifications, aside from the fact that it served in the {{g|The Eastern Luminant|Eastern Luminant}}, and experienced several clashes involving the Etrean Navy, in which they emerged victorious. Gideshu himself is noted as having distinguished himself in one battle by bolstering crew morale during an Etrean boarding - possibly by starting to sing the eponymous march, suggesting his fellow crew were familiar with his penmanship. It is believed August Gideshu may have penned several more songs during his service aboard the CASS 'Zephyr', though any potential copies of the written texts have not survived to reach our time. Indeed, a substantial trove of records kept by the crew was lost when the ship ran aground in the outskirts of the Starswept Valley, whereupon the {{g|Authority}} force was ambushed by a unit of the Hundred Legions. August Gideshu's fate remains uncertain, but official records note the crew were 'thoroughly defeated'. The CASS 'Zephyr' was subsequently captured, looted, stripped for parts, and wholly destroyed. ---- I would like to thank Alloras Munet, a {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}} navy recordkeeper, for allowing me access to certain relevant texts kept within {{g|Authority}} archives. This monograph would not have been possible without their invaluable help.

title: The Great Sharko Rumbling
content:
{{NonCanon}}
{{Cleanup}}
{{Event|date2=March 12th 2022 9:21PM EST|type=Bug Compensation|date1=Winter 1291|effects=Treasure chests doubled for three days|image1=Sharko Shrine.png}}

''"Winter 1291 marks that fateful night, when the rumbling of a million Megalodaunts thundered in our ears. They laid waste to our homes... And what little lands we had left to squabble over. But, in the strange and inscrutable ways of the Deep, an age of plenty soon followed. So soon after a fall, our people were once again prospering..."''

The Great Megalodaunt Rising was an event in the Winter of 1291. After many years of fishing, fishermen decided that their harvests were not enough. They invented a new creation, the "Megalodaunt Bait", in which they would be able to attract [[Megalodaunt]]s to civilized locations, as to be easily harvested by the locals in a safe method and location.

This started out fine, but slow. The fishermen wanted more, and thus, they placed dozens, even hundreds of traps. They expected their haul of Megalodaunts to increase, and that it did, but to an extent nobody thought was even possible. Hundreds of Megalodaunts, led by tens of Crimson Megalodaunts, rose onto the shores of civilized Islands all over the Luminant, causing untold destruction and the deaths of thousands of innocents.

Adventurers, warriors, pirates, mages, gladiators, and anyone else who could fight were called back to the islands to make a desperate last stand, and they succeeded in tiding off the literal, and metaphorical wave of Megalodaunts, sending them back reeling to the deep.

After the re-building of society, the economy was able to boom due to the influx of treasures gained from the Megalodaunts.

== Origin of the event ==
During the update that introduced Megalodaunt Bait, players figured out that Megalodaunt Bait could be repeatedly used. With this, players started placing multiple Megalodaunt Bait in a singular area (most notable one being Etris Docks), resulting in a large amount of Megalodaunts flooding a singular area, swarming players and guards alike, giving them almost no chance to survive and fight back. The baits were quickly disabled, made unavailable for a very long time.

{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue

{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}What are you lookin' at? Show some respect. I'm a bit of a big deal around here. Bit of a big shot. You might've heard of me. They call me 'The Guy'. Why, you may ask? There's nobody else like me, I'm simply The Guy. The pinnacle of confidence and swagger, the pride of Summer Company. And you, rat?
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'm an adventurer, seeking permission to enter Summer Isle.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}Ha! What, did our world-class artillery blow you out of the water? That's sweet. Heh, and you come all the way over to The Guy himself to ask for help. Aren't you somethin' special.. heh. Well, maybe if you can do some ''errands'' for me I can register you as a business partner with the Summer Company. That way, you'll have free passage onto our land.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I can help out.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}You're a fraud, a scoundrel. You'll never be 'The Guy'. You're a joke. [Charisma]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Now that's a good dog, loyal to The Guy. You see, we need to test our new springlock mechanisms with the silk of spider eggs. Ah, but why can't I do it myself, you may wonder? You see, The Guy is just sooo busy. I'm simply loaded with work! I cannot be bothered to enter a terrify-... ''simple'' spider cave. My workload simply won't allow it, I am above ''meager'' tasks like that.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}[Player has at least 40 Charisma]
{{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|action}} {{!}}[Player fails Charisma check]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'll bear through it to enter through Summer Isle.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}W-what? What do you mean? I.. no, I ''am'' The Guy! You.. I.. no. The confidence in your words. The bravery in saying such a foul thing to someone as prestigious as me. I.. you are the '''''real''''' The Guy. Just.. take my spectacles. They're my symbol. You'll be.. the next '''The Guy'''. You've shown you're better then me. I'll put you on the business list and.. take my leave.
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Alright. Those shoes? The equivalent of an Erisia bandit's life's worth. Those clothes are the most poor quality excuse of an 'outfit' I've ever seen; where'd you get that one, off a corpse? Don't even get me started on all these gaudy knick-knacks you're wearing; this isn't fashion, this is an embarrassment. I bet you regret your words right now. Bet you want to run home to mother. Look at you, all embarrassed and shaking. What, do words like that hurt? You wouldn't have survived a minute in the Rumbling of 1291. Swine. And what even is that haircut? I've seen mudskippers with a better sense of style then you. No wonder everyone picks fights with you, have you looked in a mirror? And ugh, that stench. Clean yourself up, you smell ''awful''. Do you really think you matter to The Guy? Give up. Go back home and never leave it. Don't ever look at me again.
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Now you're thinking like a ''true'' disciple of The Guy. We need three spider eggs to test the new springlock. Bring it back to me and you'll gain safe passage.
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue]
{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], quest starts

{{!}}-{{!}}Quest End=

{{!}}-
{{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}Look who comes crawling back. Go on. Show me what you found. Let's see if a lowlife like you can scrounge up anything worth selling.
{{!}}-

{{!}}-

Perhaps, even goosebumps.*'' I am The Guy afterall; a deal's a deal. I'll write you down on the business partner register. You should (''should'') have free access to our state of the art isle now. Oh, how I could've done it myself.. you're so, so lucky I happened to be too busy to gather them!
{{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Hah! What are you, scared? Poor little traveler can't handle going into a disgus- ''peaceful'' cave of spiders? Pathetic. If The Guy was there, he'd simply swoop them all up! Too bad he's so, so busy. Bring back the three eggs, ''dog''. You do want safe passage to Summer Isle, don't you?

The Hall of Shattered Wills is an office workspace. This location is inaccessible to non-moderators, attempting to enter will result in a death by "The Office Creature" (no visuals, you are simply killed on the spot with this kill reason)

It has some basic functions but merely acts as a safe place for moderators to work undisturbed.

title: The Hammer's Call
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
The Hammer's Call
=== from Vincent Zeneke's monograph cycle 'Songs of the Sea' Fine workers of the Union, Come hear the hammer call! We'll stand in solidarity - Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall! Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall! The {{g|The Old World|Old World}} sank beneath the tide, Yet workers, shore to shore, Together toil, and never hide - Mighty, united, like none before! Mighty, united, like none before! With arms and tools in every hand - A pickaxe and a blade, - From depths to peaks, across the land, Work we in concert, and hone our trade! Work we in concert, and hone our trade! It matters not how hard the chore, How punishing the way; For you we'll fight, retrieve, explore - Only if you can our costs defray! Only if you can our costs defray! ---- But if you do not pay your dues To workers, fair and square, The Union will be out to bruise - Labour entitles to each their share! Labour entitles to each their share! And neither mountain, rock, nor stone Can keep us from our mark! Our tools ignite, a path is blown - Onwards we march, powered by a spark! Onwards we march, powered by a spark! Alone, we're fingers on a palm - Together, we're a fist! Our might is like a powder bomb, And like a fuse, may we long persist! And like a fuse, may we long persist! Fine workers of the Union, Come hear our hammer call! We'll stand in solidarity - Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall! Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall! ----
"The Hammer's Call" is a labour song, originating with the workers of the Ignition Union - the renowned freelancer company and labour union. The song itself is based on the tune of an old {{g|Adretian}} folk song, called "The Winding Homeward Road", and the words for this particular version - alongside with the modern arrangement, - were authored by Ignition Union member Gawain Corbet in 1272. Over the coming decades, the song would gain popularity among the Union labourers - with empowering lyrics and a steady rhythm, "The Hammer's Call" provided a convenient means for simultaneously keeping a consistent pace of labour between a group of people, as well as keeping up worker morale. Of interest to present day scholars is the emergence of this song in the context of the Union's identity - similarly to the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}}, the Ignition Union is also a boiling pot of ethnicities and cultures. Unlike the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}}, however, the Union's identity is not defined wholly by internal hierarchy, lingering military traditions, and loyalty to power. Instead, it is rooted in the solidarity of toil - a sense of kinship among those working for the same goal. ----

==Description==
[[The Heavens]] are the other half of [[Glossary#Lumen|Lumen]], which forms an inverted dome suspended above the [[Glossary#Surface|Surface]]. Previously, a home to the [[Celestial]]s, but currently only a part of the [[Lightborn]] reside there.<ref name="Glossary">{{Ref/Glossary|The Heavens}}</ref>

Civilization is dotted all around the Heavens in the Celestial Cities.

Waters of the Heavens are called the [[Nightsea]]. They are inky black, studded with twinkling points of light, known as [[Stars]].<ref name="Glossary1">{{Ref/Glossary|The Nightsea}}</ref>

==Celestial Cities==
[[Constellia]]: One of the largest Celestial Cities. Fell 77 years after the Heavensfall as a result of [[Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethiron]] sending the [[Kyrsgarde]] to ravage it. Before it's fall it served as the Guiding Star to the [[Glossary#Surface|Surface]] folk.<ref name="Kaide" />

==Notable Figures==
[[Spellhardt family]]: A noble and wealthy family, currently residing in [[The Floating Keep]]. Their keep was well-manned and the family had a lot of servants before the fall of [[Constellia]], but afterwards it was left to be managed by the family itself. Every year they host a tradition, called [[Hallowtide]].<ref name="Misha">[[Mikhail Spellhardt]]</ref>

[[Kaide, the Drowned Light]]: The last king of [[Constellia]]. After losing the battle against the [[Kyrsan]]s, the city of [[Constellia]] fell and he was captured and taken to [[New Kyrsa]].<ref name="Kaide">[[Kaide, the Drowned Light]]</ref>

[[Zhatarn]]: A [[celestial]], driven mad by his attempt to draw power from [[the Moonseye]]. He was exiled and doomed to roam the [[Voidsea]] forever. He wielded the [[Soulthorn]].<ref name="KaideSoulthorn">[[Kaide, the Drowned Light#Dialogue|Kaide's dialogue if the player has the Soulthorn equipped.]]</ref>

'''The Hidden Grove''' was a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It was a small cave behind [[Summer Isle]].

== Overview ==
The Hidden Grove featured a waterfall and flower fountain. To activate the fountain, players had to interact with the shrine using a canteen filled with any liquid. This caused 6 [[Ingredients#Lotuses|Lotuses]] to spawn around the fountain. These Lotuses lasted for 45 seconds before vanishing and were randomized according to the current season in the game. Additionally, the fountain had a 60-minute cooldown per player across the server.

* Spring: [[Miasmic Lotus]], [[Zephyr Lotus]].
* Summer:  [[Empyrean Lotus]], [[Hellfire Lotus]].
* Autumn: [[Skyvalor Lotus]], [[Zephyr Lotus]].
* Winter: [[Brilliant Lotus]], [[Skyvalor Lotus]].


== Location ==
=== '''This area is currently no longer in the game.''' ===

== Trivia ==
* When interacting with the fountain while having no water or while holding a canteen, the player is prompted with "I don't have anything to water this..."
* Upon attempting to interact with the shrine repeatedly, the shrine said "It seems its harvest has blossomed all it can, for now."
* Despite being removed as a physical location, the area trigger still exists roughly under the bridge from the Summer Isle castle to the small area with the cannon.

'''The Hidden Village''' is a [[Locations|location]] found in ''Deepwoken''. It is a landmark found in the [[Towerstruck Lands]].
==Description==
The Hidden Village is a small, abandoned town located in the [[Towerstruck Lands]] in [[Upper Erisia]]. The main way of entering is through a wooden door  that must be broken down with a [[Mantras|Mantra]] or a Heavy Weapon Critical. An alternative path is to climb up the mountains that leads you a tunnel to the village. 

Inside the Village are a few NPCs, [[Rotskipper]]s, a bountiful amount of [[Ore#Erisore|Erisore]], and a fountain that can allow you to teleport to [[Greathive Aratel]] if you meet the requirements. It is also home to the [[Deep Shrines/Shrine of Blasphemy|Shrine of Blasphemy]], where one can make a deal with. At the front of the village, you can find the [[Deep Crucible]], which requires an [[Artifacts|Artifact]] to activate.

==Potential Enemies==

*[[Authority Footsoldier]]
*[[Etrean Soldier]]
*[[Legion Soldier]]
*[[Knife of Eylis]]
*[[Knives of Eylis Captain]]
*[[Megalodaunt]]
*[[Rotskipper]]
*[[Deep Owl]]

==Missions==
Events that spawn in The Hidden Village that involve combat. For more info, see [[Random Encounters]].

* [[Etrean Soldier]]s vs  [[Authority Footsoldier]]s

==Contents==

===NPCs===
* [[Nimea]], an [[Etrean]] who gives you insight about Lightkeepers and their place in the world.
*[[Deep Shrines|Shrine of Blasphemy]], who allows you to take 3 power levels (45 attunement points), however you also get a random flaw you don't already own.
*[[Marcus]], a chill [[Stonespark]] who loves sipping coffee. Gives good life advice in a few words.

==Maps==
A map can be found at [[Maps#Surface]]

==Trivia==
* You can find one of [[The Hive]]'s fountains here. Invoking with it will transport you to [[Greathive Aratel]].
* You can find plenty of [[Ore#Erisore|Erisore]] here.
*You can find [[The Meat Lord]] here.
*The Stonelife Lord from the description of the place might refer to Duke Erisia

[[The High Convocation]] is the council of [[the Citadel of Markor]] which consists of retired senior staff drawn from [[the Citadel of Markor|the Citadel]]'s various divisions. Members of the council are known as Convocants.<ref name="Fathoms" /><ref name="Glossary" />

The High Convocation was the host of the first expeditions into [[the Depths]]. They theorized on the concept of the dead returning back to life for a long time, before it was confirmed that the souls of the dead were sent to [[the Depths]], from which only the strong could return. title: The Hive
content:
{{InProgress|Title=This page is still in progress!|Body=Please have patience, and aid the creation of this page!}} {{Quotes|quote=DO NOT STAND IN THE WAY OF TRUE PROGRESS.|author=Hive Construct}} {{Factions |image1=The Hive Icon.png |caption1=The emblem of The Hive |territory=[[Greathive Aratel]]
[[Greathive Approach]]
[[The Lordsgrove]] |goals=Saving themselves from the drownings via construction of Greathives}} ==Description== The Hive is a faction that operates within large trees known as Greathives. An example of these is the relatively new [[Greathive Aratel]], which is located in the upper north of Aratel Island. It can only be accessed through washing your face in the [[Lightkeeper Temple]] before using the shrine teleporter. The Hive was founded by the ancestors of the [[Vesperian]]s and [[Ganymede]]s. They are ruled by an overarching Greatlord who delegates the management of each Greathive to their respective Hivelords. Statues of them have been built in honor at the entrance of [[The Lordsgrove]] to commemorate their efforts in creating and advancing the Hive. The Hive uses an unobtainable attunement known as [[Lifeweave]], which allows them to transfer life energy for a variety of applications, such as creating organic technology in the form of [[Hive Construct]]s, and for being used to power devices, such as the teleporting fountains in the East Luminant. In addition to that, Kaab, the shipwright of '''Greathive Aratel''' states that he is able to "Lifeweave modifications" onto ship vessels. While they are extremely far behind in "conventional" technology, their ability to tap into the biotech niche allows them to compete with other factions. They frequently get into battles with [[Etrea]], who attempt to steal their Lifeweaving artifacts for unknown reasons. ==Reputation== As with all other groups in the game, having too low of a reputation with the Hive will have multiple adverse effects. The [[Antiquarian]], [[Blacksmith]] and all Store NPCs will refuse to trade with you if the Hive considers you an enemy. As per any other guard, [[Hive Guard]]s will attack you on sight below a certain Reputation. In addition to that, Hive Adjudicators and [[Golem Constructs|Constructs]] will also spawn and attack you if your reputation with the Hive proceeds to worsen. To restore your reputation with the Hive, head to [[The Lordsgrove]] behind the huge gate in [[Starswept Valley]]. To unlock access you must wash your face at a fountain on a cliffside far right of Aratel island. After that, you can get through the door to The Lordsgrove, as you traverse through The Lordsgrove, you encounter a Ganymede named [[Zirik]], who is standing outside a small ruin. Talking to this NPC whilst your Reputation with the Hive is favourable will not result in anything. However, if you speak to him whilst you are considered an Enemy of the Hive, he informs you that "your name has spread quickly among the trees". After that, he also mentions your name being a "good name" before implying that he could help. In addition, helping Hive Guards in the following events will allow you to increase your reputation with the Hive: *Hive Guards vs Vigil Swordsmen ([[Starswept Valley]]) *Hive Construct vs Authority Commander ([[Starswept Valley]]) ==='''Dialogue'''=== Good Reputation: *"I hope your journeys outside the Hive go well, [Name]." *"Welcome back, [Name]. It's good to see you among us again." Neutral-Good Reputation: *"Welcome, Traveler" *"Greetings, Traveler" *"Welcome, friend of the Hive." ([[Vesperian]], [[Ganymede]] and [[Chrysid]]) *"Pleasant journeys, friend." ([[Vesperian]], [[Ganymede]] and [[Chrysid]]) Neutral Reputation: *"''*The guard remains silent, barely registering your presence. *''" Neutral-Bad Reputation: *"" *"" ==Notable Members== [[Laplace|Laplace Diri]]: A Ganymede who is a member of the Diri Family. He is capable of changing the enchantment of a weapon by wrapping the three enchants together in Linen (Flax Plant fibers turned to Textile). [[Regek]]: A Vesperian who is the librarian of the Greathive Aratel, through their errand of collecting sap from soulblooms located around the Greathive they will let the player increase the potency of their Attunement-less Mantras, they also explain the origins of how the Greathives are created. [[Suri]]: A Vesperian who tasks the player to bring a flower to the grave of his brother located at the [[Isle of Vigils]] through unknown reasons, his quest can be restarted if the [[Delicate Flower]] becomes ruined. [[Kaab]]: The shipwright of The Hive who will only grant the player access to ships when they hold maximum positive reputation with The Hive, unlike other shipwrights he is capable of modifying boats with lifeweave though this is never seen in game. ==Associated Enemies== File:Hive Arbiter.png|link=Hive Scout|[[Hive Scout]] File:Hive Guard.png|link=Hive Guard|[[Hive Guard]] File:Hive Adjudicator Soldier.png|link=Hive Adjudicator|[[Hive Adjudicator (NPC)|Hive Adjudicator]] File:HivemechIcon.png|link=Hive Construct|[[Hive Construct]] File:Arbiter.png|link=Hive Arbiter|[[Hive Arbiter]] ==Trivia== *All Hive members/NPCs are either [[Vesperian]]s, [[Ganymede]]s or [[Chrysid]]s. *One of two factions to create and utilize [[Monsters]], the other being [[The Ignition Union]]. *They have four Greathives in Lumen, with the Greathive in the Eastern Luminant being the most recently created ones while the biggest Greathive is located in The Central Luminant. *They use Heat stones for their resting camps instead of fire. {{Nav|Factions}} [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:The Hive]]

title: The Hundred Legions
content:
{{Quotes|quote=The Empire's wrath will come down on you if you stay on this path...|author=Legion Soldiers}} {{Factions |image1=The Hundred Legions Icon.png |caption1=The emblem of The Hundred Legions |territory=Western Luminant
Vipers Jaw Camp |goals=Destroy the Authority.}} '''The Hundred Legions''' is a major faction in Deepwoken. ==Description== A superpower native to the Western Luminant, the Hundred Legions are a powerful empire boasting, as the name implies, a hundred legions of soldiers. They once allied themselves with The Authority, but were betrayed. The 11th Scouting Legion were sent to the East to gather information of the conflicts going on there. Their ranks consist mainly of Khans, but they are open to recruiting other aspects. They are creators of the Legion Kata fighting style and masters of [[Galebreathe]] as the only way to train your Galebreathe is through Gale Kata, described to be made by the Legion. The Legion has several war heroes that are depicted by either their ornaments or their weapons, an example being the [[Legion Shield]]. Examples of war heroes are Akilles and Acheron. Akilles, who was in charge of the 11th Legion and brought them to the East when an imminent conflict was brewing, and Acheron who is the owner of the infamous [[Acheron's Warspear]] who seemingly lost it to a [[King Thresher]], but survived, and can be found in Aratel Island as part of the Legion Kata questline. ===Legions=== The Hundred Legions consists of one hundred legions. *The 11th Legion. **consists of [[Amara]], [[Atra]], [[Caitus]], [[Gaius]], and [[Lars]]. **Has associated outfit, [[11th Legion Plate]]. *The 21st Legion. **Has an associated [[Specialist Plate|Specialist set]] style. *The 49th Legion. **consists of [[Polymarch Legion Soldier]]s and [[General Titus Juventius]], now known as [[Titus Fulminus Destellus]]. **Has an associated [[Specialist Plate|Specialist set]] style. *The 77th Legion. **Implied to be the inventers of the [[Imperator's Fury]] *The 84th Legion. **Has an associated [[Specialist Plate|Specialist set]] style. Other notable members of the hundred legions. *The Evanspear Centurion. **Has associated equipment, [[Evanspear War Helmet|Evanspear War set]] and [[Reinforced War Helmet|Reinforced War set]]. **Has an associated weapon, the [[Evanspear Greataxe]] *The Immortals **Has an associated [[Specialist Plate|Specialist set]] style. ==Relationships== *Enemies with [[The Hive]] *Enemies with [[The Authority]] *Enemies with [[The Kingdom of Etrea]] *Enemies with [[The Starkindred Church]] ==Reputation== By default, every single [[Origins|Origin]] starts with an enemy [[reputation]] with The Hundred Legions. Notably, [[Authority Ensign]] has less starting Hundred Legions reputation than any other Origin. Being a Khan increases your starting reputation with the Legions to neutral. There is no reputation reset NPC for The Hundred Legions and have a singular [[Bounty Hunting|Bounty Board]] by their camp in [[Lower Erisia]]. Doing the [[Quests#Lars|Lars quest]] nets you enough reputation to become neutral with The Hundred Legions if you're not a [[Khan]] and haven't done anything else. And the best way to increase the reputation with The Hundred Legions is through doing jobs on the [[Job Boards]]. Specifically, the Job Boards in [[Starswept Valley]] or [[Lower Erisia]]. Though another way to gain reputation with The Hundred Legions is also through helping them fight in specific [[Random Encounters]]: *[[Legion Soldier]]s {{FactionIcon|Hundred Legions}} vs [[Authority Officer]]s {{FactionIcon|Central Authority}} ([[Upper Erisia]]) *[[Legion Captain]] + [[Legion Soldier]] {{FactionIcon|Hundred Legions}} vs [[Authority Officer]]s {{FactionIcon|Central Authority}} ([[The Viper's Jaw|The Vipers Jaw]]/[[Upper Erisia]]) *[[Legion Captain]] {{FactionIcon|Hundred Legions}} vs [[Authority Lieutenant]] {{FactionIcon|Central Authority}} ([[Starswept Valley]]) ==Notable Members== *[[Amara]] *[[Brutus]] *[[Titus Fulminus Destellus|Titus]] *[[Theros]] ==Associated Enemies== File:Legion Soldier.png|link=Legion Soldier|[[Legion Soldier]] File:49th Legion Soldier.png|link=Legion Soldier (The Polymarch)|[[Legion Soldier (The Polymarch)]] File:LegionCaptain.png|link=Legion Captain|[[Legion Captain]] File:Hostile Legion Captain.png|link=Legion Sniper|[[Legion Sniper]] File:TitusIcon.png|link=Titus Fulminus Destellus|[[Titus Fulminus Destellus]] ==Trivia== *Their aesthetic draws from the Greek and Roman empires. *From the camp in [[The Viper's Jaw]] we can meet a Khan with an unobtainable aspect variant, meaning that there might be more types of Khans than the ones that have made their way in the East. *Considering that the Battle Royale map is of Legion territory, The Hundred Legions is the first faction to get its own exclusive game mode, and by extension, the only ones to have a server wholly dedicated to them. *[[Evengarde Rest]] had fought alongside the Legion against [[the Starkindred Church]] in the West, upon doing so he had acquired the [[Pale Briar]]. This implies they once were in good standing with the [[Etrean]]s. However, their intrusion in the east means the two are now prone to skirmishing. {{Nav|Factions}} [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:The Hundred Legions]]

title: The Ignition Union
content:
{{InProgress}} {{Quotes|quote=Fine workers of the Union,
Come hear our hammer call!
We'll stand in solidarity -
Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall!
Shoulder to shoulder, together, tall!|author=The Hammer's Call}} {{Factions |image1=The Ignition Union Icon.png |caption1= The emblem of The Ignition Union |territory=[[Miner's Landing]]
[[The Frontier Furnace]]
[[The Chariot's Spire]] |goals=Competing with [[The Summer Company]] and [[The Divers]].
Gain territory in and explore [[The Depths]].
|major_npc=*[[Alpha]] *[[Delta]] *[[Deepdelver Gamma]] *[[Deepdelver Myra]] *[[Deepdelver Tau]]}} ==Description== '''The Ignition Union''' is a faction found primarily throughout the [[Luminants|Eastern Luminant]] and [[The Depths]]. They are a renowned freelancer company and labor union that specializes in trade, technology, R&D, and Depths exploration. During the [[Etrean Civil War]], the Union attacked the [[Etrean Royalists]]' forces in order to claim their land for their own. They converted the area into the mountainous [[Miner's Landing]], located in the Eastern Luminant. Additionally, they have established two field bases in the Depths: [[The Chariot's Spire]] in [[First Layer|Scyphozia]] and [[The Frontier Furnace]] in the first floor of the [[Second Layer|Eternal Gale]]. They are responsible for producing weapons such as the [[Ignition Deepcrusher]] and the [[Boltcrusher]] along with the [[Railblade]], as well as technologies such as the [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arc Suit]] and [[Union Pager]]. They are one of the three factions contracted by [[The Central Authority]] alongside [[The Divers]] and [[The Summer Company]]. The Ignition Union are specifically tasked with going into the Depths and "killing anything that crawls out". However, the Union do not view the employers favorably and would rather not see them attain greater power.[[Alpha]] They have instigated and maintains a mutually hostile relationship with the Summer Company; alongside various ideological differences, the Summer Company manufactures valuable gunpowder and explosives that are of use to the Union in their many research projects. The union also shares an unfriendly rivalry with the Divers, and they frequently engage in petty, violent squabbles over territory in the Depths. [[Akira]], who does not view them as human beings anymore, refers to them as "[[Mudskipper]]s" after killing several of them with his [[Resonance]], and the aforementioned members of the Union that engaged him in combat seemed prepared to callously kill him on the spot. According to [[Alpha]], this rivalry stems from the Divers receiving funding from the Authority, conveniently ignoring the fact the Union are in that exact same boat. Deepdelver Gamma implies it also stems from the Divers' seeming callousness towards the lives of their members. Unlike the traditional hierarchy practiced by the likes of The Divers and the Central Authority, the ranks of the Ignition Union are primarily structured on the value an individual has contributed to the collective. High-ranking Ignition Union members are known as [[Ignition Deepdelver]]s, and are known for their heavy contribution and sacrifice to the Union and its members. == Reputation == Like other factions such as [[The Summer Company]], having negative [[reputation]] will have vendors deny you service within their affected territories. Additionally, you will be attacked by guards on sight. If the player has positive reputation, guards will not finish you off if they down you and will instead scold you and return to their post. You can reset your reputation with [[Maura]], who is standing inside a house on top of a cliff in Miner's Landing. Reaching her requires either parkour, mobility mantras, or the Union Hook [[Talents|Talent]], and the price range is 30 to 600 Notes. The Ignition Union is among the factions to have a Bounty Board, which means that negative reputation with them leads to being hunted by [[Voidwalker]]s. Having Hunted reputation will cause you to be hunted by [[Ignition Union Arcwarder|Arcwarders]] and [[Mechalodaunt]]s. ===Dialogue===
''The following dialogue is spoken by guard NPCs if the player interacts with them at a corresponding Reputation rank.''
Ally-Hero Reputation *"Alright, ? Good to see a familiar face." Friend-Ally Reputation *"How's it going mate?" *"Sea's treating you well and all, yeah?" Neutral Reputation *"Don't interfere with our work here, alright?" *"Come on, quit dawdling, I'm sure you have better places to be." Enemy-Neutral Reputation *"You on your break or something? Some of us still have work." *"Come on, get moving, I'm sure you have better places to be." == Notable Members == [[Deepdelver Tau]]: A [[Ganymede]] Deepdelver in charge of leading players into expeditions into the [[Saramaed Hollow]], Tau is in charge of bringing the Deep Drill back to the surface when a signal is called by the player via the radio communication system inside the drill. [[Adar, Master of Metal|Deepdelver Adar]]: An [[Etrean]] with the rank of a Deepdelver in one of the towers in Miner's Landing studying on how to bring Ironsing back into the modern world. He has been in the Union presumably since birth from the Union taking him off the streets, due to the living Ironsingers guarding the secrets of the attunement he is hidden with the comrades of the Union not knowing where he is as he would be punished for attempting to turn a normal person into an Ironsinger. [[Deepdelver Gamma]]: A [[Khan]] Deepdelver who resides in the Chariot's Spire along with Renau and Myra and is in charge of the area working with supplies and finding a lost member in the Eternal Gale, he has been in the first layer all his life. [[Renau|Deepdelver Renau]]: A [[Canor]] Deepdelver who resides in the Chariot's Spire along with Gamma and Myra and is in charge of sending or going to expeditions into the second layer, he is worried of the current batch of union members who are in the Eternal Gale as they were unqualified with the most being Epsi. [[Finnegan The Lost|Deepdelver Finnegan]]: A Former Deepdelver who wields one of the prototypes of the [[Boltcrusher]], he had a lover who has deceased from unknown reasons. Because of this his mind broke causing his sanity to crumble attacking anything he sees, as the Ignition Union tasks you to bring him down. [[Deepdelver Myra]]: A [[Tiran]] Deepdelver who resides in the Chariot's Spire along with Renau and Gamma, it is unknown what she does but upon interaction she is scheduled to enter the [[Second Layer]] with some of her peers. [[Gawain Corbet]]: A presumed [[Adret]] Deepdelver of The Ignition Union who created the song "The Hammer's Call", his current whereabouts are unknown. [[Alpha]]: An old Canor seeming as the leader in the Frontier Furnace. [[Delta]]: A Canor residing inside Miner's Landing and is presumably one the inventors of the [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arc Suit]] as he is capable of giving you the oath. [[Epsi]]: A young [[Gremor]] boy working for the Ignition Union and was brought to the second layer with Alpha's team, tasked with communicating with the other members using the radio, his fate is left at the player depending on their actions. [[Miner's Landing#Orion Quest|Orion]]: A [[Celtor]] that tasks the player with killing Summer Goons that invade Miner's Landing. [[Llevyn]]: An Adret who can call down the Ignition Deepdrill for the player to escape the Eternal Gale without the Lighthook. [[Sunway]]: A [[Vesperian]] who explains the function of the Wormwarder Lanterns to the player along with the parasites of the Eternal Gale explaining their origin. ==Associated Enemies== File:Ignitionunion343.png|link=Ignition_Union_Fighter|[[Ignition Union Fighter]] File:IgnitionUnionGuard.png|link=Ignition_Union_Guard|[[Ignition Union Guard]] File:IUArcwarderNPC.png|link=Ignition_Union_Arcwarder|[[Ignition Union Arcwarder|Ignition Union Arcwarder]] File:MechalodauntIcon.png|link=Megalodaunt|[[Mechalodaunt]] File:Drowned Delver.png|[[Finnegan The Lost]] ==Trivia== *Whilst being executed, Ignition Union NPCs may call the player a "scab". A [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strikebreaker# scab] is a pejorative term for individuals hired during an ongoing labour strike to keep a company operating at the bare minimum efficiency until the strike is dissolved. Alternatively, it may just be an insult based on the substances that forms over wounds. *Despite Alpha suggesting the Union are aware of the Central Authority's evils and oppose their ideology, outside of competition with the Divers, the Union shows no signs of attempting to actually subvert the Authority for their actions that they are so ready to verbally condemn. Furthermore, the [[Authority Ensign]] Origin actually spawns with higher starting reputation with the Union than the Summer Company, despite the company being shown to have far less reservations without their partnership, suggesting that, ironically, the Union are rather easy to buy. *The Ignition Union has its own [[Books#The Hammer's Call|anthem]], titled "The Hammer's Call," a modern adaptation of an [[Adret]]ian folk song penned by a "Gawain Corbet" in the year 1272. *[[Miner's Landing]] is one of two cities in-game to be focused on industrialism more than medievalism along with [[Summer Isle]]. *The Ignition Union is one of four factions that have an [[Oaths|Oath]] tied to them. *One of two factions to create and utilize [[Monsters]], the other being [[The Hive]]. *Some Ignition Union NPCs are named after Greek terms: **'''Alpha''', '''Delta''', '''Epsilon''', '''Gamma''', and '''Tau''' are letters in the Greek alphabet. **'''Orion''' is one of the 48 constellations listed by Ptolemy, an ancient Greek astronomer. *Opposed to what their name might suggest, they’re predominantly [[Ironsing]] users. *The Ignition Union has the most Owned Territories out of every Faction at 4, and is tied with [[The Divers]] for the most Passive NPCs at 7. **The Ignition Union have more by technicality, due to [[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract|Chaser]] and [[Karliah]] being former members of The Divers rather than active members. *The Ignition Union is Communist, as hinted at by the [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arcwarder]] description, which references a popular quote from the Communist writer, Karl Marx. As well as the name of the faction itself being a nod to the Communist nature of The Union. {{Nav|Factions}} [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:The Ignition Union]]

title: The Interrogation Of Ranger Santiago Talo
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
The Interrogation Of Ranger Santiago Talo
===
[SUNSDAWN, 9TH BLOOMFALL, 904 CE] // TRANSCRIPT OF MEETING WITH RANGER SANTIAGO TALO - CONDUCTED BY: RANGER COMMANDER ULYSSES DISII, BLACK DIVER - TRANSCRIBED BY: SCRIBE MEMNOS TULAD COMMANDER ULYSSES DISII: Now that the scribe is writing down our conversation, Ranger Talo, let me repeat the crux of our discussion hereto once again, for the written record. You diverted your scouting party away from your assigned patrol path, heading towards the direction of the Landfall. And you did this despite your superiors' direct orders to the contrary, which command all scouts to give the area a wide berth. Did you order this course of action? RANGER SANTIAGO TALO: Commander, with all due respect, I must state again-- CMDR: Answer the question, ranger. RNGR: Yes. CMDR: Were you given permission to divert the group from the assigned route by your superiors? RNGR: No, Commander. [subject hesitated] CMDR: Why did you defy direct orders from your superiors? RNGR: Things had settled in the area, and it was quiet. We heard a strange commotion, and considered that there might be a threat to the other active {{g|The Divers|Diver}} groups in the area. Therefore, we decided to investigate. CMDR: And did it ever occur to you that this was a reckless course of action, Ranger? Your party was assigned a substantial detachment of fresh {{g|The Divers|Diver}} recruits, and your patrol mission was meant to provide training and onboarding for them. If High Command has not issued a scouting mission to the vicinity of the ruins yet, they must have good reason to believe the area remains dangerous - and you led a squadron of rookies there, for Akarad's sake! What were you thinking? RNGR: We figured it might have been someone in trouble, Commander. It sounded like voices. I assessed that we could try aiding them. CMDR: Yes, and surely your training taught you of the effect the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} have on the mind, Ranger? Or have you forgotten of the audiovisual hallucinations and delusions {{g|The Divers|Divers}} experience from long-term exposure? Are you telling me that you advanced - again, in defiance of direct orders! - without even being sure of what it was you were investigating, or if it was even real? RNGR: The others heard the voices clearly, too, so I ruled out the possibility of hallucinations. CMDR: And so you advanced? RNGR: I followed the protocol-- CMDR: Up to that point. That's irrelevant, given your insubordination. How did you proceed? RNGR: I went forward myself, first. I led a small detachment of the more seasoned members of the party at the vanguard. CMDR: Whom did you assign to this task alongside yourself? RNGR: Ranger Emirad and Ranger Bykof. CMDR: And you left the new recruits in the rear, unattended by seniority? Did you suffer a mind-scrambling head injury during your last mission, Ranger? Is your brain leaking out of your ears? Were I not bound by regulations, I ought to-- //[REDACTED]// [commander reasonably displeased] Scribe Tulad, please strike that last statement from the record. Your admission of insubordination is damning, Ranger Talo, and disciplinary action will have to be taken. Unfortunately for me - and maybe fortunately for you, - your punishment will not be decided by me. Your suggestion of intel complicates matters, and I will need to file a report on the incident, which is why Scribe Tulad here is transcribing this meeting for reference. RNGR: I understand, Commander. CMDR: What happened next? Your empty-headed self led the vanguard? RNGR: Yes, the van advanced. We encountered the bodies of two recently deceased individuals. CMDR: How did you determine the deaths were recent? RNGR: I judged by the voices we heard. It sounded like someone calling for help. It also looked like there had been a recent struggle. Marks on the ground and such. CMDR: A struggle? Against? RNGR: A stray thresher, Commander. It was devouring the bodies. As we know, threshers do not scavenge, and seek mostly fresh prey. Myself, Ranger Emirad, and Ranger Bykof dispatched of the beast without issue. CMDR: The splint on your arm suggests otherwise, Ranger. RNGR: The thresher clamped down onto my arm, but Ranger Emirad dealt the killing blow to the beast moments after. The others were uninjured. The surgeons told me that the crushing force broke several bones, but I was still capable of completing our assignment. CMDR: How resolute of you. Should we clap? Should the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} throw you a party? Should we invite {{g|Drallis Ehr}}? You're lucky you did not lose your arm, you -- //[REDACTED]// [commander reasonably displeased] CMDR: Scribe Tulad, strike the last segment from the record once again, please. This should go without saying. We are in understanding? Good. As for you, Ranger, I hope you understand how incredibly lucky you were during this moronic excursion of yours, given that our scouts are not equipped for prolonged direct confrontation. Now, you mentioned bodies - who were the casualties? RNGR: {{g|The Surface|Surface}} folk, Commander. Celtorian citizens. By my reckoning, survivors of the disaster. Until the thresher got to them, anyway. They looked ragged, and had signs of heavy injury. CMDR: Our initial intel indicated there were no survivors. RNGR: I am aware, Commander. But these people were decidedly from Celtor. Ranger Bykof can attest to it, being from the city himself. He recognised the distinct style of clothing. He said they looked upper class. CMDR: Scribe Tulad, make a note for a meeting with Ranger Bykof in my schedule. High Command will want to hear more of this. Was there anything else, Ranger? RNGR: We advanced the rest of our unit to rejoin the vanguard, and... We saw it, Commander. The city. Or what's left of it. CMDR: Of course you have. Every bloody living thing in the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} has seen it. Hard to miss those hulking ruins given their size. What else? RNGR: We didn't just see it from afar, Commander. We ended up quite close to it. CMDR: And? Was there anything of interest to be seen, or are you wasting our time here? RNGR: We saw that the city was fractured. It looked like it was sundered along several fault lines, and the elevation was all broken up. The outer walls and districts were in shambles, but we saw that the centre of the city looked mostly intact. CMDR: Intact? RNGR: Yes. The cathedral in the city centre was still standing. We could see the walls and the cathedral spire from our location. Some of the structures had been damaged, though. We also saw movement at the gates, but we couldn't make out what the situation was. Looked like some small group of people heading into the city, advancing slowly. If I may offer a comparison, their pace was not unlike a funeral procession. CMDR: What did they look like? RNGR: We couldn't see close enough, Commander. Dark clothing, perhaps armour, but certainly not {{g|The Divers|Diver}} attire. Ranger Bykof suggested some of them looked like the Celtorian city militia, but given the distance, we could not confirm this. CMDR: Interesting. What next? RNGR: We decided not to journey further, and returned to our assigned route. CMDR: It sounds like your brain found a way to plug the leak in your ears at the last moment. Ranger, this entire incident is a gross breach of scouting protocols. Your actions also potentially endangered inexperienced recruits. Do you understand the danger you placed your unit in? RNGR: Yes, Commander. CMDR: Do you understand you were needlessly putting yourself and your comrades at risk of death? RNGR: Yes, Commander. CMDR: And do the few drops of intellect still rattling about in your hollow skull understand that this misstep could cost you your position in the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} organisation? RNGR: Yes, Commander. But you must understand-- CMDR: I will not hear it. Your orders were clear. You've already admitted your insubordination. Nevertheless... Up until this point, our intel on the Landfall was incredibly limited. Even though your reckless actions were idiotic, the information gleaned by your unit will likely be of interest to High Command. Although your punishment will not be in my power, I will strongly recommend your assignment to sanitation duties at the {{g|Citadel}} for two weeks. However, as a former Ranger myself, it occurs to me you may be suffering from maladies of the mind. Prolonged exposure to the environment of the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} can impair a {{g|The Divers|Diver's}} judgement and critical thinking abilities. Thus, in my report to High Command, I will also include a recommendation for a week's leave, for recuperation. RNGR: I understand. Thank you, Commander. CMDR: If that is all, you may be dismissed. RNGR: Commander, if I may ask a question before I go? CMDR: Make it quick. RNGR: If there are survivors in the city, shouldn't we be mounting rescue operations? CMDR: This is beyond my power, Ranger. [subject hesitated] RNGR: I see. CMDR: Under current conditions, it would be too dangerous to risk the lives of our {{g|The Divers|Divers}}. We lose too many each year as is, and our recruitment numbers are low at the moment. In my opinion, if we had a forward operating base in {{g|Scyphozia}}, perhaps we could. But as you already know, High Command is intensifying scouting missions in the region for that same reason. These recent... happenings... might start a fire under the seats of the {{g|Convocants}}, though. Maybe it's about time things got moving.
--
RNGR: I understand, Commander. Thank you. CMDR: Dismissed. // END OF TRANSCRIPT
==Characters== *[[Memnos Tulad]] *[[Santiago Talo]] *[[Ulysses Disii]] [[Category:Books]]

title: The Interstice
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}{{Location|name=The Interstice|caption=Just what is this place?}}
[[File:The Interstice_POV.png|thumb|center|900px]]
== Content ==
The Interstice is a liminal dimension with varying structures littered throughout. 
Its ground is made of a purple marble surface, with a thick enough fog to make the marble appear grey. 
Only accessible to those with the [[Dimensional Travel]] resonance. Each step taken here makes you go much further than you would outside of the dimension. Incredibly useful for travelling.

Pay attention while travelling through here however, as there are potholes that will immediately kick you out of the dimension should you fall into them.

== Trivia ==
* The center of The Interstice is located at X 50000, Y 150, Z 50000.
* The Interstice is a [[Voidzones|Voidzone]] in the Overworld due to its in-game location technically being above the [[Voidsea|Voidsea.]]

title: The Knives of Eylis
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Your heart is of empty will, Knife. A soul as vast as the Voidsea itself, yet unchanging in tide. Why are you here?|author=The Voidmother}}
{{Factions|image1=The Knives of Eylis Icon.png|caption1=The emblem of The Knives of Eylis|territory=[[Voidheart]]
Central Luminant Sewers|goals=Get the job done no matter what banner they serve under.|major_npc=[[Eylis, the Punished Dreamer]]}}
==Description==
'''The Knives of Eylis''', also known as the '''Silver Whalers''', are an organization of ruthless mercenaries. They serve Eylis, the Punished Dreamer. They are hired by [[The Central Authority]] to cause carnage in the East Luminant, raiding Etrean naval vessels. Their base is found in the [[Voidheart]], a mysterious location said to exist within the [[Voidsea]]. They are also said to live in the sewers in the Central Luminant.  

The [[Voidwalker]] [[Origins|Origin]] is associated with this faction. It grants the player two exclusive [[Voidwalker]] items upon spawn, the [[Voidwalker#Voideye|Voideye]] and the [[Voidwalker#Grasp of Eylis|Grasp of Eylis]]. 

The Voidheart itself doesn't actually exist, it's actually a collective dream that the Knives of Eylis have while sleeping at night. The Voidheart heavily resembles the Trial of One but there's no information in-game that talks about this. It's speculated that the "deal" that the Voidmother and Eylis made granted the players the ability to travel to their bounties using the Grasp of Eylis and the Voideye.

== Reputation ==
Every [[Origins|Origin]] excluding [[Voidwalker]] and [[Authority Ensign]] starts with an enemy [[reputation]] with the Knives of Eylis. If you are a Voidwalker, you start with a friend reputation.

There is no [[reputation]] reset [[NPCs|NPC]] for the Knives of Eylis. Despite this, they still have a [[Bounty Hunting|Bounty Board]], located in the [[Voidheart]]. This Bounty Board includes bounties from all other factions with Bounty Boards, which include [[Etrea]], [[The Hive]], [[The Ignition Union]], [[The Summer Company]], [[The Central Authority]], and [[The Knives of Eylis]]. The default negative reputation with the Knives that every non-Voidwalker player has makes players susceptible to being hunted. 

Voidwalkers can be hunted by other Voidwalkers at power 5 due to their starting negative reputation with [[The Hive]] and [[The Kingdom of Etrea]], both of which are factions with Bounty Boards.

If you are a [[Voidwalker]], you may gain reputation by completing Knives of Eylis bounties on the [[Voidheart]] Bounty Board.

If you are not a [[Voidwalker]], there is only one event in which you may help the Knives of Eylis and gain reputation:

* [[Etrean Soldier]]s {{FactionIcon|Etrea}} vs [[Knife of Eylis|Knives of Eylis]] {{FactionIcon|Knives of Eylis}} ([[The Aratel Sea]]/[[The Etrean Sea]])

There is no dialogue that changes depending on the reputation with the Knives of Eylis. If you gain negative reputation with the Knives as a [[Voidwalker]], you may lose access to certain amenities in the Voidheart, such as the [[Antiquarian]] or [[Banker]].

You do not need positive reputation to obtain the [[Voidwalker]] [[Origins|Origin]].

*[[Etrea]] |image1=File:Lord Regent Raldified.png}} ==Description== The Lord Regent is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. He is the acting Regent of [[Etrea]]. Zi'eer, more commonly known as the Lord Regent, or by his title, the Fourth Prophet of [[The Ministry]], is a mysterious and powerful NPC that resides exclusively inside his palace within [[Etris]]. He is the interim ruler of Etrea, holding absolute power over the entire nation until the "King" returns to his people. Nobody is sure of his origins, but they accept him for his formidable power, as well as the fact that his actions appear to be in the best interests of Etris. However, [[Warden Jericho]] believes that The Lord Regent is a member of the long thought deceased Contractors, and may bring about a 'great war' which will cause the second Great Drowning. While he appears as an Etrean, his true form is a dark creature covered in emerald eyes and black tentacles. Whether this is his true species or aggressive mutations from his meddling with the world's natural order is unknown.{{Ref/Book|Operation 'Puppet Master' Report}} The Lord Regent seems to be very secretive about where he obtained power, and will exterminate anyone who attempts to uncover it. When [[Kennith]] had doubts on the Lord Regent's actions, he was executed and his mangled corpse was hung on a wall after he tried acquiring information about the Lord Regent from the locals of the city. When he rose to power, he had the City's Official History Office decommissioned, seemingly to ensure he will be the only history the people of Etris will ever know. He also had a mental veil installed in the people of Etris, giving them each conflicting ideas of where he came from and how long he was in power for. The throne upon which he sits is an artifact from [[The Depths]], amplifying the power of whoever sits on it. The Lord Regent likely stays on it to maintain the mental veil on the inhabitant of Etris. As stated by Authority [[Inquisitor Lotus]] during [[Operation 'Puppet Master']], mental veils aren't something new, but are usually limited to a single person, but applying it on an entire town goes beyond the ability of the common man. He has a particular interest in a powerful object referred to as 'The Forge of Sin.' Fragments of it, simply called Artifacts, are scattered over Erisia. Turning these into [[Banker|banks]] gives a hefty reward and is lorewise sent to the Palace. If given reason to, the Lord Regent can suspend his target in the air, using an attack similar to the "Judgement" mantra from the [[Oath: Contractor|Contractor]] [[Oaths|Oath]], before instantly executing them. This attack is only unleashed on players that enter the throne room without permission for entry. It kills you regardless of level or equipment, and is impossible to escape. The attack is disabled when the player is granted an audience, being limited to his immediate surrounding instead (don't get too close). File:Manners.png|Lord Regent killing a player whom dared to step on his Coral Throne. ===Merchandise=== File:Lord Regent Plush 1.png|[[Lord Regent Plush]] File:Lord Regent Plush 2.png File:Lord Regent Plush 3.png File:Lord Regent Plush 4.png File:Lord Regent Plush 5.png ==Trivia== *His throne produces steam. *Talking directly to the Lord Regent while standing on the coral throne (so that he glows white, like all other npcs while talking to them) will result in you being executed by his Judgement. **This occurs even while the player has the [[Oath: Contractor|Contractor]] [[Oaths|Oath]]. ***Funnily enough, when the player does that, the Lord Regent says the default dialogue as if you talked to him indirectly. *He was based on [https://guiltygear.fandom.com/wiki/Zato-ONE Zato One] from Guilty Gear, both being villainous, though formerly in Zato's case, blindfolded men with long fair hair who have shadow powers. *If you finish his quest and you defeat Duke Erisia, do not go back to him unless going for [[Oath: Contractor|Contractor]] with the first step complete. He will end up killing you after confirming dialogue with him. **Attunement uncaps will however be given immediately after killing [[Duke Erisia]]. *It is theorized that his strength comes from [[The Depths]], which he draws from using an unknown source (perhaps by exploring The Depths himself or through some kind of reservoir). This is suggested by the fact that his throne is decorated with a variety of corals. **As [https://gyazo.com/c88d7bf4c887e776dd4334887393e916 stated by Arch_Mage], he does not in fact use Shadowcast, and his "black tendril"/Judgement ability likely stems from another source. **It is unclear if him sending Contractors to the Depths to kill Oath bearers empowers him. *[https://gyazo.com/9c4be296352d1c88e02318fd518a8917 A comment from ragoozer] states that the Coral Throne Zi'eer sits on boosts his power. * He appears to hold a particular disdain towards [[Canor]] people. Schnitzel (the Canor merchant found in the Etris Docks) notes that the "new leader [is] very strange", suggesting that previous rulers of Etrea allowed the entry of Canor merchants into Etris and that the Lord Regent does the opposite for reasons unknown. However, being a Canor does not change interactions with Lord Regent. It's possible he only holds prejudices against the specific subset who deal in Attunement ingredients, due to their seeming lack of education. *Seemingly has a negative connection with the Knives of Eylis and its members, calling Voidwalkers "filthy, void-touched assassins." **This may be because of the Knives of Eylis' current deals with the Authority. *There are free chests that contain [[Erisia]] tier loot on the Throne. *Whenever you try to spook him with a Hallowtide Mask, he doesn't get spooked and instead says one of these lines: **“What a foolish tradition." **"You'll find that I'm being very merciful right now." **"How cute. Care for me to show you true horror?" **"Take that stupid thing off." ***Note: You do have to go up to directly up to him if you want to get this dialogue, but Lord Regent will not kill you. ****Initially he would kill you for attempting it, but that feature was removed. ****You must activate progress [[Kennith|Kennith's Questline]] to the point you can enter [[Etris Palace|Lord Regent's Room]] without being executed, otherwise you will be gripped for Daring To Trespass, like normal. *Zi'eer (Lord Regent) Hex Code Colors: #f7eae3 Skin | #DBCECE Hair | #111111 Blindfold | #8c0f82 Pupils (Hidden) | #cbd2ff Sclera (Hidden) *Zi'eer's blindfold is unobtainable, ours has curves, his blindfold is straight. You can however try to dye the default blindfold into black instead of getting the actual black variant of the blindfold to replicate his. Alternatively, you can also edit a black headband down to your eye level. **This is due to the blindfold he wears being worn backwards, hiding the curved part. *Zi'eer (Lord Regent) hair ID: 6536289312; and the link: https://www.roblox.com/catalog/6536308118/Long-White-Hair (colored differently ingame) *Roblox clothing: [https://www.roblox.com/catalog/9639911906/Dark-Elf-Outrider-Slight-Fix Shirt] / [https://www.roblox.com/catalog/7434547604/Dark-Elf-Outrider Pants] *The Lord Regent is supposed to be voiced by Deepwoken Content Creator [https://www.youtube.com/@demstormz demstormz]. However, despite having fully recorded voice lines for his dialogue, they for some reason were not implemented. ==References== {{History}} [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:Quests]] [[Category:Etrea]] [[Category:The Ministry]] [[Category:Oath Trainer]] [[Category:NPCs located in the Etrean Luminant]] [[Category:Heads of government and state]] [[Category:Humanoids with Unobtainable Outfits]] [[Category:Prophets of The Ministry]]

title: The Lordsgrove
content:
{{Location|name=The Lordsgrove|territory=The Hive|lawless=true|caption=Generations of Hivelords stand watch over the lush passage, a stark contrast to the blasted wastes beyond it.}} [[File:Lords Grove.jpg|center|thumb|900px]] '''The Lordsgrove''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a sub-location in [[Aratel Island]] found in the [[The Aratel Sea|Aratel Sea]]. ==Overview== The Lordsgrove is a jungle-like passage that is accessed through [[Starswept Valley]] behind a massive gate. To open this gate, you must wash your face in the [[Lightkeeper Temple]]. The Lordsgrove contains a fountain that will transport you to [[Greathive Aratel]]. It also includes Zirik, an NPC who can alter your reputation with The Hive. Large statues of [[Vesperian|Vesperians]] and a [[Ganymede]] can be seen to the sides of the Lordsgrove. == Contents == === NPCs === * You can find Zirik, an NPC who will alter your [[reputation]] with The Hive in cost of [[Notes]]. * [[Loot Bag Gacha|Marae]], a loot bag gacha NPC. === Miscellaneous === * You can find one of The Hive's fountains here. Invoking with it will transport you to [[Greathive Aratel]]. [[File:The fountain.png|center|thumb|380x380px]] === Owl Spawn === *In an update, (06/2/23) something called a "Static [[Deep Owl]] spawn" was added into The Lordsgrove, which is self-explanatory. It is advised you be careful in The Lordsgrove, even if it's not guaranteed that it will spawn. You can see where the [[Deep Owl]] spawn is (map below) ''Its very common for it to spawn.'' When it spawns, it is automatically aggroed, and will attempt to kill the closest player. [[File:Owlspawnhive2.png|center|frameless|577x577px]] == Trivia/Notes == * The music for this area is [[The Sun, Gleaming]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]] * In order to use the fountain that transports you to [[Greathive Aratel]], players must have wash their face and be at least Power 10. *The statues lined along the walls of The Lordsgrove depict previous Hivelords, including one with the unique [[Oath: Blindseer|Blindseer]] [[Oaths|Oath]] variant for Vesperians. *One of the statues hinted at the [[Hivelord Mask]] prior to its addition to the game. *Attempting to glide through the open space where the giant door was will knock you off your glider.
