title: The Ministry
content:
{{Quotes|quote=GODSEEKERS, PROPHETS IN BLACK, OFFERING THIS CITY OF STONE AS IF IT WERE FESTERING MEAT. A PALTRY OFFERING, BUT MORE THAN YOUR KIND USUALLY AMOUNT TO.|author=Yun'shul on Celtor and the Ministry}}{{Factions |image1=The Ministry Icon.png |caption1=The emblem of The Ministry |territory=[[Outpost Antumbra]],
[[The Understrand]] |goals=*The sinking of the Overworld into [[The Depths]]
*Silence the [[The Children of Navae]] }} ==Description== The Ministry is a group of mysterious users of [[Shadowcast]] who seek to cause Great Drownings in order to achieve Godhood. They are led by the Nine Prophets, with the First Prophet being the strongest mortal alive, the Second Prophet being the one who pioneered [[Bloodrend]] and spread it to their followers in the form of an Oath, and the Fourth, [[The Lord Regent|Zi'eer]], being the current Lord Regent of Etrea. They have some sort of hostility against [[The Children of Navae]] and desire to clear them out of [[Summer Isle]], presumably due to The Children of Navae's allegiance with a [[Celestial]], Navae, while the Ministry seeks the favor of the [[:Category:Drowned Gods|Drowned Gods]]. This is a rather one-sided rivalry. The exact time of their founding is unclear, but by 1272,{{Deep dates|Verse2}} the original incarnation of the Ministry who had fought to conquer [[Minityrsa]] were considered ancient.[[Gran Sudaruska]] description They are responsible for the drowning of [[The City of the Drowned|Celtor]]. The city was drowned as an offering to [[Yun'Shul]], though they did not care for the surprise gift and did not give the Ministry any reward for it.{{Ref/NPC|Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|quote=IT DOES NOT KNOW? THOSE THAT BROUGHT RUIN TO THIS PLACE? GODSEEKERS, PROPHETS IN BLACK, OFFERING THIS CITY OF STONE AS IF IT WERE FESTERING MEAT. A PALTRY OFFERING, BUT MORE THAN YOUR KIND USUALLY AMOUNT TO.}} They enjoy recruiting people to kill others, sometimes to kill specific individuals, sometimes just to kill random people. They are refered to as originating from the [[Luminants#Western Luminant|Western Luminant]].{{Ref/NPC|Cestis|quote=I'm Cestis. I have a few generous benefactors from the {{g|The Western Luminant|Western Luminant}}, perhaps you know who I'm speaking of?}} == Reputation == Everyone starts with a deep enemy reputation with the Ministry. The [[Adret]] aspect does not counteract this enough to have a neutral or above reputation. Doing the repeatable bounty quest (called "Party Trick") increases your reputation with the Ministry. This may be done by talking to either [[Emel]], [[Imel]], or [[Rimil]] and killing a player in the required location. Dying to [[Nostor, Master of Shadow|Nostor]] allows you to gain some reputation as well, but, due to it being in [[The Depths]], you will be wiped. Doing the bounty quest and obtaining [[Murmur: Tacet]] from [[Cestis]] will also net you some reputation. Going to the [[Soothsayer]] in the [[Starfield Tundra]] and giving them [[Knowledge]] will also grant you Ministry reputation. There is only one [[Random Encounters|random event]] in which you can assist The Ministry and gain reputation: * [[Eastern Nomad]] + [[Eastern Nomad Leader]] {{FactionIcon|Children of Navae}} vs [[Ministry Scout]]s {{FactionIcon|Ministry}} ([[Summer Isle]]) Reputation with The Ministry is gained much more rapidly than that of most other factions. == Notable Members == *[[The Lord Regent|Zi'eer]] *[[Cestis]] *[[The Stranger]] *[[Nostor, Master of Shadow]] *[[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract]] *[[Emel]] *[[Imel]] *[[Rimil]] *[[Volu]] == Associated Enemies == File:MinistryCultist.png|link=Ministry_Scout|[[Ministry Scout]] File:MinistryCaptain.png|link=Ministry_Captain|[[Ministry Captain]] File:Cultist Necromancer.png|link=Ministry_Necromancer|[[Ministry Necromancer]] File:MinistryEnforcers.png|[[Ministry Footpad]] File:Ministry enforcer.png|[[Ministry Enforcer]] File:MinistryBloodrender2.png|[[Ministry Bloodrender]] File:Nostor Enemy.png|[[Nostor, Master of Shadow]] File:ChaserBody.png|[[Chaser, Scholar of the Crimson Contract]] File:The Ministry IRS Agent..png|[[Ministry Agent]] File:Heartbleeder.png|[[Ministry Heartspiller]] == Trivia == *[[Ministry Scout|Ministry]] [[Ministry Necromancer|enemies]] all use a [[Krulian Knife]], besides the [[Ministry Enforcer]], [[Nostor, Master of Shadow|Nostor]], [[Ministry Agent]], [[Chaser, Scholar of the Burning Blood|Chaser]] and [[Ministry Heartbleeder]]s. *The Ministry's emblem appears as a polar opposite to Lost Celtor, especially being associated in [[Lost Celtor|drowning the latter's capital]] as well as the "arrow" motifs. ==References== {{Nav|Factions}} [[Category:Factions]] [[Category:The Ministry]]

title: The Monkey's Paw
content:
{{Location|name=The Monkey's Paw|caption=Be careful what you wish for.}}
{{Location|name=Primadon's Hunting Grounds}}
[[File:Monkey's Paw exterior.jpg|center|thumb|900px]]

== Description ==

The Monkey's Paw, as the name suggests, is an island shaped like the paw of a monkey. It has a large beach, with a ship post and many palm trees. Nearer the center of the island is an opening in the rock, with leaves falling from the top, similar to the [[Deep Owl]]'s feathers. This leads to the main area of the island.

Once you enter the main area of the island, there is a ridge which overlooks a massive flat ground. To the left and to the right of the ridge, there's 2 ropes that lead down into it.

The island is very abundant with food. Calabash, wheat, mushrooms, and other things can be found at this island. If you're a carnivore, there's not much for you to eat besides the players who come here to fight [[Primadon]] or the [[Elder Primadon, The Titan Warlord|Elder Primadon]].

On the edge of the ridge there's a fire that is always burning. You can interact with the fire and make a sacrifice. You can sacrifice food, mantra modifiers, and raw materials. This fire is used to summon the [[Primadon]], a massive aquatic ape, or the [[Elder Primadon, The Titan Warlord|Elder Primadon]], a stronger variant. The recognized items that work to summon [[Primadon, Titan of the East|Primadon]] are three Umbral Obsidian or five Megalodaunt hides, and for [[Elder Primadon, The Titan Warlord|Elder Primadon]], it's a singular Sinner's Ash. Once the [[Primadon]] is successfully summoned, the island's name changes to the [[Primadon]]'s Hunting Grounds.

==Trivia==
*The music for this area when fighting [[Primadon]] and the [[Elder Primadon, The Titan Warlord|Elder Primadon]] is [[A Symphony Of Strife]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]]
*The location's name is likely a reference to the story "The Monkey's Paw" by W.W. Jacobs, where a family of three receives a severed monkey's paw that will grant them three wishes. However, each wish comes with a terrible consequence.
**The wish in this game is the items used in the Sacrificial Flame, and the "consequence" is the [[Primadon]] coming up from out of the water.
**Additionally, the island tells you to "Be careful what you wish for." which is the central idea of the story.
*Be careful while you are here, as this is a popular ganking spot for many players and you may stumble upon people which will attack you after you kill Primadon or even during it. Exercise caution and make sure no undesirable third party is waiting to ambush you here before starting Primadon's boss fight.
*With the release of Verse 2 The Monkey's Paw previously used Roblox terrain. This was later reverted to its original part terrain used during Verse 1 in the January 19, 2026 update.
*The old caption for Primadon's Hunting Grounds was "You shrink like an ant in the face of a true predator."

==Description==
'''The Moonlit Faith''' is a religion, members of which worship the [[Moonseye]]. The Faith originates from the [[Chrysid]]s of the [[Lullaby Isles]].

Devotees of the Moonlit Faith believe that the [[Moonseye]] is the gate to the afterlife, from which their ancestors look down on them from it and that in order to gain access to afterlife the [[Moonseye]] asks for sacrifices.

With the Lady Confessor's ascension to power, she took the society in her hands and forbid leaving the [[Lullaby Isles]], unless their leave is sanctioned by the Faith.<ref name="Marro">[[Marro]]'s dialogue after talking to [[Lake]].</ref> Anyone, who would dare to come back would most likely be sacrificed and set ablaze in the name of the [[Moonseye]].<ref name="Pardoner">[[O Pardoner of Mine]]</ref>

==Notable Members==
[[The Lady Confessor]]: The mysterious leader of the Lullaby Isles, where her word is law. Not much is known externally of her location, or condition, but interactions with scholars visiting the [[Luminants#Etrean and Eastern Luminants|East]] suggest a sense of great reverence and sincerity towards her decrees.<ref name="Pardoner" /><ref name="Glossary">{{Ref/Glossary|The Lady Confessor}}</ref>

The Acolyte / [[Thal'assis Linnaes]]: The Acolyte is a lead ambassador for the Lullaby Isles, leading groups of scholars to and from the [[Greathive Aratel]] in order to exchange knowledge, updates and information.<ref name="Missives" /><ref name="Glossary1">{{Ref/Glossary|The Acolyte / Thalassis}}</ref>

[[Council of the Moonlit Faith]]: Council, which resides in the city of Echelon. The highest form of government within the Lullaby Isles, consisting of a handful of the philosophical, theological, and academic members of the Lullaby Isles. Their purpose is to put [[The Lady Confessor]]'s decrees into action and ensure the operations within the Echelon and wider archipelago run smoothly.<ref name="Missives">[[Strange Missives]]</ref>

[[Prophet Pariah]]: The original writer of the [[Moonseye Tome]]; a short-lived Prophet of The Moonlit Faith who died in [[Voidsea|The Voidsea]] searching for a starway to the Heavens.

==Trivia==
*The act of [[Chrysid]]s setting themselves ablaze in the name of the [[Moonseye]] is most likely a reference to Moths accidentally setting themselves on flames in real life by flying too close to a fire.

The expensive headpiece grants the user the following talents: The {{t|Cauterized Wounds}} Talent reduces all blood '''damage''' taken. Blood drain effects completely ignore this effect. The {{t|Blood Necrosis}} Talent reduces the healing from [[Bloodless Gem]]s by 33%. This changes the Bloodless Gem formula to:
ScaledDamage \times 0.8 \times 0.67 \times 0.3 The {{t|No Limits}} Talent increases the cap on [[Bloodless Gem]] healing from 15 to 30. Due to the reduced conversion rate of damage to healing, you will need a scaled damage of 187 to hit this healing cap. ==Gallery== File:GifSwirls.gif|Particles File:GifAscendingThingy.gif|Ascending particles File:GifParticles(Head Toggled).gif|Particles (Head Toggled) ==Trivia== *When equipped, even while its visibility is toggled off, the crown has swirling blood and the ascending circle effects. *[[Dye Packet|Dyeing]] it will only make the crown darker, not changing the color of its effects and itself. *Because Bloodless Gem healing is reduced, this equipment should only be used in fights against a large amount of enemies, and on builds that have a lot of extremely large AoE Mantras to hit multiple targets at once. Otherwise, this can be attributed to a net '''loss''' in your sustain, as your general Bloodless Gem healing will be largely reduced. **For reference, it now takes 94 scaled damage to heal 15 health, as opposed to 63 scaled damage without this equipment. {{History}} {{Nav|equipment}} [[Category:Equipment]] [[Category:Head]] [[Category:Ornaments]] [[Category:Craftable]] [[Category:Equipment with Talents]] [[Category:Equipment with Non-exclusive Talents]] [[Category:Equipment with Exclusive Talents]]

The Pastry Paster is a Club with a very odd appearance; a rolling pin which is supposed to be in the kitchen, until you wielded it as a deadly weapon.

The Pastry Paster can be upgraded with the [[Chef's Toque]] equipment, granting it a 35% chance to steal 1.95 * ln(D) + 1.075 hunger and thirst from your opponent on weapon hits, where D = scaled damage dealt (calculator [https://www.desmos.com/calculator/yktgme7xnc here]). This has a 3 second cooldown per proc attempt, going on cooldown even if it didn't proc. This stacks additively with [[Gluttony]].

Wind up your rolling pin and strike your target, applying [[Dazed|Daze]] and dealing 22 posture damage if blocked.

This critical has a cooldown of '''5 seconds'''.

title: The Pioneers
content:
{{cnp}}
{{Factions
|image1=Silhouette.jpg
|leader=[[Deukalion Akarad]]
|goals=*Learn more about the nature of [[the Depths]] and come back to [[the Citadel of Markor]].
|dissolved=59 CE}}

__TOC__

==Description==
'''The Pioneers''', also known as the Pioneer Divers, were the first ever [[Divers]] to descend into [[the Depths]]. They used a cave system, which went deep into the Depths. All of them tragically perished, most got caught off-guard by the beasts of [[the Depths]], but those who successfully came back to [[Surface|the Surface]] perished shortly after stepping out of the caves, due to a concept, known as "boundary death".

The concept of [[The Depths|the Depths boundary]] was able to be further expanded upon thanks to the expedition.

All of the Pioneer Divers' names were carved in the tremendously-sized monoliths in a vast memorial hall within [[the Citadel of Markor]] by the [[Memorial Masons]].

==Notable Members==
'''[[Deukalion Akarad]]:''' The first leader of the [[Black Divers division|Black Divers]], who was also assigned to lead the first expedition into [[the Depths]]. He was also known to Diver recruits as "father Diver", indicating he was seen as a paternal figure in the organization. Perished among the Pioneer Divers in the first ever expedition into [[the Depths]] in 59 CE.

==Trivia==
*[[The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation]] was commissioned in the name of their expedition by [[The High Convocation]] and performed at the ceremony by the Scholars' Orchestra of the Scholars of Markor.

'''The Polymarch''' is a massive flagship belonging to [[the Hundred Legions]]. It houses 4 Polymarch Legion Soldiers and the memory task location of General Titus Juventius.

==Contents==
This ship is the area where General Titus Juventius and his Legion resides. Titus can be spawned on the deck in the middle of the legion shield, and other notable parts of the ship include the bowsprit which Titus may stand on if a player he was previously fighting is defeated, and also the Cargo Hold which is below the deck. The Cargo Hold is a safe option for fighting Titus in case you get hit by his Throw move. Inside the Cargo Hold is a ladder which leads to the Legion Ship boundary as well as the Cabin which connects the Cargo Hold to the Deck. However, due to Boundary being located at the top of the ladder, the ladder is effectively rendered useless as attempting to use it will just send you through the Boundary.

{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=The Scoundrel's Bounty|caption=Home to the Rotten Lot, a vessel carrying crew members of countless origins hoping for a brighter future.}}[[File:ShipBounty.png|center|thumb|900px]]

'''The Scoundrel's Bounty''' is a dungeon that serves as the [[tutorial]] for the game. She is a large ship operated by the [[Rotten Lot]], and captained by [[Cap'n Orlandeau|Orlandeau]]. It does not function as a [[Boats|boat]] and is an immovable location, similar to an island. 

==Contents==
=== Antiquarian ===
* Players can find an [[Antiquarian]] who will purchase their sellable items.
* Players can purchase training gear from the [[Training Gear|Gear Cabinet]] for {{c|Notes|25}}.

==NPCs==
*[[Cap'n Orlandeau]]
**A tall Felinor wearing [[Flame Worshipper Armor]], the [[Celtor Commander Plate]] and a [[Vagabond's Bicorn]]. He teaches the player the basics of combat, resting and equipment, how Antiquarians work, and Talent and Mantra hands. Captain of the ship.
**After the events of the tutorial, he drowns and ends up in [[Castle Light]], where he is then kicked out by [[Klaris Llfiend, Mother of Lights|Klaris]] and sent to [[Second Layer#New Kyrsa (F2)|New Kyrsa]].
*[[Flabbernaster Filingree, the First Mate|Flabbernaster Filigree]]
**A Gremor wearing the [[Skeptic Pioneer]] outfit. First Mate of the ship. Appears to be well-versed in combat, considering how she devastated the player in sparring the day before.
*[[Frank F'alzone]]
**A Celtor wearing the [[Verdant Sniper]] outfit. Presumably the cartographer/janitor of the ship.
*[[Pete]]
**A Vesperian wearing the [[Duelist's Attire]] outfit. Appears to have at least some proficiency in combat, given the stat requirement of said attire.
*[[Mr. Quarters, Halfmaster|Mr. Quarters]]
**An Adret wearing the [[Darksteel Plate]] outfit. Halfmaster of the ship.
*[[Serendi]]
**A 'short' Etrean wearing the [[Eager Tradesman]] outfit, propped up on two crates. She hints towards the incoming Authority attack by mentioning the ship that she sees on the horizon.

==Trivia==
*You can drop barrels into the water.
*The Etrea versus Knives of Eylis event can spawn here, although it's likely unintentional.<ref>[[File:Event in tutorial.png|250px]]</ref> 
*The ship bears a great resemblance to the [[Beloved Zofia]], found in the [[Voidsea]], where [[The Dreadstar]] resides. The resemblance is likely coincidental and they are simply a similar make of boat.

title: The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation
content:
==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text== ===
The Song of Fathoms / Oscillation
===
from Vincent Zeneke's monograph cycle "Song of the Sea" Hail to the Tide! Honoured by the sea, Journey to the fathoms in bravery! Us you will guide, Bravest of the brave! Even should the ocean become your grave! May you return, Victory in hand, May you once again tread on steady land! Glory you'll learn, Echo shall your name In the books of history, crowned in fame! Onward, to the darkest chasms! May you never falter, And may your way be led by {{g|The Song|Song}}! Onward, to the deepest fathoms! May the light protect you, May you return triumphant, strong! ------------ ---- "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms", colloquially also known as "Oscillation", is a popular tune well-known around {{g|Lumen}}. Despite this, it remains a musical piece surrounded by discussion and dispute. In spite of the fact that we know exactly how old the piece is, and who the original author is, certain events and clauses of history mean that we cannot reliably verify its true arrangement and original text. Thanks to the robust access to the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel of Markor's }} historic archives provided to this monograph's author, this and more shall be elaborated on in the following paragraphs, with useful historical context provided for the reader. The roots of "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms" reach to the first days of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} organisation, and the early attempts at Depths-delving made by the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel of Markor}}. After the {{g|Citadel}} was founded in what is now broadly considered to be Year 1, or 1 CE ({{g|Citadel}} Era), the institution's research to better understand the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} for the purpose of combatting them reached a plateau within mere decades. To further their knowledge in the area, the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} of the {{g|Citadel}} - a council of {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} seniority, composed of {{g|Convocants}}, retired high-ranking officers of the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} various divisions, - turned to some of the surviving {{g|The Old World|Old World}} treatises they had access to. These texts, it should be noted, were obtained via a tentative cooperation project with the Society of Luminance (often abbreviated as 'The Solum'), one of the now-defunct precursor organisations to the {{g|The Old Stewards|Old Stewards}}. The {{g|The Old World|Old World}} records and writings on the {{g|The Song|Song}} were some benefit, as they offered some theoretical insights on how a realm such as the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} may function. Nonetheless, despite the initial usefulness of these sources, they were still problematic. The {{g|The Old World|Old World}} texts touched more so on the metaphysical concepts of the {{g|The Song|Song}} than the practicalities of the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}, and did not prove of much use beyond understanding some of the elementary forces that work within them. Realising the stagnation that befell their efforts of fighting the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}, the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} launched the first inquiries into a more practical approach towards combating the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. Scholars and agents were soon dispatched to scour the {{g|The Luminants|Luminants}} for any knowledge regarding the dead and the drowned. And indeed, these efforts bore fruits, as the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} soon began receiving unusual reports of individuals seemingly returning from the dead. At the time, it was speculated that when a person died on the surface, their soul - and sometimes bodies - are dragged to the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. Now, the {{g|Citadel}} had proof that this was the case in the form of testimony. Indeed, certain strong enough individuals, having woken from their deathly slumber, now told the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} agents of the strangest things, which the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} had a hard time believing. Regardless, the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} finest scholars were set to work processing these testimonies of the formerly drowned, to see if they were of any substance. The drowned were often either still in shock, or displayed mild signs of mania or insanity - therefore the reliability of their testimonies individually was questionable. However, after dozens of testimonies, singular details kept emerging - an enormous sub-aquatic cavern system, remnants of {{g|The Old World|Old World}} structures swallowed by the tide, their sunken façades, vile beasts beyond our ken, enormous column-like stalagmates holding the caves firmament, and other most outlandish things. However, most curiously, in some testimonies, the drowned recall noticing tunnels high above in the ceilings of the caverns, from which rays of light and seemingly bubble-pockets of air were filtering through. This greatly piqued the interest of the {{g|Convocants}}. A new theory was posited - if what these resurrected individuals were saying was true, there is likely a direct physical connection between the surface and the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. Another theory came to be - if this truly were the case, and return were a possibility, a well-trained team of agents could be sent down into the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} for exploration, reconnaissance, and combat. With enough effort, perhaps a permanent forward operating base could be established. The fight against the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} could, therefore, theoretically be taken to the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} themselves. Thus, in the year 57 CE, a new branch of the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel of Markor}} was established - formally called 'The {{g|Citadel}} Divers', the organisation soon became colloquially known as simply 'the Divers'. Their seniority came to be known as the '{{g|Black Divers}}' division', or simply 'the Black Divers'. With the stated mission of learning to better understand the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} in order to combat them, the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} were established as a {{g|Citadel}} branch intended for field research, exploration, and combat operations - so to say, a militant counterpart of the Scholars of Markor. Training of new recruits began immediately, with the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} utilising what knowledge they had available to them. In the meantime, {{g|Black Divers|Black Diver}} agents would be sent on numerous surface missions around the {{g|The Central Luminant|Central Luminant}}, with the goal of potentially finding a cave system that would physically connect to the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. Success was achieved when the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}} eventually received reports of a cave from which beasts of the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} were occasionally emerging - creatures that were little known at the time, but that are now known to us as 'threshers', 'mudskippers' and 'megalodaunts'. A small outpost, now known as Fortress Vinda, was established outside the cave, and within two years of the organisation's founding, in 59 CE, the first expedition of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} was set to take place. It was intended to be led by the first leader of the {{g|Black Divers}}, Deukalion Akarad, nicknamed "father {{g|The Divers|Diver}}" by apprentice {{g|The Divers|Divers}} at the time. As the first foray was considered to be a historic moment for the {{g|Citadel}}, some pomp and ceremony was afforded for the event. Each of the {{g|Convocants}} gave speeches on the momentous occasion, followed by an inspiring speech from Akarad. Then, following the formalities, as the observers cheered on, the first expedition force - 'The Pioneers', with Akarad at the fore - descended the cave system and dived into its waters, following the path until they disappeared from sight. At their descent , a musical piece, then called "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms", was performed by Scholars' Orchestra of the Scholars of Markor. The piece itself was commissioned for the ceremony collectively by the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}}, and the performance was conducted by the Chambermaster of the orchestra, Ingrid Jura. This song was the last sound the Pioneer {{g|The Divers|Divers}} heard before descending the caverns. Tragically, however, all of the Pioneers perished during the expedition. Based on the notes brought back to the surface by Akarad, some of the group perished in the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} after the group seemingly pushed too far into unknown territory and were caught off-guard by the beasts of the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. The surviving {{g|The Divers|Divers}} that did reach the surface perished very suddenly, not long after stepping out of the waters of the cave, as "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms" started - and quickly horrifiedly stopped - playing again. Although this contextual foray is already far outside the original scope of the monograph, we shall divulge some more details on this occurrence - the author refuses to miss an opportunity such as this, to freely peruse the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} historic archives under the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation's}} blessing. Though it was not well understood at the time, it is now believed the cause of the Pioneers' demise was what is now known to be 'boundary death'. For a simplified layfolk explanation - as a quasi-metaphysical realm, the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} is believed to exert a pulling force on one's soul, based on one's proximity to the deep. So to say, once one is in the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}, their soul experiences a constant downward pull. If one tries to leave the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} by simply physically exiting it upwards, without the aid of ritual or other preparation, they will cross what is known as 'the boundary' - a limit beyond which a soul cannot continue physically travelling in your body. Ergo, the body continues upwards, while the soul is pulled downwards, until the two are wholly separated, and the person dies. And, since the person's soul is in the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} at the time of their death, they therefore perish wholly, without a chance to return to the surface. The name of the Pioneers who died, as well as the names of subsequent {{g|The Divers|Divers}} who have since retired, or perished in the line of duty, are forever carved on a series of tremendously size monoliths in a vast memorial hall within the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel of Markor}}. With the estimate (or, some say, rumored) 98% yearly casualty rate of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, the {{g|Citadel}} has appointed a small subdivision of skilled stonemasons for the purpose of keeping the memory of the deceased alive, as more {{g|The Divers|Divers}} give up their lives in the fight against the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. Though formally referred to as 'Memorial Masons', led by a 'High Mason', they are often colloquially called 'Deathscribes', led by a 'Head Deathscribe'. Their main job is maintaining the so-called Hall of Memory, and carving new names on the monoliths practically daily. According to the current High Mason, Horus Helsen, the Hall of Memory has seen twenty-five expansions since it was built, with a twenty-sixth currently underway. Although grim, it stands as a defiant reminder to the world on the {{g|The Divers|Divers'}} behalf - that humanity's path to victory is paved with many valiant dead, and that neither the {{g|The Divers|Divers}} nor the {{g|Citadel}} intend to surrender to the {{g|The Tides|Tides}} without a fight any time soon. Regardless, returning from the historic anecdotes to the matter of the "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms", the song is known to have had lyrics at the time of its creation - however, their true version remains disputed. The lyrics, as well as nuances of authorship, are still hotly debated topics among certain scholars. During a small fire in the {{g|Citadel}} archives in 108 CE, a few of the early records of the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} history were lost, alongside the original songbook of "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms". A reconstruction of the songbook was attempted by Scholar Marcille Samico, an attendant of the first foray ceremony, and a close friend of Chambermaster Jura, who had already passed in 98 CE. Scholar Samico's version attributes the song's authorship to Jura, and it is also the version that the author has chosen to display in this monograph, as it is considered to be the most accurate one by many historians. Scholar Samico was closely familiar with Jura's work, and although detractors of her version insist she was rumored to experience bouts of mental deterioration towards the end of her life, contemporaries mark her as 'keen-minded and sharp until her death'. Soon after Scholar Samico's version was published and instated in the archives, a different version emerged, written by a different {{g|Citadel}} member - an apprentice of Chambermaster Jura, the young Scholar Mephisto Massi. With slightly different lyrics, and a different melodic and a compositional arrangement, Scholar Massi insisted his version was based on an old original draft of the piece that Jura had shown him, and which he committed to memory. Whether the text truly was an original draft by Jura, or if it was Massi's invention in an attempt to upstage Scholar Samico for a shot at personal fame, remains hotly debated. The veracity of Scholar Massi's claim remains difficult to verify to this day, and it was challenged even his time, as some of the notes of notes of Chambermaster Jura have been lost in the years following her death in 98 CE due to recordkeeping errors. It is not unlikely that Jura's notes have been mislabelled and tucked away in the vast collective of documents in the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} enormous library - however, to rediscover them would be not too dissimilar to finding a needle in a haystack, given the size of the archives. Nevertheless, as Scholar Samico's claim is more verifiable than Scholar Massi's, the monograph shall discuss the former version in greater detail - furthermore, it is also the one that gained the most popularity after Chambermaster Jura's death. The opening line, "Hail to the Tide!", is often misinterpreted as the author praising or worshipping the rising sea, which sometimes confuses novice scholars. However, any historian, anthropologist, folklorist or musicologist worth their salt will know that the line signifies a warlike greeting of the {{g|The Divers|Divers'}} foe - the {{g|The Depths|Depths}}. The {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, knowing that each expedition might result in their deaths, face the prospect with a grim determination and defiance, embodied by the song. Lending further credibility to Scholar Samico's version as the 'correct' version, in the author's opinion, are lines XIII and XVI of the song. They contain the motto of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, "To The Darkest Chasms", and the motto of the {{g|Black Divers}}, "To The Deepest Fathoms". In Scholar Massi's version, the adjectives of the two mottos are swapped with one another - though Massi himself attributes this Jura's own error, claiming the similarity of the mottos, coupled with recentness of the {{g|The Divers|Divers'}} existence as an organisation at the time, caused the Chambermaster confusion, upon which she allegedly remarked in her missing notes. In the decades following the Pioneers' expedition, "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms" gained popularity among the ranks of {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, who saw it as a grim yet hopeful reminder of their goal, their cause, and the rewards their work may reap. As time passed, the song remained popular among the ranks of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, and was often used for certain ceremonies, especially at the start of large expeditions, before the establishment of {{g|Castle Light}}. After {{g|Castle Light}} was established and made operational, a new musical piece was commissioned by {{g|Convocant}} Kyntair Pahaset to commemorate the occasion. Called "In Akarad's Steps", after Deukalion Akarad, the previously mentioned first leader of the {{g|Black Divers}}, it became an official anthem of the {{g|The Divers|Divers}}. Although, "The {{g|The Song|Song}} of Fathoms" never quite went out of style in the organisation, and can be heard sung by even apprentice {{g|The Divers|Divers}} to this day. Once individual adventurers, as well as other groups and powers, began to make their own forays into the {{g|The Depths|Depths}} in the coming centuries, the song spread among the ranks of the new Deep-delvers as well. Its catchy, melodically oscillating refrain of V-B|-N|-ZZ-N|-ZZ-N|-B-B| earned it the colloquial name "Oscillation" among non-Divers, and its repeating lead melody solidified the song's status as an iconic classic of modern folklore. For certainly, in our time, if one calls "Hail to the Tide!" at any port or tavern in any {{g|The Luminants|Luminant}}, they are sure to hear the hearty response of "Honoured by the sea!" ---- My great thanks goes to {{g|The High Convocation|Convocant}} Aurelia Imari, one of the key present day member of the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}}, for granting me access to the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel of Markor's}} historic archive. I am endlessly appreciative of the honour bestowed upon me to be permitted to write and publish this monograph, containing never before seen historic elements of the {{g|The Citadel of Markor|Citadel's}} past. I am also forever grateful for the great hospitality provided to me by the {{g|The High Convocation|High Convocation}}, the {{g|Citadel}} {{g|The Divers|Divers}}, and the Scholars of Markor - my research stay within the {{g|Citadel}} was most enjoyable and informative.

==Description==
The Starkindred Church is a powerful and malevolent cult, presumably originating from the [[Luminants#Western Luminant|Western Luminant]]. They are practitioners of the Starkindred Faith and their power stems from drinking the holy ichor of the [[Celestial]]s and feasting on their flesh. Those with high enough ranking in the cult to do so are called [[Oath: Starkindred|Starkindreds]].

As powerful as the [[Oath: Starkindred|Oath]] may seem, if the Oathtaker's faith falters - the ichor rejects their body and they turn into a [[Maljuror]], a wretched beast, wandering the world, seeking salvation.

[[The Hundred Legions]] and [[Maestro Evengarde Rest]] once went on an excursion against the Starkindred Church, defeating a Cardinal, and coming back victorious with the [[Pale Briar]] as a trophy, which afterwards fell into the hands of [[Maestro Evengarde Rest|Maestro]] and can be obtained by the player by defeating him.

In the [[Luminants#Eastern Luminant|Eastern Luminant]], their only base is the [[Derelict Highchurch]] above the [[Ancient Rotlands]].

==Notable Members==
[[Samael]]: Grants the player the [[Oath: Starkindred|Starkindred]] [[Oaths|Oath]], if they meet the requirements and kill [[Iblis, The Fallen Angel]]. Reveals information about [[Maljuror]]s.

'''The Starswept Valley''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a sub-location of [[Aratel Island]] found in the [[The Aratel Sea|Aratel Sea]].

==Overview==
The Starswept Valley is the middle and northern part of [[Aratel Island]]. Most of the area is a dead desert and is filled with conflicts between various factions and monsters. There is a large green-lined doors in the center that leads to [[The Lordsgrove]], which open after you wash your face at the [[Lightkeeper Temple]]. This is also the largest land mass in the [[Luminants|Eastern Luminant]].

title: The Summer Company
content:
{{Quotes|quote=If you're not here to buy something, then leave.|author=Summer Company Guard}}
{{Factions
|image1=The Summer Company Icon.png
|caption1=The emblem of The Summer Company
|territory=Summer Isle
|goals=*Profit, no matter who's the customer
*Aggresively compete with the [[Ignition Union]]
|leader=[[Gunsmith Rosen]]
|founded=Before or during 1062 CE<ref name="Our Fort">[[Our Fortress (Of Smoke And Steel)]]</ref>}}
==Description==
The Summer Company is a faction that operates in their headquarters, [[Summer Isle]], in [[The Aratel Sea]]. They are the premier manufacturers of firearms and ammunition in Lumen.

The company was founded prior to 1062 CE when the [[Gunsmith Rosen|son of a young village blacksmith]] who journeyed into the sea, returning with the innovations of guns and forever changing the art of combat.<ref name="Our Fort" /><ref>[[Flintlock]] description</ref> 

Alongside [[The Ignition Union]] and the [[Divers]], the Summer Company is employed by [[The Central Authority]]. Notably, there was an incident surrounding the Authority when [[Gunsmith Hierka]] of the [[Bureau of Research]] was sent to steal the company's secrets, resulting in the creation of the [[Rifle Spear]].

They frequently come to blows with [[Ignition Union]], who steal their gunpowder and explosives for themselves, In retaliation, they snuck into [[Miner's Landing]] and accidentally activated unfinished prototypes of the Union's security devices, the [[Megalodaunt|Mechalodaunts]], making the cyborgs aggressively attack friend and foe alike.

==Reputation==
All [[origins]] except for [[Ignition Delver]] start with neutral [[reputation]] with the Summer Company, while Ignition Delver starts with Enemy. Upon having negative reputation with the Summer Company, being within the vicinity of Summer Isle will cause a foghorn to blare and have their cannon fire at the player afterwards, dealing heavy damage.

[[Nepo]], who is located in a bridge behind the castle at Summer Isle, can reset the player's reputation with the Summer Company.

[[Trig]]'s Unfinished Business quest allows the player to net a good chunk of Summer Company reputation if the player retrieves the money from [[Asius]].

The Summer Company has jobs posted on [[Job Boards|job boards]] in Summer Isle and [[Songseeker Wilds]], making reputation gain somewhat limited.

In addition, turning in explosive crates and sacks to [[Scope]] and [[Mercille]] in Summer Isle and [[Bluster Rift]] respectively increases reputation with the Summer Company.

The Summer Company is among the factions to have a Bounty Board.

Assisting the Summer Company in the following [[Random Encounters]] can grant positive reputation:

* [[Summer Company Guard|Summer Company Guards]] {{FactionIcon|Summer Company}}vs. [[Bandit|Bandits]] (Summer Isle)
* Summer Company Guards {{FactionIcon|Summer Company}} vs. [[Ignition Union Fighter]] {{FactionIcon|Ignition Union}}(Summer Isle)
* [[Summer Goon|Summer Goons]] vs. [[Mechalodaunt]] ([[Saramaed Crossing]], [[Saramaed Summit]])

===Dialogue===
Good Reputation:

* Welcome back to the Castle, [name]. Keep making Rosen proud.

Neutral-Good Reputation:

* "Hello friend, make any new discoveries?"

Neutral Reputation: 

*"If you aren't going to buy something, then leave."
*"If I see you near the storage caches, you're done."

Neutral-Bad Reputation:

* "Keep your hands to yourself, thief."
* "We've got our eyes on you."

==Notable Members==
[[Gunsmith Rosen]]: A Vesperian who is the current leader of the Summer Company and reintroduced firearms into the modern era. His last name is unconfirmed as Gunsmith is a title given to him, one of his personal creations The [[Rosen's Peacemaker]] is considered a mastercraft among the goons of the company along with the [[Iron Blunderbuss]] being one of his designs, he is presumed to be somewhere in Summer Isle due to him signing off the creation of one of the most powerful weapons of the company, [[Stormseye|The Stormseye]].

[[Gunsmith Hierka]]: Former protégé of Rosen who's aspect is currently unknown, they acted as a member deceiving him hiding in the ranks as a member of the Authority's [[The Central Authority|Bereau of Research]] in order to steal blueprints of the Summer Company resulting in the creation of the [[Rifle Spear]] which resulted in a tension between the two factions.

[[Funke, Master of Thunder|Black Diver Funke]]: A Canor Black Diver who is in the second floor of the Summer Castle capable of turning an [[Attunement-less|Attunementless]] person into a [[Thundercall|Thundercaller]] via the use of spark glands.

[[The Guy]]: Simply The Guy, a Canor who commands his team who dislikes him near [[Meteor Isle]], by giving him three spider eggs he grants you access to the Summer Company Cannon which can be used as a quick traverse to Songseeker Wilds. He can also be Charisma checked to turn into, Guy.

[[Jarvis]]: A member of the Summer Company who is located inside the castle and has the talent capable of smelting equipment, he is presumably the inventor of the technique and has probably shared it with [[Guild Bases|Artisan]] who can be hired inside as a smelter in the guild base.

[[Scope]]: A Vesperian located inside the explosive storage rooms guarding the boxes from Bandits and The Ignition Union, he tasks the player with taking care of the two near Summer Isle fighting each other.

[[Trig]]:  A Gremor located near the Inn in Summer Isle who tasks the player to find Asius, an Adret who hasn't been paying the Summer Company his dues.

[[Mag]]: A Gremor inside the bowels of the Summer Castle who can turn ores into bullet casings, he is implied to be an Ironsinger due to to being the only member who deals with metals.

[[Thula]]: A Celtor dragoon who is stationed at [[Songseeker Wilds]] with her group, investigating the nearby mines for entrances into the [[The Boundary|Boundary]].

[[Ignacio]]: A Canor dragoon who is stationed at Songseeker Wilds with his group, investigating the nearby mines for entrances into the Boundary.

[[Clint]]: An Etrean gunslinger within the Songseeker Wilds' windmill. He is seen attempting to open a trapdoor, which holds nothing inside but bricks.

[[Amethyst (NPC)|Amethyst]]: An Adretian dragoon inside an entrance of the Songseeker mines, questioning the waterway systems that lie within the cave.

*There is presumably an '''[[Ironsing|Ironsinger]]''' among their ranks because the [[Summer Dragoon]] armor has Ironsing resistances and is implied to be Mag due to how he can make bullet casings with ore.

'''The Sunken Railways''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a sub-location of [[New Kyrsa, The Sleeping City]].

==Overview==
The Sunken Railways is a gloomy sub-location of [[Second Layer/New Kyrsa]]. It is where one of the five Obelisks required to access where the [[Scion of Ethiron]] boss fight is located. Its most notable feature is its bottom floor, containing a Kyrsan Obelisk, two railways with trains on them, and there may be a [[Kyrsan Medallions]] chest spawn.

The top floor mostly does not have anything important, but does contain an additional [[Kyrsan Medallions]] chest and many spawns for [[Kyrsgarde Crawler]]’s after the Obelisk is activated.

title: The Temple of the Forgotten Flame
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=The Temple of The Forgotten Flame|caption=A temple old as the island itself, robbed of its heart.}}
[[File:Totff2.png|center|thumb|900px]]


'''The Temple of the Forgotten Flame''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a landmark of [[Upper Erisia]].

==Overview==
Temple of the Forgotten Flame resembles a run-down temple in [[Upper Erisia]] that perches over the beach of [[Lower Erisia]]. The Temple can be found above the Bandit Village in [[Lower Erisia]], or across from the upper exit of the [[Megalodaunt]] Nest. ([[The Viper's Jaw]])

To enter the Temple, you must either:

*Enter [[Temple Courtyard|the courtyard]], where a [[Watcher]] and bandit spawns can be found.
*Climb around the walls and enter through the rear garden.
*Use a fountain found in [[Greathive Aratel]], that will teleport you to the rear garden.

Inside the temple, [[Neero]], a Pathfinder, can be found in the entrance. Mysterious glyphs can be found on the wall in the room to the left as well. These glyphs play an important part in obtaining [[Oath: Blindseer]].

title: The Understrand
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=The Understrand|territory=The Ministry|lawless=true|caption=A sprawling network of hidden passages utilised by the Ministry in their covert operations. The righteous would never stray so far.}}
[[File:Understrand2.png|center|thumb|900px]]

The Understrand is a sub-location. It is a network of tunnels used by [[The Ministry]].

==Overview==
The Understrand appears as a rugged hallway that leads to a church-like room with large black pillars and a bright diamond-shaped emblem consisting of multiple lights shining through it.

This area is accessible by using [[Shadow's Flight]] or [[Talents#Shadow Travel|Shadow Travel]] near certain events. These events are [[Silhuett]] in the [[First Layer]] of [[the Depths]] or The [[Random Encounters|Ministry Cache]] event in [[The City of the Drowned|The Drowned City of Celtor]] or [[Minityrsa]]. 

The Understrand is primarily used for the obtainment of the [[Deepspindle]], [[Deepscorn Casque]] and the [[Darkened Bastion]] schematic, via the [[Ministry Agent]]. It is also part of obtaining the [[Strange Tomes|Strange Tome]] Volume 3 for the [[Bloodfouler]] quest at a chance if entered through an alternative way.

==Contents==
===Ministry Agent===
* A [[Ministry Agent]] can be found here. They can be fought/conversed with to obtain the [[Deepspindle]], [[Deepscorn Casque]] and the [[Darkened Bastion]] schematic depending on the player's reputation with the Ministry if entered through Silhuett's event.
* Alternatively, the Ministry Agent will always initiate combat with the player if the entered through the Ministry Cache event inside various districts in [[The City of the Drowned]] or at [[Minityrsa]]. They will spawn a chest that has a chance to drop the [[Deepspindle]], [[Deepscorn Casque]], [[Darkened Bastion]], [[Dormant Splinter]], [[Idol of Yun'Shul]], [[Strange Tomes|The Strange Tome]] Volume 3, [[Crypt Blade]], [[Shadebolt]].
** Through this method, the player will fight the following enemy depending on their reputation:
*** Low Ministry Reputation: [[Ministry Agent]]
*** Somewhat high friend with ministry and neutral with divers (may need more testing) [[Mudskipper Broodlord]]
*** Ally Ministry and Low Divers Reputation: [[Black Diver (NPC)|Black Diver]]

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="275" position="center">
File:TheUnderstrandArea Deep.png|The Understrand's appearance when entered through the Ministry Cache event.
File:MinityrsaMinistryCache.png|Ministry Cache event in Ministyra near a zipline

File:Silhuett Full.png|Silhuett in the Celtor Wastes
File:SilhuettInCityCeltor.png|Silhuett in the City of Celtor
</gallery>

==Trivia==
* This used to only be accessible in [[The Depths]] but became accessible through [[Outpost Antumbra]] and [[Minityrsa]].
* If you're trying to get here, it's not that ridiculously hard. A great and easy method is to go to [[Outpost Antumbra]] at Minityrsa, and server hop then look around the outpost. Eventually, you will find the purple lights with the dark sigil in the outpost in one of the server. Note that you may need to have a sharp eye to spot the lights, as sometimes they are pretty faint due to the fog. This is less time consuming than having to search the Depths for Silhuett, as you are covering less area, and also less risky as you won't wipe in the Overworld.
* There will be a pattern on the ground signifying that you have found it its a black circular pattern. The pattern will appear and disappear repeatedly.
* It is recommended to get shadow travel since getting the desired item may take multiple tries.
* When entering in the overworld, the combat theme is Lacrimosa Dies Illa, which is the default combat theme for [[The Depths]].

==Overview==
The Vat is a dungeon located in a hidden cave in the depths. The room itself is a dome with ornate floor patterns with [[The Gaunt Man]] standing in the middle. Upon completion, you'll be able to trade spires and world boss parts for three exclusive enchants and a new deep gem.

==Contents==

The Vat is an arena where [[The Gaunt Man]] subjects players to three escalating trials. Each trial features a powerful opponent, increasing in difficulty as the challenge progresses:
*First Trial: [[Fury Nautilodaunt]]
*Second Trial: [[Prime Megalodaunt]]
*Third Trial: [[Parliament]]

Upon completing all three trials, you'll be reunited with [[The Gaunt Man]]. He will have many dialogue options but most notably his shop, which contains:
*[[Curse of Void]] [[Enchant Stone]]
**25 [[Void Spire]]s, 10 Crowns
*[[Rain (enchantment)|Rain]] [[Enchant Grease]]
**25 [[Rain Spire]]s, 10 Crowns
*[[Parasol's Blight]] [[Enchant Stone]]
**[[Parasol Part]]
*[[Aegis Gem]]
**[[Doom of Caeranthil's Scale]]
*[[Charged Bonecharm]] ([[Monster Mantras#Bone Wisp (★★☆)|Bone Wisp]])
**[[Kyrsan Necklace]]

title: The Vigils
content:
{{Cleanup}}
{{Quotes|quote=A solemn sanctuary carved in stone, where warriors hone the dancing steps of war.|author=Isle of Vigils description}}
{{Factions
|image1=Etrea Icon.png
|caption1=The emblem of The Kingdom of Etrea
|territory=[[Isle of Vigils]]
|goals=Defend and liberate The Kingdom of Etrea}}

==Description==

'''The Vigils''' are a taciturn society of swordsmen in service to the Kingdom of [[Etrea]], an offshoot colony that trains members of the Etrean military in the way of the sword. They are led by the current Maestro [[Evengarde Rest]], with [[Stratos]] as the second-in-command. Residing on the aptly-named [[Isle of Vigils]], they train youths to fight and serve Etrea. All Vigils wield the [[Galebreathe]] attunement, paired with Etrean [[Katana|specialty weapons]].

Not much is confirmed about their ranking system since most Vigils maintain a position of silence towards outsiders, but the descriptions of various pieces of equipment reveal some details about how they function. Their leader is known as a "Maestro", and they operate an autobiographical recordkeeping branch known as the Scholars of the Cloud. What is notable, however, is their impartiality regarding races; much unlike [[The Central Authority]] and Etrea itself, Vigil guardsmen are of varied backgrounds and their histories often have no bearing on their treatment. Vigils are very closely-knit, showing a level of distrust to anyone other than themselves—even if the person is highly regarded by Etrea. It is only when an individual performs massive favours, such as [[Isle of Vigils#Lost Sibling|saving one of their lives]], that Vigils become more hospitable to them. 

*The lowest rank of Vigils are initiates, who don [[Vigil Initiate|brown robes]] and do not participate in real fights.
*Their qualified swordsmen are known as [[Blade Temple Guard]]s, who wear the [[Cloak of Winds]] alongside the [[Glassdancer Wraps]], with a [[Vigil Hood]] to keep their identities secret. They are posted across the Isle, fighting [[Bandit]]s and criminal players.
*Certain non-apprentice Vigils are granted the Deepwoken Cloak in place of their Glassdancer Wraps.
**There exists apprentices who are granted the [[Deepwoken Cloak]]. Their name implies they are in training to become a fully fledged swordsman.
*Elites of the Etrean military are known as [[Vigil Swordsman|Vigil Swordsmen]], though their exact affiliation to the Vigils, and whether or not their name is an indicator of their loyalties, is left ambiguous. Them being exclusively [[Etrean]] suggests that they were already serving in the Etrean military before being selected by the government to receive training in the Temple of the Blade.
*"Keepers" are operatives of the Scholars of the Cloud.
*Untitled second-in-command.
*Maestro, the leaders of the Vigils. There can only be one Maestro at a given time.

After befriending Evengarde, he reveals his knowledge about the true nature of Etrea's government. His stance towards [[The Ministry]] implies that the Vigils aren't held under the same sort of control that Etrean citizens and soldiers are.

==Trivia==
*Maestro is an Italian word, meaning "master" or "teacher". The term is most often used to refer to orchestral conductors, though it can also be used to address teachers of music.

'''Viper's Jaw''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken.'' It is a landmark found in [[Lower Erisia]].

== Overview ==
The Viper's Jaw is the general name of the [[Lower Erisia]] cave system. 

It is divided into three parts. One entrance is behind the bandit village, where two guaranteed [[Megalodaunt]] spawns are located; the second entrance is on the side of the bandit village. An opening leads to Upper Erisia's broken bridge. A library plays an important role in [[Attributes Unbound|intelligence unbound]]. A Legion camp is also settled here, which allows for the player to learn both [[Legion Kata]] by giving a Legion Captain’s Recommendation to [[Amara]], and [[Imperium Kata]] by completing [[Caitus]]' quest of giving the [[Legion Intelligence]] to [[Titus Fulminus Destellus|Titus]] and then coming back to him.

Note that none of these areas are directly connected to each other.

==Description==
The Voidmother is an [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. It is an entity that helps run [[The Knives of Eylis]] and perpetuate the [[Voidheart]].

She is a formless, shapeless being. She is located in the Voidheart, and can help you leave it by teleporting you to where you last used your Voideye, or to [[Lower Erisia]]. She is also located in the Trial of one, right above the player when they first get teleported to the Trial of one, as well as the roof of [[The Diluvian Mechanism]].

The Voidmother views the player as naive, often referring to them as "dull knife" or "Knife." She condemns shallow or superficial desires like fame or strength, commenting that they should "seek a future worth living instead," or they can "find more tangible purposes here." She appreciates motivations that have a worthful purpose, like taking care of someone.

==Description==
The Weaving Web is a Medium Weapon in the Spear category.

Like all other Hallowtide exclusive weapons, it cannot be dropped to other players.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:TheWeavingWebCrit.gif
</gallery>

The user firmly smacks the staff to the ground, creating a pink web explosion (gif is currently outdated) and summons a spiderling that assists them in the fight. The spiderling will not despawn when aggroed, but when idle, it despawns in 20 seconds. The spiderling can use all of the [[Deep Widow]]'s attacks asides from Deep Webbing. It can swipe 1 or 3 times, dealing 35 damage per hit. The spiderling's unblockable bite deals 40 initial damage, ~9% poison damage, and applies slight insanity. The spiderling has 1000 HP and ~40% physical resistance.

The critical has a cooldown of '''45 seconds.'''

===Notes===
* The spiderling likely has the same AI as the normal mobs which means that they will not attack anything by default unless it's a player, a [[golem]] enemy, or a humanoid NPC.
** The player can gain EXP when it is killed.
* The spiderling can be hit to gain {{t|Chain of Perfection}} stacks.
* The spiderling can be hit by the summoner's [[Whirling Blade]] to proc {{t|Cruentare}} and recover health.
* The spiderling can attack other mobs, but sometimes you need to hit it for it to aggro.
* The spiderling has a chance of being {{cl|corrupted}} if summoned in [[the Depths]].
* The spiderling can't hit the person who summoned it. However, if "No Holds Barred" is enabled in settings, the user is able to [[Taunt]] their own spiderling which causes it to target and attack the user. The spiderling can't hit or damage the user.
* The spiderling counts as an ally and can be buffed.
** The spiderling will not count as an ally if you have "No Holds Barred" enabled in settings.
* The spiderling won't despawn if it attacks someone, allowing you to spawn more than one if you manage to keep them aggroed on someone.
* The Weaving Web has synergy with the [[Familiar Occultist's Armor]] due to the spiderling counting as a summon.
* Spiderlings spawned by [[Oath: Visionshaper|Visionshaper]] clones or [[Lightning Clones]] will be able to target you, as they're technically not ''your'' summon.
**'''These summons can autogrip you if you are knocked.'''

The Needle's Eye |family=*[[Erisia family]]
**[[Nir Erisia]] (son){{Ref/WeaponDescription|Needle's Eye}} |aspect= |pronouns=She/her |death=Allegedly died of blood loss following a dispute }} ==Description== As a member of the [[Erisia family]], Thera served as the duchess of [[Erisia]]. According to surviving records, in the form of statues, she was the third of her family name to bear this title. Thera was well renowned for wielding a rapier, earning her her title of "The Needle's Eye". She had a son, [[Nir Erisia]], who would go on to inherit the duchy from his mother. The exact circumstances of Thera's death are unclear. However, it's widely believed that she found herself in a dispute that turned violent, during which she was attacked by numerous other individuals. Allegedly, she survived the assault, only to succumb to her wounds in the arms of her son. As far as we know, Thera was the first and only Duchess of Erisia, with all prior and subsequent leaders were men. [[Needle's Eye]]s were produced as replicas of her famed rapier. ==References== [[Category:Individuals with She/her pronouns]] [[Category:Members of the Erisia family]] [[Category:Deceased characters]]

This Memento centers itself around the [[Blightsurger]] Oath. NOTE: If you unequip your [[Imperator's Edge]], you will '''not''' be able to re-equip it. {{clear}}
==Starting Abilities==
*Electrify [Common Talent] - Shock yourself and apply {{status|Amped}} for 15s. Can be used while {{status|Carried}} to escape. **Deals self damage if used without being carried. *{{cl|origintl|Imperium Kata}} [Common Talent] - Wield an advanced form of the Legion's martial arts. **Allows you to use [[Imperium Kata]], a [[Fists|fist style]]. *[[Oath: Blightsurger|{{cl|oathtl|Oath: Blightsurger}}]] [Oath Talent] - Fists and storm. Wield sacred lightning, tear through foes and leave them withered. (+2 Combat Mantra Slots +1 Wildcard Mantra Slot) *{{cl|oathtlnf|Sovereign State}} [Oath Talent] - Landing physical hits builds your Blight Meter. At full gauge, enter a Blight State that changes your critical and empowers Blightsurge abilities. **Blight Meter gain has no cooldown. Landing Blightsurger Mantras grants 15% Blight Meter. Landing Basic Attacks grants 10% Blight Meter. Landing weapon criticals, [[Thundercall]] Mantras, or [[Galebreathe]] Mantras grants 5% Blight Meter per hit. **At full Blight Meter, Sovereign State lasts 12.5 seconds. **Sovereign State has a 10 second activation cooldown once the duration runs out. **You can press {{Input|keybind|X}} while having at least 30% Blight Meter to activate Sovereign State early. While in Sovereign State, your Blight Meter will passively decay, and it cannot be deactivated. ***This keybind can be changed in settings. **While in Sovereign State, your weapon will be replaced with the ''[[Sovereign Bangle]]''. **Skycrash will be automatically used twice in quick succession while in this state. **Increases the Wither damage that Sovereign Drive and Warp Kick deal. {{MantraInfobox|newtable|end |name=Warp Kick (☆☆☆) |image=Warp kick.gif |desc=Perform a kick, then warp to your enemies for a second followup kick. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} + {{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs=N/A |effect=''Perform two kicks of devastating strength.'' *Has a base damage of 20 per hit (2) with 1.65 Strength scaling. *Knocks the opponent back on the second hit, despite what is shown in the gif below. *Teleports to opponents within range. *This attack is counted as a weapon critical for Talent effects. *Applies Blightshock on hit. }}
==Deck of Recollection==
===Starting Deck===
*Knuckle Guard [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Hitting [[Dazed]] enemies grants you 10% posture resistance for 15s. **Knuckle Guard's duration will be reduced by 0.1s for every point of Fortitude and Strength below its requirements, having a minimum possible duration of 10.4 seconds with 30 Fortitude and 4 Strength, though this isn't very realistic. *{{cl|oathtlnf|Blight Pierce}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Your Blightshock attacks pierce through your enemies hyperarmor and gain more penetration. **Blightshock now works similar to regular {{status|Shock}}, canceling hyperarmor. **Sovereign Bangle, the Blightsurger exclusive weapon, and Blightsurge Mantras gain +?% more PEN. **This Talent is bugged and currently does not work. *{{cl|mementotlnf|Storm Return}} [Memento Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Being under lightning/wind status effect causes your Basic Attacks and Criticals to do 10% more damage. (Amplified with [[Lightning Cloak]]) **Being under the effects of Electrify and Lightning Cloak will proc this effect. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Skycrash (☆☆☆) |image=Skycrash.gif |desc=Dash forward in a blink, knocking down enemies in your path. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} + {{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs={{c|notes|250}} |effect=''Leap towards your opponent and crush them with your might.'' *Has a base damage of 35 with 1.65 Strength scaling. *While under the effects of Sovereign State, Skycrash will automatically be used a second time. **This followup strike has a base damage of 20 with 1.65 Strength scaling. *Ragdolls and applies Daze on hit. *During the leap, you will have hyperarmor for 1 second. File:SkycrashSovereignState.gif|Sovereign State variant }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Tornado Kick (☆☆☆) |image=Tornado Kick.gif |desc=Kick a gust of wind forward, if it hits an enemy leap into the air and launch 3 more. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|galebreathe|Wind}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |reqs={{c|notes|250}} |effect=''Perform a kick that sends out a surging projectile of wind, leap up and send out 3 more AoE projectiles if the mantra hits a registered target.'' *Has a base damage of 18/20.5/23/25.5/28 per level, per hit (4) with 2.75 Galebreathe scaling. *Deals 15 posture damage on the first hit with all subsequent hits (3) dealing 5 posture damage each. *The first two hits have a windup of 0.55 seconds while the third and fourth have a windup of 0.5 seconds. Has a cooldown of 8 seconds *Projectile is medium-ranged and explodes on impact. *Initial hit pushes people away without applying hitstun. }}
===Power 5===
*Sunken Predator [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Enemies you hit in the water or the depths have their speed buffs nullified and are slowed. (+1 Passive Agility) **Monsters are greatly slowed for a few seconds and can be frozen in place with enough hits. **Players are only slowed a little bit for less time instead. *{{cl|raretl|Chronostasis}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Landing a Basic Attack or Critical puts the target's [[Resonance]] on cooldown for a short duration. (+1 Posture) *{{cl|raretl|Everchanging Aegis}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - You take 20% less from attacks the same element as the last element you were hit with, but 10% more damage from attacks from different element. (+7 Carry Load) **Getting hit by another element immediately changes your resistance to that element. i.e Getting hit by Shadowcast Mantras while having Galebreathe resistance will immediately change your resistance type to Shadowcast and vice versa. ***This means that multi-hitting Mantras are much less potent, even if your Everchanging Aegis type was not attuned to that Mantra. **Your Aegis type can swap on block, dodge, and parry. You do not need to actually be ''hit'' by the attack for the swap to occur, largely mitigating the downside. **The damage type you become resistant to is indicated by a colored shield, continuous damage of the same element will give a colored outline of the damage type. ***Flamecharm: Orange / Frostdraw: Blue / Thundercall: Yellow / Galebreathe: Green / Shadowcast: Purple / Ironsing: Grey / Bloodrend: Red *{{cl|raretl|Showstopper}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - When an enemy would roll through one of your physical attacks, stomp the ground, dazing anyone nearby. Removes speed buffs from target upon landing. *{{cl|raretl|Speed Demon}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Your attacks now inflict a reduced-strength bleed while you have a speed boost. 1s cooldown. (+1 Passive Agility) **Bleed is not accounted for in the damage modifier cap and bypasses armor. **Speed Demon's bleed deals 5% of your weapon's damage every 0.3s, three times. This totals to +15% damage over a 0.9 second period. **Works with M1s and criticals. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Windfall (☆☆☆) |image=Windfall.gif |desc=A devastating crash of wind. |ethercost={{stats|ether|100 Ether}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |dmgtype={{stats|galebreathe|Wind}} |reqs={{c|notes|450}} |effect=''Stomp the ground and leap upwards before crashing down with a strong downdraft.'' }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Emotion Wave (★★★) |image=Emotion Wave.gif |desc=Conjure up surging waves of lightning that travel along the ground. |ethercost=70 Ether |mantratype=Combat Mantra |dmgtype={{stats|thundercall|Lightning}} |reqs={{c|notes|450}} |effect=''Conjure and slam a bolt of lightning into the ground from the user's right hand, causing volleys of lightning strikes to spread out.'' *The initial hit has a base damage of 20.25/22.95/25.65/28.35/31.05 per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *The lightning strikes have a base damage of 15/17/19/21/23 per level, per hit with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 13.5 posture damage on the initial hit + 10 posture damage per lightning strike. *30 second cooldown. *Can be modified with ''[[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s'' to increase the size of the hitbox. *Can be modified with ''[[Crystal Lens|Crystal]]/[[Perfect Lens]]es'' to increase the range of the lightning strikes. }}
===Power 10===
*{{cl|questtlnf|Critical Attack}} [Quest Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Landing a hit with your critical restores 30% of your posture. (+1 Posture) *Suffocating Impact [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Flourishing enemies into walls applies [[Winded]] and [[Suffocation|Suffocating]] for a short duration. (+2 Passive Agility) *{{cl|oathtlnf|Blighted Touch}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Landing Basic Attacks during Sovereign State now applies Blightshock. **This allows your Sovereign Bangle to apply Wither on hit. *{{cl|raretl|Cheap Shot}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Your attacks gain 10% PEN multiplicatively when you have an active speed boost. (+6 Passive Agility) **It multiplies your PEN by 1.1x. IE: if you are at 30% PEN, Cheap Shot will give you an additional 3% PEN. **Cheap Shot cannot bypass the PEN cap. **Cheap Shot's PEN multiplier will be reduced by 0.11% for every point in Agility below 65, having a minimum multiplier of +7.22% PEN (or 1.072x PEN) at 40 Agility. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Rising Wind (★★☆) |desc=Use wind to uppercut and propel yourself into the air. Press {{Input|keybind|parry}} after hitting an opponent to impale them |image=Rising Windo.gif |mantratype=Combat Mantra |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|galebreathe|Wind}} + {{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs={{c|notes|700}} |effect=''Ascend while uppercutting your target, rapidly damaging them.'' *Has a base damage of 6/6.9/7.8/8.7/9.6 per level, per hit (5). The first hit has 2.75 Galebreathe scaling while the last three have 5 Galebreathe scaling. *Deals 5 posture damage and cancels when blocked (even if it guard breaks). *Has a windup of 0.5 seconds with a 14 second cooldown. *Gems apply ONLY to the last hit, making Bloodless' healing very low. *Pressing F during the animation lets you kick your opponent down into the ground, applying daze and knockdown. *Gives I-Frames to yourself and your opponent throughout the duration of the Mantra. *Can be vented to cancel it early. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Updraft (★☆☆) |desc=A lifting torrent of wind. |mantratype=Combat Mantra |image=Updraft.gif |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|galebreathe|Wind}} + {{stats|slash|Slash}} |reqs={{c|notes|700}} |effect=''Ready yourself and then spin, creating a vertical column of sharp winds.'' *Has a base damage of 22/24/26/28/30 per level, with successive each hit dealing 35% of the damage of the last (eg 22 -> 7.7 -> 2.7). Has 2.75 Galebreathe scaling. *Deals 7 posture damage per hit (3). *Has a windup of 0.45 seconds with a delay of 0.1 second in between each hit. Has a cooldown of 13 seconds. *Sends opponents flying into the air. }}
===Power 15===
*Matador [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Deal +20% more damage to human enemies with hyperarmor. **Doesn't work on Non-Humanoid [[Monsters]]. *Stratoshock [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Your lightning deals an additional +5% damage when in the rain. **Thundercall damage innately gains a 5% damage buff during rain, with Stratoshock increasing this to +10% damage. *Vacuum Punch [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Your Gale Punch pulls enemies in before you hit them. **Gale punch mantra will now pull players towards the user during the windup of the mantra. (Cannot be feinted) *Windup Battery [Common Talent] '''{{c|notes|100}}''' - Landing 3 Thundercall Mantras without whiffing reduces the windup of your next Mantra by 10%. (+7 Carry Load) **Applies this bonus to non-Thundercall Mantras. *{{cl|oathtlnf|Anchor Shock}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Your Blightshock prevents targets from using mobility mantras. **This puts your opponent's mobility slot Mantras on a 3 second cooldown whenever Blightshock is applied from a Blightsurger Mantra. **This does '''not''' proc on the Blightshock from the Sovereign Bangle weapon. *{{cl|raretl|Static Fakeout}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - Roll cancelling immediately after a parry will cause you to teleport behind your opponent. *{{cl|raretl|Stifled Jump}} [Rare Talent] '''{{c|notes|250}}''' - [[Suffocation|Suffocating]] now applies [[Dazed]] if enemies jump. (+2 Passive Agility) **Similar to the Bear Trap talent, procs Daze when you jump. **The daze effect lasts for 1 second. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Gale Punch (★☆☆) |desc=Form a punch of wind in your fist and release it. |mantratype=Combat Mantra |image=Gale_Punch.gif |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|galebreathe|Wind}} + {{stats|slash|Slash}} |reqs={{c|notes|950}} |effect=''Conjure a wind AoE punch that deals damage and knocks targets away.'' *Has a base damage of 12.5/13.75/15/16.25/17.5 per level, per hit (3) with 2.75 Galebreathe scaling. *Deals 8 posture damage per hit (3). *Has a windup of 0.55 seconds with a 0.7 second windup in between each hit. Has a cooldown of 9.5 seconds. *Can break objects at level 2+. *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s and [[Crystal Lens|Crystal]]/[[Perfect Lens]]es to increase the size and distance respectively. *Can be modified with [[Vibrant Gem]]s to increase the speed of the push, or pull with '''Vacuum Punch'''. *Can be upgraded with the "'''Vacuum Punch'''" Talent, pulling in targets on hit at the cost of 0.1s extra windup. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Sovereign Drive (☆☆☆) |desc=Dash forward in a blink, knocking down enemies in your path. |mantratype=Combat Mantra |image=Soverign drive.gif |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|oath|Oath}} + {{stats|blunt|Blunt}} |reqs={{c|notes|950}} |effect=''Rush forwards and knock down your foe.'' *Has a base damage of 18 with with 1.65 Strength scaling. *Applies Daze and Blightshock on hit. *Knockdowns on hit. }}
===Power 20===
*{{cl|oathtlnf|Blightlash}} [Oath Talent] '''{{c|notes|200}}''' - Your swing range is enhanced during Sovereign State. **Increases the range of the Sovereign Bangle from 6 to 7. {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Lightning Cloak (★★★) |image=Lightning Cloak.gif |desc=A cloak of lightning itself. |ethercost={{stats|ether|20 Ether}} |mantratype=Mobility Mantra |dmgtype=N/A |reqs={{c|notes|1,250}} |effect=''Enveloped in lightning, increase the user's agility, swing speed (+10%), and granting them lightning dashes (long dodges).'' *Has a base duration of 8/8.5/9/9.5/10 seconds per level. *To increase the duration, you must parry, get parried, block, or attack, refreshing the duration entirely. **Lightning cloak has a maximum duration of 60 seconds. *Increases your swing speed by 10% for its full duration. *Grants a 35% speed boost for its full duration, proccing speed boost-reliant Talents (such as "'''Speed Demon'''"). *Turns all dashes into lightning dashes for its full duration, increasing their distance travelled and i-frames duration. *If you have no Tempo, the duration as well as the refreshing duration will be halved, applied retroactively. *If the caster's Ether goes to 0, Lightning Cloak will immediately end. *All '''base''' Ether regeneration is disabled during Lightning Cloak. Ether regeneration from sources like [[Talents]] or [[Outfits]] will still work however. }} {{MantraInfobox|end |name=Rising Thunder (★★★) |image=risingthundergid.gif |desc=Rise up with your opponent and crash down as a bolt of lightning. |ethercost={{stats|ether|70 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|thundercall|Lightning}} |mantratype=Combat Mantra |reqs={{c|notes|1,250}} |effect=''Rush forward quickly with arms charged of lightning, sending the user up into the air and stunning any target(s) hit, user jolts rapidly in the air before crashing down into the ground.'' *Has a base damage of 10+25/11.8+29.5/13.6+34/15.4+38.5/17.2+43 per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 5 posture damage. *0.5s wind-up and completely safeguards user when landed. *15 second cooldown. *Ragdolls target(s). *Can be blocked. }}
==Boss Unlocks==
===Shogun of the Prophet's Guard=== *Brute Strength [Equipment Talent] - Your vent is replaced with a ground slam attack that knocks back enemies. **Deals 35 Blunt damage with 20 Posture damage. **Cannot be buffed through damage modifiers. **Increases your Vent's windup from 0.25s to 0.5s. **Procs all "on Vent" Talents and effects. **This will not stack if you equip an [[Imperator's Fury]] ===Dravik, The Rat King=== *{{cl|mementotlnf|Spark of Theros}} [Memento Talent] - Your Thundercall is imbued with the spark of Theros, altering its appearance and properties. **Turns your Thundercall white. **Changes the Shock status effect to Blightshock, applying [[Wither]] to the target. ***This causes your Electrify to self-apply Wither on use. ===True Heart of Enmity=== Your arms equipment will be forcibly '''replaced''' with a [[Titus's Cape]], voiding your previous arms equipment.
==Trivia== *This Memento originally had Fists as the only allowed weapon type, but was shadow changed to allow Spears and Staffs. *Despite being entirely centered around the [[Thundercall]] and [[Galebreathe]] Attunements, this Memento has 0 Attunement investment. What's stranger, is it also has 5 Songchant, which does almost nothing due to the lack of attunement investment. {{Nav|Mementos}} [[Category:Mementos]]

title: Thief
content:
'''Thieves''' are a [[Enemies|humanoid enemy]] in ''Deepwoken''. {{EnemyInfobox |image1=Thief.png |health=100 |weapon=[[Silver Dagger]] |moves=*Assault *Critical |drops=Lesser [[Mantra Modifiers]] |caption1=empty ur pockets bruv}} ==Description== A Thief (Also known as a bandit assassin) is an enemy NPC that can be found in [[Erisia]] spawning in groups of three. Unlike all other enemies, they don't kill their victims, but steal their money and disappear. A Thief wears a [[Headband|Black Headband]] and the [[Shadow Hunter]] outfit. ==Moveset== Their arsenal only consists of a [[Silver Dagger]]: {| class="fandom-table" !Name/Danger !Description |- |
'''Assault'''
(★☆☆) |Performs 3 basic attacks before sending the opponent away with a flourish. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |- |
'''Critical'''
(★★☆) |Unleashes a quick flurry attack onto their opponent. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |} === Finisher === * Smoke Bomb - Releases a smoke bomb after mugging the player before disappearing. ==Tips== *Be cautious of your blood level during a fight with thieves as daggers can drain your blood very quickly. *Whenever they start to get the upper hand on you, Vent. Thieves, unlike Bandits, can't parry. *Dying to them is not impactful unless other NPCs or players are around, as you are left knocked with only a smaller wallet. ==Trivia== *Despite stealing your money, they still half grip the player, but backing off before the animation finishes. *They can also mug NPCs like the [[Authority Officer]]. {{History}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:Enemies that can wield Enchantments]] [[Category:Bandits]]
