title: Thresher
content:
{{Quotes|quote=[...] It appears these crocodilians were subject to such phenomena, having traded their eyesight for a keen sense of smell and an arsenal of lethal weaponry that has allowed them to flourish following the Tides.|author=Thresher Spine Description'}} {{Monster Infobox |health=1100
2750{{cl|corrupted|(Corrupted)}}
500{{To1Color|(Trial of One)}}
1000(Void)
|spawn_location=*[[Starswept Valley]] *[[Lightkeeper Temple]] *[[The Depths]] *[[Trial of One]] *[[The Diluvian Mechanism]] *[[Saramaed Hollow]] |behavior=Hostile |drops=(Common) *[[Thresher Spine]] *[[Umbral Obsidian]]
(Rare)
*[[Mantra Modifiers]] *[[Thresher Talon]] *[[Serrated Warspear]] ({{cl|corrupted|Corrupted}} and Void only) |attacks=*Talon Swipes *Rending Maul *Tail Sweep *Burrow |image1= File:ThresherNewed.png|Regular Voidthresher.png|Void |challenges= {{Bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}}}} ==Description== The Thresher is a large crocodilian [[Monsters|Monster]] that is commonly found in the [[Starswept Valley]] and [[The Depths]]. It can frequently be found as lone threats on the surface or in trios when spawning as a part of a static event, and more rarely standing alongside the [[King Thresher]]. In The Depths it will always spawn in duos with another Thresher. There are other Thresher variants such as the '''Void Thresher''', located in [[Voidsea]] [[Random Encounters|sea events]], and the [[Nightmare Thresher]], located in the [[Ancient Rotlands]]. When found in the [[Voidsea]], Threshers become Void Threshers, having slightly less health and a more grayscaled appearance as well as having white cracks along their bodies, as a result of the Voidsea's influence. Appearing as a blind crocodilian with large teeth and green scales, they have an incredible sense of smell as well as possessing an arsenal of sharp claws that can easily hunt and kill their prey respectively. They are evidently social creatures as they tend to live in nests, though the density and size of their nests affect the behavior of male Threshers. This leads into a competition between the males, emerging a [[King Thresher|King]] in their stead that leads the pack. Threshers are an ancient species, and the people of [[Aratel Island]] carved charms in their likeness in the past.[[Thresher Charm]] They are not all hostile though, as [[Sordino]], a man found at the [[The Starswept Valley|Starswept Valley]], that has managed to tame some of these Threshers in which you can ride as a [[Mounts|mount]] - provided you have the [[Crowns]] to buy such an elusive beast. ==Attacks== {| class="sortable article-table" !Name/Danger !Description !GIF |- |
'''Talon Swipes'''
(★☆☆) {{AttackTags |slash }}
|The Thresher stands on its hind legs and swipes twice. Deals moderate damage and 15 posture damage. Deals {{cl|bleed|Bleed}} and chips through block. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Thresher Talon Swipes.gif|border|frameless]] |- |
'''Rending Maul'''
(★☆☆) {{AttackTags |slash }}
|The Thresher bites three times in quick succession. The 3rd hit is slightly delayed compared to the animation. Deals moderate damage and 15 posture damage. Deals {{cl|bleed|Bleed}} and chips through block. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Thresher Rending Maul.gif|border|frameless]] |- |
'''Tail Sweep'''
(★★☆) {{AttackTags |blunt }}
|The Thresher brings its tail back and flicks around to deliver a powerful blow that deals moderate damage and 20 posture damage. Attacks following this move come out sooner. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y, jump, ragdoll |type2_color = DarkOrange }} |[[File:Thresher Tail Sweep.gif|border|frameless]] |- |
'''Burrow'''
(★★☆) {{AttackTags |blunt }}
|The Thresher burrows underground to avoid being hit and digs towards the player, jumping out once close enough or after a few seconds and dealing moderate damage. *While burrowed, a red circle effect will flash on where they would normally be, serving as an indicator for their location. *When about to jump out of digging, a purple telegraph will flash, use this to time your defense. *When in [[The Depths]], Threshers will remain burrowed indefinitely, only rising out when they have reached their target. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll }} |[[File:Thresher Burrow.gif|border|frameless]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Serrated Claws''' - Threshers have 100% PEN and inflict Bleed on hit. *'''Thresher Scales''' - Threshers have ~50% Physical attack resistance. *'''Thick Hide''' - {{PAGENAME}}s automatically extinguish [[burn]]. ==Finisher== {| class="fandom-table" ! Name !Description |- |'''Death Rattle''' |Picks the victim up in its mouth and violently shakes it around, tearing them to pieces. This is deceptively quick. |} ==Tips== *When it is using '''Rending Maul''', parry the first attack and then parry the other two using muscle memory. This isn't like the [[Megalodaunt]]'s '''Slash''', meaning you'll have some time to react in between the bites. * If you see it turn around, then it's using its '''Tail Sweep''', and you can wait for around half a second to press block. This will usually parry it and you should be fine. If you accidentally react too quickly and miss the parry window, don't be afraid to roll backwards. You'll usually have enough time to get your roll cooldown back even if it uses '''Burrow'''. **Threshers recover more quickly from their '''Tail Sweep''' than their other moves. Swing one less time to ensure you can avoid the next attack. *When you see it '''Burrow''', it is going to pop up to hit you after an unparriable icon flashes. To avoid this, dodge as soon as you see the first flash. You can also block, although it may deal moderate posture damage. *Although inconsistent and difficult to pull off, you can space yourself with a spear or gun and kite it from outside of its attack range. *If you get hit by its '''Tail Sweep''' attack, press {{Input|keybind|feint}} to quickly get back up. This will allow you to parry its next attack instead of laying on the ground. *Due to it's animations being very janky, it is sometimes recommended for players to zoom into first person to react to attacks such as the bites, being hard to see. *Threshers are very hostile towards [[Stone Knight|Stone Knights]], so if you need to get one off of you, lure it towards them. ==Gallery== File:Thresher concept art.png|Concept art File:Thresher New Model Render.png|New Model Render File:Threshers Model Render.png|Model Render File:ThresherBestiary.png|Bestiary art File:ThresherSwag.png === Legacy === File:Thresher1.png File:Thresher2.png File:Thresher3.png ===Merchandise=== File:Thresher Longboi 1.png|Thresher Longboi Plush File:Thresher Longboi 2.png File:Thresher Longboi 3.png File:Thresher Longboi 4.png File:Thresher Longboi 5.png File:Thresher Longboi 6.png ==Trivia== *You can use [[Thresher Bait]] to spawn Threshers near water, just like Megalodaunt Bait. *Prior to October 1st, 2023, the [[Thresher Spine]] had no description, making it the only [[Monsters|Monster]] drop not to have one. *Originally, no Thresher could swim. If they ended up in the sea they would sink and despawn. ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Monsters}} [[Category:Monsters]]

==Description==
The '''Thresher Longboi''' was a plush released as part of a Deepwoken and Makeship collaboration. Classified under the "longboi" category, it featured the [[Thresher]] mob. Its campaign ran from May 3rd, 2025, to May 10th, 2025, before selling out. The plush measured 12.0 cm in height and 13.0 cm in length. It was made from polypropylene cotton and plush fabric (ultra soft fleece).

<poem style="text-align: center">
"Burrowing crocodilian nightmare from below, the Thresher is here to season your home with a small pinch of terror. And maybe a few handfuls of dirt.

Perfect for those who're always asking "Why can't my draft excluder bite my ankles, too?"

But we're sure you can maybe get some kind of value from this guy, too!"

content:
{{PathfinderEx}} {{NPCInfobox |name=Thula |aspect=Celtor |pronouns=She/her |affiliation=[[The Summer Company]] |location=[[Songseeker Wilds]] |image1=Thula.png}} ==Description== Thula is a [[Celtor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. She is a dragoon of [[The Summer Company]]. Thula is presently in charge of a detachment of dragoons assigned to the [[Songseeker Wilds]] to survey its mines and potential relation to [[the Boundary]]. ==Location== Thula is located in the [[Songseeker Wilds]]. Thula Map.png ==Dialogue== |-|Base Dialogue= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*The Celtor lady is looking over the paper on the small table in front of her, muttering.*'' ...Double-check the measurements, send copies in triplicate, consult Amethyst's findings... ''Trust'' me. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}And why's that? {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}The Etreans sure seem to have left a bunch of their equipment behind. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}It wasn't just due to their faltering political state, and the fact that the minerals started running dry. ''Monsters'' started emerging from the mine in great numbers, attacking the workers - each beast more terrible than the last. In a desperate bid to protect themselves, the Etreans caved some of the mineshafts in. The worst of it stopped, but further operations were deemed too dangerous. {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See first instance] {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}The 'worst' of it? So there's still monsters in there? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*The dragoon sighs.*'' There's still occasional Mudskippers that somehow manage to claw their way past the rubble. Nothing worse than that - but they're still a nuisance. Yet, that can be enough to take out {{g|Pathfinders}} who get caught unaware. That one, by the entryway... Lucien, I think was his name? He says he's lost his friends that way. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Is your crew going to help that guy? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*She seems mildly embarrassed.*'' Uh... Well... We're going to, after we're done with our current task... But, that might take a while.. I won't lie, I do feel bad for him. I think, whenever I have a moment, I might go try clearing them out myself. Shouldn't be that hard. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Best of luck with that, I guess. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Luck? Luck is for rookies. ''*She places a palm on one of her pistols. her expression turning prideful.*'' You don't get to become a Company dragoon through luck. title: Thundercall
content:
{{Quotes|quote=Fury is not a singular emotion. It can be harnessed by the saint and the sinner alike. Do you wish to wield it as a Thundercaller?|author=Funke, Master of Thunder}} [[File:Thundercall.png|thumb|''Thundercall icon'']] ==Description == [[File:Thundercall blade.png|thumb|254x254px|''A Thundercall infused sword'']] '''Thundercall''' is an [[Attunement]] which grants the user the ability to control, conjure and create thunder and electricity, giving them access to abilities which focus on combat, stunning, and movement. Thundercall makes use of a highly unpredictable nature due to its speed and high slow/stun potential. ==PvE Mechanic(s)== Hitting an armor broken [[Monsters|Monster]] with a [[Thundercall]] Mantra will extend the stun, with the increased stun duration scaling on your Thundercall investment. At 100 Thundercall, this doubles the armor break stun for default Thundercall, and increases it by 50% for Surge Path Thundercall. This can only be applied once per armor break. The {{status|Electrified}} status effect lasts twice as long on PvE enemies. ==Obtainment== The [[Sparkblood]] Potion can be obtained by giving [[Funke]], the Thundercall trainer located inside the [[Summer Isle#The Castle|Summer Isle Castle]] two [[Spark Gland]]s. Alternatively, you can simply select Thundercall as your starting Attunement in Character Creation. ==Training== {{text|att-training |train=using the [[Self-Conducting Loop]] to increase the attribute after either landing {{PAGENAME}} Mantras or eating [[Spark Gland]]s to gain enough EXP |trainer=[[Funke]] at [[Summer Isle]] }} ===Mantra Damage Calculation=== {{text|mantracalc}} ==Cantrip(s)== Cantrips are, often minor, passive abilities that are granted upon obtaining any Mantra from the respective Attunement. ===Produce Spark=== This Cantrip allows the player to light [[Campfire]]s without [[Flint]]. This Cantrip is shared with [[Flamecharm]], though the sound effect differs based on the attunement. File:Produce Spark.gif {{col|sec|

Mantras

}} ===Combat Mantras=== {{MantraInfobox|newtable |name=Jolt Grab (☆☆☆) |image=Jolt grab.gif |desc=An electrified chokehold. |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=1 Thundercall |effect=''Dash forwards with the character's left hand charged with lightning; if a target is hit, slam them into the ground before sending out a small AoE around the user.'' *Deals 20/22/24/26/28 base damage per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *[[Magnet Spark]] variant deals 25/27/29/31/33 base damage per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 5 posture damage regardless of spark variant. *Magnet Spark variant has a windup of 0.5 seconds. *Has a 10 second cooldown. *Shares a cooldown with all other [[grab Mantras]]. *Can be modified with a [[Magnet Spark]], causing the user to perform a short wind-up while charging their left hand with lightning before teleporting to a nearby target while dealing a shocking AoE. **Magnet Spark variant activates only when the cursor is locked onto a target. **Knockdown is removed from the Magnet variant. *Jolt Grab can be modified with [[Crystal Lens|Crystal]]/[[Perfect Lens]]es to increase the distance travelled/AoE hitbox. Jolt Grab Magnet Spark.gif|Magnet Spark }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Lightning Beam (☆☆☆) |image=Lightning_Beam.gif |desc=Fire a beam of lightning. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=1 Thundercall |effect=''Cast out a straight beam of lightning from where the character is facing.'' *Deals 30/31.5/33/34.5/36 base damage per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 7/8.5/10/11.5/13 posture damage per level. *10 second cooldown. *Has 0.43 seconds of wind-up. *Can break objects. *Can grant an optional effect with the {{t|Shocking Finish}} Talent, in which Lightning Beam is instantly castable after flourishing an enemy, pretty much guaranteeing a hit after flourish. *Shares a cooldown with [[Ice Beam]]. }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Lightning Blade (☆☆☆) |image=Lightning_blade.gif |desc=Arcing blades of electricity. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=1 Thundercall |effect=''Dash forward before performing two slashes, sending out 2 short-ranged arcs of lightning forward that pierce through targets.'' *Initial hits deal 7/8/9/10/11 base damage per level, per hit (2) with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *The [[Magnet Spark]] variant adds an additional hit that deals 8.75/10/11.25/12.5/13.75 base damage per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Stormcaller Slash deals an additional 12.25/14/15.75/17.5/19.25 base damage per level with 5 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 3 posture damage per initial hit (2), Stormcaller Slash adds an additional 5 posture damage. *10 second cooldown. *Has 0.35 seconds of wind-up. *The arcs can completely phase through an enemy if you cast it too close to them, therefore mind the spacing. *Can be cancelled midway after the first 2 slashes by right-clicking. *At end of Mantra, performs a "'''Stormcaller Slash'''", a former Talent which is now innate. **Can be canceled by feinting right after the flash of lightning. This puts the Mantra on cooldown for 5 seconds. *Can be modified with a [[Magnet Spark]], which causes the mantra perform an additional short-ranged teleporting slash immediately after the first two. File:Lightning Blade Magnet Spark.gif|Magnet Spark }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Electro Carve (★☆☆) |image=Electro_carve.gif |desc=Produce a highly potent field of electromagnetism, shocking all inside. |ethercost={{stats|ether|55 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=20 Thundercall |effect=''Conjure a shocking orb from the end of your weapon, dealing rapid damage.'' *Deals 8/8.5/9/9.5/10 base damage per level, per hit (7) with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *The Blast Spark variant has a base damage of 7/7.5/8/8.5/9 per level, per hit (9) with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *The Magnet Spark variant has a base damage of 10 (flat) + 7/7.5/8/8.5/9 per level, per hit (7) with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 1 posture damage per hit (7, 9 if Blast Spark). *The Magnet Spark variant's initial hit deals no posture damage. *10 second cooldown. *Projectile moves along where the character is facing. *Shocks opponents inside of it while dealing damage. *{{text|slowturn}} *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s to increase the AoE. However, this will reduced the Mantra's damage. *Can be modified with a [[Blast Spark]] to conjure up a shocking AoE around the user. *Can be modified with a [[Magnet Spark]] to deploy a sticky projectile to a target that activates the shock after around 3 seconds. *The '''base damage''' of this Mantra is increased by 15% if you are wearing the full [[:Category:Equipment with Set Bonuses|Specialist Set]]. Additionally, it will become a green color. File:Electro Carve Blast Spark.gif|Blast Spark File:Electro Carve Magnet Spark.gif|Magnet Spark }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Fleeting Sparks (★☆☆) |image=Fleeting Sparks.gif |desc=Call forth motes of electricity that seek out your foes. |ethercost={{stats|ether|60 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=20 Thundercall |effect=''Perform a gesture, conjuring 3 orbs of lightning above and beside the user before sending them towards target(s).'' *Has a base damage of 5/6.5/8/9.5/11 per level, per hit (3) with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *Deals 5 posture damage per hit (3). *14 second cooldown. *Shared a cooldown with [[Ice Daggers]]. *Can be modified with a [[Multiplying Spark]] to double the amount of projectiles conjured, but halve the damage and posture damage per projectile. *Can be modified with a [[Magnet Spark]] making the projectiles home towards the target and removing the beams of thunder. File:Fleeting Sparks Multiplying Spark.gif|Multiplying Spark File:Fleeting Sparks Magnet Spark.gif|Magnet Spark File:Fleeting Sparks Multiplying Spark + Magnet Spark.gif|Both Sparks }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Lightning Clones (★☆☆) |image=Lightning clone.gif |desc=Replicated forms of yourself conjured from electricity. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=20 Thundercall |effect=''Perform a short wind-up before snapping fingers to summon a clone of lightning beside the user, the clone proceeds to attack a nearby target once before disappearing.'' *Clones deal 125% of your weapon's base damage on hit. Having a Blast Spark reduces this to 100% of your weapon's base damage. *Blast Spark will make your clone deal an additional 12/15/18/21/24 base damage per level in an AoE upon hitting a target. *15 second cooldown. *If summoned while there are no nearby target(s), it will attack the first enemy to deal damage the user or the first target the user deals damage to. *Can grant a different effect with the {{t|Static Flash Clone}} Talent, which causes the mantra to summon a clone briefly as an afterimage before disappearing, granting the user a small speed boost and making them invisible for a short period of time before resurfacing from invisibility. **When used with the [[Blast Spark]] mantra variant, the clone conjures a '''Lightning Strike''' when it disappears. *Only 6 clones can exist at a time. *Modifying the mantra with [[Aeon Logstone|Aeon]]/[[Eternal Logstone]]s ''increases the health'' and amount of time the clones are active. Note that while their health is increased they still die after dealing 1 hit. **The health modifications do not affect the second clone if a Multiplying Spark is used. **With 3 Aeon & Eternal Longstones the clones will last for 80 seconds. **The health modifiers are disabled if more than 2 clones are spawned. *Can be modified with a [[Blast Spark]] to cause the clone to detonate and shock upon hitting a target/death. *Can be modified with a [[Multiplying Spark]] to summon an additional clone. File:Lightning Clones Blast Spark.gif|Blast Spark File:Lightning Clones Multiplying Spark.gif|Multiplying Spark File:Lightning Clones Multiplying Spark Blast Spark.gif|Both Sparks Lightning Clones Static Flash Clone.gif|Static Flash Clone Lightning Clones Static Flash Clone Blast Spark.gif|Static Flash Clone with Blast Spark }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Lightning Impact (★☆☆) |image=Lightning_Impact.gif |desc=Slam those under you with a lightning empowered kick. |ethercost={{stats|ether|80 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=20 Thundercall |effect=''Leap into the air before slamming down into the ground, dealing moderate Lightning damage in an AoE before ascending the user and target(s) hit into the air.'' *Has a base damage of 23/24.5/26/27.5/29 per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. *The ''Rain of Static'' Talent adds an additional 5/5.375/5.75/6.125/6.5 base damage per level, per hit (4) at the start of the Mantra. *Deals ?/?/?/?/? posture damage per level. *Rain of Static hits deal 1 posture damage each (4). *12 second cooldown. *Can destroy surfaces and light flammable terrain such as patches of grass on fire. *Applies Knockdown. *Can grant a different effect with the {{t|Rain of Static}} Talent, which makes the user rain down orbs of lightning from the air before slamming down. *Can proc {{t|Meteor Impact}} Lightning Impact Rain of Static.gif|Rain of Static }} {{MantraInfobox |name=Lightning Strike (★☆☆) |image=Lightning Strike.gif |desc=A strike of thunder at your desired location. |ethercost={{stats|ether|50 Ether}} |dmgtype={{stats|ltn|Lightning}} |reqs=20 Thundercall |effect=''Perform a gesture before conjuring strikes of lightning at the cursor's location, dealing moderate damage.'' *Deals 5/6/7/8/9 base damage per level with 2.75 Thundercall scaling. These damage values scale down the more duration modifiers you have on the Mantra. *Deals 3.15 posture per hit. *Has a 10 second cooldown. *The first hit applies knockdown. *Can be cancelled at any point by clicking. **This includes being hit by the user's own Lightning Strike. (they removed the self damage in a shadow patch) *Can be modified with [[Cloudstone|Cloud]]/[[Stratus Stone]]s to increase the hitbox of the projectiles. *Can be modified with [[Aeon Logstone|Aeon]]/[[Eternal Logstone]]s to increase the number of strikes. Works on Surge stacks that weren't applied by you. Does not work on Surge stacks applied to yourself. |- |} ==Trivia== *All Thundercall damage receives a 5% damage buff when it is [[rain]]ing. {{cl|ltn|Stratoshock}} further increases this damage buff to 10%. *Out of all Attunements, Thundercall has the most color variants (5). **This includes: default Thundercall's yellow, Surge Path's blurple, [[Theros Disciple]]'s white, [[:Category:Equipment with Set Bonuses|Specialist Set]]'s green, and [[the Ferryman]]'s pink. *{{cl|ltn|'''Electro Carve'''}} was formerly a 0-star mantra. *{{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Strike'''}} prints out the coordinates of where the strike was in the F9 log. This means that you can use {{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Strike'''}} as a makeshift or bootleg compass. *{{cl|ltn|'''Bolt Piercer'''}} was formerly a "legendary" Mantra, being much rarer than it is now. *{{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Cloak'''}} used to be named '''Vanishing Cloak'''.[[File:Vanishing_Cloak.png]] *In the book Our Fortress, Vincent Zeneke notes that the Thundercaller's use of the Canjolin instrument spawned a method of overdrive. **Linking music theory, the use of overdrive is made to alter the sound of an electrical instrument.[[File:Grand Javelin fixed.gif|thumb]] *The Mantra {{cl|ltn|'''Grand Javelin'''}} is similar to the Miracle '''''[https://darksouls.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning+Spear Lightning Spear]''''' from ''[https://darksouls.wiki.fextralife.com/Dark+Souls+Wiki Dark Souls]'', having a shared sound effect and casting animation. *The Mantra {{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Beam'''}} is likely a reference to ''[https://dragonball.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Page Dragon Ball Z's]'' technique ''[https://dragonball.fandom.com/wiki/Masenko "Masenko" (魔閃光,Masenkō)]'', which is performed by the user placing both hands above the head with the palms facing the target and one hand in front of the other with the fingers going in opposite directions, similiarly to {{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Beam'''}}. *In Deepwoken testing, known as Oldwoken, Thundercall used to be blue instead of yellow. Even with the addition of Surge Path, the original color is still lost to the ages. **Surge is a more purple shade compared to Oldwoken Thundercall, which was a light blue. *Thundercall used to be the most damaging attunement before it was nerfed greatly. *{{cl|ltn|'''Rising Thunder'''}} is a reference to Kakashi's Raikiri: Sōraishin from the videogame ''Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm''. *{{cl|ltn|'''Lightning Impact'''}} with the "{{cl|ltn|Rain Of Static}}" Talent, allows the user to lower their elevation by sliding, making the windup on their slam way shorter but at the same time keeping them at an unsafe level. The user can also increase their elevation off the ground through by any means such as aerial combos or hopping off a wall to make the wind-up on their slam longer, not letting opponents auto-parry it due to parrying the projectiles. *Similarly to every other Wisp mantra,{{cl|ltn| '''Thunder Wisp'''}} gives the player a finger on the hand that casts the mantra *During the early days of Deepwoken, {{cl|ltn|Grand Skewer}} was notorious for a bug that allowed it to instantly kill whatever it hit if an entity was already stuck on it. This often occurred when the already-skewered victim died. Dying to this bug would take lives in the overworld and wipe you in [[The Depths]], and it was fixed a little over two months after the game's release. **For this reason, [[Legion Sniper]]s were considered to be fairly dangerous when fought as a group. *{{cl|ltn|'''Emotion Wave'''}} is a direct reference to the [https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ancient+Dragons'+Lightning+Strike '''''Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike'''''] incantation from [https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden+Ring+Wiki ''Elden Ring'']. It also possibly gets its name from Lightning Style: Emotion Wave. Shown in Naruto Shippuden Episode 202. **'''Emotion Wave''' also had it's PvE scale nerfed, a total of three times. *Thundercall is needed for every [[oaths|Oath]] that requires an [[attunement]], those being: [[Oath: Arcwarder|Arcwarder]], [[Oath: Blightsurger|Blightsurger]] and [[Oath: Saintsworn|Saintsworn]]. *It is said by [[Neero]] that Thundercall can "power" golems to "give life" to them. *The [[Railblade]] was originally intended to be a legendary weapon for this attunement. *Before the Perfect Cast mechanic was removed, {{cl|ltn|'''Jolt Grab'''}} and [[Flame Grab]] were among very few abilities and the only Mantras to have an innate unique interaction with it. When Perfect Casted, the duration of these Mantras would be shortened and capped, playing "extinguish"-like VFX unique from the regular version. **A video summarizing this effect can be found [https://youtu.be/o3AJne5Y04U?si=Jzim_sMEg3q-qTkX here]. [[File:Grandjavelin.mp4|thumb|176x176px|left|none|Virudhaka's Sword]] [[File:Javelinsound.mp4|thumb|none|left|Sound from Occult A+B]] {{clear}} ==References== {{Nav|Attunements}} [[Category:Attunement]]

==Description==
The {{PAGENAME}} is an [[NPC]] located in a small cave on the northern side of [[Boatman's Watch]]. It must be located and interacted with, along with [[Saintsworn Obelisks|4 other element-based obelisks]], to obtain the [[Saintsworn]] [[Oath]].

It can only be interacted with if you have at least 15 [[Thundercall]]. When interacted with, [[Tessa]], the Hero of Lightning, will speak to the player.

==Description==
Tideknights can only be found within the later waves of [[The Diluvian Mechanism]].

They wear the [[Celtorian Tideknight]] Outfit and have a wide array of weapons, Mantras, and Oaths. Every Tideknight NPC in the mechanism is a variant of an already existing hostile NPC, being any of the four Songseeker variants, [[Black Diver (NPC)|Black Divers]], Starkindred Angels, [[Iblis, The Fallen Angel]] and all six of the [[Spelltrainers]].

==Moveset==
Tideknights contain the same moveset as the following NPCs depending on their variant. 

* [[Songseeker Galebreather]]
* [[Songseeker Thundercaller]]
* [[Songseeker Flamecharmer]]
* [[Songseeker Frostdrawer]]
* [[Black Diver (NPC)|Black Diver]]
* [[Nell, Master of Frost]]
* [[Friid, Master of Gale]]
* [[Amashi, Master of Flame]]
* [[Nostor, Master of Shadow]]
* [[Funke, Master of Thunder]]
* [[Adar, Master of Metal]]
* [[Iblis, The Fallen Angel]]
* [[Astaroth, Sinner of Wind]]

==Trivia==
*They share the same armor with the [[Celtorian Guard|Celtorian Guards]].
*It is unknown who or what they're supposed to be. Perhaps they could have been stronger, deadlier guards that patrolled Celtor before the Great Drowning.

title: Timeline
content:
{{Outdated}} {{Cleanup}} {{Quotes|quote=so weep for ash, and weep for ruin -
for embers fade, and swells the sea.
hold on to hope, and in so doing
beware - the Tide comes too for thee.|author=To Sleep, Dreaming (Contour 4) Description}} == Description == This page presents a possible reconstruction of the timeline of events that occurred within the world of Deepwoken. ==Old World== This section of the timeline does not have a specific year range. Historians believe that it predates the "The Tides" and the concept of measuring time through years. ===Historical Context=== Before the arrival of the Tides, most of the land was populated by a variety of animals, including domesticated, predatory, and livestock species. In addition, animals were not only used for their resources but also served as means of transportation.Sourced from Bookkeeper Andros dialogue; In the present world, there are five major landmasses, but during the era of the Old World, the Luminants were predominantly interconnected, with the World's Edge delineating its outer limits. The World's Edge, now known as the Voidsea, proved to be impassable at all times.More can be found in the book: Studies on Canticlysm, Vol. IV Alongside this, a currency systemSourced from Mr. Quarters; predating notes relied on coins, with quarters serving as a measurement unit. Another trace from the Old World are the Old TextsBookkeeper Andros is in possession of a book left by his grandfather, one of the Old Stewards and keeper of the knowledge of the Old World, which comprise a collection of historical records inscribed in glyphs or preserved within books. However, their existence in the current world remains uncertain, concealed in mystery and the passage of time - keepers of knowledge known as Old Stewards may be in possession of such vestiges and further knowledge about the Old World. It is believed that some pieces of this collection are housed within The Condemned Archives, a forbidden repository which texts were once deemed too dangerous for common consumption. The exact location of the Archives remains unknown, and it appears intentional that we are not meant to discover its whereabouts.Description of the 1v1 arena map: ''"A forbidden store of Old World texts once deemed to be too dangerous for common consumpton, now laid bare for profiteers."''; On a more enigmatic note, the origin of the Adret aspect is intriguing and sets them apart from other aspects in the world, as they do not share any animal characteristics like the Felinors with cats, Canors with dogs or Vesperians with beetles. This distinction is a primary point of contention for many aspects, who view the Adrets as unfamiliar and alien. It is important to note that the Adret aspect is not associated with fish either.According to Ishan, an Etrean man located in the Stronghold within the Summer Isles, the appearance of the Adrets seemed sudden and unexpected. It is believed that historically they had a tendency to be isolationist, dwelling in the mountainous regions and rarely interacting with other aspects until the advent of the Tides. However, with their tallest mountains now submerged, the Adrets have emerged into the wider world. ===Pre-Canticlysm Period=== During this period, mankind made the discovery of the Song and gradually refined its utilization into a vague yet powerful force. Nonetheless, its application remained limited and infrequent. As a result, cultural practices and techniques revolving around the Song, as we now understand them, had not yet been created or extensively researched. ==The Canticlysm== ===Arrival of The Canticlysm=== As the utilization of the Song grows and understanding of it deepens, it culminated and reached its peak during a distinct period referred to as The Canticlysm. This period, often referred to as the Golden Age of the Song, is renowned for its supposed peace and tranquility and characterized by remarkable innovation. During this transformative era, significant advancements lead to the creation of the four primary attunements known as [[Flamecharm]], [[Frostdraw]], [[Thundercall]], [[Galebreathe]], and the newly emerging attunement called [[Ironsing]]. The formation and development of Ironsing began after the discovery of pluripotent alloys, marking a significant milestone in the understanding and manipulation of metallic objects.Sourced from the description of Pluripotent Alloy: ''"[...] The discovery of the Pluripotent Alloys is said to have sparked the development of Ironsing during the Canticlysm."'' Additionally, legendary weapons of rare and mysterious nature, such as the Crypt Blade and the Curved Blade of Winds, are said to have been forged, along with many others whose existence remains shrouded in mystery. It is believed that, despite how it seems the four primary Attunements were created during the Canticlysm, that they, [[Shadowcast]], and other Attunements possibly, were actually merely discovered, as they seem to come from the Drowned Gods and be inherent to the Song, however other Attunements were created by mankind, artificial to the Song, such as Lifeweave, [[Bloodrend]] and Ironsing. ==The Tides== An event that happened near the end of The Canticlysm and continued a few years afterwards, it was called the first Great Drowning. Its cause was the Drowned Gods, who were almost woken up by the overuse of The Song. They exerted their power over Lumen, corrupting the Sea. This caused immense destruction, dividing the world into the 5 Luminants. Alongside this, they caused the Voidfog to be drawn to the Sea, merging them into the Voidsea. Raging on, it led to the formation of [[the Ministry]]. The tides ended with the Great Drowning of Celtor, in which the Celtorian Horror dragged The City of Celtor underwater and into the first layer of [[The Depths]] - [[First Layer|Scyphozia]]. It caused [[Moonseye (symbol)|The Moonseye]], a symbol of the afterlife, to be replaced with the Depths; When you die, rather than ascending, you now [[Death|drown]], taken into the depths. Escape is only possible through the [[First Layer#Escaping First Layer|Depths trial]] or by making [[Shrine of Yun'Shul, Keeper of Hearts|a wish]], but doing so will pull you back in eventually due to the pull on your soul, but certain rituals can negate this effect. ==The Resurgence/The New World== The Resurgence is the period of time we're currently in. It is when mankind started to adapt to the calamities brought by the Tides. It's said to have started sometime in the fifth century BCE. It's referred to as a dying world by the game's description. ==Footnotes==

You also highlight enemy health whenever you hit them during your rage. This can only be activated while under 50% health and has a 3-minute cooldown. It is highly recommended that you farm [[Elder Primadon]] over regular [[Primadon]] for the better drop rates. *Although activating Primal Rage drains your ether bar, it does not share the same 100% ether requirement as {{t|Ardour Scream}}. **[[49th Legion]] |image1=TitusStanding.png |title1=Titus Fulminus Destellus |challenges={{bi|{{PAGENAME}}|small}}}} ==Description== '''Titus Fulminus Destellus''' is an instanced [[Bosses|Boss]] fought and contained at the [[Merit Detainment Core]] within the [[Map:Eastern Luminant|Eastern Luminant's]] [[Fort Merit]]. He was the commander of the [[49th Legion]] and a user of the [[Blightsurger]] [[Oath]] before being captured by [[The Central Authority]] for the sake of strategy.{{Ref/Book|Legion Intelligence|quote=A CHALLENGING DECISION HAS BEEN TAKEN TO DELAY YOVR FREEDOM IN FAVOVR OF THE IMPROVEMENT OF OVR STRATEGIC ODDS.}} A Khan with great stature, he's around twice the height of the player. He has darkened yellow eyes and wrinkles across his face, signifying his older age. Titus wields the [[Worldpiercer Gauntlets]] and wears the [[Titus's Raiment]] with his [[Titus's Cape]]. He also carries a bell on his hip, signifying that he is strong enough to have obtained a [[Resonance]]. His sheer size creates a physical resilience against attacks, but is also mentally resilient as well.{{Ref/NPC|High Inquisitor Merey|quote=He's rather physically and mentally resilient. (...) In fact the shocks only seem to invigorate him. And, his astonishingly high pain threshold makes it difficult to apply most other methods.}} Alongside this, he had a unrivaled, strategic mind, allowing him to catch The Authority off-guard, and even survive when outnumbered.{{Ref/NPC|Sentinel Augustus|quote=He'd catch us in ambushes, set traps for us, and always be three steps ahead of us. When outnumbered, he would often survive just through sheer strength and discipline. I couldn't stand it.}} Upon his capture, he intentionally let his guard down to get captured by [[Sentinel Augustus]], for the sake of gathering intel within the confines of the Authority.{{Ref/NPC|Sentinel Augustus|quote=But... Something was off, when we fought in Aratel. I can't put my finger on it. It felt like he wasn't giving it his all.}}{{Ref/NPC|Caitus|quote=Rumour has it he was meant to gather intel from the inside, then break out - or be broken out. Some say it was meant to be some sort of pincer attack on Merit.}} Titus was expected to retire after a few missions prior to his capture, but may have given up on it after receiving the message from the player.{{Ref/NPC|Caitus|quote=He was supposed to retire after his final few missions, including this one... Guess he's thrown that straight into the sea.}} ===Initiating the Fight with Titus=== #Have high 'Ally' or above reputation with [[The Hundred Legions]]. #Speak with [[Caitus]] at the Legion camp at [[Lower Erisia]] to obtain the [[Legion Intelligence]] quest item. #Having the Legion Intelligence or [[Imperium Kata]] will unlock a unique set of dialogue with Titus. Selecting it will start the fight. Rep for Caitus.png|Required reputation needed to obtain Legion Intelligence ==Moves== {| class="fandom-table" !Name !Description !Media |- |
'''The Legion's Martial Arts'''
(★☆☆) |Titus firmly swings his fists at his opponent with hyperarmor. *These moves are typically slow and can often lead to the player missing a parry. *Because he has the effect of Commander's Rage and throughout the entire second phase, this attack becomes Unparryable being telegraphed. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} | |- |
'''Vent
(Brute Strength)'''
(★☆☆) |Titus quickly slams down both arms into the ground, knocking players away with a powerful vent. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.y, dodge.y }} |[[File:Titus Vent Slam.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Worldpiercing Deluge'''
(★★☆) |Titus winds up with both arms and smashes them into the ground, causing three consecutive shockwaves that send players high into the air. *This attack must be avoided by jumping. *Titus is most likely to follow up with Warp Kick if landed, which can be very problematic if you're ragdolled. {{AttackTags |indicator = jump |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, jump,ragdoll |type2_color=darkred }} |[[File:Titus Shockwave but clearer.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Worldshattering Smackdown'''
(★★☆) |Titus winds up with both arms, grabbing the opponent before smacking them into the ground. *This move is very similar to Worldpiercing Deluge, in which it shares the same animation. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.n, dodge.n, grab |telegraph=parry}} |[[File:Titus Cripple.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Commander's Rage'''
(★★☆) |Titus unleashes an echoing roar that temporarily amplifies his attacks. * This move can cause debris to fall. {{AttackTags |parry.y, block.n, dodge.n |telegraph=parry}} |[[File:Titus Angry.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Commander's Whirlthrow'''
(★★★) |Titus firmly grabs his opponent, spins around, and sends them flying. *Almost always leads to Warp Kick if Titus lands this move. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, ragdoll, autogrip, grab }} |[[File:Titus Throw.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Splitting Ascension'''
(★★★) |Titus ascends into the air, crashing into the ground and knocking down opponents. {{AttackTags |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, knockdown }} |[[File:Titus Ascension.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Sovereign Drive'''
(★★☆)
|Titus dashes forward in a blink, briefly ragdolling enemies in its path. *This move may be used twice or more. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, ragdoll }} |[[File:Titus Drive.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Skycrash'''
(★★☆) |Titus leaps towards their opponent, stomping and knocking them away when hit. *This move may be used twice or more. *When amplified by Commander's Rage or in second phase, Titus will use Skycrash again if he does not hit anyone initially *This move will briefly stun him if he bashes into a surface. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, knockdown, jump }} |[[File:Titus SkyCrash.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Warp Kick'''
(★★☆) |In a flash, Titus warps to a random opponent and kicking them away. *This move is most commonly used when the player is far away from him, especially if he landed moves like Commander's Whirlthrow or Worldshattering Smackdown. *This move may be used twice or more, and is more dangerous as the player will be constantly ragdolled and Dazed. *This move is technically dodgeable, however, it is only possible at the very last moments of the attack. It's advised to block the attack instead dealing 10.46 posture. {{AttackTags |indicator = block |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, ragdoll |type2_color=darkorange }} |[[File:Titus Warp Kick.gif|thumb]] |- | |Attacks unlocked in phase 2 | |- |

(★☆☆) |Titus slowly winds up before releasing a stomp that sends opponents into the air. *This move can be easily avoided by jumping. *Titus will only use this move in his second phase. *sends those hit very high up. {{AttackTags |indicator = dodge |parry.n, block.n, dodge.y, jump,ragdoll |type2_color=darkred }} |[[File:Titus Wrathful Stomp.gif|thumb]] |- |

(★★☆)
|Titus summons three orbs of white lightning that lock onto the nearest opponent. If they are struck by this, they will be held in the air for a short time. *This move is easy to avoid if you run back or dash back. {{AttackTags |indicator = highposture |parry.n, block.y, dodge.y, autogrip |type2_color=darkorange |type3_color=darkorange }} |[[File:Titus Bala.gif|thumb]] |- |
'''Chorus Divide: Shattering Crescendo'''
(★★☆) |Titus channels his bell into two high-pressure beams of wind in a 360 degree motion. Those who are hit by the beams will be ragdolled and flung at a considerable distance. *This move can cause debris to fall. *These beams are combined with the [[Wind-Up]] blasts per hit, making this move '''very deadly'''. *While he is winding up, it is best to start running or getting to higher levels to avoid the beams. *You can counter this by using [[Attunement-less|prediction]] requiring the talent [[Talents|successive prediction]] {{AttackTags |indicator = avoid |parry.n, block.n, dodge.n }} |[[File:Titus Divide.gif|thumb]] |} ===Passives=== *'''Enough with Restraint''' - Upon reaching 50% of his health, Titus will initiate a cutscene, healing to 60% in the process and advancing to the next phase. For a brief moment, the Detainment Core will shake, causing debris to collapse from the ceiling. He will also be in Sovereign state for the rest of the fight. **The fact that he heals his health to 60% upon advancing to the next phase can be problematic when using [[Poser's Ring]] or [[Moppet]] since he'll, unlike other boses, heal up to 60% instead of having a small remainder of health upon other miscalculations of how much damage you've done. *'''Weakling Beater''' - Titus will deal extra damage to NPCs in the Detainment Core. *'''Commander's Respite''' - Titus will begin regenerating health when not actively engaged in combat. *'''Thorn Guard''' - Titus is immune to the effects of [[Providence's Thorns]]. *'''Unharvestable''' - Healing from [[Bloodless Gem]]s are less effective. ===Talents=== *Brute Strength - Titus' vent is replaced with a ground slam attack that knocks back enemies. *Blight Pierce - While Titus is in sovereign state his attacks will interrupt attacks through hyperarmor. ===Finishers=== * Despite lacking a proper execution animation, Titus will use Commander's Whirlthrow to quickly execute knocked opponents. ==Battle== ==Tips and Strategies== *'''Utilizing Guards for Healing''': The guards in the main cell block can be used as a source of healing. However, be aware that Titus can eliminate them with a single blow before even having a chance to deal enough damage to receive a healing orb. They also do not respawn, so this is a one-time opportunity. *'''Second Phase Transition Healing''': During the brief dialogue sequence as Titus transitions into his second phase, there is a small window that can be used to place a campfire down and recover health. *'''Vampirism Enchantment''': An enchanted weapon with '''Vampirism''' is highly effective in this fight. This is because it grants temporary health rather than an outright heal, which allows the effects of '''Blightsurge Wither''' to be bypassed. *'''Evading Chorus Divide''': Titus' '''Chorus Divide''' attack can be easily avoided by gaining elevation. Climbing onto the generator or the scaffolding near the walls will provide a safe haven from this ability. *'''Second Phase M1 Attack''': It is important to note that his standard M1 attack now has a '''Dodge Only''' Telegraph. *'''General Strategy''': As a general rule, do not overcommit to attacks. Focus on maintaining defense and punishing his attacks rather than forcing openings. It is often more valuable to use healing items and regenerate consistently than to risk taking damage in a risky trade. Stay mobile and use mantras for ranged damage when necessary. *'''Prediction''': If you land a [[Prediction]] on Titus's '''Chorus Divide: Shattering Crescendo''' it will deal approximately 15000 damage which helps out plenty when fighting him. '''This strategy requires a good understanding of Titus' abilities and timings. Miss the timing and you will pay a hefty price.''' ==Rewards== Titus drops a variety of unique items that cannot be found elsewhere. You are guaranteed to get 1 [[Wrath Gem]] and [[Might Gem]] for every time you defeat Titus Fulminus Destellus. In addition to his unique chest (see below for the table), an additional chest is rewarded for each participating player, dropping at their feet. This chest can include: *[[Weapons]]: [[Imperator's Edge|{{cl|mythical|Imperator's Edge}}]], [[Imperial Staff|{{cl|mythical|Imperial Staff}}]], [[Summer Hullwrecker]]. *[[Relics]]: [[Armorer's Needle|{{cl|relic|Armorer's Needles}}]], [[Moonseye Tome|{{cl|relic|Moonseye Tomes}}]], [[Smith's Alloy|{{cl|relic|Smith's Alloys}}]], [[Idol of Yun'Shul|{{cl|relic|Idol of Yunshul}}]], [[Stone|{{cl|relic|Stone}}]] and [[Storm|{{cl|relic|Storm}}]] [[Enchant Stone|{{cl|relic|Enchant Stones}}]]. *[[Items]]: [[Deep Gems]], [[Gale Stone]]s.

==Gallery== File:Titus.png|[https://x.com/Deepwoken/status/1929026679181017536 Teaser image] File:TitusBack2.png|Titus' back (standing) File:TitusFace.png|Titus' face File:Titus2.png File:TitusBack.png File:TitusDowned3.png|Titus being downed in his first phase File:TitusDowned.png|Titus being downed in his second phase ==Trivia== *Titus' name is actually a little fudged, neither "Fulminus" nor "Destellus" exist within classical Latin literature as words, and instead appear to be loosely based on existing Latin root words and existing agnomen/victory titles of famous Roman generals. **The name Destellus is based on the Latin word destellar, a verb meaning "to sparkle" or "to twinkle", deriving further from stella, the noun for star, or stellare, a verb for, roughly, "to cover with stars". **The other name, Fulminus, likely references the Latin verb "fulminare," literally "to cause/strike like lightning" but more poetically it could mean "thundering". **And of course, "Titus Juventius" is somewhat close to what an actual Latin name could be, signifying "Titus the young (adult)," but the more classically accurate name would be "Titus Iuvenis" or "Juvenis", given that it is an alternate spelling of the former. *Titus uses a unique variant of the [[Chorus Divide]] [[Resonance]], which is combined with [[Wind-Up|Wind-Up's]] blasts per hit. *The placeholder name "Franky Strabes" will appear on Titus' combat tag. *The theme that plays during his fight is [[Chainbreaker]]. *It is implied that Titus uses both [[Galebreathe]] and [[Thundercall]] due to the variant of his [[Chorus Divide]] being Galebreathe as well with [[High Inquisitor Merey]] stating that shocking him with Thundercall only makes him stronger. *Strangely enough, unlike other bosses, Titus does not drop [[Pluripotent Alloy]] nor [[Ardour Manifestation]] and doesn't count in the bestiary under normal circumstances. **This is because Titus does not actually die nor despawn when you defeat him most of the time. If you do manage to autogrip him however, he will appropriately grant these rewards. *Titus second phase can be bypassed when the player uses [[Poser's Ring]] (if quick enough) or the [[Moppet]] weapon. When this happens, a loot chest will drop and Titus' health will fall to zero. He will then enter his second phase animation and his health will return, but he will stay completely docile and will not attack the player. Killing him again will not give any extra loot. *The windup for Warp kick matches the windup of the critical for the [[Imperium Kata]] ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Bosses}} [[Category:Enemies]] [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:Bosses]] [[Category:Enemies with Oaths]] [[Category:The Hundred Legions Enemies]] [[Category:Humanoids with Unobtainable Outfits]]

{{PathfinderEx}} {{Quotes|quote=This is what people with muscles do, right? Eat rocks, push boulders... Y'know?|author=Tolkat}} {{NPCInfobox |title1=Tolkat |image1=Tolkat.png |name=Tolkat |aspect=Canor |pronouns=He/him |location=[[Miner's Landing]]}} ==Description== Tolkat is a [[Canor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]] who can unbound the player's [[Strength]]. Being a muscular Canor, he was given a job by '[[Boss man]]' to push a [[Boulder]] up a hill, though he struggles. With (75) Strength, the player can punch the boulder straight up the hill. ==Location== Tolkat is located at [[Miner's Landing]], he is found near the docks at a small hill. title: Tomb of the Nameless Warrior
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Location|name=Tomb of the Nameless warrior}}
[[File:TombOfTNM.png|center|thumb|900px]]
'''Tomb of the Nameless Warrior''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It is a landmark below the [[Burning Stone Gardens]] found in [[Upper Erisia]].

== Overview ==
Tomb of the Nameless Warrior is a cavern that is home to a single [[Rotskipper]]. A hidden door behind the [[Rotskipper]] can be broken open with any destructible Mantra. It is an Authority Stronghold disguised as a place of rest, however it appears the Etrean military have become aware of this and have destroyed sections of it, though are yet to find the segment hidden behind the door.

The entrance can be found on a shore around the rear of [[Erisia]].

This location has [[Erisore]] in abundance, an ore primarily used to craft certain [[Outfits]].

'''Towerstruck Lands''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken.'' It is a sub-location in [[Upper Erisia]] and is not owned by any faction.

== Overview ==
The Towerstruck Lands is a section of [[Upper Erisia]] with sandy mountainous terrain. Ruins of towers lay littered across the surface. The Towerstruck Lands will precipitate acid rain, rather than normal rain. 
== Points of Interest ==

==== [[The Hidden Village]] ====

* Players can find [[Ore#Erisore|Erisore]] here, a substantial part to building an outfit.
* Players can find Nimea here.

title: Traan Zakshun
content:
{{Topbuttons|p, {{iv|Naan Zakshun}}}} {{PathfinderEx|counterpart}} {{Quotes|quote=Here's the current lineup. Try not to drool.|author=Traan Zakshun}} {{NPCInfobox| |name=Traan Zakshun |aspect=Canor |pronouns=He/him[[Naan Zakshun]]{{Ref/WeaponDescription|Scoundrel's Saber}} |location=[[Lower Erisia]] |family={{iv|Naan Zakshun}} (grandmother) |image1=New Traan Zakshun.png}} ==Description== Traan Zakshun is a [[Canor]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. He is a merchant who sells various outfit schematics, equipment, and weapons labelled as "Traan's Salvaged Stock". He is a middle-aged carafe brown Canor with short, dark green hair that sweeps to the right. Both of his eyes are in a vibrant lime hue, accompanied with a small upwards crescent. On his face is a scar that forms from the bridge of his nose to the left side of his face, and markings that consist of a fading green eyeshadow on the top, with downward facing crescents that have three individual streaks on the bottom. He wields an [[Iron Twinblade]] on his back and wears the default variant of the [[Carefree Garments]] outfit, complimented with an ivory [[Suncross Pendant]]. Traan also wears a hat made out of kelp on his head, fashioned with two kelp leaves attached by a {{c|crowns|crown}} which he claims is for later consumption. Traan got into the business by working alongside his grandmother, [[Naan Zakshun]], during the [[Etrean Civil War]]. During this time, he learned to create kelp hats and gave one to her to wear. He also has a love of ongos that dates back to his youth. Traan Zakshun's shop runs on an hourly rotation. Every hour, he sells two to eight items chosen at random from a list. He can sell the same item multiple times, on the same rotation, and across multiple rotations. Most of their shop consists of uncommon weapons and schematics that are geared towards mid-game. Once every 20 hours Traan Zakshun will appear hosting a [[#Black Market|Black Market Cache]] for rare items such as [[Relics]] and Legendary [[Weapons]]. These items are only sold for {{c|crowns|[[Crowns]]}} and only one item total can be purchased per black market visit. ==Location== Traan Zakshun is located at [[Lower Erisia]], inside of a cave near the Legion camp. Depending on the rotation, he can sell 1 to 8 items at once. Typically, he sells 3 to 6 items each visit.
Traan's item descriptions will change randomly each time he sells goods from his Salvaged Stock:
*''A rare find indeed.'' *''An item most regal!'' *''Check out the drawing on the package - that's a handsome fella, surely that makes you want this on your shelf!'' *''Colour makes us hungry - everything's connected!'' *''C'mon, everybody and their grandma wants to buy something like this.'' *''DON'T drop it...'' *''Found this one in my nan's home during clearance - all pieces still intact!'' *''Hard sell, eh?.. What if it was purple?'' *''Hey now come on, it's not that expensive...'' *''Hey, you break it - you buy it.'' *''I dropped a boulder on the guy I stole this from.'' *''I threw the guy I stole this from into the Megalodaunt nest not too far from here. Hey, that rhymed a little...'' *''It's not overpriced, I swear!'' *''I'd keep this for myself, since it's so lovely... But I'd love it more if you were to buy it instead!'' *''I'm getting bored of describing these. Maybe you should just bag yourself this bargain!'' *''I've seen these for sale for three times the price, but I'm throwing you an aaabsolute curveball with this deal here...'' *''Look at all those shiny colours!'' *''Looks valuable, you should buy it!'' *''Lovely weather for buying something exactly like this, eh?'' *''No change - no problem! I'll keep the difference as a tip!'' *''Now see, I would buy this. From myself.'' *''Oh, haha, that's not dust, that's, uhm... an expensive finish, probably a fashion thing.'' *''Oof, man. No no, in the business, we call that a 'remaster'!'' *''That's *gotta* be one of a kind, right? And it could be yours!'' *''That's in good condition for its age!'' *''The Legendary Boot?.. It increases my mercantile skill.'' *''These are perrr~fectly reasonable prices, stop giving me a hard time.'' *''They don't make 'em like they used to anymore, you know?'' *''They say you should never look a gift horse in the mouth! ...Well, these aren't gift horses. Look all you want! Buy, even!'' *''This catch your eye?'' *''This could almost be an antique, I think?'' *''This is a real steal, probably.'' *''This one really stood out when I was looting the guy who had it.'' *''This one's so valuable it's been sitting around for years!'' *''This usually isn't the case, but I almost drowned getting this, haha.'' *''This will surely have you saying: 'shut up and take my money'!'' *''Traan Zakshun has wares if you have coin-- erm, I mean... notes. Yes.'' *''Truly a divine thingymabob.'' *''Used to know a guy who made these, you know... What happened to him? Oh, he's fine. He just doesn't make these anymore.'' *''Use my special offer! You can get TWO items, for the price of one-plus-one item! Isn't that a steal?'' *''What's that? Do I have a reegahl... reeg... regi... Reh-gah-lee~ yah? You're talkin' crazy, pal.'' *''Who's your buddy there behind you?'' *''Yes, this is my real name... legally.'' *''You got any Ongo slices? I could really go for a snack...'' *''You know, I'm told that Drallis Ehr guy *really* likes this one... ==Black Market== Once every 20 hours, instead of a regular item rotation, Traan Zakshun will sell goods from their black market stock. For reference to calculate when the black market is available, every five days, the black market will be available at both 00:00 UTC and at 20:00 UTC on the same day. These items are a variety of [[Relics]] and Legendary [[Weapons]], sold exclusively for [[Crowns]]. Only '''one item total''' can be purchased per visit. Like any normal shop rotation, the black market will only last one hour. Prices appear to fluctuate depending on the day. The [[Gilded Needle]] for example has been seen at both ten [[Crowns]] and five [[Crowns]]. Listed prices are what appears most frequently. ===Shop UI===
{{ShopTable|newtable|end |title=Traan's Black Market Cache |name=[Item name] |currency=Crowns |price=[Item price] |desc=I barely know what I'm looking at here. }}
The black market can have up to 8 items at once with a minimum of 4.

This is only further reinstated by him being a merchant. **Traan's name was originally "Trahne Zakshun", however it was changed in the {{VersionHistory|2025|June 30th}} update, as too many people were pronouncing it as "train saction" and not "transaction". *Traan's shop dialogues contain references to other media: **"''A strange blue turnip salesman once told me that deep forests, like the ones in Upper Erisia, bring in good coin. Gotta say, he's right.''" is a reference to the turnip salesman from ''Rogue Lineage''. **"''...What's an 'angel statue'? Look, I think you're confusing me for someone else here, buddy.''" is a reference to a running joke in ''Terraria'' that involves several merchant NPCs referencing the Angel Statue item. **"''Traan Zakshun has wares if you have coin- I mean... notes... yeah''" is a reference to Khajiits from ''The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim'', travelling merchants who, when interacted with, will say the line "Khajiit has wares if you have coin". **"''You want it? It's yours, my friend! As long as you have enough crowns.''" is a reference to Morshu from ''Link: The Faces of Evil''. **"''Colour makes us hungry - everything's connected!''" is a reference to the song ''Redesign your Logo'' by Lemon Demon. **"''Got somethin' that might interest ya...''" is a reference to a line from the Merchant in ''Resident Evil 4''. *As stated by Traan himself and Nuttoons, the developer who made the character, Traan mugs freshies and bandits around Erisia for the wares that they sell in his regular shop rotation.[[File:Trahne Zakshun troll.png|400x|400px]] This draws similarity to the [[Loot Bag Gacha]] NPCs, although unlike Traan, the loot bag gacha NPCs collect their goods off of corpses rather than getting his hands dirty himself. *Traan's original appearance did not have a scar, nor green makeup. ==Reference [[Category:Individuals with He/him pronouns]] [[Category:NPCs]] [[Category:NPCs located in the Etrean Luminant]] [[Category:Vendors]] s== {{History}}

==Description==
'''Training Gears''' are a variety of tools that increase the player's [[Attributes]] and [[Attunements]] accordingly. More information regarding [[Attributes]] and [[Attunements]] can be found on their respective pages.

They can be found in different [[Gear Cabinet]]s around Lumen, each one costing {{c|Notes|25}} and selling for {{c|Notes|3}}. Fresh spawns will start with three Training Gears, one correlating with their highest attribute, one correlating with their highest attunement, and a [[Weapon Manual]]. In the case of a player not having any attunement investment, they will spawn with a Training Gear correlating with their second highest attribtue instead.

==Usage==
Most of the attribute training gears are self explanatory, though some training gears have their own quirks to bear in mind.

*'''Boulder''' is a convenient way to simultaneously increase Attributes under "Body". You can keep using it while having no [[Leveling|experience]] as well, as long as you have enough health. <u>'''Though beware: You can die if you use it while having no health.'''</u> 
*'''Training Vest''', after equipping it, will only work if someone hits you. Boulder is recommended over Training Vest because of this reason.
*'''[[How to Make Friends]]''' can be trained by clicking the words around the screen. You don't necessarily have to type to use this.
*'''Encyclopedia''' is useful for those who are too lazy to do the minigames of [[How to Make Friends]] or Math Textbook. Although the downside of this is that it takes a long time to use it once, making it slower to use. You train both Intelligence and Charisma with this.
*'''[[Weapon Manual]]''': You can switch which weapon attribute you are training depending on the type of the weapon that you are using.

===Training Messages===
Attempting to train an attribute may display a certain message, hinting at something that needs to be done before you're able to train.

title: Training Mode
content:
{{InProgress}}

== Overview ==
Training Mode is a mode accessible from the Main Menu, which teleports you to [[Temple Sparring Hall (Dungeon)]], allowing the player to spar one-on-one with an instructor. It serves as a place for players to figure out the [[Combat Mechanics|combat system.]]

If accessed through the main menu, you will be given a character with 50 stats in every stat, no traits & a random [[Aspects|Aspect]], which adds to the 50 points in its respective attributes. The instructor uses a sword and is a novice by default.

Training Mode can additionally be accessed within the player's slots and talking to a training instructor, [[Das]] or [[Regarde]]. 

There is a portal that allows the player to leave Training Mode.

== Options ==

=== The Player ===
The player has an option to use a [[Stiletto]], [[Sword]], and a [[Battleaxe]]. You can also reset or heal your character. You also wear the [[Vigil Initiate]] [[Outfits|Outfit]]. 

If the player entered through their slots, they retain their data.

=== The Instructor ===
The Trainer has 3 types of Trainer Strengths, Novice, Vigil, and Instructor. They can use the available weapon types that the player has. Individual properties can be modified separately, such as being able to move, block, parry, dodge, roll, attack, and use criticals.
The trainer has 200 health and after taking enough damage they may remark the players skills, such as "Keep that Up!" and will remark when your hp runs out like "Don't give up yet!"

Novice seems only know how to do basic attacks if in range, but is capable of blocking if the '''only''' modifier turned on is block/parry, with a rare parry every 20 years.

Vigil seems comparable to a [[Bandit]] in terms of difficulty, being able to block and parry somewhat and perform critical.

Instructor seems to be weaker than the original [[Blade Instructor]], with its AI probably similar to a [[Bandit Leader]].

== Trivia ==

* Training Mode replaced the [[Blade Instructor]] from [[Isle of Vigils]], which featured similar mechanics.

title: Traits
content:
== Description ==
Traits are attributes given to you to further increase your strength beside basic attributes, gears and Talents. 

Every player has a maximum of 12 trait points, given at every even number '''[[Power]]''' up, so Powering up from Power '''2, 4, 6, etc.''' gives you a Trait point. The only exception are the '''1st, 9th and 19th''' Power up.

Each trait can only be increased up to 6 times.

===<u>Vitality</u>===
*Increase maximum Health by 10 per point. (Maximum of +60 Health)

===<u>Erudition</u>===
*Increase max [[Ether]] by 25 and max [[Combat Mechanics|Tempo]] by 5 per point, also increase Tempo gain by 5% each point. (Maximum of +150 Ether, +30 Tempo, and +30% Tempo gain)

===<u>Proficiency</u>===
*Increase [[Weapons|Weapon]] '''investment scaling''' by 6.5% per point. (Maximum of 39% increase from '''scaling''')
**Because the scaling increase is a percentage increase, it is much more effective the higher your weapon's innate scaling is.
**This is combined multiplicatively with your weapon's innate attribute scaling.
**This applies to every weapon with no exceptions.
**Weapons that have no scaling will not benefit from Proficiency's scaling bonus unless you equip [[Scaling Rings]], as Proficiency's scaling bonus is a percentage increase. These weapons are: [[Saintsblade]], [[Sovereign Bangle]], [[Handcuffs]], and [[Formless Shard]].
*Increase [[Weapons|Weapon]] '''PEN''' by 2.5% per point. (Maximum of 15% increase from '''PEN''')
**The PEN increase is additive to PEN from other sources, including your weapon's innate PEN.

===<u>Songchant</u>===
*Increase [[Mantras|Mantra]] '''investment scaling''' by 7.5% per point. (Maximum of 45% increase from '''scaling''')
**This is combined multiplicatively with your Mantra's innate attribute scaling.
**Most Mantras have 1.65 (if [[Attunement-less]]) or 2.75 (if [[Attunements|Attuned]]) investment scaling. Because the scaling numbers are so low, an increase to your Mantra scaling won't increase it's overall damage by a large amount, even at 6 Songchant. Because of this, Songchant is more often taken for the PEN rather than the damage bonus that higher scaling provides.
*Increase [[Mantras|Mantra]] '''PEN''' by 2.5% per point. (Maximum of 15% increase from '''PEN''')
**The PEN increase is additive to PEN from other sources.
*On [[Oaths|Oath]] and [[Monster Mantras]], instead increase their damage output by 2% per point.
*This does NOT affect the scaling on attunement-based weapons like the [[Hero Blades]], only Mantras.

==={{iv|i|<u>Dexterity</u>}}===
*This Trait is exclusive to {{iv|Vow of Iron}}.
*Increase the height and distance of air dashes.
*Increase sprint and slide speed.

title: Transmogrification
content:
== Description ==
Transmogrification (Transmogging for short) is a mechanic that allows you to keep the attributes of an [[Equipment]] or [[Outfits|Outfit]] but impose the appearance of another Equipment or Outfit onto it. It's typically used for the sake of fashion and improving the aesthetics ([[Terminology (game)|drip]]) of one's character, or can also be used to hide the true power of your character and make it seem like your character is low level.

Transmogging an outfit can be done at a [[Blacksmith]] in the outfits menu. Equipment is transmogged through the process of smelting, which is done by [[Jarvis]] or an [[Artisan]] in the Trophy Room of a [[Guild Bases|Guild Base]]. In smelting, the 2 pieces of equipment are combined into one to keep the stats of one piece, while keeping the appearance of another.
__TOC__
==Outfits==
The stats of your currently equipped outfit will be kept.

===<u>Notes</u>'===
*You are unable to transmog while wearing [[Stranded]] or transmog Stranded's appearance onto another outfit.
*Transmogging while your equipped outfit is dyed will keep the dye.
*In order to transmog the outfit you spawned in with (e.g Stranded, [[Whaler Initiate]]) you must get the schematic for it and craft it again at a [[Blacksmith]].
**This applies even if you are already wearing it.

===<u>To transmog outfits</u>===
*Talk to a [[Blacksmith]] and open the armor crafting menu.
*Select a crafted outfit other than the one you have equipped. 
**You must have more than your current outfit crafted for the Transmog button to show up on an unequipped outfit.
*Press '''Transmog'''.
[[File:Transmog UI 222.png|thumb|none|Transmog UI]]
*You will maintain the stats and dye of the outfit you previously had on, while using the appearance of the outfit you just pressed '''Transmog''' on.
*The transmog can be reverted by going back to your main, equipped outfit and pressing '''Revert'''.

==Smelting==
Two equipment of the same type (e.g. Leather Boots and Enforcer Boots) are combined into one.

===''<u>Important things to note before smelting</u>''===
* '''It costs {{C|notes|1000}} (Jarvis at Summer Isle) or {{C|notes|800}} (Guild Base) to smelt equipment.'''
*'''The ''<u>first piece</u>'' you hold out is the one you <u>''keep the stats of''</u>, while the <u>''second piece''</u> is the one you <u>''keep the appearance of.''</u>'''
**This does not apply to dyes; if one or both pieces are dyed, the first piece's dye will take priority over the second piece's.
***This may mean you have to re-dye said equipment.
*Once an item is smelted it can't be unsmelted.
*What carries over from the first item held:
**Stats
**Equipment [[Talents]] (including Blinded)
**Enchantments (''The enchanted item will remain soulbound if worn/equipped previously'')
**Stat requirements (''You can smelt the appearance of an item you don't have the stat requirements for onto another piece of equipment that you do'') (pictured)
***Stat Requirement is based on the equipment smelted for its stats (i.e. the first one held out)
[[File:Smelting Moment.png|alt=|none|thumb|539x539px|A Power 1 freshie wearing a Fleet Warden Cape smelted onto a Tundra Scarf but can't wear the Vanguard Brace smelted onto a Beige Aristocrat Coat.]]
*Smelting items '''<u>WILL NOT</u>''' soulbind the new item, even if you equip it, unless the new smelted item is enchanted afterwards. You can equip/unequip and drop them as you please. (needs testing)
**''Do note that this means you have the potential to drop the smelted item upon death if it isn't being worn.''
*If you back out of the dialogue without completing the smelt, [[Jarvis]] (or the guild Artisan) will hold the items for you until you come back.
*Rings are '''not''' able to be smelted.
*Smelted items can be passed down.
*You can smelt pieces of equipment that have already been smelted.
**For example, smelt '''A1''' with '''B2'''. The resulting equipment ('''AB''') keeps '''A1'''’s stats but takes '''B2'''’s appearance.
***You can then smelt '''AB''' with another item, '''C1''':<nowiki/>
***If '''AB is the 2nd item''', the result ('''CAB''') keeps<nowiki/> '''AB'''’s appearance, meaning it still looks like '''B'''.
***'''A + B → AB''' → looks like '''B'''
***'''C + AB → CAB''' → s<nowiki/>till looks like '''B''' If '''C is th'''<nowiki/>'''e 2nd item''', the result keeps '''AB'''’s s<nowiki/>tats but takes '''C'''’s appearance.
***'''A + B → AB''' → looks like '''B''' '''AB + C → AB''' → now <nowiki/>looks like '''C'''

===<u>To smelt items</u>===
* Head to [[The Furnace]] found at [[Summer Isle]] and talk to [[Jarvis]].
** Alternatively, you can purchase your own personal [[Artisan]] for {{C|notes|10,000}} by building the Trophy Room in your [[Guild Bases|Guild Base]].
* After talking to either Jarvis or the Artisan, they will ask you to hold out the piece of equipment you want to keep the stats of.
* Have the item physically held in your character’s hand, then continue the dialogue.
* They will then ask you to hold out the piece of equipment you want to keep the appearance of.
* Again, have the second item physically held in your character’s hand, then continue the dialogue.
* Your equipment will now be smelted.

====Other notes====
*You can smelt an item with another copy of the same item.
*Attempting to wear equipment styled after the [[Ganymede]] hat while not being a Ganymede yourself will be ignored, only showing the appearance of the item it was smelted onto.

==Description==
An [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]] that is the first purchasable inside of your [[Guild Bases|Guild Base]] that cost {{c|Notes|500}} Notes.

Once hired the Treasurer gives you access to the Guild Treasury, where you can deposit Notes, it is also where all the Notes from [[Guild Banners]] go. You can only deposit Notes into the guild base but not take them out, Notes in the Guild Treasury can be used to expand and get more rooms.

You can donate Notes to other Guilds through talking to their Treasurers.

title: Treasures
content:
::''Not to be confused with [[Deep Gems]] or [[Ore]]s.'' 

'''Treasures''' are a category of item commonly found in [[Chests]]. They can be sold to the [[Antiquarian]] or a [[Mantra Collector]] for various amounts of {{c|notes|[[Notes]]}}.

Obtaining Treasures from chests will automatically convert them into [[Trinkets]], a currency that can be exchanged for [[Notes]] at an [[Antiquarian]].

[[Deep Gems]] are also categorized as Treasures. Unlike traditional Treasures, these drop from specific sources.

==Trivia==
*Previously gems and their drop rates represented real world values.<ref>{{VersionHistory|2025|July 24th}}</ref>
*Along with [[Gold Ring]]s, Gold Bars can be melted down into [[Gold]] at a campfire. Strangely, the [[Gold Plate]] cannot melted down into raw Gold.
**The melting point of gold is 1,064 °C, which means campfire must be ludicrously hot.
*The Emerald's description is a reference to Chaos Emeralds from the ''Sonic'' franchise. While the former reference is more likely, Emeralds were also used in ''Rogue Lineage'' to unlock the Faceless class, which is Chaotic Aligned.
*The Diamond's description refers to the term "blood diamond", which is a diamond mined during times of conflict to fund the conflict.
**Ironically, conflict is usually how one obtains a Diamond in ''Deepwoken'', since they only appear in chests, and the money is used to improve one's strength, and thus ability to pursue conflict.
*All gems are held slightly lower than [[Deep Gems]] in the player's hand.
*Emeralds, which are used in crafting [[Familiar Assassin's Armor]], can be found commonly in [[Songseeker Wilds]], as the chests have a high chance to drop them.

==Description==
Trenti is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. He is a citizen of [[Etris]].

He is usually the first NPC [[The Pathfinder]] will talk to. He can help new players figure out where to go when starting out, directly mentioning the island of [[Erisia]]. He can also give {{C|notes|25}}, which is useful starting out.

He has a counterpart in the [[Isle of Vigils]] named [[Aristo]].

==Location==
Trenti is located in the [[Etris]] inn, leaning against a wall beside the entrance to it.
