title: Voidsea
content:
{{Location|name=Voidsea|area=Voidzone|caption=Here, the dying light collects like dregs at the precipice of a waterfall. The ultimate fate of all things becomes apparent.}}
[[File:Void Sea.png|thumb|800x800px|center]]


'''The Voidsea''' is a [[Locations|location]] in ''Deepwoken''. It functions as an effective boundary for the playable [[Luminants]].

The '''Voidsea''' is an elusive and dangerous region which lays outside of Lumen. The '''Voidsea''' covers the surrounding sea of the Luminants and will appear when you sail too far off from the surrounding islands.

The '''Voidfog''' within the sea can cover vision making navigation difficult, you may also experience illusions with time since the '''Voidsea''' is nothing but void.

The '''Voidsea''' is similar to [[Voidzones]] in many ways, progressing here will give you twice the XP although dying while in the '''Voidsea''' will send you to [[The Depths]] immediately. This does not happen when killed/combat tagged by a player, though everything else be it starvation, drowning or any other method of death will Depthsend you. So be careful when grinding here, as it is a dangerous and unforgiving place.

==Points of Interest==
*[[Beloved Zofia]]
*[[Boatman's Watch]]
*[[Moon's Eyrie]]
*[[Simforea]]
*A tall spire on the edge of the Voidsea in the Eastern Luminant, northwest from Port Merit. Legends say a [[Chill Broodlord Drillah|Broodlord]] with a gold chain lay upon its peak.

==Potential Enemies==
{{EnemyGallery
|BrainsuckerIcon.png|Brainsucker
|Kaijufinal.png|Dread Serpent
|LionfishIcon.png|Lionfish
|Semblance.png|Semblance
|StarKnight.png|Star Knight
|Voidthresher.png|Thresher
}}

==Gallery==
<gallery widths="300" position="center">
File:Void.png|A boat floating over the Void
Fishin.png|Fishing in the Voidsea
</gallery>

==Trivia== 
*The music for this area is [[What Mends Shall Fray]] by [[User:Naktigonis|Naktigonis]]
* Patches of bubbles may appear while in the Voidsea. Waiting near one for long enough will cause a [[Dread Serpent]] (bigger '''patch''' of bubbles) or a [[Lionfish]] (smaller '''patch''' of bubbles) to spawn.
*As seen from the book, ''Studies on Canticlysm, Vol. IV'', the Voidsea was originally called The World's Edge.
*Dying in [[Boatman's Watch]], [[Beloved Zofia]] and [[Moon's Eyrie]]  will send you to [[The Depths]].
*You lose sanity here but it's so low that it won't be a problem
*Island events that spawn in the Voidsea take on a monochrome appearance.
*If you are playing on Low Graphics mode, sailing past 100k in an axis will remove the sea texture, causing you to sail above "the void." Note that it is safe to jump off your boat and swim, and turning off Low GFX will make the sea re-appear.
*Prior to May 2, 2026, ships would occasionally teleport to another place in the Voidsea, inflicting damage to ship health and making it risky to return to the Luminants by just simply doing a U-turn. This was disabled in a hotfix update on May 2, 2026.

title: Voidwalker
content:
{{PathfinderEx}}
{{Quotes|quote= The contract is sealed, enlisting you into an otherworldly mercenary group, the Knives of Eylis. Despite the brutal training, it seems Eylis herself has a plan in mind for you.|author=Origin description }}
[[File:VoidwalkerIcon.png|center]] __TOC__ '''''If you're looking on how to get rid of Voidwalkers - visit the [[Bounty Hunting#Tips and Advice|Bounty Hunting]] page instead.''''' ::''Voidwalker'' is a PvP-focused [[Origin]], greatly favoring, but not mandating, [[Bounty Hunting]] for experience gain. Voidwalker is the counterpart of [[Justicar]]. ==Description== Voidwalkers are those who are under [[Eylis]]'s contract. [[The Voidmother]], who is Eylis's supposed "friend" said that the contract strips away all freedom that every Voidwalkers once had. Voidwalkers are affiliated with [[The Knives of Eylis]]. ==Obtainment== To obtain the Voidwalker [[Origin]], the player must do all of the following: # Have 5 player executions on a single character (Kills from the [[Chime of Conflict]] only count as 0.5 of an execution, which equates to 10 victories). # Talk to [[Eiris]] on the [[Random Encounters#Fights between Factions|Knives of Eylis vs Etrea sea event]]. # Enter a [[Subtle Knife of Eylis|Subtle Knife of Eylis']] [[Subtle_Knife_of_Eylis#Moveset|Time-Slowing Bubble]] and teleport to the [[Voidheart]]. # Talk to [[Eylis, the Punished Dreamer]] and obtain the Origin, after which the player is teleported back to their last location (Similar to the Voideye). ==Spawn== Voidwalkers spawn anywhere within the Etrean Luminant, with the [[Whaler Initiate]] Outfit and {{c|notes|25}}. To teleport into the [[Voidheart]], players must use the "Voideye" tool. In order to exit the [[Voidheart]], the player will have to speak to [[The Voidmother]] and choose the dialogue option "I wish to depart." ==Effects== Successfully completing a bounty grants EXP and [[Full Training]] points based on the amount of bounty stars, and a chest with loot. If the target kills their Voidwalker, the target will instead receive a chest and EXP, the amount of EXP granted is instead dependent on the Voidwalker's amount of bounty stars. ===Voidwalker Contract=== *''In-game description'': You progress much faster from completing bounties, and less from events. Gain access to the [[Voidheart]], and factions have a negative outlook on you. *You get increased EXP gain from bounties and decreased EXP gain from everything else. *Your starting [[reputation]] with [[The Children of Navae]], [[The Kingdom of Etrea]] and [[The Hive]] will be set to "Enemies", which allows other Voidwalkers to take your bounties until you gain neutral reputation with [[The Kingdom of Etrea]] and [[The Hive]]. ===Voideye=== *''In-game description'': Voidmother's blessing, the method to travel back to the [[Voidheart]]. *An ability that allows Voidwalkers to access the [[Voidheart]] by teleporting them. *Upon using the ability the user will start floating in the air with black swirls appearing around them, after a ~7 seconds delay. *This takes 1 minute to recharge. Completing a bounty will fully clear the Voideye's cooldown. *If the user attempts to access the [[Voidheart]] whilst having below Neutral Knives reputation you will be denied access, followed by the prompt "You call out, but there's no response..." ===Grasp of Eylis=== *''In-game description'': You can temporarily teleport to locations near your bounty target, if one can be found. However, you must stay close, or be desynchronized. *An ability that allows Voidwalkers to teleport near their bounties. If you go too far away from your target you will have a prompt appear on the upper side of your screen, signifying that you're about to lose your target and get teleported back to the [[Voidheart]]. *Upon using this ability a menu will appear, allowing you to choose your target. After choosing your target you will be given two choices of how you want to hunt: Ferocity and Stealth. **Upon choosing the Ferocity option you will be teleported near your bounty, while their silhouette will be highlighted with red through walls every ~30 seconds. However, when teleporting a sound effect will play, and you will have a very obvious black whirling visual effect coming out from your body. Grasp of eylis ferocity.gif|Ferocity option **Upon choosing the Stealth option you will be teleported near your bounty. You will not have anything identifying you as a Voidwalker, however you are not granted a vision of your target. Although, you can guess where the bounty is located just from the general location of it and if you guess wrong, you will have a prompt appear on your upper side of the screen signifying that your prey is about to escape, so you can try and change directions to catch up with them. GraspOfEylisStealthAnim.gif|Stealth option File:GraspOfEylisMenu.png|Grasp of Eylis menu. ==Pros and Cons== ===Pros=== *This [[Origin]] is very PvP centered. If you like this kind of content, this [[Origin]] will appeal to you. *The Voideye can act similar to a guild base, being a location to stock up on necessities or sell items at the [[antiquarian]]. Additionally, unlike the [[Chime of Dwelling]], the Voideye can be accessed from anywhere. *As long as you complete your bounty, you can use the bounty teleport as a way to "fast travel" around the map, skipping the time spent travelling. However, because you must find a bounty that's around your level, this may not always be a choice for you. *You start with [[Whaler Initiate]], which has decent stats for a starter armor. *The Voideye is a very good place to find people to start ganking. ===Cons=== *This Origin is very PvP centered. If you do not like this kind of content, this Origin will not appeal to you. *To further push the above point, experience gained from non-bounty sources is reduced. *You have Enemy starting reputation with almost half of all factions in the game. *Almost everyone playing any other origin hates you, Especially Justicars, who directly progress from killing you. ==Reputation== Your starting faction [[reputation]] is: *'''{{cl|ligreen|Friend}}''' of [[The Knives of Eylis]] {{FactionIcon|Knives of Eylis}} and [[Lost Celtor]] {{FactionIcon|Lost Celtor}} *'''{{cl|lipurple|Enemy}}''' of [[The Kingdom of Etrea]] {{FactionIcon|Etrea}}, [[The Children of Navae]] {{FactionIcon|Children of Navae}}, [[The Hive]] {{FactionIcon|Hive}}, [[The Hundred Legions]] {{FactionIcon|Hundred Legions}} and [[The Ministry]] {{FactionIcon|Ministry}} *'''{{cl|liorange|Neutral}}''' with all other factions {{FactionIcon|Divers}} {{FactionIcon|Ignition Union}} {{FactionIcon|The Summer Company}} {{FactionIcon|Central Authority}} {{FactionIcon|Etrean Royalists}} *''Note: Your chosen [[Aspect]] may affect your starting reputation.'' ==Trivia== *Both Voidwalker and [[Deepbound]] were suggested by user MrTheBest2, who was later made a tester.[[File:Origins'Origin.png|250px]] *Having the [[Two-Faced]] Regalia allows you to purchase the other [[Origin]]'s exclusive tools from [[Rook Rethige]] for {{c|knowledge|20}}. These include: Deepbound's [[Call of the Deep]], Authority Ensign's [[Horn of Authority]], and Ignition Delver's [[Union Pager]]. **After purchasing one of the tools, the shop will no longer be accessible to you, removing your ability to get another. *Initially, the Grasp of Eylis tool only had the option to hunt with Ferocity. This naturally made bounties unreasonably difficult and annoying, as the large particle effects that gave your intentions away immediately allowed people an abundant amount of time to log out before you could fight them. Fortunately, (or unfortunately depending on who you are) this was redone to add the Stealth option, allowing you to trade the initial sight of your bounty for the ability to attack and leave the target unaware until they were already fighting you. ==References== {{History}} {{Nav|Origins}} [[Category:Origins]] [[Category:Character]] [[Category:The Knives of Eylis]]

{{InProgress}}

== Overview ==
Voidzones are places of high risk and high rewards, with each Voidzone having unique environmental hazards, enemies and loot. They can be found across Lumen, and sometimes house important events such as [[Oaths]] or [[Quests|questlines]].

'''Voidzones grant both 2x Attribute EXP and 2x Character EXP.'''

While inside a Voidzone:

*The edge of the screen are covered in white sparks. This merely represents your presence within a Voidzone.
*Dying immediately sends the player to The Depths.
*Campfires only last up to 6 seconds.
*ALL healing sources have EXTREMELY reduced effectiveness. (ALL healing sources, meaning Vampirism enchant, Warriors Respite, etc)

content:
{{Weapon Infobox |name=Vortex Echo |image=Vortex Echo.png |type=Fist |requirements=65 LHT, 65 CHA |damage=13.5 |damage type=Blunt |scaling=LHT: 8 CHA: 3.5 |posture damage=4 |range=6 |range type=Sweep |attack duration=0.5s |swing speed=1.12x |obtainment=*[[Crafting]]: [[Weathered Timepiece]] + [[Temporal Crux]] + [[Kyrsan Schematic]] in a Crafting Table {{iv|Vow of Iron}}: *[[Strange Merchant]] Memento |selling price=100 |description=A small, pulsating vortex of [[Ethiron, The Maelstrom's Eye|Ethironal]] gale churns endlessly within this timepiece, driving its resonant ticks in eternal rhythm. Its ornate ivory white frame radiates an unnatural chill, as though the air surrounding it twists under the weight of some otherworldly force. Reaching in to grasp the ethereal chain, a sudden rush sources through you, a sensation like no other, being wrenched through the fabric of time itself. In those fleeting moments, you feel yourself grow just a bit older. |special effect=Crit lowers all cooldowns by 30 seconds |m.equip=No |enchantable=No |rarity=Relic |droppable=No}} ==Description== The '''Vortex Echo''' is a [[Relic]] [[Fists]] weapon that requires 65 LHT and 65 CHA, being crafted with a [[Weathered Timepiece]], [[Temporal Crux]], and [[Kyrsan Schematic]] using a Crafting Table. The weapon harnesses the power of space-time distortions from the [[Second Layer]], allowing you to use your many abilities again, it '''does not''' match your current [[Fists|Fist]] style, defaulting to [[Legion Kata]]. ==Critical== Vortexecho front-optimize.gif|A front view of the Vortex Echo's critical. Vortexecho top-optimize.gif|A top view of the Vortex Echo's critical. '''Vortex Echo critical sound effect''' [[File:vortex echo.mp3]] The Critical attack will reduce almost all active cooldowns by 30 seconds (Mantras, Talents, Resonances, etc.) while applying 40 flat Wither damage to the user. This attack has no hitbox and deals no damage. 30 seconds cooldown (named Temporal Fatigue). If you do not meet Vortex Echo's attribute requirements, the cooldown reduction on critical will be halved to 15 seconds. Note: Mantras that have a cooldown that's longer than 15/30 seconds will not display Vortex Echo's effects correctly on their tooltips. Additionally, Temporal Fatigue IS a critical cooldown, you cannot swap to a different weapon and use their critical while Temporal Fatigue is on cooldown. {| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !List of unaffected cooldowns: |- |Windwaker
Voideye
Buster Call |} ==Gallery== File:Vortex Echo Bright.png|Bright File:Vortex Echo Dark.png|Dark File:Vortex Echo Very Dark.png|Very dark File:Vortex Echo vfx.gif|Visual effect ==Trivia== *Vortex Echo utilizes [[Legion Kata]]s M1 animations regardless of your chosen Fist Style. **This, paired with [[Jade Vigil's Weave]] critical not working on Vortex Echo makes [[Fang and Coil]] a very bad Fist Style for this weapon. *[[Deepscorn Casque]] does not lower the wither gain upon crit usage. *Vortex Echo's critical allegedly used to fully reset cooldowns regardless of how long they were, before the weapon was made publicly available. *[[Warmaster's Medallion]] works on Vortex Echos cooldown, lowering it down to 26 seconds (outside of [[Chime of Conflict]]). *The cooldown reduction also functions on Hive Fountains. *When not in use, the Vortex Echo is holstered on the character's left hip. {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Fists]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Criticals]] [[Category:Core-Attribute based weapons]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Animations]] [[Category:Relics]] [[Category:Legendary Weapons]] [[Category:Light Weapons]] [[Category:Relic Weapon]]

title: Vow of Iron
content:
{{IronVowEx}} {{Quotes|quote=Wield the memories of the fallen.
The path ahead is not a forgiving one.|author=Path description}} [[File:VowOfIronIcon.png|center|150px]] ==Description== Vow of Iron is one of two Paths (gamemodes) available in ''Deepwoken'', the other being [[Pathfinder]]. In Vow of Iron, you relive the events of {{iv|left|Zi'eer, the Fourth Prophet|Zi'eer's}} rise to power in 1233 CE through {{iv|left|Mementos}}, the memories of the fallen that you, [[The Inheritor]], wield in an attempt to find a detail or weakness that would allow the [[Circle of Honor]] to defeat Zi'eer in present days. Vow of Iron is, in essence, a hard mode of ''Deepwoken''. Featuring new enemies, bosses, restricted and tweaked progression, and a new map, showcasing Lumen as it was 38 years before the arrival of the Pathfinder. ===In-game Description=== ''Each Memento plays differently and has its own pool of Talents and Mantras to purchase.'' ''Experience the Eastern Luminant as it was in 1233 CE by reliving the memories of the fallen.'' ''Face a gauntlet of uniquely challenging bosses, searching for a way to bring down the monstrous Lord Regent.'' ''Any death will send you to the Depths. Banking and trading are disabled.'' ==Differences from Pathfinder== Vow of Iron feature many differences from Pathfinder, aimed at providing a new, more complicated and punishing experience to the player. ===General=== *Any Weapon or Schematic can be equipped as long as your Memento's '''final''' attributes meet their requirements, rather than your current attributes needing to meet their requirements. **Some Mementos only allow certain weapon classes or lock your outfit to the one you spawn with however. **For example you can equip the {{iv|left|Darksteel Cleaver}}, a 100 Heavy Weapon requirement weapon, on [[Berserker]] at Power 1, because Berserker has 100 Heavy Weapon in its final attributes. *You effectively have infinite Mantra slots, with the only limiting factor being how many Mantras your Memento gives you. *[[Gliders]] have unlimited uses. *The [[Echoes|Echo]] system is entirely absent in Vow of Iron. You will not gain your Echo Talents or bonuses from the Echo Upgrades and Unlocks you've purchased in Pathfinder. **The Roguelite aspect of progression in this gamemode is obtaining new Mementos. *Vow of Iron features a separate [[Aspect]] slot used exclusively for the mode. You can swap between your Pathfinder and Vow of Iron aspect freely in the character creation menu. You cannot use your Vow of Iron Aspect in Pathfinder. **There are also unique Aspects available in Vow of Iron, and all Aspects receive an additional new [[Talents#Innate|innate Talent]]. **Purchasing an {{c|robux|Aspect Reroll}} on either gamemode will give you an '''Aspect Reroll Token''' for the opposite gamemode. This allows you to reroll your Aspect for free. Reroll Tokens are account wide and can be cashed in on any slot. Aspect Swap 1.png|Aspect Swap Aspect Swap 2.png|Aspect Swap Reroll Token.png|Reroll Token Reroll Token2.png|Token Confirmation *A lot of Pathfinder NPCs are absent, with Vow of Iron counterparts. *Legendary Weapons can be [[Enchantments|Enchanted]]. ===Mementos and Progression=== *In Vow of Iron, players do not progress their own build. They choose one of the {{iv|left|Mementos}} available, embodying the memories of the fallen. **These Mementos can have unique restrictions applied to them (such as being unable to use certain weapon type) and have a set stat distribution, which is gained as you Power Up. *To progress, Power Ups must be purchased from the {{iv|left|Reclaimer of the Recollection}} in {{iv|left|The Cerebral Spire}} for {{c|notes|Notes}}. You must also purchase Talents and Mantras directly from him. Your available Talents and Mantras depend on your Power and the Memento you are using. **You unlock a set of Talents and Mantras to purchase at Power 1, 5, 10, 15 and sometime 20. *You will be level locked at Powers 5, 10, and 15, but defeating the following bosses will allow you to surpass these limits; **Defeating {{iv|left|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard (Temple of Mur)}} will allow you to progress 5 levels past your current limit. **Defeating {{iv|left|Dravik, The Rat King}} will allow you to progress 5 levels past your current limit. **Defeating {{iv|left|True Heart of Enmity}} will allow you to progress 5 levels past your current limit. *Defeating a certain boss does not set your limit to that power, you will only get 5 more levels per boss. *Uniquely to these bosses, dying will instead revive you, gives you 50% Wither and heal the boss to full HP, along with doubling your damage. **This effect will only trigger once per fight. Failing and returning to the boss will reenable this effect. *Additionally, defeating the above bosses may grant you additional Talents or Mantras, depending on your Memento. ===Combat=== *Vow of Iron has no passive health regeneration whatsoever. Most damage you take is semi permanent, unless you have access to some of the rare sources of healing available. **{{iv|left|Etris Flask|Etris Flasks}} can be quickly drank to restore 50% HP (60% with [[Etrean]]). However, this is a limited resource that will only be refilled by returning to {{iv|left|The Cerebral Spire}}, entering {{iv|left|The Depths (Vow of Iron)|The Depths}}, or by escaping The Depths. Upon creating your character, you will only have 1 Etris Flask charge, but more charges can be bought across the Luminant. **[[Campfire]]s can still be used to restore your health. **Health Packs only grants 5% HP. Enemies in The Depths provide no Health Packs. **Entering a Boundary will heal you to full however. (You can also enter a Boundary while being Combat Tagged.) *Vow of Iron characters have a permanently stained health bar. Any death will send them to The Depths. *Vow of Iron characters face a unique Depths Trial that features [[Bone Keeper]], [[Parliament]], [[Prime Megalodaunt]] and {{iv|left|Nautilodaunt Officiate}}. *Auto Parry is completely removed, requiring you to manually parry continuous attacks. **There is still an extremely brief window where following attacks will not hit, but it is much smaller, and doesnt trigger auto parry. *Monsters are now able to be guardbroken much like players, even from a parry. ===Loot=== *Defeating enemies yields only one item. This item is usually an equipment or weapon drop and is rarely a miscellaneous item unlike Pathfinder. **Dedicated loot drops are almost entirely absent in Vow of Iron, only existing through Chest drops. *Chests cannot be opened. Instead, they must be carried and brought to certain NPCs or The Cerebral Spire to be opened. Chests yield random loot and large amount of Notes, which is necessary for progression. **Interacting with a chest will have you carry it in a sack on your shoulder. You can't carry multiple chests at once, however, getting put in hitstun or ragdolled will have you drop the sack. *There are static items around the map that can be picked up. For example, the [[Pleeksty's Inferno]] can be found at [[Saramaed Summit]]. *Black loot boxes can be found around the map, where you spend {{c|notes|Notes}} to obtain a random item. ====Static Spawn Items==== Certain items can be found laying on the ground in a given spot and can be picked up. Items marked with {{iv|icon}} are exclusive to this gamemode. *[[Blindseer's Ring]]: Sitting on top of the [[Eastern Interstitial Lighthouse]] *[[Bloodtide Trident]]: Resting near the [[Hell Mode|Hell Bell]] *{{iv|l|Darksteel Cleaver}}: In depths at the location of [[The Chariot's Spire]] *{{iv|l|Depthsplitter}}: In depths near the divers encampment *{{iv|l|Deranged Treasure}}:Located under some corals near where [[Nostor, Master of Shadow|Nostor]] would be *{{iv|l|Duskshot}}: Located behind a door to the right of "flat side" gate *{{iv|l|Frost Gauntlets}}: By the back room of {{iv|The Indigo Citadel}} *[[Frost Ring]]: Sitting on the ground next to [[Starfield Tundra]] *[[Halberd]]: Lodged into a tree on the edge of [[Merit's Reach]] *{{iv|l|Icepick}}: Sitting on top of an ice structure in [[Starfield Tundra]] *[[Iron Requiem]]: Above the blacksmith in [[Summer Isle]] *[[Kanabo]]: By the back room of {{iv|Viridian Sanctuary Ruins}} *{{iv|l|Night Star}}: Located left of [[Marauder's Entrance]], near an ignition union camp *[[Petra's Anchor]]: Located on the southwest island bordering summer isle *[[Pleeksty's Inferno]]: Sitting on a rock in the middle of a lava pool at {{iv|Saramaed Summit (Vow of Iron)|Saramaed Summit}} *{{iv|l|Prototype Railblade}}: Near a {{iv|Golem Magma|Magma Golem}} at {{iv|Saramaed Summit (Vow of Iron)|Saramaed Summit}} *[[Rifle Spear]]: On a raised platform on the south east corner of the Legion Camp {{iv|Boundary}} *[[Stormseye]]: Near the Summer Abandoned Castle {{iv|Boundary}} in a box near the east corner. -4460 97 650 *[[Transfusion Ring]]: Located just past the "South" icon on the map compass *{{iv|l|Void Ring}}: On an island behind {{iv|Etris (Vow of Iron)|Etris}} *[[Warden Ceremonial Sword]]: Near the exit/entrance of the Miners Cave {{iv|Boundary}} *[[Whaling Knife]]: Inside a red tent in a camp east of the Aratel Temple {{iv|Boundary}} ===Lumen and The Depths=== *As the events of Vow of Iron take place 38 years ago, the world reflects this time period, featuring tweaked, reworked, missing, or entirely new locations. *Vow of Iron takes place in a game instance separate from Pathfinder. Pathfinder and Vow of Iron characters cannot interact with each other in any capacity. *The Etrean and Eastern Luminant are combined into a singular map. The map is much more compact, with islands being much closer to one another. *Ziplines are heavily dotted around the map, allowing quick traversal. *The Depths have also changed. You can see the VOI Depths [[The Depths (Vow of Iron)|here]]. *Events now only include bosses such as [[The Doom of Caeranthil]] **At times where either Doom of Caeranthil or Interluminary Parasol would appear in Pathfinder, only Caeranthil appears instead. *{{iv|left|Boundary|Boundaries}} can be found in set, static locations. Boundaries act as a fast travel point to enter and leave [[The Cerebral Spire]]. The locations of these Boundaries can be found on the [[Boundary]] page. **Boundaries save between characters made on that same slot. **Entering a Boundary will heal you to full and will automatically cash in any chests you are carrying. ==Gallery== VOI Sneakpeak.png|Vow of Iron initial announcement teaser VOI Teaser 1.png|Sneakpeek 1, showing the {{iv|left|True Heart of Enmity}} VOI Teaser 2.png|Sneakpeek 2, showing the {{iv|left|Maestro Alkhurst Legato}} VOI Teaser 3.png|Sneakpeek 3, showing {{iv|left|The Golden Rat}} VOI Teaser 4.png|Sneakpeek 4, showcasing a player wielding a [[Katana]] enchanted with {{iv|Ether Surge}} facing off against a {{iv|left|Shogun of the Prophet's Guard}} VOI Teaser 5.png|Sneakpeek 5, showcasing {{iv|left|Fragments of Else}} VOI Game Icon.png|''Deepwoken: Ironsworn'' Game Icon ==Tips== Learning to properly play through Vow of Iron will require a lot of patience, as boss attack patterns are tricky to deal with at first. It is recommended to play extremely safe for your first couple of playthroughs, and picking a high health memento to learn the bosses, like Saint's Jay or Breaker, is recommended so that you don't die too fast. ===Recommended progression=== *Power 1-5: Jobs at [[Meteor Isle]], or if you're more experienced, defeat the Shogun and use the {{C|notes|2,000}} to power up. *Power 5-10: Jobs at the [[Red Lotus Keep]], which you can pick up from the red job board and then glide down to the jobsites, or, if you have a weapon that deals blunt damage, the Legion Camp boundary is a great way to power up as each of the 3 [[Moss Knight|Moss Knights]] gives {{C|notes|500}} and they individually respawn every 2 minutes. *Power 10-15: Jobs at the [[Red Lotus Keep]], which you pick up from the blue job board and then glide to the jobsites. *Power 15-20: Jobs at the [[The Indigo Citadel]], where you '''only''' pick the war of attrition job as Shogun Specialist and The Etrean Apostle too much time and are very risky compared to the Shogun. ===Other tips=== *After defeating the Shogun, you can gain elevation and glide east from the Temple of Mur to the Viridian Sanctuary Ruins where you can buy the [[Etris Flask]][[File:mur to viridian.mov|360px]]. After that, you can glide all the way down to the legion Camp Boundary to to get back to the cerebral spire[[File:Viridian to Legion camp.mp4|360px]]. *If you have the slots available, consider keeping 1 slot as a Power 20 to do the War of Attrition quests and then once you get all 3 in a single lootbag, you can hide it somewhere so that on a different slot, if you rejoin the same sever, you can access the high value loot bags at an early level. ==References== [[Category:Game Modes]] [[Category:Paths]] [[Category:Character]]

title: Vow of Mastery
content:
''This page is about the Vow of Mastery Talent. If you were looking for the mechanic that allows you to make alliances with other players, see [[Vow of Allegiance]].'' {{Quotes|quote=Come on, boys. Won't you shake a poor sinners hand? |author=some random Celtor trying to solo his Linkstrider Oath}} [[File:Vow of Mastery.png|right|frameless|289x289px]] ==Description== '''Vow of Mastery''' is a [[Talent]] which allows the user to make other players into subjects and issue commands to those subjects. While any player can be a subject (so long as they don't already have a master), the Talent is required to become a master, and has a requirement of 20 Charisma. ==How to Use== [[File:Vow.png|thumb|alt=|Confirmation menu when accepting a Vow of Mastery.]] To become a master, you must ask a player:
"Wanna make a vow of mastery [First Name]?" Additionally, you can also use the Vow of Mastery tool and click on "Offer a Vow of Mastery". The player must respond positively ("yes" "sure" "alright" etc.) After responding so, the subject will have a menu appear which warns them and lets them accept or decline the vow. Once accepted, an animation of shaking hands will play and the player will become your Subject. You can now use commands on them, by typing them into chat or use the Vow of Mastery tool. However, most of the more useful commands must be unlocked through additional [[Talents]], which require more [[Attributes|Charisma]]. Subjects cannot undo the vow without making a wish at [[Yun'Shul]] or wiping, and can only have one master, making the decision relatively permanent. In addition to using the name of a specific Subject, commands can use the names "''all'' " or "''everyone''" to affect all Subjects, but this doesn't work for all commands, and will still be used on one subject. Multiple commands can be stacked in a single message, for example the command "''[Name]'', say I will sleep now." will both cause the Subject to sleep, and also say "I will sleep now." '''Disclaimer''': Keep in mind that the commands will activate should you say their prompts at any part your message; saying "what if I said explode all" will cause the Explode command to trigger on all of your subjects. Be cautious of what you say. ==Commands== {| class="fandom-table" !Command !Requirements !Effect |- |

You can hide a bunch of alts in an nearby location and sacrifice them for HP whenever you need it. Alternatively, you can raise one alt to have high Charisma and use it to tell your main to live. The second method is recommended as you will not need to train Charisma on your main, plus "live" counts as a revive. ** This method is currently highly ineffective as commands such as ''Live'' and ''Sacrifice'' now have significant range caps, making it exceedingly difficult to hide alternate accounts nearby in ganks. *You can still make the Vow of Mastery in Fragments of Self, however no commands work there. *Mentioning any command in any part of a sentence will cause its effect. Example: "I could just explode all" *Trying to use the say command to force a vow to say "Sorry [Name]" or "My bad [Name]" won't work. **Similarly using the say command to force your vow to use a Roblox chat command will make them say it, but not use it, for example: "[Name] say /e dance" will make the subject say "/e dance" but they won't start dancing. *The leech command will always drain the subject of all their ether, no matter if the master has 40%, 50%, 60% or even 99% ether. *''If a Vow Master (A) has a Vow on another Vow Master (B), (A) can use their commands on (B)'s Subjects and (B) themselves (granted that both are in the same server).'' *Locate command highlights the whole player model, including a thresher if they mounting it, or if they are disguised as a campfire. title: Vows
content:
[[File:Jotalovow.png|thumb|Two players making a Vow of Mastery (courtesy of [https://www.youtube.com/@TankFish69 Tank Fish])|377x377px]]

== Description ==
'''Vows''' are a power parallel to, but distinct from,<ref>[[File:VowSong.png]]</ref> the Song. They are made by making a 'promise' of sorts through words that emanate from the soul, however, unlike Oaths, Vows seem to be able to be made exclusively between two people. Most Vows only exist for narrative purposes, but a few are available for gameplay use.

== Known Vows ==

=== <u>[[Vow of Mastery]]</u> ===
The '''Vow of Mastery''' allows a master to make other people their subject, being able to verbally command their subjects to perform specific actions. Experienced masters are able to issue more powerful commands, such as ordering a subject to immediately return to them or to defy all odds and fully restore all their health to continue living. A Master may have multiple subjects at once, however, a subject can only be in a Vow with one master.

=== <u>Vow of Allegiance</u> ===
The Vow of Allegiance allows a person to be considered an ally by one's abilities, taking reduced damage and being able to be affected by supporting skills such as Reinforce and [[Oath: Blindseer|Blindseer's]] Mindsoothe. Your guildmates are already considered allies and thus do not need to perform a Vow of Allegiance with you. Friends on Roblox are automatically allies as well. This can be activated by saying "Wanna make a vow of allegiance, [Player Name]?"

=== <u>Vow of Safekeeping</u> ===
The Vow of Safekeeping is often used by [[banker]]s to keep specific important items, such as soulbound equipment, [[Enchantments|enchanted items]], [[Weapons|legendary weapons]] and [[relics]] safe. It is unclear how the Vow works in detail, But it can be assumed that it prevents the banker from tampering with or losing the received item. Ingame, this Vow costs 1 [[Knowledge]] to perform.

=== <u>Vow of Companionship</u> ===
The Vow of Companionship is different due to the fact that it is created between a human and an animal, allowing for a bond to be created and a 'language' of sorts to be developed between the creature and the human. The only person who mentions this vow is [[Sordino]], who sells you [[mounts]].

=== <u>Hereditary Vows</u> ===
These are Vows that were made prior to the arrival of most animal-based [[aspects]] in Lumen, and the ones that allowed said aspects to exist in the first place. They were made a long time in the past by pagan tribes who worshipped animals, causing the descendents of those tribes to have animal-characteristics, as described in the book [[Books|"Vows by the Sea: Inheritance"]]. The only aspect that does not possess a hereditary vow are the [[Adret]].<ref>[[Books#Vows by the Sea: Inheritance]]</ref>

=== <u>{{iv|Vow of Iron}}</u> ===
The Vow of Iron is both a separate gamemode for the players to experience (see more at {{iv|Vow of Iron}} page), and a lore based Vow. The goals of Vow Of Iron is to find a way to take down {{iv|Zi'eer, the Fourth Prophet}} (Currently and widely known as [[The Lord Regent]].) in the past (1233 CE) by wielding the Memories ({{iv|Mementos}}) of those killed by his hand during his rise of power. Vow of Iron is the Vow everyone in the {{iv|Circle of Honour}} took.

title: Vows by the Sea: Inheritance
content:
[[File:Vows by the Sea Symbol.png|right|255x255px]] {{clear}} ==Description== '''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is a [[Book]]. ==Text==
===
Vows by the Sea: Inheritance
=== by Steward Bridges The contemporary understanding of the origins of the {{g|Aspects}} of {{g|Lumen}} can be said to stem primarily from the ‘Gremor Hypothesis’ posed by Steward Heidegard in his 877 CE study. In this essay, Heidegard delves into the spoken histories and folklore of the Gremor nomads, and proposes that the poorly understood mechanisms of {{g|Vows}} might be behind the internal ‘compass’ spoken of by the nomads. Gremor folklore speaks of the descent of Navae to this world, the nursing of the falling goddess back to life by a wandering nomad, and a {{g|Vows|Vow}} made between this nomad and the {{g|The Celestials|celestial}} Navae. While there are naturally accounts of the deer-horned Gremor during the {{g|The Old World|Old World}}, it is only in post-tidal sources that we find any mention of the innate compass the nomads use to navigate the seas. Heidegard suggests that the {{g|Vows|Vow}} made in the stories was a ‘Hereditary Vow’, one that would be passed on to future descendants as part of the terms of the Vow. It is said that through this {{g|Vows|Vow}}, the children of the nomad were blessed with ‘Navae’s guidance’, though not the nomad herself. The mechanics of such a {{g|Vows|Vow}} have not yet been replicated to such an extent through modern experimentation, but the question is posed - if a supernatural gift such as the blessing of Navae could be conveyed through a {{g|Hereditary Vow}}, what else could be a result of such an effect that we have taken for granted? It is well known that while there are hybrids in nature, there are not hybrids between the {{g|Aspects}} of Man - we are of the same species, but bear only one distinct {{g|Aspects|Aspect}} each. The traits we inherit are not a mixture of the different {{g|Aspects}} we hold as our heritage - the child of a Gremor and a Celtor will take after the traits of only one of the parents. The mechanics of which parent takes priority in this assignment of traits are poorly understood and have widely been concluded to be down to a variety of disparate factors, such as the 'liveliness of one’s spirit' [sic], one's aptitude with the {{g|The Song|Song}}, or the intensity of one's Soul {{g|Soul Murmur|Murmur}}. There is naturally a taboo surrounding the use of {{g|Vows}} to enforce religious tenets. The origins of this taboo are unclear, but there exist some records of the religious institutions present in the days between the {{g|The Tides|Tides}} and the establishment of the {{g|Citadel}}. Recovered holy texts speak of sacraments made and promises broken on pain of death, and of the mandatory persecution of non-adherents. Of the faiths that survive from those days, such as the Covenant of Flame, none extant today enforce {{g|Vows}} upon their members. Many isolated and less integrated cultures often adhere to the worship of animal deities, of spirits that embody nature. Without the taboo brought by history - or perhaps ancestral memory - it is believed that some of these pagan faiths may utilise {{g|Vows}} on some level. These cultures may resemble the early days of our own cultures, and this can perhaps be seen in the continued reverence of our 'patron' animal counterparts. The wild deer hunted by the Gremor nomads are afforded the same burial rites as their own kind, after all. It is a somewhat poorly understood but apparent property of {{g|Vows}} that the number of those sworn to one magnifies the resultant effects of the {{g|Vows|Vow}}. This can be seen in the strength granted by {{g|Oaths}} to their adherents. It can therefore be theorised that this may lead to potent and dramatic effects if extended to the size of a religion thousands - or even millions - strong. So, having stated the relevant background information, I posit that the {{g|Aspects}} of {{g|Lumen}} are the result of a {{g|Hereditary Vow}}. Supposing that a Vow was able to bestow upon the Gremor a preternatural ability such as Navae’s guidance, I believe that as a matter of course another Vow made long in the past may have originally bestowed the traits that the {{g|Aspects}} of {{g|Lumen}} exhibit today. Free of the taboo of Religious {{g|Vows}}, the animal worship of our ancestors gave way to an attribution of the traits of the animals worshipped as tenets of the {{g|Vows|Vow}}. In the urging of the {{g|Vows|Vow’s}} adherents to emulate the traits of sacred animals in their actions (e.g. in the case of {{g|Canor}}, the loyalty of a wolf), they were physically granted the traits of said animals as the {{g|Vows|Vow}} was brought into fruition. This may have happened over some generations - the mechanism of how {{g|Hereditary Vow|Hereditary Vows}} are passed on through descendants isn’t fully known yet, but it seems plausible that, just as words are warped through consecutive exchanges, the {{g|Vows|Vow’s}} terms naturally evolved to be more explicit in its inclusion of the animal traits. If {{g|Aspects}} emerged from {{g|Vows}}, we can also suppose that our far-flung ancestors would have had appearances more closely in line with one another. Working backwards, we might suppose that - with the common features shared between the {{g|Aspects}} - our ancestors may have once resembled the {{g|Adret}}. This is of course a matter of some dispute as, were the {{g|Adret}} a 'vowless' {{g|Aspects}}, they would have been 'bred out' over the generations due to {{g|Vows}} taking precedence. It’s possible that some trait of the {{g|Adret}} was not shared by our common ancestors, and that that is why they continue to exist today.
==Trivia== *The book is named after the group that made Deepwoken, which was formerly known as Vows by the Sea. [[Category:Books]]

==Description==
Vtreshi is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. She is an [[Apprentice Diver|apprentice Diver]] who was a member of an expedition to the [[Second Layer]].

Following her desertion from Chaser's expedition team to [[the Ignition Union]] in hopes of escaping the Second Layer, she was ultimately turned away and left to rot in the [[Ethironal Shrine Sanctuary]], unable to receive a [[Talent_Quests#Union Hook|union hook]] for herself.

Let's talk our horrific future. |drops=None}} ==Description== Vyrelda is an [[Etrean]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]] who acts as both progression for the [[Oath: Silentheart|Silentheart]] [[Oaths|Oath]] and the [[Bloodrend]] trainer. She was a former student who studied under the Second Prophet alongside Chaser. She joined the Ministry solely to gain access to Bloodrend, though she does not wish to affiliate with them for unknown reasons. Vyrelda appears to be friendly, albeit stern toward the player. She is first seen treating a wounded Diver, clotting their wounds and restoring their blood through blood magic despite not being affiliated with the Divers. The outfit she wears is [[Sanguine Finery]], obtained exclusively from the [[Carnival of Hearts]]. ==Location== Vyrelda is first found inside an igloo in [[Firfire]], located in the [[Second Layer/The Ethironal Shrine|Ethironal Shrine]]. While doing [[Oath: Silentheart|silentheart's]] progression or after obtaining Bloodrend, she can be found in [[Derelict Highchurch]] account-wide. title: War Mode
content:
[[File:War Mode Thumbnail.png|center|thumb|900px|The mighty Warcaller Bell, looming over the Eastern Luminant to the those who wish to shed blood]] ''This is a page for War Mode. Make sure you're not mistaking it for [[Hell Mode]].'' ==Description== War Mode is a player-activated event that can be started on a cliff at [[The Entropy Catalyst]]. War Mode is an activity available in the '''Eastern Luminant''', pitting players from different Guilds to fight each other for domination of the Luminant, with riches available to participating players and even greater riches to those who successfully manage to impose themself on the sea. ==Activation== War Mode can be initiated at the Warcaller Bell located near [[The Entropy Catalyst]] (on the side of the water lock). With at least 2 different guilds and at least 10 players, ringing the bell will initiate a small preparation phase before War Mode begins, then last for 20 minutes. War Mode is a competitive activity in the '''Eastern Luminant''' where players from different Guilds battle for control of the sea and its riches. It is activated by ringing the Warcaller Bell near [[The Entropy Catalyst]] (by the water lock). With at least 2 different guilds and 10 players present, a short preparation phase begins before War Mode starts, lasting up to 20 minutes. ==Effects== During War Mode, part of the game will be tweaked to accommodate for the event. The new rules are as follow: *The server will publicly display the tag "[WAR]" next to its player count and will be tinted orange. Servers undergoing war will be pushed to the top on selected slots that are Power 20.[[File:War Mode Tag.png]] *All Power 20 players will be marked with their guild emblem. **Killing marked players grants a chest and adds points to both the guild and the Warchest. **Marked players deal and receive half damage when fighting players below Power 20, and vice versa. *Random Event spawn checks are disabled for marked players, and static events do not respawn, resulting in little to no PVE presence. **Bosses such as the [[Dread Serpent]] and [[Primadon]] can still be summoned. *Guild Banners can only be captured by marked players. **Once the Warchest reaches 300 points, Guild Banners begin contributing to both guild score and the Warchest. *The [[Dimensional Travel]] and [[Teleportation]] Resonances are heavily weakened. **Dimensional Travel's distance multiplier is reduced to 1x, providing no distance increase. **Teleportation is limited to 1000 studs and has its cooldown doubled. ==Rewards== *If the Warchest fails to reach 300 points within 10 minutes, War Mode ends early with no rewards. By killing marked players and keeping hold of Guild Banners, players accumulate points for their guild, working towards the Warchest. Marked Player kills are worth 100 points while Guild Banners periodically generate 10 points each. Note that Guild Banners will only begin to generate points once the Warchest reaches 300 points. It is worth noting that flooding the server has a downside, as you incur a point gain penalty if there are too many guild members in the server. The Warchest is a collective point pool and encompass the total score generated during War Mode. Once War Mode ends, the guild with the highest score wins. The Warchest score will dictate the value/amount of rewards to the winning guild, which is then shared with every living members with a chest spawning for each one. ==Loot Table== Upon killing marked players or completing War Mode, several chests will spawn, these chests have several desirable items including: *Multiple Mid-Late Game [[Weapons]] for each weapon class, along with [[Deep Gems]], Legendary Rings and other [[Equipment]]. *[[Prophet's Cloak]] and other Outfits. *Good endgame items and relics, such as; the [[Warmaster's Medallion]], the [[Curved Blade of Winds]], and [[Relics|Lesser Relics]]. The full loot table is listed below:

Their presence in public affairs is seen as a move to strike fear into their enemies.}} ==Description== The Warden's Ceremonial Sword is a midgame Medium weapon and can be obtained from chests from [[Fort Merit]], [[Duke Erisia|The Duke]] and [[The Depths]]. Its critical is a dash followed by a wide slash, similar to the [[Prominence Draw]] Mantra. ==Critical== File:Warden Sword Crit.gif File:WardenCeremonial.gif|Critical + Follow-up The user dashes forward and performs a 360° horizontal slash. Landing the first part of the critical will clear its cooldown. Using the critical after the initial hit performs a second 360° horizontal slash that hits twice. Has a 1.25x scaled damage multiplier on the first hit, and then a 0.75x scaled damage multiplier on both hits of the followup. The critical has a cooldown of '''6 seconds''', even after the follow-up critical is landed. {{text|m1tag}} ==Trivia == *Has the second fastest medium sword swing speed in the game, alongside the [[Falchion]], but is beat by the [[Scimitar]]. *Has similar stats to the [[Alloyed Falchion]], differing only by having 1 more base damage, a lower stat requirement, a unique critical, and by the lack of innate pen. *It's model is a slight redesign of the oldest model for [[Curved Blade of Winds]], with a slight change in the color and type of handguard, the color of the handle and the width of the blade. {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Swords]] [[Category:Weapons with Unique Criticals]] [[Category:Weapons of The Central Authority]] [[Category:Medium Weapons]]

title: Warden Jericho
content:
{{PathfinderEx}} {{Quotes|quote=May you become the light that guides the blinded in the dark, may you burn bright as the Authority's undying flame, and may triumphant vanquish you the foes of humankind.|author=Warden Jericho}} {{NPCInfobox |image1=NPC Warden Jericho.png |name=Jericho |aspect=Adret |pronouns=He/him |affiliation=*[[The Central Authority]] *[[Circle of Honour]]{{Ref/Book|Jericho's Journal}} |family=*[[Aladrian]] (father)
*[[Octavius]] (father) |location=[[Fort Merit]] }} ==Description== Warden Jericho is an [[Adret]] [[:Category:NPCs|NPC]]. He is a high-ranking official within [[The Central Authority]] as the head of its Eastern garrison. He appears as an aged Adretian man with red eyes and markings, with a faded scar on his right eye. His hair is a dark blue color, and is combed back precisely to reach the back of his neck, with his bangs asymmetrically leaning towards the right. To the right of his head is a glowing white "crown" in the shape of three four-pronged stars connected with each other, likely as a result of being a [[Oaths|Warmaster]]. Much like the rest of him, his personality is still a mystery. Unlike most members of the Authority, he appears to actually pity the [[Etrea]]ns, knowing that [[The Lord Regent]] is dragging them into this 'war they cannot understand' and sees their Lord Regent as a 'thing' rather than a person. He dons a red [[Royal Duelist]] and is clad over a [[Authority Captain Uniform]]. A gold-colored [[Warmaster's Medallion]] sits on his neck and a pair of [[Vanguard Boots]] on his feet. He holsters a bell on his hip, signifying his strength to obtain a [[Resonance]]. On his other hip, he wields the [[Rite of Authority]]. ==Location== Warden Jericho is located inside the war room of the fortress at [[Fort Merit]]. NPC Map Warden Jericho.png ==Dialogue== |-|Authority Ensign= {{#tag:tabber|No division= {{#tag:tabber|Private / Corporal= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*The Adretian officer standing before you is without a doubt the legendary Warden Jericho - every {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}} soldier knows his name. He turns his dulled crimson-eyed gaze away from the maps on the table, and towards you.*'' ...[Rank]. It appears you may have gotten a little lost. Junior ranks have no pressing business in the war room, unless summoned by me. If you're looking for guidance, I recommend seeking Drill Sergeant Kernel Senior at the training grounds. You may be dismissed. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] {{!}}-{{!}}Lance Corporal= {{#tag:tabber|Meets requirements= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*Warden Jericho stands before you, looking over what appears to be strategic maps of the local {{g|The Luminants|Luminants}}. You salute him stringently.*'' ...You must be Lance Corporal [Last Name]. I was expecting you. I'm told you are eligible for a promotion to one of the divisions. The Command division is open to anyone willing to serve in it, if they are willing to become an officer. Will you serve thusly under my command? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Yes, Warden. {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I'd like some time to think about it, Warden. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You salute the Warden. His own salute radiates brilliance.*'' Lance Corporal. By the powers vested in me, in the name of our {{g|The Sovereign Drallis Ehr|Sovereign}} of Eras, {{g|The Sovereign Drallis Ehr|Drallis Ehr}}, I name you an Officer of the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}}. You will server under my direct supervision from now on. May you become the light that guides the blinded in the dark, may you burn bright as the {{g|The Central Authority|Authority's}} undying flame, and may triumphant vanquish you the foes of humankind. Report back to me at your earliest convenience. {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*Jericho's expression appears inscrutable, but you could swear you saw him smirk.*'' The waves may rush, but crash they still against unmoving stone. I think you would be a good fit for the Command division, Lance Corporal. A strategic mind weighs all of it's available options first. If you change your mind, you may return to me. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue], player joins Command Division {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] {{!}}-{{!}}Does not meet requirements= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*The Adretian officer standing before you is without a doubt the legendary Warden Jericho - every Authority soldier knows his name. He turns his dulled crimson-eyed gaze away from the maps on the table, and towards you.*'' ...Lance Corporal. It appears you may have gotten a little lost. Junior ranks have no pressing business in the war room, unless summoned by me. If you're looking for guidance, I recommend seeking Drill Sergeant Kernel Senior at the training grounds. You may be dismissed. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] }}}} {{!}}-{{!}}Command Division= {{#tag:tabber|Warrant Officer= {{#tag:tabber|First Encounter= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*Jericho, the Warden of the East, notes your approach. You exchange stringent salutes.*'' Welcome once more to the Command division of the {{g|The Central Authority|Central Authority}}. As you already know, I am Jericho, Warden of the East, by the grace of our {{g|The Sovereign Drallis Ehr|Sovereign}} of Eras, {{g|The Sovereign Drallis Ehr|Drallis Ehr}}. You would do well to quickly learn that strategic thought and steadfast leadership are key to being an Officer. I would request that you remind me your rank and name. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I am Warrant Officer [Full Name], Warden. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You salute the Warden. His own salute has a peerless quality about it.*'' Good. It is proper to salute your superior officers. Learn and respect the chain of command, Warrant Officer [Last Name]. It will serve you well not only as a soldier, but also as an Officer. I expect you to perform to the best of your abilities, and beyond. I imagine you must have questions for me. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Could you tell me more about the Command division? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}Drill Sergeant Kernel Senior will have given you a basic explanation of each division, I'm sure. But to elaborate on what you know, the Command division is the mind which guides the body of the {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}}. The position of an Officer demands steeled, calculated thought. You must understand not only strategic thinking and tactical methodology, but also the comrades who serve under your command - for it is your job to guide them on the field, as well as on home ground. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}I think that's all, thank you Warden. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You exchange salutes once more.*'' Very well. You may return to your duties, Warrant Officer [Last Name]. I expect you to report to me once again soon enough. In the meantime, you will perform the tasks demanded of you by your position with utmost diligence. You may be dismissed. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] {{!}}-{{!}}Subsequent Encounters= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You salute the Warden. His own salute radiates brilliance.*'' You return, Warrant Officer [Last Name]. I expect that you have been keeping up with your workload. Though, I imagine your new responsibilities may take some time to adapt to. I imagine you have questions for me. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Could you tell me more about the Command division? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See first instance] }} {{!}}-{{!}}Captain / Commander= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You salute the Warden. His own salute radiates brilliance.*'' You return, [Rank] [Last Name]. I expect that you have been keeping up with your workload. Though, I imagine your new responsibilities may take some time to adapt to. I imagine you have questions for me. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Could you tell me more about the Command division? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See first instance] {{!}}-{{!}}Seneschal= {{#tag:tabber|First Encounter= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*Warden Jericho turns to face you as you approach. You exchange salutes commanding respect. He seems wearier than usual. Has he always been like this?..*'' Seneschal [Last Name]. It is good to see you again. It is diligent of you to report to your superiors. May your behaviour set an example for others in the Command division. ''*He procures a pristine weapon, and gives it to you.*'' Take this. The Rite of {{g|The Central Authority|Authority}}. It is your mark of power as a Sensechal. Treat it with respect.
[Player obtains [[Rite of Authority]]] {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}May I ask you something, Warden? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*Warden nods with a solemn air*'' Go ahead, Seneschal. You are welcome to inquire. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}Could you tell me about yourself? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="4" {{!}}''*The Warden sighs without sighing.*'' I am not entirely certain you will find my personal history particularly fascinating, Seneschal. my upbringing does not exactly feature tales of overcoming hardship in my upbringing. But you may ask regardless. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}How did you join the Authority military? {{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}How did you become the Warden of Fort Merit? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*His eyes of dulled crimson gaze towards the middle distance, his focus drifting towards the past.*'' I grew up around military tradition. It was only natural that I'd enlist eventually. Both of my fathers served in the military. One of them, Aladrian, is a decorated veteran of high rank, who served as Warden of the East before me, overseeing a period of peaceful trade. The other, Octavius, is the former Inquisitor Maximus of the Central Authority, overseeing all High Inquisitors. {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*His mind wanders in distant recollection.*'' Once my father Aladrian retired from his position as Warden of the East, I was assigned as his successor by order of our Sovereign of Eras, {{g|The Sovereign Drallis Ehr|Drallis Ehr}}. When I took upon the office, I was instructed to establish a spearhead in the {{g|The Eastern Luminant|Eastern Luminant}}. Determining that Fortress Cascabel, a former prison on the outer reaches of Etrean influence, would be the best position for establishing a foothold, we laid siege to it, and conquered it. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}How did you become the Warden of Fort Merit? {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}That is all, Warden, thank you. {{!}} colspan="2" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}So, Fort Merit was built on a former Etrean prison? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See first instance] {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You exchange stern salutes with the Warden.*'' Very well, Seneschal. I expect you will keep me informed of your progress on the field. You may be dismissed. {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}''*The Warden nods.*'' The defending garrison fought valiantly. But valour alone is sometimes not enough when faced with vastly overwhelming firepower. The Etrean people insist that the takeover was the display of our 'barbarity'. But I would call it a necessary, if drastic, measure. Nothing in {{g|Lumen}} can compare to the evil which sleeps within that Kingdom. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}} {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|end}} {{!}}[End Dialogue] {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}How did you join the Authority military? {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}That is all, Warden, thank you. {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}} {{!}} colspan="2" {{!}}[See first instance] {{!}}-{{!}}Subsequent Encounters= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*Warden Jericho turns to face you as you approach. You exchange salutes commanding respect. He seems wearier than usual. Has he always been like this?..*'' Seneschal [Last Name]. It is good to see you again. It is diligent of you to report to your superiors. May your behaviour set an example for others in the Command division. I hear you have been doing well in the field. Was there something you wanted to discuss? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|reply}} {{!}}May I ask you something, Warden? {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}[See previous instance] }}}} {{!}}-{{!}}Inquisition Division= {{{!}} class="mw-collapsible fandom-table article-table" style="width: 100%; text-align:center;" {{!}} colspan="1" {{cl|begin}} {{!}}Begin Dialogue {{!}}- {{!}} colspan="1" {{!}}''*You offer a stern salute to the Warden of the East. ==Description==
The {{cl|war|'''Warmonger'''}} is a Heavy Greathammer, an enhanced variant of the [[Steel Maul]] with higher requirements. This weapon bears a brown appearance with a stone texture and a red swing trail, distinguishing it from base Steel Maul.

{{text|warwep}}

==Talents==
{{text|wtal}}

{{etal|weapon|Pugnacious}} procs on basic attack, applying various buffs to the user. On proc, you gain +10% to the following stats: damage, posture damage, elemental damage resistance, physical damage resistance, chip damage, and speed boost '''per combat tag''' you have.

The damage, posture damage, and chip damage bonuses are additive and ignore the damage and posture damage modifier caps. These effects cap at +30% (3 or more combat tags), and are applied to Mantras as well. The chip damage bonus will only apply if some amount of chip is already present.

The elemental and physical damage resistance is multiplicative to other resistance sources.

The {{status|Speed Boost}} has no cap and is applied '''per M1'''. For example, if you land 5 m1s and are combat tagged by 5 people, you will gain +250% speed. Each speed boost stack lasts 5 seconds and does not refresh upon acquiring another. Additionally, being hit by an m1 will also proc this bonus.

You gain a further damage buff upon gripping a player.

title: Warring States Era
content: The '''Warring States Era''' was the 2024 April fools event similar to [[Mudwoken]], where 3 teams compete for points by killing players from the other factions (10 points in the overworld, 2 in chime), Solo'ing Bosses, and [[fishing]]. The list of teams includes: * '''The Blue Skippers''' *'''The Red Daunts''' *'''The Green Threshers''' The winning faction were The Red Daunts, receiving a new sticker in the server, while the Green Threshers came in second and the Blue Skippers got third. [[File:Certified Red Daunt.png]] You would also get a Roblox badge by gaining a point for your team. The name Warring States Era is most likely a reference to "The Warring States Period" from the real period in Chinese history. ==Faction Appearances == File:SKIPPER K TILL MY BONES DECAY.png|A player in the Blue Skipper faction. title: Watcher
content:
{{Quotes|quote=WE WILL WAIT FOR THE NEXT LIGHT. AS WE HAVE A THOUSAND TIMES BEFORE YOU. WE HOPE THAT THEY TOO SHALL HAVE EYES LIKE YOURS. SUCH DELICIOUS PEARLS OF AGONY.|author=Watcher Dialogue}} {{Monster Infobox|image1=Watcher.png|attacks=*Watcher's Gaze *Leap|health=100,000|locations=[[The City of the Drowned]], [[Temple of the Forgotten Flame]]|}} ==Description== Watchers are environmental hazards that have a lamp-like head with a slender, skeletal appearance. Watchers cannot be damaged by any means, but will summon [[Hollow Angel]]s to attack the player. Watchers can be found in scattered across [[The City of the Drowned]] while one only exists in the [[Temple of the Forgotten Flame]]. Their body is malnourished to an extent that their ribcage is visible, and their abdomen being nearly hollowed out. They have extremely long arms, with five fingers on each hand with long claws. Their legs are nearly the same length as their arms, having nearly the same characteristics. Their head appears as a flower, with the outer "petals" being a dark olive color, its outer layer being wrinkly and veiny. ==Description==
Water Wells are a source of drinkable water for players, usually located in major cities or towns.

Interacting ({{Input|keybind|interact}}) with a Well restores ~50% thirst. Clicking on a Well with a [[Canteen]] can collect up to 5 uses of clean water.

content: {{Weapon Infobox |bankable=No |droppable=No |enchantable=No |damage type=Blunt |attack duration=0.5s |range type=Sweep |type=Fist |requirements={{t|Way of Navae}} Talent |damage=12 |posture damage=3 |range=6 |swing speed=1.13x |obtainment= #Find a [[Navaen Nomad]]. #Turn it in to [[Eastern Camp Master]], [[Eastern Nomad Leader]], or [[Beiruul]]. OR #Have high positive reputation with The Children of Navae. #Speak to a [[Eastern Nomad Leader]]. |description= |-|Weapon=''The mysterious martial arts style of the [[Children of Navae]]. Each strike is said to be dedicated to a different constellation.'' |-|Talent=''Adopt the fighting stance of the Way of Navae.'' |image=Way_of_Navae.png |scaling=LHT: 7 |m.equip=No |rarity=N/A }} ==Description== Way of Navae is a martial arts-based fighting style obtained by rescuing a Nomad from [[Erisia]] or [[Fort Merit]], or by speaking to an [[Eastern Nomad Leader]] while having high positive reputation with the Children of Navae. While Way of Navae has the same damage as other traditional fist styles, the critical possesses more range and is able to instantly guard break if the opponent fails to parry it. While the windup for the critical is longer, this is a great mix up when using your normal M1's which is what usually leads to guard breaks. '''After unlocking Way of Navae, you can choose it as your starter weapon in the character menu'''. Once you unlock Way of Navae, it is available on all slots. {{text|fistswitch}} ==Critical== File:Way of navae kick .gif User raises their leg with a slow windup before slamming it down, breaking the opponent's guard. This attack has a scaled damage multiplier of '''1x''' and guardbreaks if blocked. This attack has a '''5 second cooldown'''. ==Obtainment== To obtain it, you must find a [[Navaen Hostage]]. They are mostly found in [[Erisia]] but it is also possible to find them in [[Fort Merit]]. Once you've acquired one, you can bring them back to either one of these NPCs: *[[Eastern Camp Master]] at [[Etrean Wilds]] *[[Beiruul]] at [[Meteor Isle]] It may also be obtained by speaking to an [[Eastern Nomad Leader]] with high positive reputation with [[The Children of Navae]], granting you the Fist Style without having to find and rescue a [[Navaen Hostage]]. Completing either of these methods will grant you the Way of Navae Talent which enables you to use the fist style and unlock it for consecutive uses on the Character Creation screen. ==Gallery== File:Way of navae idle gif.gif|Idle Animation File:Way of navae m1's.gif|M1 Animation File:WayOfNavaeicon.png|Icon on Character Creation screen File:Alt navae obtainment.gif|Way of Navae being obtained by just talking to the leader with high positive reputation ==Trivia== *Slide jumping with using the '''Way of Navae''' critical can make it easier to land. **You'll use your sliding momentum to dash forward. *While the {{iv|Blessed Nomad Pendant}} is equipped, all of your swing sound effects will change and your swingspeed will be increased. {{History}} {{Nav|Weapons}} [[Category:Fists]] [[Category:Fighting Styles]] [[Category:Light Weapons]] [[Category:Weapons of The Children of Navae]]

Twins are thought to have a unique compatibility with Vows, their souls' murmurs being compliments of one another. Through identical Vows taken by twins, a form of entanglement and pairing can be granted to objects. The wielder of one of these objects can always sense the whereabouts of its counterpart. ==Description==
The Weal and Woe are a pair of Legendary [[Shadowcast]] spears.

To obtain Weal and Woe, you need to craft one [[Umbral Candle]]; you can craft Candles with one [[Beeswax]] and one [[Fiber]], then combine the Candle with one [[Umbrite]] or [[Umbral Obsidian]] to make an Umbral Candle.

After you obtain the Umbral Candle, enter [[Lost Celtor]]. Inside a building in the bottom right quarter, there will be a ritual circle riddled with other objects of ritualistic importance. Upon placing an Umbral Candle on the ritual circle and lighting it with a Flint or alternative, two twin NPCs, [[Goesh and Draud]], will spawn nearby, each wielding one of the two spears. Defeat both of them to obtain the weapon.

<gallery>
File:With this treasure i summon.png|Summoning circle for Umbral Candle.
File:TwinsRitualLocation.png
</gallery>

Note: Upon gripping one of the twins, the other will become enraged, getting up if they've been knocked and healing. When the twin becomes enraged a thunder strike sound effect will play, with a darkness forming around the NPC for a brief moment, once this clears, they will grow a second horn that glows; they will also be wielding ''both'' Weal and Woe. '''Carrying one of the twins while executing the other will prevent them from healing.'''

Obtainment Tip: Due to the Hallowtide Weapons having a unique property on grip, they break the obtainment of the weapon. Do not use Hallowtide Weapons while trying to obtain this weapon.

==Critical==
<gallery widths="300px">
File:Weal and Woe Standing Critical.gif|Standing Critical
File:Weal and Woe Running Critical.gif|Running Critical
File:Weal and Woe Aerial Critical.gif|Aerial Critical
</gallery>
Weal and Woe has three different criticals.

For the '''standing''' critical, the user spins around and raises both spears before striking their opponents with both weapons at the same time. This attack guard breaks.

For the '''running''' critical, the user casts a barrage of strikes with their spears, gradually increasing in damage per hit and finishing with a heavy thrust. There are a total of 6 hits total, with the final hit guard breaking. 

For the '''aerial''' critical, the user jumps into the air and strike down the opponent with three Shadowcast-infused slashes.

All three criticals have a '''10 second''' cooldown.

==Description==
The '''Weapon Manual''' is a [[Training Gear]] used to increase the player's [[Attributes#Weapon Attributes|weapon attributes]] depending on what they have equipped.

All characters will spawn in with a Weapon Manual. Additionally, they can be purchased from [[Training Gear#Gear Cabinet Locations|Gear Cabinets]] across Lumen, for {{c|Notes|25}}.

In order to train your weapon attributes, you'll have to use your weapon to complete a short "training exercise" consisting of blocks, parries and dodges.

==Usage==
To use the Weapon Manual, either hold it or click it in your inventory. The manual will force whatever weapon you have equipped into your hands and start a quick-time event minigame.

===Minigame===
Once you equip your manual, the mini-game will begin. You'll be forced to either block, dodge or parry right as the circle closes in on you. Failing will only result in a hurt animation, and won't damage you. 

Each prompt will have it's own designated sound, color and icon to help indicate the action.
<gallery position="center" captionalign="center">
DodgeTelegraph.png|A red circle will require you to dodge.
ParryTelegraph.png|A green circle will require you to parry.
BlockTelegraph.png|A blue circle will require you to block.
DuckTelegraph.png|A yellow circle will require you to crouch.
JumpTelegraph.png|A purple circle will require you to jump.
</gallery>

Do this five (5) times and you will receive a message on the top center of your screen saying one of three things:
{| class="article-table" style="width:100%"
!Message
!Results
|-
|You reflect on your mistakes and feel inspired to correct them.
|Minimal experience
|-
|You did well, but you know you can do better.
|Moderate experience
|-
|Your flawless performance inspires further progress.
|Maximum experience
|}

==Trivia==
*The results can vary even if you performed well, parries do not get recognized.
*The Weapon Manual has the same model as [[How to Make Friends]].

File:Groose GFX Mudskipper 2-2.png
__TOC__ ==Description==
''Tools constructed with the intent to harm others, polished to be efficient killing devices.''
Weapons are the main tools used for attacking enemies in ''Deepwoken''. They can be bought from shops or obtained from [[Chests & Sacks|chests]]. There are 3 main categories of weapons: '''Light, Medium, and Heavy Weapons'''. Each of these types correspond to an [[Attributes#Weapon Attributes|Attribute]] that can be [[Training Gear|trained]] while you have a weapon of that type equipped. Training your Weapon stat requires you to land a hit or parry with your weapon. A weapon's damage will scale based on your investment of certain [[Attributes]]. Weapons often scale off of the same attributes required to wield them, mainly being the 3 weapon attributes, but may scale off of any attribute, such as the [[Light's Final Toll]] scaling with Willpower, or even [[Attunement]] attributes, such as the [[Hero's Blade of Wind]] scaling with solely Galebreathe. Weapons may scale off of multiple attributes at once, as is the case with the [[Gran Sudaruska]] scaling off of both Frostdraw and Heavy Weapon. When obtaining a weapon, it can come with up to 3 quality stars on it, which add either +2% extra damage per star, +5% extra penetration per star, or +4% weight (posture damage/posture max) per star. Additionally, the sell price of a weapon increases by {{c|notes|5/20/50}} based on the amount of quality stars. {| class="fandom-table" style="text-align: center" !Type||★||★★||★★★ |- |Damage||+2%||+4%||+6% |- |Weight||+4%||+8%||+12% |- |Penetration||+5%||+10%||+15% |} It is best to obtain 3 quality stars for the weapon you want in order to maximize effectiveness. However, this may prove a tiresome task considering how rare a favourable weapon can be. Non-Legendary weapons can be [[Enchantments|Enchanted]], granting new, additional effects to the weapon, depending on the Enchant used. Enchanted weapons can be found from chests, or an enchant can be applied to a weapon by using an [[Enchant Stone]]. Enchanted weapons always have at least one quality star. (Re-equipping your weapon will add a quality star to it if it does not already have one.) All weapons within the game have the chance of being found with or without different Enchantments or qualities along with them. Even if the characteristics of your current weapon are not to your liking, there are multiple different mechanics in the game that can change the qualities of your weapon. *[[Smith's Alloy]]; a Relic that adds one quality star to your currently equipped main-hand weapon or extracts a [[Motif]]. If you already have max stars (3), the bonus will be rerolled (Ex: 3 Star PEN - > 3 Star Weight). *[[Laplace]]; an [[NPC]] who will Enchant your current weapon (whether it already has an enchantment or not) in exchange for 3 Enchanted items. *[[Enchant Stone]]s; Relics that applies their respective enchantment to your currently equipped weapon. *[[Pluripotent Alloy]]; a Relic that Alloys [[:Category:Alloyed Weapons|eligible weapons]], turning early to mid-game weapons into endgame variants with increased stats and requirements.
